Aşağıdaki sıra yalnız bir görsel özet de.en: The sequence below is not just a visual summary; it is the actual logical order that watch checks and fault isolation will follow.

Aşağıdaki nedenler teşhis başlangıcıdır..en: The causes below are a starting point for diagnosis. This list does not recommend replacing parts or bypassing a protection before measurement and isolation have been carried out.

Uluslararası sözleşme ve kod asgari çerç.en: International conventions and codes set the minimum framework. The flag State, class, type approval, the approved ship plans, the manufacturer's manual and the company SMS determine the detail to be applied on the actual ship.

Menü planlaması, seferin süresi, rota üz.en: Menu planning is based on the length of the voyage, the provisioning ports on the route and the crew composition. The cook usually prepares a 7-, 10- or 14-day "menu rotation" (cyclic menu); this rotation prevents menu fatigue while making stock planning and order quantities predictable. On long ocean passages (e.g. a transpacific crossing of 14-21 days), the menu is staged according to the order in which fresh produce runs out: the first days are planned mainly around fresh vegetables/fruit and fresh meat, and the last days mainly around frozen and canned food.

Aşçı menü döngüsünü kurarken her öğünü b.en: When setting up the menu cycle, the cook balances each meal in terms of food groups: main meals include one protein source, one complex carbohydrate, at least two vegetable side dishes and one dessert/fruit. Eggs, bread, cheese, jam, cereals and a hot drink are standard at breakfast. For the night watch (watchkeepers), a "night lunch" (night meal) available 24 hours a day is planned separately; sandwich ingredients, hot soup and snacks are left ready.

Hazırlanan menü döngüsü ve haftalık menü.en: The menu cycle and the weekly menu prepared are usually submitted to the Master or the chief steward for approval. Approval is a checkpoint both for the budget (the daily victualling rate per person) and for crew satisfaction. The approved menu is posted in the mess room; this provides transparency and also strengthens the cook's daily preparation discipline.

Modern gemilerde mürettebat çoğunlukla f.en: On modern ships the crew is usually made up of different nationalities (e.g. a mix of Filipino, Indian, Turkish, Ukrainian and Chinese). The cook considers the crew's religious requirements (halal, vegetarian, beef/pork restrictions) and eating habits. In practice, offering an alternative protein or a neutral option (e.g. chicken/fish) alongside the main dish at each meal is the standard way of resolving conflicting preferences within a single menu.

Domuz eti taşıyan/servis eden gemilerde.en: On ships that carry/serve pork, separate preparation and storage (to prevent cross-contact) are required; separate knives and serving dishes are used for crew members who observe halal. An alternative to beef is planned for Hindu crew members, and seafood-only/vegetarian alternatives for some other crew members. These adaptations are built into the menu cycle from the start and are not left to last-minute improvisation.

Gıda alerjisi olan mürettebat üyesi, gem.en: A crew member with a food allergy should declare it when joining the ship (pre-employment medical / familiarization); the cook records this information. The main allergens are gluten, milk, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, soya, fish and shellfish. The cook prevents cross-contamination in the meals served to this person: a separate cutting board, separate containers, and no shared oil/water.

Hazır/işlenmiş ürünlerin etiketleri aler.en: Labels of ready-made/processed products are read for allergens; "may contain" warnings are heeded. When in doubt, the cook prepares a separate meal for the person with the allergy from basic ingredients known to be safe. In case of a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis), the location of the adrenaline auto-injector in the ship's medical locker and the telemedicine contact must be known.

Aşırı kızartma, doymuş yağ ve şeker yükü.en: Excessive frying and a high intake of saturated fatty acids and sugar lead in the long term to weight gain, fatigue and health problems among the crew. The cook limits frying and alternates baking, steaming, grilling and boiling. To control salt intake, balanced seasoning during cooking is preferred to extra salt at the table.

Aşçı, menüyü taze ürünlerin bozulma hızı.en: The cook orders the menu according to how quickly fresh products spoil. The most perishable items (leafy vegetables, strawberries, fresh fish) are planned for the first 3-5 days of the voyage, the moderately durable ones (apples, carrots, cabbage, potatoes, onions) for the middle period, and the most durable ones (canned food, dried pulses, pasta, frozen food) for the end of the voyage. This staging both reduces food waste and makes stock management easier.

Ara ikmal yapılmayan bir seferde aşçı, \.en: On a voyage without intermediate provisioning, the cook predicts when each item will run out by calculating "consumption rate x number of days". The stock depletion table is linked one-to-one to the menu cycle; for example, if fresh milk runs out in the last week, the menu switches to powdered/UHT milk and suitable recipes are chosen.

Hava muhalefeti, liman beklemesi (anchor.en: Adverse weather, waiting off port (anchorage) or a machinery breakdown can extend the voyage. The cook always keeps an "emergency provisions" buffer for a set number of days; he or she must be able to produce at least several days' additional menu from dry and canned stores. If the voyage is extended, portion discipline is tightened, waste is reduced to zero and durable ingredients are favored.

Profesyonel mutfak prensibi olan \"mise.en: The professional kitchen principle of "mise en place" (everything in its place) is also fundamental in the ship's galley. Before meal service, the cook cleans, chops and weighs all ingredients and prepares the stations. This is the key to a one- or two-person galley team being able to serve three meals on time within limited hours.

Aşçı, dondurulmuş ürünleri bir gün önced.en: The cook moves frozen products to the refrigerator a day in advance for controlled thawing; thawing at room temperature is not done because of the bacterial risk. The thawing plan for meat and fish is carried out a day in advance according to the next day's menu.

Sıcak yemekler servise yakın bitecek şek.en: Hot dishes are timed to be ready close to service; keeping food hot for a long time both lowers quality and creates a safety risk (the danger temperature zone). Until service, hot food is kept above 63°C and cold preparations below 5°C. By finishing the main dish and the side dishes as close to service as possible, the cook ensures both flavor and safety.

Çoğu gemide ayrı subay mess'i (officers'.en: Most ships have a separate officers' mess and crew mess; the cook serves the same menu to both, with an appropriate service arrangement. Self-service (buffet) or set-menu service may be used; for the night watch, food is left in hot-holding units. Cleanliness of the service area, cutlery hygiene and the drinks station are the responsibility of the cook/mess man.

Porsiyon disiplini, hem bütçe hem de gıd.en: Portion discipline matters both for the budget and for food waste (food waste under MARPOL Annex V). By observing consumption data, the cook calibrates the quantity cooked; constant leftovers indicate overproduction, while pots that are emptied indicate too little. If leftover food is safe, it is used appropriately at the next meal; if not, it is disposed of in accordance with the Annex V rules.

MLC 2006 Standard A3.2, belirli müretteb.en: MLC 2006 Standard A3.2 requires ships operating with more than a prescribed number of crew (usually 10) to carry a trained and qualified ship's cook. The cook must have been trained in food preparation, food and personal hygiene, food storage, stock control and environmental protection. The flag State issues the Ship's Cook Certificate in accordance with national legislation.

Aşçı dışındaki yemek hazırlık personeli.en: Food preparation personnel other than the cook (mess man, steward) must also receive basic training/familiarization in food hygiene. Records of this training are presented during MLC inspections (PSC or flag State).

Tekrarlayan menü, uzun seferde moral düş.en: A repetitive menu is one of the main causes of low morale on long voyages. The cook maintains variety by lengthening the cycle, adding theme days (e.g. a national cuisine day) and considering crew feedback. Small touches (the smell of fresh bread, a home-style dessert) have a disproportionately large effect on morale.

Beklenenden hızlı tükenen bir malzeme me.en: An ingredient that runs out faster than expected can upset the menu. With flexible recipe knowledge, the cook adapts the menu to the ingredients on hand; for example, when fresh meat runs out, he or she prepares a balanced alternative with frozen/canned protein. This flexibility is the key skill that distinguishes an experienced ship's cook.

Gemi aşçısının başarısı, fark edilmediği.en: The success of a ship's cook comes from a system that works best when it goes unnoticed: meals that are on time, balanced, safe and suited to the crew's taste. A well-planned menu cycle, disciplined preparation and the ability to adapt flexibly are the quiet but decisive foundation of crew health and morale on long voyages.

HACCP, gıdadaki tehlikeleri (biyolojik,.en: HACCP is a preventive approach that systematically identifies hazards in food (biological, chemical, physical) and manages them at critical control points (CCPs). The seven principles are hazard analysis, determining CCPs, setting critical limits, monitoring, corrective action, verification and record keeping. In the ship's galley, this brings every stage of the flow under control (receiving → storage → preparation → cooking → cooling → service).

Gemi mutfağında başlıca CCP'ler; soğuk z.en: The main CCPs in a ship's galley are the cold chain (storage temperature), core cooking temperature, hot/cold holding and reheating. The cook applies measurable limits at these points (e.g. chicken core temperature ≥75°C) and keeps daily records. The records are evidence both for verification and for inspections (PSC, flag, charterer inspection).

Patojen bakteriler yaklaşık 5°C ile 63°C.en: Pathogenic bacteria multiply rapidly between about 5°C and 63°C (the danger zone); growth is fastest at around 37°C. The cook's basic rule is to keep food in this range for the shortest possible time. Hot food is kept above 63°C and cold food below 5°C; the total time spent in the danger zone is limited.

Soğuk zincir, ürün gemiye teslim edildiğ.en: The cold chain means keeping a product cold without interruption from the moment it is delivered to the ship until the moment it is consumed. During provisioning, the cook measures the delivery temperature of chilled/frozen products and rejects any product showing signs of thawing (softening, water, signs of refreezing). Products received are placed in the appropriate store without delay; they are not left standing in the heat on the quay.

Depo içinde aşçı, buzdolabı ve dondurucu.en: In the stores, the cook measures refrigerator and freezer temperatures at least twice a day and records them in the cold chain log. If a temperature goes outside the limits (e.g. due to a compressor failure), corrective action is taken: the products are moved to another cold store, the fault is reported to the engineer, and the safety of the affected products is assessed.

Dondurulmuş ürün, en güvenli şekilde buz.en: Frozen products are most safely thawed under control in the refrigerator (≤5°C); this is slow but the safest method bacteriologically. In an emergency, they can be thawed under cold running water or in a microwave (if they are to be cooked immediately). Thawing at room temperature is not done; while the surface warms up, the inside stays frozen and bacteria can grow on the surface.

Pişirme, patojenleri öldürmenin temel CC.en: Cooking is the main CCP for killing pathogens. The cook measures the core temperature at the thickest point of the food with a probe thermometer. Poultry, minced meat and stuffed products require the highest temperature; whole cuts of meat can tolerate lower ones. The thermometer is cleaned and disinfected after each measurement.

Genel hedef olarak kümes eti ve kıyma ≥7.en: As a general target, poultry and minced meat are cooked to a core temperature of ≥75°C, fish/eggs to ≥63-70°C, and reheated food to ≥75°C. It is essential to confirm by measurement, not by eye, that the target has been reached; a change in color is not conclusive proof that the food is cooked.

Pişmiş yemek tekrar kullanılacaksa hızlı.en: If cooked food is to be used again, it is cooled quickly: brought down from 60°C to 10°C within 2 hours if possible, then placed in the refrigerator. When reheating, the food is brought to ≥75°C in one go; lukewarm heating creates an ideal environment for bacteria. A dish is reheated only once, not repeatedly.

Çapraz bulaşma, çiğ gıdadaki (özellikle.en: Cross-contamination is the transfer of pathogens from raw food (especially raw meat/chicken/fish) to cooked or ready-to-eat food. The cook uses separate cutting boards, knives and containers for raw and cooked food; color-coded equipment (e.g. red = raw meat, green = vegetables) makes this separation easier. After handling raw meat, the cook does not move on to another task until hands, surfaces and equipment have been washed and disinfected.

Depolamada çiğ et daima alt rafta, pişmi.en: In storage, raw meat is always kept on the bottom shelf, below cooked/ready-to-eat products, so that dripping water/blood does not contaminate the shelves above. Products are stored in covered containers. This simple placement rule largely prevents cross-contamination in cold stores.

Tezgâh ve ekipman, işler arasında temizl.en: Worktops and equipment are cleaned and disinfected between tasks. Preparing salad on a worktop where raw chicken has been cut is a typical chain of errors. The cook designs the workflow to run in one direction, from raw to cooked; where possible, raw and cooked preparation areas are separated in time or in space.

Temizlik, görünür kir ve yağı uzaklaştır.en: Cleaning removes visible dirt and grease; disinfection reduces microorganisms to a safe level. They are separate steps: first wash with detergent (the dirt comes off), then apply the disinfectant. For the disinfectant to be effective, the contact time specified by the manufacturer must be allowed; rinsing immediately reduces its effect.

Aşçı, yüksek temas yüzeylerini (tezgâh,.en: The cook frequently disinfects high-touch surfaces (worktops, handles, taps, knives). Cleaning cloths should be single-use or color-coded; the raw meat area and the salad area must not be wiped with the same cloth. Dishes are cleaned either in a dishwasher at high temperature or by the three-stage wash-rinse-disinfect method.

Gemi mutfağında yazılı bir temizlik prog.en: The ship's galley has a written cleaning schedule defining which area is to be cleaned, how often, with which chemical and by whom. Daily tasks (worktops, floor), weekly tasks (oven interior, hood filter, cupboard interiors) and periodic tasks (deep cleaning) are listed separately. Completed tasks are verified by a signed record; this record is presented during inspections.

El yıkama, gıda güvenliğinin en etkili t.en: Handwashing is the single most effective food safety measure. The cook washes his or her hands with soap for at least 20 seconds when starting work, after handling raw meat, after using the toilet, after handling waste/cleaning and when changing tasks. Clean work clothes, a hair covering (cap/hat) and, when necessary, gloves are worn; gloves do not replace handwashing and are changed frequently.

Takı, saat ve tırnak ojesi gıda hazırlığ.en: Jewelry, watches and nail polish are removed/not worn during food preparation; they are both a physical contamination hazard and a carrier of bacteria. Nails are kept short and clean.

İshal, kusma, sarılık veya enfekte yara.en: Personnel with diarrhea, vomiting, jaundice or an infected wound are barred from preparing food; they may spread pathogens. If the cook or mess man has gastrointestinal symptoms, this is reported to the Master and the person is kept away from food handling until recovered (usually 48 hours without symptoms). Wounds are covered with waterproof dressings.

Birçok gemide, servis edilen her ana öğü.en: On many ships, a reference sample is taken from each main meal served and kept in the refrigerator for at least 48 hours (usually up to 72 hours). If food poisoning is suspected, this sample is used for laboratory examination and the source of the agent can be identified. Samples are kept in clean, covered containers labeled with the date/meal.

İzlenebilirlik için ikmal kayıtları (ted.en: For traceability, provisioning records (supplier, batch, expiry date) are kept. In the event of an outbreak, the product it came from can be traced back. The cook labels opened products with the date of opening.

Birden fazla mürettebatta benzer semptom.en: If similar symptoms (diarrhea, vomiting, fever) appear in more than one crew member, a foodborne outbreak is suspected. The cook withdraws the suspect food from service, preserves the samples, informs the Master and supports the instructions given through telemedicine/by the health authority. Intensified cleaning/disinfection is carried out in the galley; surface disinfection is especially critical for norovirus.

Aşçı; buzdolabı, dondurucu, sıcak tutma.en: The cook enters refrigerator, freezer, hot-holding and cooking temperatures on daily record forms. These records are evidence of the HACCP "monitoring" and "verification" principles. Thermometers are calibrated regularly (e.g. against iced water at 0°C and a boiling water reference) and a calibration record is kept.

Port State Control ve bayrak devleti den.en: Port State Control and flag State inspectors examine galley hygiene, temperature records, the arrangement of the stores and the cook's competence under the MLC. If a deficiency is found, rectification is required; serious hygiene defects can lead as far as detention of the ship. Regular internal inspection is the way to be ready for a surprise external inspection.

Gıda güvenliği, görünmediğinde başarılıd.en: Food safety is successful when it goes unseen. A disciplined cold chain, measured cooking, barriers to cross-contamination and personal hygiene are the first line of defense for crew health in the closed environment of a ship, where a single outbreak can put the whole ship out of action. The temperature records and samples kept by the cook are the basis of both prevention and traceability when a problem arises.

Gemilerde gıda harcaması, kişi başı günl.en: On ships, food expenditure is managed through a daily budget per person (victualling rate, USD/person/day); this rate is set according to company/charter policy and regional prices. The cook must provide the adequate quantity, nutritional value, quality and variety required by the MLC without exceeding this rate. Total budget = victualling rate × number of crew × number of days; the cook fits menus and orders into this framework.

Bütçe yönetimi bir kısıt değil bir disip.en: Budget management is not a constraint but a discipline: ordering correctly (not buying too much or too little), reducing waste with FIFO, making smart use of seasonal/cheap but nutritious ingredients (pulses, eggs, seasonal vegetables) and taking advantage of prices at provisioning ports all protect the budget. The aim is not the lowest cost but the highest nutritional quality within the budget.

Aşçı, harcamaları (provision faturaları,.en: The cook regularly records expenditure (provision invoices, quantities received) and periodically compares it with the budget; if a deviation is spotted early, the menu/orders can be adjusted. These records are reported to the company and presented during inspections. Transparent cost tracking supports budget control and prevents drifting to either extreme of overspending or underfeeding.

Gemi çalışanının enerji ihtiyacı, vardiy.en: Seafarers' energy needs are high because of the watchkeeping routine and physical work. The general target is to distribute daily energy so that about 50-55% comes from carbohydrates, 15-20% from protein and 25-30% from lipids. The cook builds this balance in practice by adding to each main meal one quality protein (meat, fish, eggs, pulses), one complex carbohydrate (rice, pasta, potatoes, whole grains) and colorful vegetables.

Bütçe baskısı altında protein dengesi, p.en: Under budget pressure, protein balance can be maintained with economical but good-quality sources such as eggs, pulses, dairy products and seafood in rotation, instead of expensive meat. Saturated fatty acids, frying and simple sugars are limited; baking/grilling/steaming are used in rotation. This looks after both health and the budget.

Porsiyon disiplini hem yeterli enerji ve.en: Portion discipline ensures both that enough energy is provided and that waste/excessive cost is avoided. The cook calibrates portions by observing consumption: constant leftovers indicate overproduction, and pots that are emptied indicate too little. It is important that crew members doing physical work get enough calories; budget discipline must not turn into underfeeding.

Uzun okyanus geçişlerinde taze ürün tüke.en: On long ocean passages, micronutrient intake falls as fresh produce runs out; this is why the cook plans deficiency prevention from the start. Frozen vegetables/fruit (which retain most of their vitamins), citrus juices and, when necessary, supplements are brought in when fresh produce runs out.

Eksiklik önleme, taze meyve/sebze stokun.en: Deficiency prevention starts with planning the stock of fresh fruit/vegetables according to the length of the voyage (see the stock management task): fresh produce is staged from the most perishable to the most durable, and as it runs out, frozen/canned products/supplements bridge the gap. This foresight prevents the fatigue and health problems that can appear toward the end of a long voyage.

Bütçenin en büyük sızıntısı israftır. Aş.en: The biggest leak in the budget is waste. The cook reduces waste at its source through FIFO rotation, correct portioning, staging fresh produce according to shelf life and using safe leftovers (with proper cooling/reheating) at the next meal. Using meat/vegetable trimmings for soup/sauce/stock (the nose-to-tail / root-to-stem approach) reduces both cost and waste.

Doğru sipariş, fazla alıp bozulmayı ve e.en: Ordering correctly prevents both spoilage from over-ordering and menu disruption from under-ordering; this is closely tied to stock management (see the related task). A well-planned order + low waste means higher quality within the budget.

İkmal (provisioning) limanları arasında.en: Prices can differ greatly between provisioning ports; the cook gains a budget advantage by stocking up on durable provisions (dry, canned, frozen) at ports where cheap, good-quality products are available. However, the quality of fresh produce comes before price; if cheap, poor-quality produce ends up as waste, there is no saving. Quality control on receipt (see stock management) is an integral part of budget management.

Beslenme kalitesi öznel bir boyut da taş.en: Nutritional quality also has a subjective dimension: the same nutritional value is perceived very differently depending on presentation/flavor. The cook monitors the crew's likes and complaints through satisfaction surveys, a suggestion box and one-to-one feedback. This data both improves menu quality and raises morale; satisfaction increases when the crew feel that "their voice is heard". Survey results are reflected in menu decisions and may be included in company reporting.

Menü rotasyonu (örn. 7/10/14 günlük döng.en: A menu rotation (e.g. a 7/10/14-day cycle) prevents menu fatigue while making budget and stock planning predictable. By keeping the cycle long enough and enriching it with theme days/special-occasion menus (see the morale task), the cook balances both variety and cost control. The rotation also makes it easier to balance the macro/micronutrient distribution over the week.

Aşçı, rotasyonu sefer profiline (süre, i.en: The cook adapts the rotation to the voyage profile (duration, provisioning, climate, crew composition) and keeps fine-tuning it with feedback. A well-designed rotation brings crew satisfaction, budget discipline and nutritional balance together in the same system.

Aşçının asıl ustalığı, \"kaliteli beslen.en: The cook's real skill is managing "good-quality nutrition" and "budget discipline" together without setting them against each other. Excessive saving leads to inadequate/unhealthy nutrition, while uncontrolled spending leads to budget overruns; the right answer is a balance of the two. This balance is achieved through correct ordering, low waste, choosing economical but good-quality sources, variety and a continuous supply of micronutrients.

MLC denetimi ve şirket gözetimi her iki.en: MLC inspections and company oversight check both sides: the adequacy/quality of the food and spending discipline. By keeping menu, order, cost and satisfaction records, the cook proves both nutritional quality and budget compliance.

Aşçı, dönemsel olarak menü, harcama ve m.en: The cook periodically reviews menu, expenditure and satisfaction data and makes improvements: adjustments that reduce waste, increase satisfaction and maintain balance. Over time, this continuous improvement cycle raises budget efficiency, crew health and morale. Well-kept records are a valuable reference both during inspections and when planning the next voyage.

Mürettebat beslenme kalitesi ve bütçe yö.en: Managing crew nutrition quality and the budget is the task that demands the highest level of the cook's skill: providing nutrition that is balanced, varied and sustainable in terms of micronutrients within a limited victualling rate. Correct ordering, low waste, choosing economical, good-quality sources, foresight that prevents deficiencies such as scurvy, and a satisfaction/rotation system together protect crew health, morale and budget compliance at the same time. A good cook uses the budget not as a constraint but as a framework that brings discipline to quality.

Gemi kumanyası dört ana kategoride yönet.en: Ship's provisions are managed in four main categories: dry stores (flour, rice, pasta, canned food, spices), chilled food (milk, cheese, fresh meat, vegetables/fruit), frozen food (meat, fish, frozen vegetables) and beverages/basic supplies. Each category is kept in a different store, at a different temperature, and has a different shelf life. The cook keeps a separate stock record for each category.

Stok takibi, kâğıt envanter defteri veya.en: Stock is tracked with a paper inventory book or the ship's software (catering/inventory module). Every receipt is entered as an addition and every use as a withdrawal, so the quantity on hand (running balance) is always known. A regular physical count (usually monthly) reconciles the records with reality and reveals discrepancies (waste, errors).

Aşçı, her temel kalem için minimum stok.en: The cook sets a minimum stock level (par level) and a safety buffer for each basic item. In addition to the quantity needed to reach the next provisioning port, several days' "emergency provisions" are kept in case the voyage is delayed. When an item approaches its minimum level, it is added to the order list; it is replenished before it runs out.

FIFO, \"önce giren önce çıkar\" prensibi.en: FIFO is the "first in, first out" principle: newly arrived stock is placed at the back/bottom and existing stock at the front/top, so that older products are used first. This prevents products passing their expiry date and prevents waste. After each provisioning, the cook rearranges the shelves according to FIFO; putting a new box in front of the old one is a typical mistake.

Tarih hassasiyeti yüksek ürünlerde (süt,.en: For date-sensitive products (milk, fresh meat), FEFO (First Expired First Out — the product with the earliest expiry date goes out first) is more appropriate; the cook sets the order of use according to the actual expiry date, not just the order of arrival. Opened products are labeled with the date of opening and used within a short time.

Aşçı, düzenli olarak (haftalık) raf tara.en: The cook regularly (weekly) checks the shelves, moves products nearing their expiry date to the front and includes them in the menu. The difference between "best before" (recommended consumption date) and "use by" (expiry date) is understood: a product past its use-by date is not used, for safety reasons; some durable products past their best-before date may be used after assessment. A product in doubt is thrown away; "if in doubt, throw it out" is the basic rule.

Sipariş miktarı, \"kişi sayısı x gün say.en: The order quantity is calculated with the formula "number of persons x number of days x consumption per person". From previous voyage data, the cook knows the consumption per person per day of each basic item (e.g. daily meat, rice, bread and milk per person). Multiplying by the number of days until the next provisioning and by the number of crew gives the required quantity; a safety buffer is added on top.

Menü döngüsü, sipariş hesabının temelidi.en: The menu cycle is the basis of the order calculation: the shopping list is drawn up by adding up the ingredients needed for the recipes in the planned menu. In this way, neither too much (waste/spoilage) nor too little (running out) is ordered. Existing stock is deducted; only the shortfall is ordered.

Aşçı, hesapladığı eksikleri kategori ve.en: The cook collects the calculated shortfalls in a requisition list arranged by category and supplier. The list is approved by the Master/chief steward and sent to the ship chandler (ship's supplies provider). The list states the product description, brand/quality, quantity, unit and port of delivery; a vague request leads to wrong deliveries.

Şirket, kişi başı günlük gıda bütçesini.en: The company sets the daily food budget per person (victualling rate, USD/person/day). The cook keeps orders and consumption within this budget and plans a balanced but cost-effective menu. Cutting the budget with cheap filler food lowers quality and morale; extravagance, on the other hand, exceeds the budget. Striking the balance is the skill of an experienced cook.

Aşçı, dönemsel (aylık) gıda harcamasını.en: The cook monitors and reports periodic (monthly) food expenditure. Seasonal prices, expensive ports and exchange rate differences affect the budget; postponing non-critical purchases at expensive ports and stocking up at cheap ports is a smart tactic.

Gıda israfı doğrudan maliyet ve aynı zam.en: Food waste is a direct cost and at the same time a MARPOL Annex V waste burden. The cook reduces waste through portion calibration, FIFO/FEFO discipline, safe reuse of leftover food and correct storage. Spoiled products are a loss of both money and nutrients; correct storage prevents this.

İkmal teslimatı geldiğinde aşçı, her kal.en: When a provisioning delivery arrives, the cook inspects every item for quantity, quality and temperature. The delivery temperature of chilled/frozen products is measured; any product showing signs of thawing, with damaged packaging, a short expiry date or a spoiled smell/appearance is rejected. Rejected items are marked on the delivery note and returned to the supplier.

Taze sebze/meyvede tazelik, çürük/küf yo.en: Fresh vegetables/fruit are checked for freshness, absence of rot/mold and degree of ripeness. Meat/fish is assessed for color, smell, texture and temperature. The cook places the accepted delivery in the appropriate store without delay; leaving it standing in the heat on the quay breaks the cold chain.

Teslim alınan ürün, irsaliye/fatura ile.en: Products received are compared with the delivery note/invoice; short, excess or wrong deliveries are recorded. In case of a quality dispute, the cook informs the Master/company and, if necessary, documents it with photographs. Accurate records are needed both for cost control and for resolving any dispute with the supplier.

Aşçı, periyodik (genellikle aylık) fizik.en: The cook carries out a periodic (usually monthly) physical stock count, comparing the records with the actual stock. During the count, expiry dates are checked, the FIFO/FEFO arrangement is renewed and spoiled/swollen cans are removed. This routine is critical both for accurate stock information and for catching hidden spoilage early.

Stok hareketleri, sayım sonuçları ve har.en: Stock movements, count results and expenditure are sent to the Master/company in a periodic report. This report provides data for budget tracking, evidence for inspections and input for planning future voyages. Regular, accurate records are the foundation of professional provisions management.

Bir kalemin beklenenden hızlı tükenmesi.en: An item running out faster than expected (e.g. a popular product) upsets the menu; the cook updates the consumption data and increases the quantity in the next order. Conversely, products that are over-ordered and spoil are both waste and cost; the order quantity is calibrated through stock counts and consumption tracking.

Bazı limanlar pahalı veya kaliteli tedar.en: Some ports are expensive or lack good-quality supply. The cook bridges these ports by stocking up on durable items at the previous cheap/good port. Forward planning requires anticipating the provisioning opportunities along the route.

Kumanya stok yönetimi, görünmediğinde ba.en: Provisions stock management is a discipline that succeeds when it goes unseen: the right quantity at the right time, of good quality and within budget. FIFO/FEFO rotation, ordering on a person-day basis, quality control on delivery and a safety buffer are the quiet infrastructure for feeding the crew without either running out of supplies or wasting them in mid-voyage.

Profesyonel galley düzeni \"kirli alanda.en: A professional galley layout is based on the principle of one-way flow "from the dirty area to the clean area": receiving and sorting → cold preparation → cooking → service → dishwashing. Cross flow (for example, raw chicken passing over a serving plate) creates a risk of cross-contamination; for this reason, the cook fixes the preparation worktops and stations so that this direction is not disrupted. As a ship's galley is small, every square meter must serve the logic of the flow.

Her istasyonun kendi ekipmanı ve kendi t.en: Each station has its own equipment and its own cleaning responsibility: color-coded cutting boards and knives at the cold preparation station, range/oven/deep fryer at the cooking station, bain-marie and hot-holding units at the service station. The cook sets up the mise en place according to this station logic; in this way a one- or two-person team can serve three meals on time.

Gemi mutfağı karadaki mutfaktan farklı o.en: Unlike a kitchen ashore, a ship's galley is constantly moving; when the ship rolls and pitches, heavy pots, hot oil and knives become hazards. The cook uses fiddles/rails (edging) on the range top, pot clamps and non-slip mats; lips (raised edges) on shelves and latched cupboard doors are mandatory. In heavy weather, use of the deep fryer and boiling large quantities of water are restricted.

Tüm hareketli ekipman (mikser, dilimleyi.en: All movable equipment (mixer, slicer, pots) is locked in its fixed position when not in use. Unbreakable/stainless containers are preferred to glass and ceramic ones. These measures prevent both equipment damage and burn/cut injuries.

Kuru erzak deposu (dry store) serin, kur.en: The dry store should be cool, dry and well ventilated; the ideal temperature is 10-21°C and humidity around 50-60%. Products are grouped by category (cereals/flour, canned goods, spices, beverages and cleaning materials kept separately) and arranged by expiry date using FIFO (First In, First Out): new arrivals at the back, older stock at the front. The cook applies this rotation with every delivery; otherwise out-of-date products accumulate on the back shelves.

Hiçbir ürün doğrudan zemine konmaz; en a.en: No product is placed directly on the floor; the bottom shelf is at least 15 cm above the floor (protection against pests and moisture). Cleaning chemicals are kept away from food in a closed, labeled area; food and chemicals must never share the same shelf. Opened packages are transferred to labeled containers with lids.

Her kap ve raf, içerik ve açılış/son kul.en: Each container and shelf is labeled with its contents and opening/expiry date. By keeping the store readable at a glance, the cook makes both fast preparation and stock counting easier. High-turnover products are kept at an accessible height, heavy products on the lower shelves (lifting safety) and rarely used ones on the upper shelves.

Düzenli bir depo, kumanya stok yönetimin.en: A well-organized store directly supports provisions stock management (see the related task): visibility increases, losses decrease and order accuracy improves. A disorganized store, on the other hand, leads to waste and to nonconformities during inspections.

Soğuk hava deposunda (chiller, hedef 0-4.en: In the cold room (chiller, target 0-4°C), a strict vertical hierarchy is applied to prevent cross-contamination: cooked/ready-to-eat products on the top shelf, raw fish in the middle, raw meat and poultry on the bottom shelf (the greatest drip risk lowest). No raw product is placed where it can drip onto a ready-to-eat product below it. Vegetables/fruit are kept in a separate compartment.

Hava sirkülasyonu için raflar tıka basa.en: Shelves are not packed full, to allow air circulation; circulating cold air keeps product temperatures uniform. The area in front of the evaporator and near the door is exposed to temperature fluctuations; the most sensitive products are placed away from these areas. The door is kept open for as short a time as possible.

Dondurucu hedefi -18°C ve altıdır; ürünl.en: The freezer target is -18°C or below; products are separated by category and packed airtight to prevent freezer burn. The cook arranges the freezer in order of use: items to be used soon within easy reach, items that will stay a long time at the back. Each package is labeled with its contents and freezing date; thawed products are not refrozen.

Buz birikimi (icing) hem hacmi azaltır h.en: Ice build-up (icing) both reduces capacity and lowers cooling efficiency; periodic defrosting is planned. During defrosting, products are moved temporarily to another freezer/chiller so that the cold chain is not broken. The door seal and the temperature alarm are checked regularly.

Galley temizliği bir programa bağlanır:.en: Galley cleaning follows a schedule: daily (worktops, range top, floor, garbage, sinks), weekly (oven interior, fryer oil, hood filter, chiller interior) and periodic (deep cleaning, degreasing the hood duct, emptying and cleaning the stores completely). The "clean as you go" principle minimizes the build-up of dirt and the attraction of pests.

Her temizlik görevi bir kayıt çizelgesin.en: Every cleaning task is entered in a record sheet (cleaning schedule/log); this record is presented during MLC and port health inspections (Ship Sanitation). Cleaning is done with the right chemical at the right dilution; food-safe sanitizer is used on food-contact surfaces and is rinsed off if the product requires rinsing.

Davlumbaz (range hood) ve egzoz kanalınd.en: Grease that builds up in the range hood and exhaust duct is the main fuel of ship galley fires. The filter is degreased weekly and the duct periodically. This cleaning is not just hygiene but a direct fire safety measure (see the galley fire safety task). The cook also keeps his or her knowledge of the hood fan and damper up to date.

Haşere yönetimi öncelikle önlemeye dayan.en: Pest management is based first on prevention: cutting off access to food (closed containers, cleaning up spilled food immediately), cutting off access to water and eliminating harborage points. Rodents (rats/mice), cockroaches, stored-product insects (flour/grain) and flies are the main pests on board. The cook detects infestation early through regular visual inspection: droppings, gnaw marks, eggs/larvae, odor.

Liman bağlamasında halatlara rat guard (.en: When the ship is moored in port, rat guards are fitted on the mooring lines; sticky traps and bait stations are placed at designated points in the holds, stores and galley. Provision boxes arriving on board are checked for insects/larvae before they enter the stores; cardboard packaging is not kept in the stores for long (cockroach nests).

Bulaşma belirtisi tespit edilirse aşçı d.en: If signs of infestation are detected, the cook immediately informs the Master and destroys the affected products; the source of the infestation (hole, crack, open container) is identified and sealed. Widespread infestation requires professional fumigation/ULV treatment, which is coordinated with the port health authority. The detailed pest control procedure is covered in a separate task; store organization is the preventive side of this work.

Kumanya depoları ve soğuk depolar yetkis.en: Provision stores and cold stores are kept closed to unauthorized access; the keys/access are held by the cook and the chief steward. This is for both stock security (loss/wastage) and food safety (uncontrolled opening and closing, breaking the cold chain). Entering and leaving the stores follows a set discipline; the cold store door is not kept open for long.

Yürünebilir soğuk depo ve dondurucularda.en: In walk-in cold stores and freezers, being trapped inside is a life-threatening hazard; the door must be openable from inside and there must be an alarm/lighting inside. When working inside for a long time, the cook wears suitable clothing and, where possible, tells someone before entering. The door locking mechanism and the inside release handle are tested regularly.

Düzenli bir galley, atık ayrımını da kol.en: A well-organized galley also makes waste segregation easier. Food waste, plastics, glass/metal and cooking oil are collected separately; this both reduces the attraction of pests and ensures MARPOL Annex V compliance (detailed disposal is covered in a separate task). Garbage bins must have lids, be leak-proof and be emptied regularly; accumulated waste means both odor and insects.

Kullanılmış yemeklik yağ ayrı, kapalı ka.en: Used cooking oil is collected separately in a closed container and delivered to the approved system/shore reception facility. The cook integrates the waste flow into the station layout; the garbage station is located apart from the clean area, where it does not interfere with service.

Koku, çoğu zaman bir düzen/temizlik prob.en: Odor is often the first sign of a housekeeping/cleaning problem: garbage left standing, a blocked bilge/sink or spoiled products. The cook uses odor as a diagnostic tool, finding and eliminating the source. Regular emptying, lidded containers and daily floor cleaning keep both odor and pests under control.

Galley ve depolar, MLC 2006 müfettişi, l.en: The galley and stores are inspected by the MLC 2006 inspector, Port State Control (PSC) and the port health authority. Cleaning records, temperature logs, pest control records and the Ship Sanitation Control Exemption Certificate are presented during the inspection. A well-organized, documented system reduces an inspection to a routine verification.

Aşçı, kaptan adına bu alanların sürekli.en: On behalf of the Master, the cook ensures that these areas are always ready for inspection; the principle is continuous order, not "tidying up before the inspection". A nonconformity (deficiency) is one of the MLC breaches that can lead as far as detention of the ship.

Mutfak ve depo düzeni, görünürde basit a.en: Galley and store organization is a discipline that looks simple but has big consequences: a well-organized galley is faster, safer and more hygienic; it is the first line of defense against pests, fire and food spoilage. The cook's habit of "constant order" is the quiet guarantee of both crew health and inspection compliance.

Galley ekipmanı bakımının temeli, arızay.en: The basis of galley equipment maintenance is preventing failures, not waiting for them. The cook puts the periodic maintenance steps specified in each item's manufacturer's manual (cleaning, seal checks, filter replacement, lubrication, calibration) on a schedule. Regular preventive maintenance reduces the likelihood of sudden breakdowns, pressure on spare parts and food safety risks all together.

Gemide ekipman bakımı genellikle ISM Cod.en: On board, equipment maintenance is usually defined within the Planned Maintenance System (PMS) under the ISM Code. The cook enters the maintenance tasks for galley equipment in the PMS or coordinates them with the engine department; jobs requiring electrical/mechanical work are left to authorized personnel (electrician, engineer officer).

Aşçı; temizlik, görsel kontrol, filtre/c.en: The cook is responsible for cleaning, visual checks, filter/seal checks, simple adjustments and user-level maintenance. Electrical panels, gas lines, compressors, motors and jobs requiring LOTO (lock out-tag out) fall under the authority of the engine/electrical team. A clear boundary prevents both safety hazards and confusion over authority.

Elektrikli veya gazlı ocak/fırın, her ku.en: Electric or gas ranges/ovens are cleaned of grease and spills after each use; accumulated grease is both a hygiene and a fire risk. On gas systems, burner ports are checked for blockage, the flame color is observed (yellow = incomplete combustion/CO risk, blue = healthy) and connections are checked for gas leaks with a soap (bubble) test. The oven door seal affects heat loss and efficiency; a damaged seal is replaced.

Elektrikli rezistans ve termostat arızal.en: Faults in electric heating elements and thermostats cause temperature deviations; the cook periodically verifies the oven temperature with a thermometer (calibration). Abnormal smells, sparks, hot cables or a heater that does not work are reported immediately, and the equipment is not used until authorized personnel have dealt with it.

Izgara ve salamander yüzeyleri yağ birik.en: Grill and salamander surfaces are prone to grease build-up; they are scraped and cleaned after each service. In bain-maries and hot-holding units, the water level and the thermostat are checked; running dry burns out the heating element. As the surfaces of all this equipment are in contact with food, they are cleaned with food-safe products and rinsed if necessary.

Fritöz, galley'nin en yüksek yangın ve y.en: The deep fryer is the item of galley equipment with the highest fire and burn risk. The oil is filtered regularly and changed when it deteriorates (darker color, foaming, lower smoke point); the old oil is put into a separate waste container (disposal is covered in a separate task). The oil level is kept between min and max; an overfilled fryer creates a risk of overflow and fire.

Termostat ve yüksek sıcaklık emniyet kes.en: The thermostat and the high-temperature safety cut-out (high-limit cut-off) are the critical safety components of the fryer; if they fail, the oil can overheat and ignite. The cook periodically verifies that these cut-outs work and does not use the equipment if in doubt.

Şiddetli yalpada açık sıcak yağ ciddi ya.en: In heavy rolling, open hot oil is a serious burn hazard; when the bridge issues a heavy weather warning, use of the fryer is restricted or stopped. The fryer lid is closed, the heat is switched off and the equipment is secured. This is a decision for both equipment safety and personnel safety.

Soğutucu (0-4°C) ve dondurucunun (-18°C.en: Keeping the chiller (0-4°C) and the freezer (-18°C and below) running continuously at their target temperatures is the basis of food safety. The cook regularly checks the door seal (airtightness), visible dirt on the condenser/evaporator, the defrost condition and the temperature indicator. Dust/grease build-up on the condenser grille reduces cooling and strains the compressor; it is cleaned at user level.

Sıcaklıkta yükselme, sürekli çalışan kom.en: A rise in temperature, a compressor that runs continuously, abnormal noise or a water leak are signs of a fault and are reported. If a refrigeration unit fails, the products are moved to another unit while maintaining the cold chain; products at risk of spoilage are assessed or destroyed. A gas (refrigerant) leak is a job for the engine department.

Deterjan/durulama yardımcısı (rinse aid).en: The detergent and rinse aid dosing pumps are checked; too little detergent leaves dishes dirty, while too much leaves residue. If the machine does not reach sanitizing temperature, the cook switches to hand washing + chemical sanitizing and reports the fault.

Dilimleyici (slicer), kıyma makinesi ve.en: The slicer, mincer and planetary mixer are the galley equipment with the highest risk of cuts and of limbs being caught. Cleaning and blade changes are done only with the machine switched off and unplugged (de-energized); a rotating part is never touched by hand. The manufacturer's guards are never removed or bypassed.

Bu makineler her kullanımdan sonra parça.en: After every use, these machines are dismantled and cleaned (meat residue is a bacterial risk and a source of cross-contamination) and correctly reassembled. Only trained/authorized personnel use them; fatigue and distraction are the main causes of accidents.

Bıçaklar keskin tutulur (kör bıçak daha.en: Knives are kept sharp (a blunt knife is more dangerous because it slips) and stored safely (magnetic strip/block). Gloves are used for hot surfaces, non-slip shoes are worn and the floor is kept dry. Ship motion increases all of these risks; this is why equipment safety and sea fastening (see the galley organization task) are considered together.

Aşçı bir arıza/anomali fark ettiğinde (s.en: When the cook notices a fault/anomaly (noise, smell, temperature deviation, sparks, leak), he or she first puts the equipment in a safe condition (switch off/unplug/warning tag) and reports the situation to the Master/engineer officer. The report includes the equipment, the symptom, when it started and the first action taken. Electrical/mechanical work is left to authorized personnel; the cook does not go beyond his or her area of authority.

Arıza ve yapılan bakım PMS/kayıt sistemi.en: Faults and the maintenance carried out are entered in the PMS/record system; recurring faults trigger spare parts/service planning. If critical equipment fails (e.g. the main oven or a refrigeration unit), the menu and preparation plan are adapted to this loss.

Aşçının yetki alanındaki basit bakım: co.en: Simple maintenance within the cook's authority: cleaning/checking seals, cleaning/replacing filters, deep cleaning, descaling, sharpening/changing blades (under safe conditions), checking thermometer calibration and reporting visibly loose connections. These jobs extend equipment life and prevent sudden breakdowns. Anything outside this authority is reported.

Galley nemli ve ıslak bir ortamdır; su i.en: The galley is a humid, wet environment; water and electricity together are one of the most lethal risks. Damage to cables, plugs and sockets (wear, water ingress) is reported immediately and damaged equipment is not used. Equipment is not operated with wet hands; earthing and residual current protection (RCD) are the basis of equipment safety, and these are under the supervision of the engine/electrical team.

Lavabo, bulaşık makinesi ve buz makinesi.en: Water connections to sinks, the dishwasher and the ice machine are monitored for leaks; blocked drains create hygiene and pest problems. Potable water connections for equipment used in food preparation must be certified and fitted with backflow protection (details in the drinking water task). Leaks/blockages are reported and rectified.

Mutfak ekipmanlarının bakımı, görünmeyen.en: Galley equipment maintenance is an unseen but decisive discipline: regular cleaning and preventive maintenance ensure both that meals are served without interruption and that burns, cuts and electrical accidents are prevented. As the person who knows the limits of his or her authority, catches faults early, reports them correctly and carries out user maintenance with discipline, the cook is the guarantee that the galley operates continuously and safely.

Yangınlar yakıtına göre sınıflandırılır.en: Fires are classified by their fuel, and each class requires a different extinguishing agent. The most critical in the galley is the cooking oil and tallow/grease fire; this is called Class F in the European standard and Class K in the American standard. In addition, there are risks of solid-fuel fires (Class A — bread, wood, paper), electrical fires (E) and gas fires (Class C/B). The cook must know at reflex level which extinguisher is suitable for which fire.

Pişirme yağı yangını özellikle tehlikeli.en: A cooking oil fire is especially dangerous because the oil burns at a very high temperature (above its ignition point), and merely putting out the flame is not enough; to prevent the oil from re-igniting, the temperature of the surface must also be brought down. This is exactly why wet chemical systems are accepted as the standard for galleys: through saponification (oil + alkali → soapy blanket), they both extinguish the fire and prevent re-ignition.

Başlıca risk kaynakları: aşırı ısınan/gö.en: The main sources of risk are an overheated/unattended deep fryer, oil left on the range, grease built up in the hood and exhaust duct, damaged/overloaded electrical installations, gas leaks and spilled flammable liquids. Grease in the hood duct is particularly insidious; once accumulated grease ignites, it can spread the fire out of the galley along the duct. For this reason, cleaning (see the galley organization task) is a direct fire prevention measure.

Yangının en iyi yönetimi çıkmadan önlenm.en: The best way to manage a fire is to prevent it from starting. The cook never leaves the fryer unattended, checks the oil level and temperature, keeps the area around the range free of grease and keeps combustible materials (paper, plastic, oily rags) away from hot surfaces. When cooking is finished, make sure the range/oven/fryer has been switched off; the galley close-down check at the end of each working period is a routine.

Davlumbaz filtresi haftalık, kanal dönem.en: The hood filter is degreased weekly and the duct periodically. The cables/plugs of electrical equipment are checked for integrity and sockets are not overloaded. On gas systems, leak checks are carried out and the main valve is closed after use. These routines are simple, but they are the measures that do most to reduce fire statistics.

Galley, SOLAS II-2 kapsamında yangın alg.en: Under SOLAS II-2, the galley is connected to the fire detection system; heat/smoke detectors raise an alarm on the bridge. The cook ensures proper ventilation so that these detectors do not give false alarms from cooking fumes, but never switches off or covers the detectors. Early detection is the key to extinguishing a small fire before it grows.

Modern gemi galley'lerinde fritöz ve piş.en: In modern ship galleys, a fixed wet chemical extinguishing system is installed over the fryer and the cooking line. The system directs nozzles at the oil surface, the cooking appliances and the hood/duct entrance. When activated, the wet chemical agent forms a vapor-tight soapy blanket on the oil through saponification; this both cuts off oxygen and cools the surface, preventing re-ignition.

Sistem otomatik (ısı algılayıcı fuse/lin.en: The system can be triggered automatically (when a heat-sensing fusible link melts) or manually (pull station). When triggered, it typically also cuts off the gas/electric supply automatically (interlock) and brings the hood fan/damper configuration to a safe state. The cook must know the location of the manual release point (pull station) and how to pull it.

Wet chemical sistemi periyodik olarak ye.en: The wet chemical system is checked periodically by an authorized service provider (nozzle blockage, pressure, fusible link integrity, agent quantity). The cook makes sure the nozzles are not blocked with grease/dirt and checks that the fusible links have the correct temperature rating and are not coated with a film of grease. After the system has been triggered, the galley is not used; all surfaces are cleaned, the system is recharged by an authorized party and the interlocks are reset.

Galley'de pişirme yağı yangını için Clas.en: A Class F (K) wet chemical portable extinguisher is kept in the galley for cooking oil fires, and the cook knows where it is. In addition, a CO2 extinguisher for electrical fires is kept at a suitable position (on an oil fire, CO2 may be insufficient or may scatter the burning oil). The cook knows which fire each extinguisher is suitable for and the PASS technique (Pull-Aim-Squeeze-Sweep).

Söndürücülerin basınç göstergesi, mühür.en: The pressure gauge, seal and accessibility of the extinguishers are checked regularly; access to them is not obstructed. Choosing the wrong extinguisher (e.g. a water-based one on oil, or water on electrical equipment) makes the fire worse; this is why the choice is critical.

Küçük tencere/tava yağ yangınında fire b.en: For a small oil fire in a pot or pan, the fire blanket is the fastest and safest response: holding the blanket so that it protects the hands, it is laid over the fire to cut off oxygen. The blanket is NOT thrown onto the fire; it is laid over it gently and the heat source (range) is switched off; the blanket is not removed until the flames are completely out and the surface has cooled (at least several minutes). Removing it early leads to re-ignition.

Fire blanket galley'de erişilebilir, hız.en: The fire blanket is kept in an accessible position in the galley where it can be pulled out quickly (usually on a wall near the door). The cook must know where the blanket is and which way to pull it, and must replace it with a new one after use (for single-use types).

Galley havalandırması yangını besleyen o.en: Galley ventilation is critically important in a fire because it carries the oxygen that feeds the fire as well as the grease in the duct. Fire dampers are fitted in the galley exhaust duct and in the supply air; in a fire, these are closed to stop flames/smoke spreading along the duct and to cut off the oxygen supply. The cook must know the manual closing points for the dampers and how to stop the hood fan.

Otomatik suppression sistemi tetiklendiğ.en: When the automatic suppression system is triggered, it typically brings the fan and dampers to a safe position; however, the cook must also know how to do this manually. During a fire, stopping the fan and closing the dampers are the basic steps for containing the fire within the galley.

Birikmiş yağ kanal içinde tutuşursa yang.en: If accumulated grease ignites inside the duct, the fire is not directly visible and can spread quickly; this is one of the most dangerous galley fire scenarios. The response is to stop cooking, trigger the suppression system, stop the fan and close the dampers, and call the ship's fire party. The cook does not try to tackle a duct fire alone; he or she raises the alarm and an organized response is started.

Galley yangınında müdahale sırası nettir.en: In a galley fire, the response sequence is clear: 1) cut off the heat source (switch off the range/fryer/gas), 2) if the fire is small and controllable, tackle it immediately with a suitable extinguisher/fire blanket, 3) raise the alarm (fire alarm button/bridge), 4) if it grows or gets out of control, trigger the suppression system, stop the fan, close the dampers and evacuate the galley. Life always comes before equipment; with a fire that cannot be controlled, the rule is not to fight it but to get out and leave it to an organized team response.

Aşçı, gemi acil durum planındaki (muster.en: The cook knows his or her fire duty in the ship's emergency plan (muster list) and the escape route from the galley. STCW basic safety training (fire prevention and fire fighting) is mandatory for all seafarers; the cook takes part in the periodic fire drills.

Düzenli fire drill'ler aşçının refleksin.en: Regular fire drills keep the cook's reflexes sharp: extinguisher locations, the pull station, closing the dampers, using the fire blanket. The cook acts in the knowledge that his or her own space (the galley) is the highest-risk point; a galley scenario is rehearsed separately during drills. Training and preparedness are the only things that turn panic into action in a real fire.

Mutfak yangın emniyeti, aşçının en hayat.en: Galley fire safety is one of the cook's most vital responsibilities, because the galley is the space with the highest fire risk on board. Prevention (cleaning, supervision, switching off) is the first line of defense; knowing the right extinguisher and the fire blanket is the second; automatic suppression, damper control and an organized response are the third. Basic reflexes, such as never tackling an oil fire with water, make the difference between a minor incident and a disaster in a galley fire.

MARPOL Ek V, gemi çöpünü kategorilere ay.en: MARPOL Annex V divides ship's garbage into categories and places strict rules on the discharge of each into the sea. The categories that concern the cook most are food waste and galley-generated plastics/packaging/oil. The general principle is that "the sea is kept clean": plastics are the strictest category, prohibited from discharge into the sea in all circumstances, while food waste may be discharged into the sea only under certain conditions (such as a minimum distance from land and being comminuted).

Aşçı, mutfakta atığı kaynağında ayrıştır.en: The cook segregates waste at source in the galley: food waste, plastics/packaging, glass/metal and used cooking oil go into separate containers. This segregation is mandatory both for MARPOL compliance and for correct disposal; mixed waste (e.g. plastic contaminated with food) is handled according to the most restrictive category and increases the cost/complexity of delivery ashore.

Her gemi, gemiye özgü bir Garbage Manage.en: Every ship carries a ship-specific Garbage Management Plan, which defines how waste is to be segregated, stored, processed and delivered ashore. A person in charge of garbage management is appointed (usually an officer); the cook is the hands-on implementer of this system for galley waste and is obliged to act in line with the plan and to support the record keeping.

En iyi atık, hiç oluşmayan atıktır. Aşçı.en: The best waste is waste that is never created. The cook reduces food waste at source through portion control, correct ordering/stock management and FIFO rotation; this has a positive effect on both the MARPOL burden and the budget. By observing consumption data, the cook calibrates the quantity produced; constant leftovers are a sign of overproduction and waste.

Güvenli olan artan yemek, gıda güvenliği.en: Safe leftover food can be used at the next meal in line with food safety rules (proper cooling, correct reheating temperature); if it is not safe, it goes into the waste stream. This balance both reduces waste and prevents the risk of foodborne illness.

Gemilerde gıda atığını öğüten comminuter.en: Ships may have a comminuter/macerator that grinds food waste; discharging comminuted food waste (below a specified particle size) into the sea is conditionally permitted under Annex V when the ship is far enough from land. The permitted distance is greater for food waste that has not been comminuted. In special areas and near ports/the coast, the rules are much stricter.

Aşçı, denize atımın yalnızca uygun mesaf.en: The cook knows that discharge to sea is made only at the appropriate distance and under the appropriate conditions, with the approval of and in coordination with the responsible officer; when in port or close to the coast, food waste is not discharged into the sea but stored. Every discharge to sea or delivery ashore is entered in the Garbage Record Book (see the records section).

Kullanılmış yemeklik (kızartma) yağ kesi.en: Used cooking (frying) oil is never discharged into the sea or poured into drains/sinks; it is collected in a separate, closed, labeled container. Oil getting into the water/drainage system is both a MARPOL violation and a cause of pipe blockages and pest problems. When changing the fryer oil, the cook transfers the old oil directly into this collection container and stores the container safely and leak-tight.

Yağ atığı, geminin atık yönetim sistemin.en: Depending on the ship's waste management system, waste oil is delivered either to an approved shipboard system (e.g. an oily waste tank/incinerator, if suitable) or to a shore reception facility in port. The delivery is recorded with a receipt.

Limanda kullanılmış yağ ve diğer ayrıştı.en: In port, used oil and other segregated waste (plastics, glass, metal, food waste) are delivered to an approved port reception facility. MARPOL requires ports to provide adequate reception facilities. During delivery, the type and quantity of waste are documented; this document is matched with the ship's waste records. The cook makes the process easier by keeping the waste tidy, labeled and segregated, ready for delivery.

Denize verilemeyen veya teslim bekleyen.en: Waste that cannot be discharged into the sea or is awaiting delivery is stored on board; this storage must be hygienic. Food waste is kept in lidded, leak-proof containers and, where possible, refrigerated (long voyages, hot climates) so that odor and decay do not attract pests. The cook integrates the galley waste flow into the galley layout; the garbage station is located apart from the clean area, where it does not interfere with service (see the galley organization task).

Atık kapları düzenli boşaltılır ve temiz.en: Waste containers are emptied and cleaned regularly; accumulated waste causes odor and attracts insects/rodents. Plastics and recyclable waste can be compacted to reduce their volume (if a compactor is available), which reduces the storage burden.

Bazı gemilerde onaylı incinerator (yakma.en: Some ships have an approved incinerator or other processing equipment; however, incinerating food waste and oil is subject to the equipment's approval and to emission rules (linked to MARPOL Annex VI), and not every type of waste can be incinerated. The cook applies the methods permitted by the ship's garbage management plan; no unauthorized incineration is carried out. When in doubt, the waste is stored and the matter is coordinated with the responsible officer.

Garbage Record Book (GRB), her atık işle.en: The Garbage Record Book (GRB) is the official document in which every garbage operation (discharge to sea, incineration, delivery to a reception facility) is recorded with its category, quantity, date, time and the ship's position. The record is usually kept by the responsible officer; the cook supports it by providing accurate information on the quantities and deliveries of galley-generated food waste and oil. An incorrect or incomplete GRB entry is a serious nonconformity that can lead to heavy penalties (especially in the USA).

Aşçı, mutfak atığının türünü ve yaklaşık.en: The cook monitors the type and approximate quantity of galley waste and reports the times of delivery/discharge to the responsible officer promptly. This traceability proves the ship's compliance during MARPOL inspections and is the strongest barrier against abuses such as the "magic pipe" and falsified records.

MARPOL Ek V uyumu PSC ve liman otoritele.en: MARPOL Annex V compliance is inspected by PSC and port authorities; inconsistencies between the GRB and the actual waste flow lead to heavy penalties. By segregating galley waste correctly and reporting it correctly, the cook keeps the first link in the ship's compliance chain sound. The principle "when in doubt, do not discharge to sea: store it and deliver it ashore" is the safest rule.

Aşçı, sefer rotasını ve geçilecek özel a.en: Knowing the voyage route and the special areas to be crossed, the cook plans waste storage capacity: before entering an area with strict rules, waste is delivered ashore or sufficient storage space is set aside. This foresight both guarantees MARPOL compliance and prevents odor/pest pressure in the stores.

Atık gıda ve yağ bertarafı, aşçının deni.en: Disposal of food waste and oil is the cook's most tangible contribution to protecting the marine environment. Correct segregation, reducing waste at source, never putting oil into the sea or drains, disposing of food waste only under permitted conditions and providing accurate information for the Garbage Record Book: every link in this chain secures both MARPOL Annex V compliance and clean seas. When in doubt, always store it and deliver it in port.

Gemi çalışanı, vardiya temposu ve fiziks.en: Because of the watchkeeping routine and the energy demand of physical work, seafarers need regular, balanced and timely meals. Stable blood sugar and sufficient energy mean alertness on the bridge, quick reflexes in the engine room and strength on deck. A crew member who works hungry, on an unbalanced diet or after a heavy meal loses concentration; at sea this is a direct safety risk.

Aşırı kızartma, ağır ve şekerli öğünler.en: Excessive frying and heavy, sugary meals cause drowsiness in the short term (postprandial dip) and weight gain, fatigue and health problems in the long term. By balancing the menu so that it gives energy without being heavy, the cook supports watchkeeping performance; he or she offers light but filling options, especially for the night watch.

Yorgunluk, deniz kazalarının önde gelen.en: Fatigue is one of the leading human factors in marine accidents, and nutrition is an important part of this equation. Regular mealtimes, hot food planned to suit watch changes and a "night lunch" available 24 hours a day support the watchkeeper whose sleep-wake cycle is disrupted. Instead of the false energy of caffeine, sugar and heavy, greasy food, the cook designs meals that give sustained energy.

Hidrasyon da performansın görünmez ayağı.en: Hydration is also an invisible part of performance; water and electrolyte losses are high, especially in hot climates and in the engine room. The cook supports hydration by keeping the drinks station (water, tea, coffee and, if necessary, electrolyte drinks) accessible.

Denizde aylarca aileden ve karadan uzak.en: For crew members who live at sea for months, away from family and land, mealtime is the most anticipated social moment of the day. A good meal is a ritual that eases homesickness, brings the team together in the mess and ends the day on a positive note. The cook's small touches (the smell of fresh bread, a home-style dessert, an unexpected favorite dish) have a disproportionately large effect on morale.

Tersine, sürekli aynı, özensiz veya kali.en: Conversely, food that is always the same, carelessly prepared or of poor quality is a main source of low morale, tension and complaints. The cook reads the atmosphere in the mess as an indicator; falling morale is often a message that should be reflected in the menu.

Mürettebat ruh sağlığı (yalnızlık, izola.en: Crew mental health (loneliness, isolation, stress) is receiving more and more attention; shared mealtimes strengthen social interaction and a sense of belonging in the mess room. By offering menus that appeal to everyone's taste in a multinational team, the cook creates a dining culture in which no one is left "outside". This is a quiet but real contribution to welfare.

Özel günler, monoton sefer rutinini kıra.en: Special days are important opportunities to break the monotonous voyage routine and lift morale. The cook prepares cakes/special desserts for birthdays, and special menus specific to the culture concerned for religious festivals (e.g. Eid al-Fitr/Eid al-Adha, Christmas, Diwali) and national days. In a multinational team, observing the important days of each major group gives the feeling that no one is forgotten.

Bu menüler önceden planlanır: özel malze.en: These menus are planned in advance: special ingredients are added to the provisioning list in good time (see the stock management task), because at sea there is no way of obtaining them at the last minute. Following the calendar, the cook marks important days in the voyage plan and orders the necessary ingredients in advance.

Uzun seferlerde tekrar (menu fatigue) mo.en: On long voyages, repetition (menu fatigue) lowers morale; the cook keeps variety alive by adding theme days (national cuisine day, barbecue/grill day, a street-food-themed meal). These small variations make the cyclic menu unpredictable and enjoyable. Activities such as a barbecue on deck in good weather refresh both the menu and social life on board.

Aşçının en değerli bilgi kaynağı mürette.en: The cook's most valuable source of information is the crew itself. Observation of consumption (which dish runs out, which is left on the plate), one-to-one conversation and the satisfaction surveys/suggestion boxes used on ships feed into menu decisions. The cook reads this feedback not as personal criticism but as data for improving the service, and fine-tunes the menu cycle accordingly.

Geri bildirim aynı zamanda diyet/alerjen.en: Feedback also keeps dietary/allergen/cultural needs up to date: the preferences of newly joined crew members are recorded and changing needs (e.g. low salt for health reasons) are reflected in the menu. An open and respectful feedback culture improves both menu quality and the atmosphere in the mess.

Çeşitlilik, menü döngüsünü uzatarak (örn.en: Variety is achieved by lengthening the menu cycle (e.g. from 7 days to 10-14 days), changing cooking techniques (rotating baking, grilling, steaming and boiling) and adding recipes from different culinary cultures. The cook breaks the monotony by creating inventive variations even from the limited ingredients on hand. Variety also supports balanced nutrition (different food groups) and a continuous supply of micronutrients.

Sağlık katkısı, lezzetten ödün vermeden.en: The health contribution goes further by offering healthier options without compromising on flavor: limiting frying and doing more baking/grilling/steaming, using salt and sugar in moderation, keeping fresh vegetables/fruit at every meal and offering wholegrain options. By always having a balanced "lighter" alternative on the menu, the cook also serves crew members who watch their health.

Uzun seferde mikro besin sürekliliği (öz.en: On long voyages, a continuous supply of micronutrients (especially vitamin C) is maintained; as fresh produce runs out, frozen vegetables/fruit, citrus juices and supplements are brought in. This protects general health and prevents the fatigue/weakness that can appear toward the end of a long voyage (details in the nutrition/budget task).

Diyabet, hipertansiyon, alerji veya geçi.en: The cook provides suitable alternatives for crew members with diabetes, hypertension, allergies or temporary health conditions (stomach upsets etc.). This attentiveness protects physical health and also contributes to morale by making the person feel "seen/valued". Serious cases are coordinated with the person in charge of medical care on board/telemedicine.

Aşçının sağlık ve moral katkısı, gemidek.en: The cook's contribution to health and morale is the least visible but most strongly felt value on board. A well-fed team is more alert, safer and happier; a carefully prepared special-day menu or a surprise favorite dish can ease the tension of a long voyage. By using the plate as a tool for performance and a bridge to morale, the cook becomes the quiet but decisive foundation of both the crew's health and their solidarity.

Gemide içme suyu ya limanda kıyıdan (sho.en: On board, drinking water is either taken from shore in port (shore bunkering) or produced on board from seawater with an evaporator/RO (reverse osmosis) plant. Water from either source is not taken into the potable water tanks until it has been brought to drinkable quality; shore water is supplied to the tank through a reliable hose/connection, and produced water after mineralization and disinfection. The cook is the person who monitors that water quality is right at the end-user side (galley, mess).

Potable water tankları yalnızca içme suy.en: Potable water tanks are reserved for drinking water only; they are not used for any other purpose (ballast, technical use) and no cross-connections are made. The tanks are cleaned and disinfected periodically and backflow protection is provided. This system is generally operated by the technical team; the cook plays a part on the quality and records side.

Aşçı, gıda hazırlığında ve içme suyunda.en: The cook continuously monitors that the water used in food preparation and for drinking is safe; residual chlorine testing, visual/odor/taste checks and supporting sampling are part of this responsibility. In the event of an abnormality (color, odor, low chlorine), the cook immediately alerts the Master and the technical team; if necessary, drinking water is made safe by boiling or by using an alternative (bottled water). Water quality is an essential precondition of food safety.

Dezenfekte edilen içme suyunda serbest k.en: In disinfected drinking water, the free residual chlorine is the practical indicator that the water remains safe throughout distribution. The WHO Guide to Ship Sanitation generally recommends a free residual chlorine of at least ~0.2 mg/L in the distribution system; this level is a buffer against possible contamination between the tank and the tap. The cook/responsible personnel regularly measure chlorine at taps with a DPD test kit and record the results.

Klor çok düşükse dezenfeksiyon güvencesi.en: If chlorine is too low, the assurance of disinfection is lost (super-chlorination/dosage adjustment is required); if it is too high, there are taste/odor problems. Measuring points should also cover the farthest/least favorable points from the tank; looking only at the source is misleading. In the event of a deviation, the dosage is corrected in coordination with the technical team.

pH, klorun dezenfeksiyon etkinliğini etk.en: pH affects the disinfecting effectiveness of chlorine; at very high pH, the killing power of chlorine falls, so pH is generally kept and monitored within a suitable range (roughly 6.5-8.5). Periodic samples are taken for bacteriological safety; the presence of E. coli and coliform bacteria is a sign of fecal contamination and requires zero tolerance. These samples are assessed with field kits or by accredited laboratory analysis.

Pozitif bakteriyolojik sonuç ciddi bir b.en: A positive bacteriological result is a serious finding: the water source is isolated, super-chlorination/tank disinfection is carried out, the water is retested and alternative safe water is used until it is clear. All these steps are recorded and reported to the Master.
