Plan, mevcut çevre kuvvetlerine (rüzgar,.en: The plan assesses whether the number of lines is sufficient for the prevailing environmental forces (wind, current, swell, passing ship effect). MEG4 requires the MBL (Minimum Breaking Load) of each line and the distribution of forces relative to the SDMBL (Ship Design MBL) to be documented. The plan must be consistent with the mooring line management plan (MLMP).

Manevra öncesi Birinci Zabit, baş üstü e.en: Before maneuvering, the Chief Officer gives a toolbox briefing to the forward mooring team (bosun + deck ratings): who will operate the winch, who will throw the heaving line, who will hold the stopper and who will handle communications. Everyone must know their task and their own snap-back zone. The radio channel between the bridge and the forward/aft stations must be clear and confirmed.

Personelin PPE'si (kask, eldiven, çelik.en: Personnel PPE (helmet, gloves, steel-toe boots, lifejacket if required) is checked. Fatigue management is critical; STCW rest hours must not be violated during long maneuvers. The Chief Officer makes sure that the team is physically ready.

Halatlar düzenli olarak elden geçirilir:.en: Lines are inspected regularly for abrasion, cuts, glazing (heat damage), internal fiber breakage and UV degradation. The MEG4 retirement criteria (replacement when residual strength falls below 75%) are applied. A worn line increases the risk of snap-back.

Mooring winch'ler brake holding capacity.en: Mooring winches are set according to their brake holding capacity; MEG4 recommends keeping the brake rendering point at 60% of the SDMBL (for steel) or 80% (for synthetic). A brake test (brake holding capacity test) must be carried out regularly and recorded. A brake set too tight leads to the line parting; a slack brake lets the ship move off the berth.

Stopper (chain stopper, carpenter stoppe.en: The stopper (chain stopper, carpenter stopper or rope stopper) holds the load while the line is transferred from the winch to the bollard. Incorrect stopper technique (e.g. a chain stopper on a synthetic line) creates a life-threatening hazard. The Chief Officer checks that the correct stopper is used on the correct line. On "self-tailing" winches, the minimum number of turns of the line on the drum must be maintained.

Bir mooring line gerildiğinde içinde dep.en: When a mooring line is under tension, elastic energy is stored in it; if the line parts, this energy is released as a whiplash (snap-back) movement in both directions from the point of parting. In highly elastic lines such as nylon, this movement reaches lethal speed. Snap-back is the source of the most frequent fatal accidents in seafaring; a line that strikes a person kills instantly.

MEG4, eski \"boyalı snap-back zone\" yak.en: MEG4 has revised the old "painted snap-back zone" approach: zones are no longer treated as individual painted lines but as "the whole mooring deck being a potential danger zone", because the direction of snap-back can change with the lead angle of the line and with fairlead failure. The Chief Officer forbids personnel to stand inside a bight, in line with a fairlead, or between the line and the bollard while a line is under tension.

Birinci Zabit, ekibi line ile mümkün old.en: The Chief Officer positions the team as close as possible to right angles to the line and where the escape route is clear. Personnel throwing the heaving line move to a safe area before the line comes under load. Standard commands such as "slack away", "heave up", "hold on" and "make fast" are passed between the bridge and the station with clear radio confirmation; ambiguity is an invitation to an accident.

Römorkör yardımlı manevralarda Birinci Z.en: In tug-assisted maneuvers, the Chief Officer supervises the safe securing of the tug line (usually with the tug's own gear or the ship's messenger) to the ship's bitt/fairlead. A Panama lead, a closed chock or a bollard marked with its SWL is used. The SWL of the fairlead through which the tug line passes must not be exceeded.

Tug working area da bir snap-back ve sık.en: The tug working area also carries a risk of snap-back and of being caught or crushed; personnel stay clear of the tug line while it is under tension. The bridge coordinates with the tug master through the pilot; the Chief Officer manages the timing of making fast and letting go on deck.

SOLAS II-1 Reg. 3-8 ve MSC.1/Circ.1175,.en: SOLAS II-1 Reg. 3-8 and MSC.1/Circ.1175 require the SWL of towing and mooring fittings to be marked on board and documented. The Chief Officer must know the marked SWL of every bitt and chock in use and must not exceed it. Choosing the wrong chock (e.g. excessive load at a narrow angle) can tear the fitting out of the deck.

STS transferde Birinci Zabit, OCIMF/ISGO.en: In STS transfers, the Chief Officer supervises the arrangement of the primary (Yokohama) fenders and secondary fenders in accordance with the OCIMF/ISGOTT STS guide. The number of fenders is determined by the size of the ships and the maximum berthing speed; their positions are distributed evenly along the parallel body. The approach speed is a critical parameter and is generally kept at about 0.1–0.3 m/s.

İki gemi yan yana geldiğinde mooring lin.en: When the two ships are alongside each other, the mooring line arrangement is specific to STS; head, stern, breast and spring lines are rigged evenly between the two ships. While the POAC (Person in Overall Advisory Control) carries out the overall coordination, the Chief Officer manages the work on deck on board their own ship.

Cargo/bunker hose bağlantısı, doğru flan.en: The cargo/bunker hose connection is made with the correct flange, gasket and number of bolts; hoses are lifted with a crane/derrick of known SWL. The Chief Officer ensures that the hoses are continuously monitored for tension and chafing and that drip trays and SOPEP gear are ready. During the transfer, the ESD must be tested and functional.

Birinci Zabit, manevra emniyeti için çev.en: The Chief Officer assesses the environmental limits for safe maneuvering together with the Master/pilot. Ships with high freeboard (container ships, PCCs, tankers in ballast) are very sensitive to wind load; with beam winds above 25–30 knots, tug assistance and additional lines are needed. The current, particularly in river ports, determines the berthing angle and the approach plan.

Swell varlığında mooring line'lar dinami.en: When there is swell, mooring lines carry dynamic (ranging) loads; surging and fender working increase. In these conditions, lines are checked frequently, tension is adjusted when necessary and the operation may be suspended.

Dar kanal limanlarında geçen geminin yar.en: In ports with narrow channels, the suction/surge caused by a passing ship can subject a berthed ship to sudden tension and line parting. In such ports, the Chief Officer monitors the additional lines and the tension monitoring system (if fitted). On ships without automatic tension monitoring, periodic manual checks are made.

Her manevra sonrası mooring düzeni, kull.en: After each maneuver, the mooring arrangement, the number of lines used, tug details and any near-miss/incident are entered in the deck log. Mooring equipment inspections (lines, winch brakes, fairleads) are recorded under the MSMP. These records are examined in PSC and vetting inspections.

Bir LNG terminalinde, brake holding capa.en: At an LNG terminal, a winch whose brake holding capacity test had been neglected could not hold its line in a swell, and the ship moved off the berth; a loading arm was damaged and the ESD was activated. Lesson: brake tests and MEG4 equipment maintenance must never be skipped; automation does not remove the need for human supervision.

Bağlama ve manevra, sakin görünen ama bi.en: Mooring and maneuvering are operations that look calm but can turn lethal in an instant. The Chief Officer succeeds through a clear plan, a disciplined briefing, the right equipment and by instilling in the team a culture of "stay clear of a line under tension".

MARPOL 73/78, deniz kirliliğini altı ek.en: MARPOL 73/78 regulates marine pollution under six annexes: Annex I (oil), Annex II (noxious liquid substances), Annex III (harmful substances in packaged form), Annex IV (sewage), Annex V (garbage) and Annex VI (air pollution). The Chief Officer deals directly with Annex I in particular (deck oil operations, bunkering), Annex V (garbage) and Annex IV; bilge/sludge transfers are carried out in coordination with the engine department.

ISM Code ve şirketin SMS (Safety Managem.en: The environmental procedures within the ISM Code and the company's SMS (Safety Management System) add company standards on top of MARPOL. Companies with a "no discharge" policy prohibit the discharge of certain wastes into the sea even where it is legally permitted. The Chief Officer passes these policies on to the crew and enforces them.

Çevre uyumsuzluğu near-miss/non-conformi.en: Environmental non-compliance is reported as a near-miss/non-conformity; deliberate violations such as a magic pipe (illegal bypass line) are a crime and expose the company to heavy penalties. A culture of transparent and honest record keeping is the Chief Officer's responsibility.

Plastik HER ZAMAN denize atılması yasakt.en: Discharge of plastics into the sea is ALWAYS prohibited; they are retained on board and delivered to a shore reception facility. Food waste may be discharged at specified distances, depending on the distance from land and on whether it has been comminuted (outside Special Areas, generally >12 nm; comminuted >3 nm). The Chief Officer makes the discharge decision in accordance with the regulations.

Garbage Record Book (GRB) Part I (gemi a.en: Garbage Record Book (GRB) Part I (ship-generated garbage) and Part II (cargo residues) record every discharge/incineration/delivery operation with the date, position, quantity (m³) and category. The Chief Officer is responsible for keeping the records accurate and complete. The receipt obtained on delivery to a shore reception facility (garbage disposal receipt) is kept and cross-checked against the GRB.

Güverte tarafında yağ kirliliği genelde.en: On the deck side, oil pollution generally comes from bunkering, leaks from hydraulic equipment (cranes, winches, hatch covers) and cargo operations. The Chief Officer verifies that scupper plugs are fitted before bunkering, that drip trays are in place and that the SOPEP gear is ready. Small amounts of oil spilled on deck are cleaned up immediately with absorbent and prevented from going overboard.

15 ppm bilge separator ve Oil Discharge.en: All discharges made through the 15 ppm bilge separator and the Oil Discharge Monitoring Equipment (ODME — tankers) are recorded in the ORB. As a deck officer, the Chief Officer checks the accuracy of the discharge records (particularly slops and cargo tank washings on tankers) and works in coordination with the engine department.

Bunkering, güvertede en yüksek yağ kirli.en: Bunkering is the operation with the highest risk of oil pollution on deck. The Chief Officer (or the designated officer) applies the pre-bunkering checklist: scupper plugs, drip trays, manifold gasket check, ESD/communication confirmation, and monitoring of the maximum loading rate and tank capacity. Overflow is prevented by continuous ullaging/sounding; when a tank is 90% full, the rate is reduced for topping off.

Bunker spill durumunda SOPEP derhal devr.en: In the event of a bunker spill, the SOPEP is activated immediately: the discharge is stopped, the source is shut off, absorbent/booms are deployed, and the port authority and the company DPA are informed at once. Fast and honest reporting is the most important factor in reducing penalties.

400 GT üzeri her gemi (tankerlerde 150 G.en: Every ship above 400 GT (150 GT for tankers) must carry a SOPEP. The plan contains information on who calls whom (reporting), how to respond (mitigation) and which equipment to use. The Chief Officer regularly checks that the SOPEP locker (absorbent, booms, sorbent pads, scoops, gloves, dispersant if permitted) is complete and accessible.

SOPEP tatbikatları düzenli yapılır; her.en: SOPEP drills are carried out regularly; every crew member's role in a spill (reporting, shutting off the source, applying absorbent, rigging booms) is defined. The Chief Officer organizes the drill, identifies weaknesses and keeps records. In a real spill, speed and coordination determine the environmental and legal outcome.

Spill sonrası temizlik atığı (oily waste.en: Cleanup waste from a spill (oily waste, contaminated absorbent) is stored separately as hazardous waste and delivered to a suitable reception facility; it is never thrown into the sea. The event is reported to the company in a near-miss/accident report and a root cause analysis is carried out.

MARPOL Annex IV, pis su deşarjını düzenl.en: MARPOL Annex IV regulates the discharge of sewage: effluent treated in an approved sewage treatment plant may be discharged under certain conditions; untreated sewage may be discharged at a moderate rate at least 12 nm from land while the ship is en route at more than 4 knots. From the deck side, the Chief Officer monitors that the treatment plant is in working order and that the discharge conditions are complied with.

Special Area'larda ve liman bölgelerinde.en: In Special Areas and port areas, sewage discharge is subject to strict restrictions; most ports require the use of a holding tank and delivery ashore. Greywater is also regulated separately in some regions (e.g. Alaska, polar waters).

Deşarjın yasak olduğu bölgelerde sewage.en: In areas where discharge is prohibited, sewage is collected in the holding tank and delivered to a reception facility at a suitable port. The Chief Officer monitors the holding tank capacity and plans according to the length of the port stay; an overflowing tank is both a hygiene and a pollution problem.

Annex VI ağırlıklı makine kapsamında ols.en: Although Annex VI mainly concerns the engine department, cargo VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) emissions on tankers are a deck matter. On tankers with a VOC Management Plan, the Chief Officer applies the vapor return and loading procedures in accordance with that plan. Ozone-depleting substances (ODS) and equipment containing them are also recorded.

Incinerator kullanımı Annex VI ve Annex.en: Use of the incinerator falls under both Annex VI and Annex V; incineration of certain wastes (e.g. PVC, cargo residues) is prohibited, and operation of the incinerator may be restricted in ports and Special Areas. The Chief Officer coordinates the incineration records with the GRB.

Bulk gemilerde hold yıkama suları (cargo.en: On bulk carriers, hold washing water (containing cargo residues) is subject to HME (Harmful to the Marine Environment) classification according to the type of cargo. If the cargo is HME, the washing water must not be discharged into the sea and is delivered to a reception facility. The Chief Officer determines, from the IMSBC/shipper information, whether the cargo is HME and records this in GRB Part II.

Güverte üstü paint, kumlama (grit), kayn.en: Paint, grit (from blasting), welding slag and other operational waste on deck are prevented from getting into the sea; during deck work, scuppers are checked and waste is collected.

Paint locker ve kimyasal depolama MSDS'l.en: The paint locker and chemical storage are managed in accordance with the MSDS; leaks, spreading to the sea or deck, and fire risk are controlled. Empty chemical/paint drums are stored as operational waste and are not thrown into the sea. Antifouling paints must be compliant (AFS Convention — TBT ban).

Birinci Zabit, GRB, ORB (güverte ilgili.en: The Chief Officer keeps the GRB, the ORB (deck-related parts), sewage records, delivery receipts, the SOPEP inventory and drill records ready for inspection. PSC and vetting inspectors check the consistency of these records, whether they match the actual condition, and how the plans are implemented. Regular internal checks (self-assessment) prevent findings.

Çevre koruma, modern denizciliğin en sık.en: Environmental protection is the most strictly inspected and most heavily penalized area of modern shipping. The Chief Officer succeeds by instilling in the deck team a culture of honest record keeping, response equipment that is always ready, and the discipline of "not a single drop goes into the sea".

Gemi yaşamı boyunca çok katmanlı denetim.en: Throughout its life, a ship is subject to several layers of inspection: flag State and class certification surveys, PSC (port State control), vetting (SIRE 2.0 for tankers, RightShip for bulk carriers), ISM internal and external audits, and charterer inspections. The Chief Officer prepares for all of these as regards deck equipment, safety systems and documentation.

Her denetimin odak alanı farklıdır: PSC.en: Each inspection has a different focus: PSC focuses on deficiencies and detention; vetting measures the risk profile; class checks structural integrity and the validity of certificates. Knowing what each inspection looks for, the Chief Officer prepares the documents and the physical condition of the ship.

En etkili hazırlık, denetimden günler ön.en: The most effective preparation is not panic cleaning in the days before an inspection but a continuous "audit-ready" working culture. The Chief Officer makes real-time record keeping, well-maintained equipment and crew knowledge of procedures part of the daily routine. What an inspector looks at most is "the consistency between the records and the actual condition".

Şirket genelde bir self-assessment check.en: The company usually provides a self-assessment checklist (PSC pre-arrival, vetting pre-vet); the Chief Officer applies it before arrival in port and closes out the gaps. This proactive approach eliminates surprises during the inspection.

PSC denetimleri Paris MoU, Tokyo MoU gib.en: PSC inspections are carried out under regional agreements such as the Paris MoU and the Tokyo MoU, and ships are targeted according to their risk profile (Ship Risk Profile); high-risk ships are inspected more often and in more detail. The initial PSC inspection is a general check; if "clear grounds" (concrete grounds for suspicion) are found, it becomes a more detailed inspection. The Chief Officer aims for a clean inspection history to keep the ship's risk profile low.

Sertifikaların geçerliliği, güverte emni.en: The validity of certificates, deck safety equipment, life-saving/fire-fighting systems, MARPOL records and the crew's knowledge of their duties are the focus of PSC. Defects found are recorded as "deficiencies"; serious ones lead to detention.

Güverte tarafında en sık PSC bulguları:.en: The most frequent PSC findings on the deck side are: missing/expired LSA/FFE equipment, an incorrect muster list, emergency lighting not working, a damaged liferaft release unit (hydrostatic release), inconsistencies in records, poor hold/deck maintenance and incomplete permit-to-work files. The Chief Officer closes out these items with a self-check before arrival in port.

Mürettebat \"knowledge\" testi de yapılı.en: A crew "knowledge" test is also carried out: the inspector asks a randomly chosen rating about the fire station, releasing a liferaft or enclosed space rescue. This is why the quality of familiarization and drills directly affects the outcome of the inspection.

OCIMF SIRE 2.0, klasik checklist yerine.en: OCIMF SIRE 2.0 is a digital vetting system that, instead of the traditional checklist, works with risk-based, ship-specific questions (Core, Rotational and Campaign questions). The inspector uses a tablet and assesses the hardware, human and process dimensions together. The Chief Officer is expected to show knowledge of each procedure "by doing it, not from paper".

Vetting başarısı charterer'ın gemiyi kab.en: Successful vetting is critical for the charterer's acceptance of the ship; a failed vetting can leave the ship without charters. This is why vetting preparation is among the highest-priority tasks on tankers.

Bulker ve genel kargo tarafında RightShi.en: On the bulk carrier and general cargo side, RightShip inspections are common; the ship's age, past PSC record, casualty history and physical condition produce a risk score. The Chief Officer keeps deck/hold maintenance, the condition of lashing equipment and the documentation ready against these criteria.

Her iki sistemde de gözlem (observation).en: In both systems, if an observation is raised, it is closed out through root cause analysis and corrective action. The Chief Officer coordinates the closing of deck-related observations.

Klas; annual, intermediate, special (5 y.en: Class verifies the ship's structural integrity and equipment through annual, intermediate, special (5-yearly) and drydock surveys. On the deck side, hatch cover ultrasonic tests, structural examination of holds, mooring equipment, crane/derrick load tests and anchor/chain measurements come up. Before the survey, the Chief Officer prepares the relevant areas so that they are accessible and clean.

Condition of Class (CoC) açılırsa, belir.en: If a Condition of Class (CoC) is imposed, it must be dealt with within the specified period; otherwise the certificate is suspended. The Chief Officer follows up deck-related CoCs.

Geminin tüm güverte ilgili sertifikaları.en: All of the ship's deck-related certificates (Safety Equipment, Load Line, class certificate, hatch cover test reports, LSA/FFE service certificates) must be valid and ready for inspection. The Chief Officer monitors the certificate validity schedule and renews those approaching expiry in good time. A single expired certificate creates a serious finding.

ISM iç denetimleri, şirketin SMS'inin ge.en: ISM internal audits verify that the company's SMS is implemented on board. The Chief Officer demonstrates that deck procedures (cargo, mooring, PTW, drills, environment) are carried out in accordance with the SMS. Findings are recorded as a non-conformity (NC) or an observation.

Açılan NC'ler için kök neden analizi yap.en: For each NC raised, a root cause analysis is carried out, corrective action is defined and the evidence of closure (records, photographs) is documented. The Chief Officer ensures that deck-related NCs are closed on time and reported to the DPA.

Tekrarlayan bulgular sistemik sorun işar.en: Recurring findings are a sign of a systemic problem. By analyzing past PSC/vetting/internal audit findings, the Chief Officer prevents recurrence; for example, a repeated "lashing equipment worn" finding calls for a review of the equipment replacement policy. Preventive action is more valuable than reactive correction.

Birinci Zabit, güverte departmanının tüm.en: The Chief Officer keeps all records of the deck department in a systematic archive: drill records (abandon ship, fire, enclosed space, oil spill), PMS work orders, risk assessments, PTW files, mooring/cargo records and environmental record books. When an inspector asks for any record, it must be possible to produce it within minutes.

Elektronik kayıt sistemleri (e-logbook,.en: Electronic record systems (e-logbook, PMS software) are now common; however, backups and inspector access must be prepared in advance. Records must be legible, dated, signed and consistent.

SOLAS gereği drill'ler (abandon ship ve.en: As required by SOLAS, drills (abandon ship and fire monthly — weekly on passenger ships; enclosed space entry/rescue at least every two months, etc.) are carried out on time and recorded in detail; the scenario, participants, duration, deficiencies found and corrections are written down. Writing "done" is not enough; the inspector questions quality and realism. Familiarization records for newly joined personnel must also be ready.

Denetim günü Birinci Zabit, denetçiye gü.en: On the day of the inspection, the Chief Officer accompanies the inspector in the deck areas and shows a professional, open and non-defensive attitude. Questions are answered honestly; on an unfamiliar subject, saying "I will check and come back to you" is better than giving wrong information. An approach of cooperation, not argument, reduces the number of findings.

Bulgu açılırsa, denetçinin gerekçesi anl.en: If a finding is raised, the inspector's reasoning is understood and, where possible, the finding is corrected on the spot (on-the-spot correction). For findings that cannot be corrected immediately, an action plan with a timeline is presented.

Denetim raporundaki tüm bulgular kayıt a.en: All findings in the inspection report are recorded, corrective action is planned and evidence of closure is submitted to the company/inspector. The Chief Officer follows up carefully so that unclosed findings are not raised again at the next inspection.

Denetim hazırlığı, son dakika telaşıyla.en: Inspection readiness is achieved not through a last-minute rush but through discipline maintained every day. The Chief Officer's success comes from keeping the ship "audit-ready" at all times with honest real-time records, well-maintained equipment and a team that knows its duties. A clean inspection history directly protects the ship's commercial value and the company's reputation.

Geleneksel ticari gemilerde ana üretim 4.en: On conventional merchant ships, main generation is a 440 V or 690 V, 60 Hz three-phase system; 380 V / 50 Hz is found on some ships of European origin. Distribution is staged: 440 V goes from the main switchboard to large consumers (pumps, fans, cranes) and is stepped down through transformers to 230 V / 220 V for lighting and socket circuits. On modern large ships, 6.6 kV or 11 kV HV generation and electric propulsion (diesel-electric) are common.

ETO, single-line diagram (tek hat şeması.en: The ETO must be able to model the whole network mentally from the single-line diagram: which busbar is fed from which generator, whether the bus-tie breaker is open or closed, and which consumer is in which preferential trip stage. Correct isolation and restoration in the event of a fault are possible only with a thorough command of this diagram.

STCW Manila değişiklikleri ile resmileşe.en: The ETO certificate (A-III/6), formalized by the STCW Manila amendments, brings together electrical, electronic and control engineering competences. The ETO is responsible for the operation, monitoring and maintenance of power generation systems, for automation and control systems, for the technical maintenance of navigation/communication electronics and for the ship's security/IT systems.

Görev hiyerarşisinde ETO, Baş Mühendis'e.en: In the chain of command, the ETO reports to the Chief Engineer but is the ship's most competent technical person in electrical/electronic matters. The ETO works in coordination with the watchkeeping engineers and acts together with the engine room team, particularly during blackouts, generator paralleling and switchboard switching operations.

Brushless alternatörlerde rotating diode.en: In brushless alternators, the rotating diode bridge is a critical component; an open-circuit or short-circuited diode causes voltage fluctuation and loss of excitation. The ETO periodically tests the diodes with an RDFM (Rotating Diode Failure Monitor) or by offline measurement. The AVR sensing cables and the presence of the residual magnetism needed for voltage build-up are also checked; if necessary, the alternator is re-excited by "field flashing".

Her generator breaker'ı bir dizi koruma.en: Each generator breaker is equipped with a set of protection relays: reverse power (32), overcurrent (50/51), under/overvoltage (27/59), under/overfrequency (81), differential (87) and, on large machines, negative sequence (46). The ETO sets the setpoints of these relays according to the class-approved protection coordination study and verifies them periodically with a secondary injection test set.

Reverse power rölesi özellikle paralel ç.en: The reverse power relay is particularly critical in parallel operation: if a generator loses fuel, it goes into motoring mode and draws power from the other machine; the relay detects this and opens the breaker (typical setpoint 2–6% of rated power, 3–5 s delay). The ETO records the pickup and timing value of each relay in the annual test schedule; these records are requested at PSC inspections and class surveys.

Alternatör sargılarının izolasyon direnc.en: The insulation resistance of alternator windings falls with moisture and aging. The ETO measures stator-to-earth and rotor-to-earth IR with a 500 V (LV) or 1000–5000 V (HV) megger. The Polarization Index (PI = ratio of the 10 min value to the 1 min value) and the corrected minimum IR value (IEEE 43) are evaluated. Low values call for drying out with the space heater or cleaning of the windings.

İki generator'ı paralele almak için gele.en: To parallel two generators, the voltage, frequency and phase sequence of the incoming machine must match those of the live busbar. The ETO or the watchkeeping engineer watches the synchroscope (or the auto-synchronizer), keeps the frequency slightly higher than the busbar (slow clockwise rotation) and closes the breaker as the synchroscope approaches the 11–12 o'clock position (as the phase difference approaches zero). Closing at the wrong phase angle produces a large transient current and a mechanical shock, damaging the shaft and gears.

Auto-synchronizing sistemi check-synch r.en: The auto-synchronizing system is equipped with a check-synch relay (25); even when the breaker is closed manually, this relay prevents it from closing at the wrong phase angle. The ETO regularly checks the sync panel lamps, the voltmeter/frequency meter pairs and the sync selector switch.

Paralel generator'lar arasında aktif güç.en: Between generators in parallel, active power (kW) is shared through the governor (fuel) and reactive power (kVAr) through the AVR (excitation). The speed droop method is common: each machine lowers its frequency slightly as load increases, which shares the load proportionally. In modern PMSs, isochronous load sharing equalizes the load while keeping the frequency constant.

ETO, kW ve kVAr metrelerini izleyerek de.en: The ETO detects uneven sharing by watching the kW and kVAr meters. An active power imbalance is corrected through the governor characteristic or the load sharing line connection, and a reactive imbalance through the AVR droop setting. A reactive imbalance causes excessive stator current and overheating in one machine.

PMS, şebeke yükünü sürekli izler; yük be.en: The PMS continuously monitors the network load; when the load exceeds a set threshold, it auto-starts the standby generator, parallels it and shares the load, and when the load drops, it auto-stops a machine. From the PMS HMI, the ETO checks the auto start/stop setpoints (e.g. start at 75%, stop at 30%), the start delays and the heavy consumer interlocks (confirmation that sufficient power is available before the bow thruster or mooring winches start).

Emergency switchboard, normal şartlarda.en: Under normal conditions, the emergency switchboard is fed from the main busbar through a bus-tie. On loss of main power (blackout) this connection opens, the emergency generator starts automatically and supplies the emergency busbar within 45 seconds, as required by SOLAS. The ETO carries out the weekly auto-start test of the emergency generator and verifies that the mandatory consumers connected to the emergency switchboard (navigation lights, emergency lighting, GMDSS, fire pump, steering gear) are correctly supplied.

Generator aşırı yüklendiğinde tüm baranı.en: To prevent the collapse of the whole busbar (blackout) when a generator is overloaded, preferential tripping comes into action: the least critical consumers (air conditioning, heating, refrigeration compressors) are shed first, in stages, so that essential loads remain supplied. The ETO sets the current setpoints and the stage sequence of the preferential trip relay according to the class-approved load study.

Tipik olarak 3 kademe tanımlanır: 1. kad.en: Typically 3 stages are defined: stage 1 (e.g. 110% load, 5 s) comfort loads, stage 2 (e.g. 115%, 3 s) secondary pumps, stage 3 (120%, instantaneous) last resort. The ETO tests these stages annually and verifies that the correct consumers are shed.

Limanda emisyonu azaltmak için gemi, kar.en: To reduce emissions in port, the ship can be supplied from the shore grid (shore power / cold ironing). The ETO prepares the shore connection panel, checks that the incoming voltage/frequency is compatible with the ship's network (whether the shore supply is 60 Hz or 50 Hz, and the voltage level) and checks the phase sequence with a phase sequence indicator. A wrong phase sequence makes motors run in reverse.

Bağlantı; ya gemi generator'ları durduru.en: The connection is made either by stopping the ship's generators and making a dead-bus transfer or, in modern systems, without interruption by shore-to-ship synchronizing. The ETO verifies the protection settings of the shore breaker, the earthing connection and the shore/ship interlock.

Shore power bağlantısında protective ear.en: In a shore power connection, the protective earth (PE) connection is made first and removed last. Before inserting the shore plug, the ETO confirms with a voltage detector that it is dead, and checks that the mechanical/electrical interlock prevents the ship's generator breaker and the shore breaker from being closed at the same time.

VFD'ler, doğrultucular ve UPS'ler gibi n.en: Non-linear loads such as VFDs, rectifiers and UPSs generate harmonic currents; these lead to voltage distortion (THD), heating of transformers and cables, overloading of the neutral and nuisance tripping of relays. The ETO measures THD with a power quality analyzer (voltage THD limit typically 5–8%) and, if necessary, recommends a harmonic filter or line reactor.

Diesel-electric ve azipod tahrikli gemil.en: On ships with diesel-electric and azipod propulsion, the harmonic load is very high; active front-end drives and 12/18-pulse rectifiers are used to reduce harmonics. The ETO periodically checks the filter capacitors and fuses of these systems.

Switchboard içindeki gevşek bara bağlant.en: Loose busbar connections and terminals inside the switchboard can lead to increased resistance, heating and eventually arc flash. The ETO scans the switchboard under load for hotspots with a thermal camera; a difference of 10–20°C above normal is a sign of looseness or overload. Busbar bolts are tightened with a calibrated torque wrench.

Gemi şebekeleri genelde izole (IT) siste.en: Ship networks are generally insulated (IT) systems; the first earth fault does not stop operation, but a second fault turns into a short circuit. The ETO takes insulation monitoring device (IMD) alarms seriously and isolates the faulty circuit by branch-by-branch testing. Regular megger measurements catch gradual insulation deterioration early.

MARPOL Annex VI EEXI ve CII çerçevesinde.en: Within the framework of MARPOL Annex VI EEXI and CII, optimizing the electrical load on board helps reduce fuel consumption and emissions. The ETO controls unnecessary pump/fan running with VFDs, converts lighting to LED and optimizes the PMS settings so that generators run in their most efficient load range (70–85%).

Diesel generator'lar düşük yükte (örn. <.en: Diesel generators run inefficiently at low load (e.g. <40%) and suffer from incomplete combustion and fouling (soot). The ETO sets the PMS so that a single machine runs at high load; keeping two machines in parallel at low load is undesirable both because it wastes fuel and for the health of the engines.

Total blackout, gemi için en kritik elek.en: A total blackout is the most critical electrical event for a ship: it means loss of propulsion, steering and navigation. The ETO and the engine team quickly apply the blackout recovery procedure: confirming that the emergency generator is on line, restarting the main generator, bringing essential consumers back on line in stages and identifying the cause (fuel, protection trip, AVR failure). Regular blackout drills keep this reflex sharp.

Paralel çalışmada bir makinenin governor.en: In parallel operation, if one machine's governor responds slowly, a reverse power trip can occur. An incorrect AVR droop setting, on the other hand, leads to reactive power oscillation (hunting) and voltage fluctuation. The ETO eliminates these oscillations by fine-tuning the governor and AVR settings through on-site testing.

ETO'nun güç sistemi yönetimindeki başarı.en: The ETO's success in managing the power system is measured by the ability to make the right decision within seconds during a blackout, by protection systems that work quietly but reliably, and by catching faults before they grow through disciplined daily monitoring. The power system is the heart of the ship; the ETO is responsible for keeping this heart beating flawlessly.

Integrated Automation System (IAS), tüm.en: The Integrated Automation System (IAS) brings all machinery and auxiliary systems together on a single monitoring/control platform. The Alarm and Monitoring System (AMS) collects data from sensors, compares it with the alarm setpoints and gives the operator visual/audible alarms. The ETO must know the network topology, redundancy architecture and I/O distribution of these systems.

Kontrol katmanı genelde dağıtık PLC'ler.en: The control layer is usually implemented with distributed PLCs; each PLC manages a subsystem (jacket water, fuel oil, bilge, ballast) and reports to the central server. Field communication is via Modbus, Profibus/Profinet, CAN or a proprietary fieldbus.

UMS notasyonu için otomasyon sisteminin.en: For the UMS notation, the automation system must not put the engine room at risk through a single failure. The ETO periodically tests the redundant power supply (dual supply), the redundant network (ring topology, automatic path switching) and hot-standby PLC/server configurations. It is critical to verify that the standby system actually takes over; a "silent standby failure" is the most dangerous situation.

PLC bakımı; CPU/I/O modül LED durum kont.en: PLC maintenance covers checking CPU/I/O module status LEDs, tracking the battery life of battery-backed RAM, cleaning cooling fans and filters, checking the tightness of terminal connections, and controlling dust and humidity. The ETO monitors the temperature and humidity of PLC cabinets; excessive temperature shortens module life and leads to faulty I/O readings.

RAM yedek bataryası biterse program ve a.en: If the RAM backup battery runs down, the program and settings may be lost. The ETO takes the low battery alarm seriously, replaces the battery without cutting the power (depending on the module) and is ready to restore the program from backup. An up-to-date offline backup of all PLC programs is kept.

PLC firmware veya logic değişiklikleri k.en: PLC firmware or logic changes must be made in a controlled way. Before any change, the ETO backs up the existing program, implements the change with vendor approval under the management of change (MOC) procedure, and then carries out a function test. Unplanned "quick fixes" can lead to hidden faults and certification violations.

Otomasyon sisteminin doğruluğu sensörler.en: The accuracy of the automation system depends on the accuracy of its sensors. The ETO calibrates PT100/PT1000 temperature sensors against a reference thermometer, pressure transmitters with a dead-weight tester or a calibrated reference gauge, and level sensors (capacitive, ultrasonic, float) against known reference levels. On transmitters with a 4–20 mA output, the zero and span are adjusted.

Kalibrasyon kaydı her sensör için tutulu.en: A calibration record is kept for each sensor: the as-found and as-left values, the certificate number of the reference instrument used, and the date. These records are critically important at class surveys and in recurring fault analysis.

Akış ölçerler (manyetik, vortex, corioli.en: Flow meters (magnetic, vortex, Coriolis), speed sensors (pickup, encoder), oxygen/gas analyzers and viscosity sensors require special calibration procedures. The ETO follows the vendor procedure and watches for signs of drift that call for calibration. A wrongly calibrated sensor produces both false alarms and dangerous "missed alarms".

Her ölçülen büyüklük için alarm setpoint.en: For each measured variable, alarm setpoints are set according to vendor/class recommendations: high/high-high and low/low-low layers, pre-warning (alert) and trip (shutdown) levels. The ETO makes sure that these setpoints are correct, consistent with the engine manufacturer's limits and set so that they do not create nuisance alarms.

Shutdown ve slow-down fonksiyonları (örn.en: Shutdown and slowdown functions (e.g. main engine oil pressure low → slowdown, very low → shutdown) are safety-critical; the ETO verifies these setpoints and the actuator chain (sensor → logic → trip valve) by on-site testing. Override functions are recorded and supervised.

Aşırı alarm (alarm flood), operatörü kör.en: Excessive alarms (alarm flood) blind the operator and hide real danger. The ETO applies alarm rationalization to reduce recurring, meaningless or miscalibration-induced alarms; every alarm must have an associated action, and chattering alarms must be prevented with deadband and delay. The EEMUA 191 principles are the guide.

UMS/E0 notasyonu, makine dairesinin gece.en: The UMS/E0 notation allows the engine room to operate unattended at night or for specified periods. This depends on the high reliability of the automation and alarm system: the bridge alarm transfer, the engineers' call system, the dead-man alarm (watchkeeping engineer function), fire detection and the bilge alarm systems must work flawlessly.

ETO, UMS moduna geçmeden önce günlük UMS.en: Before switching to UMS mode, the ETO verifies the daily UMS readiness checklist: all critical alarms active, no critical alarm inhibited, automatic pumps (bilge, transfer) working, fire detection panel normal, main engine slowdown/shutdown systems in service.

Bakım sırasında geçici olarak inhibit ed.en: Alarms temporarily inhibited during maintenance must always be re-enabled before switching to UMS mode. The ETO checks the inhibit list regularly; a "forgotten inhibit" is the most common and most dangerous UMS error. Permanent inhibition of critical safety alarms is a class violation.

Otomasyon ağındaki iletişim arızaları (k.en: Communication faults in the automation network (cable, terminal or node failure) lead to loss of I/O and spurious alarms. Using fieldbus diagnostic tools, the ETO checks node status, the telegram error rate and the termination resistors. In a redundant ring topology, it is verified that when one cable breaks, the network continues to be supplied via the other path.

Entegre sistemde tüm cihazların aynı zam.en: In an integrated system, it is critical for alarm log analysis and event sequencing that all devices use the same timestamp. The ETO checks the NTP/time synchronization source, and also verifies that the data bridges (gateways) between different subsystems work correctly and that there are no scaling errors.

Alarm ve event log'ları, sistemin gizli.en: Alarm and event logs are the most valuable data source for revealing hidden problems in the system. By regularly reviewing the alarm printer output and historian data, the ETO analyzes which alarms recur most often, at what times they concentrate and in which subsystem they cluster.

Tekrar eden bir alarm; gevşek bir termin.en: A recurring alarm can be the forerunner of a loose terminal, a drifting sensor, a marginal setpoint or a developing mechanical failure. Through root cause analysis (RCA), the ETO resolves these signs before they grow and does not fall into the trap of "the alarm came, I acknowledged it, it cleared".

ETO, recurring fault analiz sonuçlarını.en: The ETO records the results of recurring fault analysis in the engine logbook and the PMS and, if necessary, reports them to the company's technical department and the vendor. These records build fleet-wide "lessons learned" and help prevent similar failures on sister ships.

Güvenlik (safety/shutdown) sistemi, kont.en: The safety (safety/shutdown) system must be independent of the control system: main engine overspeed, low oil pressure and crankcase oil mist (oil mist detector) trips are designed separately from the control PLC and fail-safe (going to the safe state on loss of power). The ETO preserves this independence and tests the trip chain periodically.

ETO, slow-down ve shutdown fonksiyonları.en: The ETO tests the slowdown and shutdown functions by simulating real conditions (e.g. by lowering the pressure at a pressure switch in a controlled way) and verifies that the trip occurs within the expected time and with the correct action. Before the test, coordination with the engine team and the necessary isolation are arranged.

Bir gemide kalibre edilmemiş yağ basınç.en: On one ship, an uncalibrated oil pressure transmitter slowly began to read low; eventually a false low-low pressure trip stopped the main engine, and the ship lost propulsion in confined waters. The investigation showed that the transmitter's calibration was overdue. Lesson: the calibration schedule for critical sensors must be followed strictly.

Bir IAS'te yedek server'ın yıllardır arı.en: In one IAS, it emerged that the standby server had been faulty for years but had gone unnoticed because it had never been tested; when the main server failed, the system stopped completely. Lesson: redundancy is assured not merely by its existence but by periodic failover testing.

Otomasyon ve alarm sistemleri, geminin \.en: Automation and alarm systems are the ship's "nervous system"; by making sure this system works quietly but reliably, the ETO safeguards both the unattended safety of the engine room and the safety of the whole ship's operation. A good ETO reads the trend before the alarm comes and intervenes before the failure grows.

Gemide bataryalar farklı görevlere hizme.en: Batteries on board serve different purposes: GMDSS reserve (communications), emergency/transitional (bridging emergency power), engine start (generator/lifeboat), UPS (critical IT/navigation) and, increasingly, energy storage for hybrid/electric propulsion. The choice of chemistry depends on the purpose: lead-acid (high current, economical), Ni-Cd (wide temperature range, robust), Li-ion (high energy density).

ETO, her bankın nominal voltajını, kapas.en: The ETO must know each bank's nominal voltage, capacity (Ah), application and chemistry; the maintenance regime and safety precautions differ by chemistry. Vented (flooded) lead-acid and Ni-Cd batteries require regular topping up with water and ventilation, whereas VRLA and Li-ion batteries require different maintenance approaches.

GMDSS reserve batarya, ana ve acil güç k.en: As required by SOLAS, the GMDSS reserve battery must supply the GMDSS equipment on loss of main and emergency power (1 hour if there is an emergency generator, otherwise 6 hours). The transitional emergency battery bridges the mandatory loads until the emergency generator comes on line (generally 30 min). The ETO makes sure that these durations are verified by an actual capacity test.

Vented (sulu) kurşun-asit bataryalarda ş.en: In vented (flooded) lead-acid batteries, water is electrolyzed during charging and the level drops. The ETO checks the electrolyte level periodically and adds only pure (deionized/distilled) water; acid is never added. Specific gravity (SG) is measured with a hydrometer: a fully charged cell reads ~1.270–1.280 and a discharged cell around ~1.120. SG is a direct indicator of the state of charge.

ETO, hücreler arası SG farkını izler; bü.en: The ETO monitors the SG difference between cells; a large difference (e.g. >0.030) points to a weak or short-circuited cell. In VRLA batteries the electrolyte cannot be reached, so SG cannot be measured; instead, terminal voltage, internal resistance (impedance) and temperature are monitored.

Batarya terminalleri korozyona (sülfat b.en: Battery terminals are prone to corrosion (sulfate buildup); the ETO keeps the terminals clean, tight and protected with protective jelly (petrolatum). A loose or corroded connection creates high resistance, heating and voltage drop. The charger's output voltage and current must suit the battery type (float/boost/equalize) and be temperature-compensated.

Ni-Cd bataryalar dayanıklıdır, geniş sıc.en: Ni-Cd batteries are robust, operate over a wide temperature range and tolerate deep discharge better than lead-acid batteries; this is why they are preferred for GMDSS and engine start applications. The ETO tops up the electrolyte (potassium hydroxide, KOH, alkaline) with pure water and monitors cell voltages. Because KOH is alkaline, alkali safety precautions are required, not acid precautions.

Ni-Cd'de SG, kurşun-asitteki gibi şarj d.en: In Ni-Cd batteries, SG does not indicate the state of charge as it does in lead-acid batteries; the KOH density does not change significantly with discharge. The state of charge is therefore assessed by voltage and capacity tests. The ETO maintains capacity through the periodic full charge/discharge cycle recommended by the manufacturer.

ETO, Ni-Cd bankının kapasitesini periyod.en: The ETO verifies the capacity of the Ni-Cd bank with periodic discharge tests and monitors the balance of cell voltages. Weak cells reduce the performance of the whole bank; if necessary, cells are replaced. Test results are recorded and the trend is followed.

Li-ion bataryalar yüksek enerji yoğunluğ.en: Li-ion batteries offer high energy density but carry a risk of thermal runaway (uncontrolled heat/fire) from overcharging, overdischarging, physical damage or excessive temperature. Li-ion banks must therefore operate with a Battery Management System (BMS); the BMS monitors and balances cell voltage, temperature and current, and isolates the bank when limits are exceeded. The ETO closely follows BMS alarms and health.

ETO, Li-ion sistemde hücre sıcaklık sens.en: In a Li-ion system, the ETO periodically checks the cell temperature sensors, the cooling system and the BMS isolation contactors. A cell that swells, leaks or heats abnormally is isolated immediately. Li-ion maintenance requires vendor-approved training and procedures; haphazard intervention is dangerous.

Li-ion yangınları geleneksel söndürmeye.en: Li-ion fires resist conventional extinguishing, call for large amounts of cooling (water) and carry a risk of re-ignition. Li-ion energy storage systems on board are fitted with special fire detection (gas/heat), extinguishing and ventilation arrangements. The ETO ensures that these systems are in good health and that the response procedure is known by the team.

Kurşun-asit ve Ni-Cd bataryalar şarj sır.en: Lead-acid and Ni-Cd batteries produce hydrogen (H₂) gas during charging; H₂ forms an explosive mixture with air in the 4–75% range (lower explosive limit, LEL, 4%). The battery room must have adequate ventilation (generally natural or forced, from the top) so that this gas cannot accumulate. The ETO verifies that the ventilation fans are running and that the vents are not blocked.

Bazı batarya odalarında H₂ gaz dedektörü.en: Some battery rooms have an H₂ gas detector; the ETO checks its calibration and alarm. All electrical equipment in the room (lighting, fan motor, switches) must be of ignition-free / ex-proof type. The ETO periodically inspects the integrity of the room, the ventilation openings and the spill (acid/electrolyte) collection arrangement.

Batarya şarj cihazı, doğru voltaj/akım p.en: The battery charger must provide the correct voltage/current profile (float, boost, equalize) and apply temperature compensation. Overcharging leads to excessive gassing, water loss and plate corrosion; undercharging leads to sulfation and loss of capacity. The ETO measures the charger's output voltage/current and verifies that it suits the battery type.

Bir bataryanın gerçek kapasitesi ancak d.en: The real capacity of a battery can only be known through a discharge test; even if the voltage looks normal, the capacity may have collapsed. The ETO carries out an annual load bank discharge test on critical banks (GMDSS, emergency) and assesses the capacity against the nominal value. Banks whose capacity falls below a set threshold (typically 80%) are replaced.

Batarya yönetimi, \"iyi görünen ama çökm.en: Battery management requires constant vigilance against the "looks fine but has collapsed" trap: the real value of a battery is the capacity it can deliver when needed. The ETO's success is measured by proving reliability through regular capacity tests, managing hydrogen and Li-ion risks with safety discipline, and making sure that this silent reserve really comes on line at a critical blackout or GMDSS moment.

IT (Information Technology) sistemleri v.en: IT (Information Technology) systems manage data: e-mail, administrative software, reporting. OT (Operational Technology) systems control physical processes: ECDIS, IAS/AMS (automation/alarm), propulsion control, steering, cargo control, ballast. An IT breach causes data loss, whereas an OT breach directly threatens navigational and machinery safety; this is why OT security is a matter of safety of life.

ETO, gemideki tüm OT varlıklarını ve bun.en: The ETO inventories all OT assets on board and their network connections (asset inventory). A system cannot be protected without knowing which network segment it is on and how it comes into contact with the outside world (satellite, USB, service laptop). This inventory is the basis of the risk assessment.

IMO Resolution MSC.428(98), geminin Güve.en: IMO Resolution MSC.428(98) requires the ship's Safety Management System (under the ISM Code) to include cyber risk management. MSC-FAL.1/Circ.3 recommends five functions in parallel with the NIST framework: identify, protect, detect, respond, recover. The ETO implements and documents the technical controls of this framework.

IEC 62443 yaklaşımıyla OT ağı, güvenlik.en: Following the IEC 62443 approach, the OT network is divided into security zones, and communication between zones passes through controlled conduits (conduits/firewalls). The ETO keeps bridge OT (ECDIS, radar), machinery OT (IAS, propulsion), cargo control, administrative IT and the crew welfare network in separate segments. Critical OT is not connected directly to the internet; the necessary data flows are restricted by strict rules.

ETO, segmentler arası firewall kuralları.en: The ETO configures the firewall rules between segments on the "default deny" principle; only necessary and justified traffic is allowed. Access from the crew welfare network to OT is blocked. This architecture limits the spread of an incident from one segment to others (lateral movement).

Üretici/servis sağlayıcıların uzaktan te.en: Remote access to OT by manufacturers/service providers for diagnostics is common but is a major risk. The ETO keeps remote access under control: access is enabled only when needed, monitored, logged and closed afterwards. A permanently open remote connection is one of the most dangerous attack surfaces.

USB bellekler ve harici diskler, OT sist.en: USB sticks and external drives are the most common route by which malware enters OT systems; ECDIS chart update media and service technicians' laptops are particularly risky. The ETO restricts the use of portable media by policy: only approved, scanned media, only on the systems that need it, and with a record kept.

ETO, gemiye gelen tüm taşınabilir medyan.en: The ETO ensures that all portable media brought on board are checked at a scanning station separate from the network (scanning kiosk). In some ports, coordination with port USB scanner systems is required. Unused USB ports on OT systems are disabled physically or by software; this is one of the simplest and most effective controls.

Yazılım/firmware güncellemeleri güvenlik.en: Software/firmware updates close security vulnerabilities but can disrupt an OT system if applied incorrectly. The ETO applies updates only from a trusted source (the manufacturer, with a verified digital signature), at a non-critical time if possible and after taking a backup. System behavior is verified before and after the update.

ETO, kritik OT yazılımlarının sürüm enva.en: The ETO tracks the version inventory of critical OT software and known vulnerabilities. On type-approved systems such as ECDIS, updates are made with the manufacturer's approved packages; random patching can compromise type approval and security.

ETO, hangi sistemin hangi yazılım/firmwa.en: The ETO keeps a record of which software/firmware version each system is running (configuration management). When a new vulnerability is announced, this inventory makes it possible to identify quickly which ship systems are affected. For legacy systems that cannot be patched, compensating controls (additional segmentation, monitoring) are applied.

ETO, OT/IT sistemlerinde rol bazlı erişi.en: The ETO applies role-based access control on OT/IT systems: each user has only the privileges their duties require (least privilege). Shared/default logins and factory passwords are among the biggest weaknesses; the ETO changes or disables them and enforces strong, unique passwords.

Siber güvenlik fiziksel güvenlikle bütün.en: Cybersecurity is integrated with physical security: physical access to control panels, server cabinets and network equipment is restricted to authorized persons. The ETO immediately disables the logins of personnel who leave the ship and carries out periodic access reviews; inactive or unnecessary logins are closed.

Bir siber olayı yönetmek için önce tespi.en: To manage a cyber incident, it must first be detected. The ETO monitors logs (firewall, server, OT devices), network traffic anomalies and antivirus/EDR alerts. In OT, unexpected traffic, a new device, abnormal system behavior or failed login attempts are warning signs. Logs are kept regularly and in a form that cannot be altered.

Bir siber olayda ETO, olay müdahale plan.en: In a cyber incident, the ETO applies the incident response plan: isolate the affected system (containment), preserve the evidence, assess the impact, report in accordance with the company/SMS procedure and recover from backup. When critical OT is affected, switching to a manual/backup operating mode (e.g. the backup ECDIS or paper charts, manual control) is vitally important.

ETO, müdahale sonrası kök neden analizi.en: After the response, the ETO carries out a root cause analysis and feeds the lessons into the SMS. Regular cyber drills (e.g. a loss-of-ECDIS scenario) ensure that the team shows the right reflexes in a real incident. Recovery relies on up-to-date backups kept off the network (offline).

Sınıf kuruluşları, gemiler için gönüllü/.en: Classification societies offer voluntary/mandatory cyber secure notations for ships (DNV, LR, ABS, BV, etc.); these require specified maturity levels for asset inventory, segmentation, access control, monitoring and response capability. The ETO meets the technical requirements of the notation held by the ship and provides evidence (policies, logs, test records) for surveys.

ETO, port USB scanner sistemleri, liman.en: The ETO coordinates with port USB scanner systems, port information systems and the company IT/SOC (Security Operations Center). Ship–company coordination is critical during an incident and for updates or configuration changes. As the shipboard technical point of contact, the ETO handles this communication.

Siber güvenlik, ETO'nun en yeni ama hızl.en: Cybersecurity is the ETO's newest responsibility, but one that is fast becoming the most critical, because a breach of an ECDIS or a propulsion control system is now as real a threat to navigational safety as a fire or flooding. The ETO's success is measured by robust segmentation, disciplined media/update/access control and the readiness to switch the ship safely to manual mode during an incident. This invisible layer of defense keeps the ship resilient against the risks of the digital age.

Yüksek gerilim, alçak gerilimden farklı.en: Unlike low voltage, high voltage can kill even without contact (by jumping across an air gap), and in an arc flash it produces extreme heat, pressure and light within seconds, causing severe burns and death. This is why HV work requires much stricter procedures and special training.

HV switchgear üzerinde yalnızca yetkin v.en: Only competent, specially trained (HV authorized) personnel may work on HV switchgear. The ETO gains this competence through STCW A-III/6 and vendor training; special equipment such as GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgear) also requires manufacturer-approved training.

HV çalışması, sıkı bir işlem sırasıyla v.en: HV work is carried out under a Permit to Work, following a strict sequence of operations: disconnect the load, open the circuit (open breaker), withdraw the breaker truck (rack out / isolate), lock and tag, verify the absence of voltage and apply earthing. Each step is taken in order and verified; skipping a step can have fatal consequences.

Voltaj yokluğu, onaylı bir HV voltaj ded.en: The absence of voltage is verified with an approved HV voltage detector; the detector is tested on a known live source before and after use (prove-test-prove). A busbar that is "apparently dead" is never earthed or touched; it is always verified first.

İzole edilen ve voltajsızlığı doğrulanan.en: An HV circuit that has been isolated and verified dead is earthed (earthing/grounding) before work starts. This makes capacitive residual charge and accidental energization safe. Earthing is done with the switchgear's earth switch or with a portable earthing set.

HV çalışmasında uygun sınıf yalıtkanlı e.en: For HV work, insulating gloves of the appropriate class (Class 2/3), an arc-flash suit, a face shield and insulating footwear/mats are used. PPE is tested regularly (glove inflation test); damaged insulating PPE is a life-threatening risk. The ETO checks the PPE before every use.

Step-up/step-down transformer, HV switch.en: Maintenance of step-up/step-down transformers, HV switchgear and GIS includes insulation resistance, connection temperature (thermography), SF6 gas pressure (GIS) and protection relay tests. This work is generally done under vendor-approved procedures and training. The ETO monitors the maintenance records and the protection settings.

HV elektrik kazasında, kurtarıcı önce ka.en: In an HV electrical accident, the rescuer does not touch the victim before isolating the source. The rescue is carried out after the circuit has been made safe; CPR and first aid for burns are given. The ETO knows the emergency procedure and the isolation points in the HV area.

Yüksek gerilim çalışması, ETO'nun en yük.en: High-voltage work is the ETO's task that requires the highest discipline; a single skipped step — unverified isolation, missing earthing, damaged PPE — can be fatal. A strict sequence of operations, prove-test-prove and the correct PPE are the unchanging foundation for working safely on HV systems.

GPS, gyro, log, echo sounder ve anemomet.en: Sensors such as the GPS, gyro, log, echo sounder and anemometer supply data to consumers such as the radar, ECDIS and AIS via NMEA 0183 (serial) or NMEA 2000 / IEC 61162-450 (Ethernet). The ETO must know the topology of this data network, its distribution units and which devices each sensor feeds; a single sensor failure can affect many devices.

Heading (gyro) verisi özellikle kritikti.en: Heading (gyro) data is particularly critical: the radar ARPA, ECDIS, AIS and autopilot all depend on the gyro. The ETO keeps the heading distribution redundant (gyro + magnetic + GPS heading) and verifies changeover to the correct source in the event of a sensor failure.

SOLAS V/19, gemi tonajına göre zorunlu s.en: SOLAS V/19 lists the mandatory navigational equipment according to ship tonnage: gyro, radar (two radars above a certain tonnage), ECDIS (with backup), AIS, VDR/S-VDR, echo sounder, speed log, BNWAS, LRIT. The ETO ensures that this equipment is working and type-approved; the failure of one item can be a cause of navigational restrictions (PSC detention).

Geleneksel radarlarda magnetron, mikroda.en: In conventional radars, the magnetron is the tube that generates the microwave power, and it weakens over time; the ETO monitors transmitter/receiver performance and magnetron health with the performance monitor (echo box). Typical magnetron life is 3000–8000 hours; weakening reduces the detection of distant targets. Modern solid-state (SSPA) radars have no magnetron, but the power module and cooling are monitored.

ETO, magnetron değişiminde yüksek gerili.en: When replacing a magnetron, the ETO follows the safety rules for high voltage (kV) and microwave exposure; work is done with the antenna stopped and the transmitter off. Tuning, gain, sea/rain clutter and performance monitor values are recorded.

Anten dönüş motoru, slip ring, encoder (.en: The antenna drive motor, slip ring, encoder (azimuth/heading marker) and waveguide need maintenance. The ETO checks the antenna mechanism, the motor brushes (if fitted), waveguide moisture (dehydrator/pressurization) and heading marker alignment. Moisture getting into the waveguide causes power loss and arcing.

ECDIS, kağıt haritanın yerini alan onayl.en: ECDIS is the approved system that replaces the paper chart; the ETO is responsible for the technical health of the hardware (workstation, display, backup power supply), the software version and the chart/update infrastructure. ENC (Electronic Navigational Chart) updates and the IHO presentation library/software version are kept up to date; an incompatible version creates navigational safety and PSC problems.

Yedekli ECDIS gereksinimi için iki bağım.en: To meet the backup ECDIS requirement, two independent workstations must operate with separate power supplies and sensors. The ETO tests the takeover scenario: it is verified that when the main ECDIS fails, the backup takes over without problems.

GPS/GNSS alıcısı, konum ve zaman kaynağı.en: The GPS/GNSS receiver is the source of position and time; the ETO checks the antenna connector, cable losses and receiver health. Because of the risk of GNSS jamming/spoofing, a backup position source (second receiver, eLoran where available) and dead reckoning backup using gyro + log have become important. The antenna must be sited so that it is not shadowed and not affected by other antennas.

Echo sounder (derinlik) ve speed log (hı.en: The echo sounder (depth) and speed log (speed) transducers are in the ship's bottom; the ETO checks the insulation of the transducer cables, the tightness of the sea valves and the calibration of the electronic unit. A Doppler log is affected by underwater fouling; the transducer faces are cleaned during drydocking.

Gyro compass, gerçek kuzeyi sağlayan kri.en: The gyro compass is the critical sensor that provides true north; modern fiber-optic (FOG) or ring-laser (RLG) types are easy to maintain, while traditional mechanical types need careful maintenance. The ETO checks the gyro power supply, heading repeater alignment, the follow-up system and the alarm functions. Because a heading error misleads all navigation equipment, gyro accuracy is critical.

AIS, gemi kimliği ve seyir verisini VHF.en: AIS transmits and receives ship identity and navigation data over VHF. The ETO checks the AIS VHF and GPS antennas, the accuracy of the static data (MMSI, IMO number, ship type, dimensions) and the dynamic data feeds (heading, ROT). Wrong AIS data is dangerous for collision avoidance and is a cause of PSC findings.

VDR (Voyage Data Recorder), kazaların \".en: The VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) is the "black box" for accidents; it records bridge audio, radar images, sensor data and radio communications. The ETO verifies that all VDR data channels are being recorded and that the final recording medium (capsule) and the float-free unit are working. The Annual Performance Test (APT) is carried out and certified by an authorized service provider.

GMDSS, deniz alanlarına (A1-A4) göre bel.en: The GMDSS requires specified communication redundancy according to the sea area (A1–A4). The ETO carries out the technical maintenance of VHF DSC (channel 70), MF/HF DSC (2187.5 kHz, etc.) and Inmarsat-C/FleetBroadband terminals. The DSC self-test, transmitter/receiver power output, antenna SWR (standing wave ratio) and the supply battery are checked.

GMDSS ekipmanının bakım stratejisi deniz.en: The GMDSS maintenance strategy depends on the sea area: in A3/A4, at least two of the methods "duplication of equipment", "shore-based maintenance" and "at-sea electronic maintenance" are chosen. If at-sea maintenance is chosen, a person holding a GMDSS Radio Electronic/Maintainer certificate (usually the ETO) must be on board.

Anten sistemleri köprüüstü elektroniğini.en: Antenna systems are the most heavily stressed external components of bridge electronics: salt, moisture, vibration and UV. The ETO checks the antenna bases, insulators and earthing and the SWR of the VHF/HF antennas. High SWR leads to power loss and failure of the transmitter output stage. Interference between antennas (mutual coupling) and shadowing are taken into account when siting them.

Koaksiyel konnektörlerde (PL259, N-tipi,.en: Corrosion and moisture are the most common causes of failure in coaxial connectors (PL259, N-type, TNC). The ETO waterproofs external connectors with self-amalgamating tape, replaces cables that have taken in moisture and keeps terminal panels clean and tight. Most signal quality problems come from bad connectors, not from the equipment.

BNWAS (Bridge Navigational Watch Alarm S.en: The BNWAS (Bridge Navigational Watch Alarm System) ensures that the officer of the watch is awake and on duty; if it is not reset within a set interval, it alerts the Master and the other officers in stages. The ETO tests the BNWAS timing, the reset sensors and the alarm chain. Correct operation of the bridge alarm panel (machinery, fire, general) is also verified.

Otopilot (heading control), gyro ve düme.en: The autopilot (heading control) depends on the gyro and the rudder feedback system; the ETO checks the electrical health of the autopilot–gyro–steering chain and the reliability of manual/automatic changeover. The rudder angle indicator and the RPM indicators must be correctly calibrated.

Bazı bölgelerde GNSS spoofing nedeniyle.en: In some regions, GNSS spoofing caused ships' positions to be reported incorrectly; ECDIS showed a false position. Lesson: the ETO must make sure that the backups for GNSS-independent position checking (radar fix, gyro + log dead reckoning) are working, and must support the bridge team so that they do not depend on a single position source.

Bir kazada VDR'ın köprü ses kanalının ay.en: After one accident, it emerged that the VDR's bridge audio channel had not been recording for months because a microphone was faulty. Lesson: regular verification of all VDR channels and never skipping the annual APT are of critical importance.

Seyir ve haberleşme elektroniği, geminin.en: Navigation and communication electronics are the ship's "eyes, ears and voice"; by keeping these systems working at all times, the ETO safeguards both navigational safety and the ability to reach the outside world in an emergency. A single silent fault in this equipment can be a matter of life and death at a critical moment.

Conventional sistemlerde dedektörler zon.en: In conventional systems, detectors are grouped by zone; the panel shows only which zone is in alarm and cannot tell which individual detector has been triggered. In addressable systems, each detector has a unique address; the panel reports exactly which cabin or corridor has an alarm/fault. On modern large ships, a loop-based addressable system is standard and makes fault finding much easier.

ETO, sistemin tek hat şemasını (loop dia.en: The ETO must know the system's single-line diagram (loop diagram) and the detector address list in full: how many detectors each loop carries, where the end-of-line resistor is and at which points the loop isolators are located. Without this information, neither fast fault diagnosis nor correct placement of spares is possible.

SOLAS II-2, makine daireleri, kargo bölg.en: SOLAS II-2 requires machinery spaces, cargo areas, cabins, corridors and escape routes to be protected by fixed fire detection. FSS Code Chapter 9 sets out the design, testing and approval criteria for the system: detectors must be designed so that they retain the ability to give an alarm in the event of a fault or loss of power, and the system must be supplied from both the main and the emergency source of power.

ETO, sistemin sınıf ve bayrak gereklilik.en: For PSC and surveys, the ETO documents the system's compliance with class and flag requirements: detector layout plans, test records and fault/repair logs are kept up to date. It is also mandatory for the system to be monitored from the repeater panel on the bridge and, where possible, from the machinery control room.

İyonizasyon dedektörleri, küçük bir rady.en: Ionization detectors use a small radioactive source (Am-241) and detect the disturbance caused by smoke particles to the current in the ionized air; they are sensitive to fast, flaming fires but are less common today because of the radioactive source. Photoelectric (optical) detectors use a photocell to detect the scattering of an LED light beam by smoke particles; they are more sensitive to slow-developing, smoky fires and are common on ships.

ETO, dedektör tipini bölgenin risk profi.en: The ETO selects the detector type according to the risk profile of the area: optical smoke detectors for cabins and corridors, and heat or multi-criteria (combined) detectors for places with a high risk of false alarms, such as the galley and the engine room. Choosing the wrong detector causes either late detection or chronic false alarms.

Heat dedektörleri iki tipte çalışır: fix.en: Heat detectors work in two ways: fixed temperature (e.g. a 57°C or 78°C threshold) and rate-of-rise (sensitive to the rate of temperature increase, e.g. >8°C/minute). Heat detectors are used instead of smoke detectors in normally hot or steamy spaces such as the galley, the laundry and the engine room. Flame detectors detect UV/IR radiation and are used for fast-flaring fires in open areas such as a tanker deck.

ETO, heat dedektörlerinin sıcaklık eşiği.en: The ETO verifies that the temperature threshold of heat detectors suits the ambient conditions. For example, if a detector on the engine room deckhead above a running engine is not of a high rating (e.g. 90°C), it will give false alarms at normal operating temperature.

Manual call point (yangın ihbar butonu),.en: A manual call point (fire alarm button) allows a person to raise the fire alarm manually; it is of the break-glass or push type and is located along escape routes at intervals complying with SOLAS. The ETO periodically tests the electrical continuity of the MCPs and the operation of the glass/button mechanism.

Aspirating smoke detection (ASD/VESDA) s.en: Aspirating smoke detection (ASD/VESDA) systems continuously draw air through a pipe network and pass it through a laser-based detector; they provide very early detection and are used in critical areas such as cargo holds and server rooms. The ETO checks the filters, fans and sampling holes of these systems for blockage.

Fire detection panel, sistemin merkezi b.en: The fire detection panel is the central brain of the system: it shows alarm, fault, disablement and test states by LEDs/LCD and provides outputs for alarm sounders, fire flaps and ventilation shutdown relays. The ETO must interpret the panel's alarm (red), fault (yellow) and power (green) indications correctly and identify recurring faults by regularly reviewing the panel event log.

Bir bakım veya tadilat sırasında dedektö.en: During maintenance or alterations, a detector or zone may be temporarily disabled (disabled/isolated); however, the ETO must ensure that this is recorded under the permit system and that it is always re-enabled when the work is finished. A forgotten disablement means loss of detection in a real fire.

Modern panellerde her dedektörün hassasi.en: On modern panels, the sensitivity of each detector and, if necessary, an alarm delay (e.g. day/night mode) can be configured. The cause-and-effect matrix defines which outputs are triggered when a detector goes into alarm (ventilation shutdown, fire damper, pre-warning of fixed gas release). The ETO ensures that this matrix remains consistent with the manufacturer's class-approved configuration.

Yanlış yapılandırılmış gecikme veya hass.en: A wrongly configured delay or sensitivity leads either to dangerously late detection or to chronic false alarms. The ETO makes sensitivity changes only at authorized user level and on record; such changes are subject to survey.

Optik smoke dedektörleri zamanla toz, is.en: Over time, optical smoke detectors lose sensitivity or give false alarms because of dust, soot and insect buildup. The ETO cleans the detectors periodically in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions (compressed air, a soft brush or a special cleaner). In addressable systems, the panel reports the contamination level of each detector; when the threshold is exceeded, it gives a "compensation limit" warning and the detector needs cleaning or replacement.

Temizlik sırasında ilgili zone panelde t.en: During cleaning, the zone concerned is put into test/isolate mode on the panel, the ship's fire patrol is informed and any interlock with the fixed extinguishing system is temporarily made safe. After cleaning, the detector's function is verified with a test device (test gas/smoke).

Her dedektör periyodik olarak gerçek uya.en: Each detector is periodically tested with a real stimulus: smoke detectors with test aerosol/smoke, heat detectors with a test heat source and MCPs with a test key. The test must verify that the alarm appears on the panel with the correct address/zone and that the sounders sound. SOLAS and the company SMS typically require a weekly panel check, monthly testing of a sample of detectors and an annual full test.

ETO, test edilen her cihazı, sonucu ve t.en: The ETO records each device tested, the result and the date; faulty detectors are replaced. During testing, it is vital that the fixed gas discharge (CO2/FM-200) interlocks have definitely been made safe; otherwise the test can cause an unwanted gas release.

Loop arızaları üç ana tipte görülür: ope.en: Loop faults are of three main types: open circuit (broken line/loose terminal), short circuit (cable short, water ingress) and earth fault (breakdown of cable insulation, leakage to earth). An addressable panel shows the address of the fault or the segment between two addresses, which speeds up fault finding. In a conventional system, the ETO works zone by zone, measuring terminal by terminal.

ETO, loop direncini ve EOL değerini mult.en: The ETO measures the loop resistance and the EOL value with a multimeter and checks whether any loop isolators have opened. Moisture and corrosion in cable junction boxes are the most frequent cause of open-circuit/earth faults on ships. Connections are cleaned and, if necessary, treated with contact cleaner and retightened.
