The Second Engineer monitors sludge generation, the tank level and disposal, and ensures that sludge never gets into the sea.

Her yağ işlemi (bilge transfer, OWS deşa.en: Every oil operation (bilge transfer, OWS discharge, sludge incineration/delivery, internal transfer) is entered in ORB Part I correctly, on time and in a way that reflects what actually happened. The Second Engineer ensures that the ORB is consistent with the physical operations (tank levels, meter readings). ORB inconsistencies are among the most frequent causes of penalties/detention at PSC.

Bir yağ kaçağı/dökülmesi durumunda SOPEP.en: In the event of an oil leak/spill, the SOPEP is activated; the response equipment (absorbents, booms), the notification list (coastal State, company, P&I) and the initial response steps are applied. The Second Engineer takes part in the rapid response and notification for leaks originating in the engine room.

Bilge, sludge ve çevresel deşarj yönetim.en: Bilge, sludge and environmental discharge management is the Second Engineer's most sensitive responsibility, both legally and ethically. An OWS without any bypass, an honest ORB and correct sludge disposal protect the sea, keep the ship away from heavy penalties and uphold the environmental integrity of the seafaring profession.

Makine dairesinde güvenlik, ekibin ekipm.en: Safety in the engine room depends on the team knowing the equipment and the risks. The Second Engineer sees training not as a formality but as the foundation of accident prevention and operational continuity. A well-trained team acts correctly both in routine work and in an emergency.

Yeni gelen mühendis/tayfa; makine daires.en: Newly joined engineers/ratings are briefed on their first day on the engine room layout, emergency exits, locations of safety equipment (EEBD, fire extinguishers, emergency stops), alarm signals and basic procedures. The Second Engineer carries out this familiarization and completes the checklist.

İkinci Mühendis; LOTO (enerji izolasyonu.en: The Second Engineer teaches the team the LOTO (energy isolation), Permit to Work, enclosed space entry and hot work procedures, and explains with examples why these high-risk jobs are subject to strict rules. A team that knows "why" it follows a procedure takes it seriously.

Bazı ekipmanlar (otomasyon, purifier, öz.en: Some equipment (automation, purifiers, special pumps, BWMS) requires manufacturer-specific knowledge. The Second Engineer coordinates access to the vendor manuals and training, and makes sure that the team uses the equipment correctly and does not damage it through incorrect intervention.

İkinci Mühendis; blackout recovery (kara.en: The Second Engineer takes part in blackout recovery (recovery from a blackout/loss of electrical power), engine room fire and flooding drills and trains the team. When these scenarios are drilled realistically, the team carries out the right actions in a real incident without having to think. Use of the quick-closing valves, emergency stops and the fixed extinguishing system is drilled.

Makine personeli eğitimi, İkinci Mühendi.en: Training of engine personnel is the most valuable investment the Second Engineer makes in the team and in the safety of the ship. Proper familiarization, sound safety training and realistic emergency drills make the engine room both efficient in routine operation and resilient in a crisis.

Şartlandırılmamış soğutma suyu, motor iç.en: Untreated cooling water causes corrosion, cavitation damage and mineral deposits (scale) on the internal surfaces of the engine (liner, cylinder cover, cooling passages). A corrosion inhibitor (DCA — nitrite-based, etc.) prevents this damage. The Second Engineer protects the internal integrity of the engine by keeping the water within the correct range.

İkinci Mühendis; nitrit (inhibitor seviy.en: The Second Engineer tests nitrite (inhibitor level), pH (acidity/alkalinity), chloride (indicator of a seawater leak) and total hardness. Low nitrite means insufficient corrosion protection; high chloride points to a seawater leak from the cooler. Each parameter is kept within its criteria range.

Klorür değerinde ani artış, cooler'da bi.en: A sudden rise in the chloride value indicates a seawater leak in a cooler and is investigated. A seawater leak both accelerates corrosion and reduces cooling efficiency; early detection prevents major damage.

İkinci Mühendis, gemi test kiti ile düze.en: The Second Engineer carries out regular (usually weekly) tests with the ship's test kit and records the results in the log. If the nitrite/inhibitor level is low, the calculated quantity of DCA/corrosion inhibitor is added. The correct quantity matters, because overdosing can also cause waste and side effects.

Gemi test kiti temel parametreleri verir.en: The ship's test kit gives the basic parameters; for a comprehensive analysis, samples are periodically sent to a shore-side laboratory. The lab report verifies the shipboard tests and reveals more subtle problems (e.g. microbiological ones).

Sonuçların trendi, ani bir sapmadan (kaç.en: The trend of the results gives more information than a single sudden deviation (leak, dosing error). By following how the parameters develop over time, the Second Engineer catches problems early. Regular records form the basis both for maintenance decisions and for inspections.

Soğutma sistemine eklenen makyaj suyu (m.en: Make-up water added to the cooling system must be low in chloride (usually distilled/evaporator water); otherwise every addition brings in chloride/hardness. The Second Engineer monitors the make-up water source and the expansion tank level.

Soğutma suyu analizi ve dozajlama, İkinc.en: Cooling water analysis and dosing is a discipline through which the Second Engineer protects the internal health of the engine "out of sight". Correct water chemistry, early leak detection and trend monitoring prevent liner/cover corrosion and secure a long service life for the main engine and the generators.

Silindir yağı iki iş yapar: liner-ring a.en: Cylinder oil does two jobs: it reduces wear by providing an oil film between the liner and the rings, and it neutralizes the sulfuric acids formed by combustion with the alkaline components in the oil (BN — Base Number). The Second Engineer manages this balance; too little oil/BN causes corrosive wear and scuffing, while too much oil causes deposits and waste.

Yüksek kükürtlü yakıt daha çok asit üret.en: High-sulfur fuel produces more acid; this is why a cylinder oil with a higher BN or a higher feed rate is needed. MARPOL Annex VI sulfur limits (e.g. changeover to low-sulfur fuel) also affect the choice of cylinder oil; a wrong match causes corrosion or deposits.

Silindir altına (scavenge/piston rod stu.en: A sample of the used oil that drains down below the cylinders (scrape-down; scavenge space/piston rod stuffing box area) is taken and analyzed: the Fe content shows wear, and the remaining BN shows the acid neutralization reserve. High Fe means excessive wear/scuffing; low BN means insufficient neutralization. The Second Engineer adjusts the feed rate according to these data.

Scavenge port'tan yapılan inspection ile.en: Inspection through the scavenge ports shows the condition of the piston rings (broken, sticking, worn), ring zone deposits and the liner surface (glazing, scuffing). If early signs of scuffing are not caught and acted upon, a risk of seizure arises.

İkinci Mühendis; scrape-down ve scavenge.en: Based on the scrape-down and scavenge inspection findings, the Second Engineer increases or reduces the feed rate and, if necessary, applies run-in (increased lubrication after a new liner/new rings). All adjustments are recorded. Data-driven management optimizes both wear and cost.

Her silindirin Fe/BN trendi ve inspectio.en: The Fe/BN trend and the inspection findings for each cylinder are recorded. A trend is far more informative than a single measurement; rising Fe or falling BN is an early sign of a problem. By following this trend, the Second Engineer prevents major failures.

Cylinder lubrication ve scrape-down anal.en: Cylinder lubrication and scrape-down analysis are among the most technical tasks through which the Second Engineer protects the heart of the main engine. The correct feed rate, data-driven monitoring and early diagnosis of scuffing prevent costly liner/piston damage and secure the reliability and service life of the main engine.

SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 34, her sefer.en: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 34 requires every voyage to be planned before it starts, and the plan to cover the whole voyage without a break, from berth to berth, including pilotage waters, maneuvering areas and the open sea. When preparing this plan, the Second Officer works on the "berth-to-berth" principle; the anchorage, the pilot boarding ground and narrow channel transits are an integral part of the plan.

Plan, IMO Resolution A.893(21) \"Guideli.en: The plan is set out in detail according to IMO Resolution A.893(21) "Guidelines for Voyage Planning". These guidelines define four stages: appraisal, planning, execution and monitoring. The Second Officer prepares the first two stages; the last two are the responsibility of the whole bridge team.

Appraisal aşamasında tüm bilgi kaynaklar.en: In the appraisal stage, all sources of information are gathered and the voyage risks are assessed; alternative routes are compared. In the planning stage, the selected route is drawn on the chart/ECDIS, and the waypoints, courses, distances, UKC and abort points are determined. These two stages are the Second Officer's desk work.

Execution, planın kaptan brifingi sonras.en: Execution means carrying out the plan after the Master's briefing; monitoring means cross-checking the position against the plan on every watch and detecting any deviation. The Second Officer ensures that the plan remains a "living document" and is updated for changes in weather, traffic or draft.

Appraisal, eldeki tüm seyir bilgisinin s.en: Appraisal is a systematic review of all the navigational information available. The Second Officer considers together the charts (paper/ENC), Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List of Lights, List of Radio Signals, Tide Tables, Tidal Stream Atlases, Ocean Passages of the World, Routeing Charts, the Mariner's Handbook (NP100), Notices to Mariners and the company's route-specific risk assessment.

Güncel meteorolojik veriler (pilot chart.en: Current meteorological data (pilot chart climatology, seasonal TRS risk), draft restrictions, ECDIS safety settings and company policies (e.g. UKC policy, squat allowance, minimum CPA) are also gathered at this stage. A missing or out-of-date publication invalidates all the stages that follow.

Appraisal'da geminin maksimum draught'ı,.en: In the appraisal, the ship's maximum draft, the expected trim and the water density as it changes along the voyage (fresh/brackish/salt) are considered. A company UKC policy usually specifies values such as a certain percentage of the draft in the open sea and a fixed minimum in restricted waters (e.g. 10% or 1.0-1.5 m).

Hava penceresi (weather window) ve tide.en: The weather window and the tide window are assessed together; for example, entry into a bar harbor is tied to a particular tide time so that there is enough height of water. The Second Officer builds the time dimension of the plan by matching these windows with the ETA calculation.

Okyanus geçişlerinde great circle (büyük.en: On ocean passages, the great circle gives the shortest distance; however, because of high-latitude risks (ice, storms), a composite great circle or a rhumb line may be preferred. The Second Officer determines the route leg by leg, balancing distance, fuel, weather and safety, and places each waypoint at a safe distance from dangers.

Her waypoint'te course, distance, planne.en: For each waypoint, the course, distance, planned speed, ETA and wheel-over point (the point at which the turn starts) are determined. The wheel-over is calculated from the ship's advance and transfer maneuvering characteristics; otherwise the ship will go beyond the safe water limit in the turn.

No-go area; geminin draught ve UKC polic.en: No-go areas are shallow/dangerous areas that the ship must never enter, given her draft and the UKC policy. On ECDIS these areas are displayed through the safety contour and safety depth settings; on a paper chart they are marked by hatching. The plan is built so that it keeps the ship in safe water at all times.

Parallel indexing (PI), radar üzerinde s.en: Parallel indexing (PI) is the technique of keeping the ship on her course by drawing a parallel index line on the radar relative to a fixed reference object. For restricted waters, the Second Officer adds PI lines and clearing bearings/distances to the plan; this gives an independent position check in the event of a GPS failure.

Abort point; geminin kanaldan/yanaşmadan.en: The abort point is the last physical point at which the ship can give up the channel transit/berthing and return to safe water or the open sea. Beyond this point, the turning room or the depth is insufficient. The Second Officer determines the abort point from the maneuvering characteristics and the channel width and marks it clearly in the plan.

Her plan, beklenmedik durumlar (makine a.en: Every plan must include contingency options for unexpected situations (engine failure, sudden deterioration of the weather, traffic congestion). The Second Officer notes in the plan suitable anchorages (holding ground, depth, swinging room), emergency anchorage positions and alternative route options.

Bu noktalar kâğıt ve ECDIS planında işar.en: These points are marked in both the paper plan and the ECDIS plan; at the Master's briefing, "if X happens, we do Y" scenarios are discussed. An unprepared ship multiplies its risk of error when it has to make a decision within minutes in an emergency.

UKC; charted depth + height of tide − (s.en: UKC is calculated with the formula charted depth + height of tide − (static draught + squat + heel allowance + uncertainty/sounding error). The Second Officer assesses each component separately: tidal prediction error, swell effect (swell/heave), density difference and survey reliability (CATZOC on the ENC) cannot be neglected.

Şirket UKC policy minimum bir değer şart.en: The company UKC policy specifies a minimum value; the planned UKC must never fall below this value. If it is insufficient, the speed is reduced (squat decreases), the tide window is moved or the route is changed.

Squat, hızın karesiyle yaklaşık orantılı.en: Squat increases approximately with the square of the speed; therefore halving the speed reduces squat to about one quarter. Squat is much more severe in narrow channels with a high blockage factor. The Second Officer sets the planned speed in critical UKC areas accordingly.

Trim by head durumunda squat baş tarafta.en: When the ship is trimmed by the head, squat increases at the bow; when trimmed by the stern, it increases at the stern. The plan must anticipate at which point the least clearance will remain by assessing the ship's trim and the trim effect of squat together.

ECDIS, rota planlandıktan sonra otomatik.en: After the route has been planned, ECDIS runs an automatic "route check" and lists the points where the route crosses the safety contour, passes through a no-go area or enters navigational warnings. The Second Officer reviews this list item by item; each warning is either cleared by changing the route or documented with its justification (e.g. acceptable within a channel).

XTD (Cross Track Distance) limitleri her.en: XTD (Cross Track Distance) limits are set for each leg; if the ship leaves this corridor, ECDIS gives an alarm. T&P notices and temporary dangers are entered in the manual update layer.

ECDIS-only gemilerde yedek, genelde ikin.en: On ECDIS-only ships, the backup is usually a second, independent ECDIS (separate power supply, separate position input). On ships with a paper backup, the critical charts are kept up to date. The Second Officer verifies that the backup system actually works and is up to date; otherwise, if the primary system fails, the ship is left without a means of navigation.

Plan, hem dijital hem fiziksel ortamda t.en: The plan must be consistent in both digital and physical form; the waypoint list, abort points and contingency points must be the same in both.

Tamamlanan plan kaptana sunulur; kaptan.en: The completed plan is presented to the Master; the plan cannot be executed until the Master has approved it (SOLAS V/34). At the briefing, the Second Officer summarizes the route, critical points, UKC margins, abort points and weather/traffic risks. The Master's instructions (e.g. criteria for calling the Master, minimum CPA) are added to the plan.

Brifing tek yönlü değildir; kaptan ve di.en: The briefing is not one-way; the Master and the other officers ask questions and test the assumptions (challenge and response). This lets the team catch a risk that one person has overlooked.

Bridge Resource Management (BRM); açık i.en: Bridge Resource Management (BRM) covers open communication, task sharing, cross-checking and a "speak up" culture. Most groundings arise from an error chain that develops because someone in the team noticed the risk but did not speak up.

İkinci Zabit, planı paylaşılan bir menta.en: By turning the plan into a shared mental model, the Second Officer ensures that the whole team sees the same picture. Even with a pilot on board, the plan is the team's reference for checking; the pilot's recommendations are assessed against the plan.

Pozisyon tek bir kaynağa (GPS) güveniler.en: The position is not taken on trust from a single source (GPS); it is cross-checked by independent methods: radar range/bearing, visual bearing, parallel indexing, confirmation of the depth with the echo sounder. Because cases of GPS spoofing/jamming are increasing, independent verification is vital.

İkinci Zabit, plana işlenmiş fix interva.en: The Second Officer keeps to the fix intervals entered in the plan (e.g. 30-60 min in the open sea, 3-6 min in restricted waters, or continuous PI). Every fix is recorded in the logbook and in ECDIS.

Gemi XTD limitini aşarsa veya UKC marjı.en: If the ship exceeds the XTD limit or the UKC margin is threatened, the officer immediately makes a corrective maneuver and, if necessary, calls the Master. If changes in weather, traffic or draft make the plan invalid, the plan is formally updated and approved again.

Vardiya devrinde plan, mevcut pozisyon,.en: At the watch handover, the plan, the current position, the critical points ahead and any special instructions are passed on clearly. An incomplete handover can break the monitoring chain and lead to an accident.

En yaygın hatalar; tarihi geçmiş harita/.en: The most common errors are using out-of-date charts/publications, setting the ECDIS safety settings incorrectly, incomplete UKC/squat calculation, not determining an abort point, and a plan that stays on paper and is not owned by the team.

Bir diğer hata, GPS pozisyonuna körü kör.en: Another error is to trust the GPS position blindly and neglect independent verification. Ignoring the ENC scale/CATZOC reliability is also dangerous.

Royal Majesty (1995): GPS anten arızası.en: Royal Majesty (1995): the GPS antenna failure went unnoticed, the ship deviated from the planned track for hours and ran aground. Lesson: do not rely on a single position source; cross-check with the depth and with independent fixes.

Muros (2016): ECDIS'te yanlış safety con.en: Muros (2016): with an incorrect safety contour on ECDIS and an inadequate route check, the ship ran aground on a shoal. Lesson: the ECDIS settings must be verified for the ship, and the route check output must be reviewed.

İyi bir passage plan, geminin karaya otu.en: A good passage plan is the first and strongest line of defense against grounding. The Second Officer's job is not only to prepare the plan but to make it a living document that is understood by the team, updated for weather and conditions, and cross-checked on every watch. Disciplined planning is the only practice that breaks, right at the start, the "human error" chain that keeps recurring in accident statistics.

SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 27, geminin y.en: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 27 requires the ship to carry adequate and up-to-date nautical charts and publications for the intended voyage. Being up to date means having been corrected in accordance with the latest published Notices to Mariners; "adequate" means charts of a resolution and scale that cover all areas from the start to the end of the voyage.

Regulation 19, taşınacak seyir cihazları.en: Regulation 19 defines the navigational equipment to be carried and the ECDIS requirement. ECDIS can replace paper charts when it is supplied with approved ENCs and used together with an appropriate back-up arrangement. The Second Officer must know clearly whether the ship operates "ECDIS-only" or "paper-backed" and how this affects the correction workflow.

Yayınlar (publications) da bu kapsamdadı.en: Publications are covered as well: Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List of Lights, List of Radio Signals, Tide Tables, Tidal Stream Atlases, The Mariner's Handbook (NP100) and Admiralty Tide Tables (ATT). If these are uncorrected or out of date, this is recorded as a deficiency in a PSC inspection.

İkinci Zabit, harita ve yayın yönetimini.en: The Second Officer is the day-to-day operator of chart and publication management: applying corrections, keeping the records, managing the folios and reporting missing items to the Master. However, the ultimate responsibility for navigational safety rests with the Master; for this reason, critical corrections (e.g. a new danger) are passed on at a briefing.

Sorumluluk, sadece \"damga vurmak\" deği.en: The responsibility is not just "stamping". This role also has to ensure that each correction is entered on the right chart, at the right position and with the right symbol, that the ENC database contains all the cells for the voyage concerned, and that the update status is 100%.

Admiralty Notices to Mariners (NtM) haft.en: Admiralty Notices to Mariners (NtM) are published weekly, and each week's edition contains numbered notices. The notices are grouped into permanent corrections, Temporary (T) and Preliminary (P) notices, summaries of NAVAREA warnings, announcements of new charts/publications, and block corrections.

Kalıcı düzeltmeler haritanın üzerine mür.en: Permanent corrections are entered on the chart in ink and remain in force. T notices report a temporary situation (e.g. a navigation light temporarily extinguished, a temporary buoy), while P notices give advance information on something that will soon become permanent (e.g. a new berth under construction). T&Ps are entered in pencil because they must be erased when they are canceled.

Her haftalık baskı, o hafta etkilenen ha.en: Each weekly edition gives the list of charts affected that week (chart index) and the texts of the corrections. The Second Officer compares this list with the charts in the ship's folio and selects and applies only the relevant corrections.

Düzeltme, kronolojik sırayla ve hiçbir h.en: Corrections are made in chronological order without skipping any week, because a later correction may build on an earlier one. The Second Officer first scans the incoming weekly edition through Section II "Charts", identifies the folio charts affected and enters each one in the chart correction log.

İş akışı genelde şöyledir: haftalık NtM.en: The workflow is usually as follows: the weekly NtM is downloaded as a PDF/online, the ship's chart maintenance record (NP133A or electronic equivalent) is opened, the relevant chart numbers are matched, the corrections are entered on the charts, the last correction number is written in the bottom left-hand corner of the chart and the log is signed.

Geride kalan düzeltmeler için UKHO'nun c.en: For outstanding corrections, the UKHO cumulative/back-correction services (e.g. Annual Summary, NP234 NtM cumulative list) are used; in this way a chart that has not been corrected for a long time can be brought up to date quickly by seeing which notices are missing.

Kalıcı düzeltmeler standart hidrografik.en: Permanent corrections are entered using the standard hydrographic symbols (with reference to INT1 / NP5011 "Symbols and Abbreviations used on Admiralty Charts"). Violet (or black) fine-point ink is used; erasures or smudges are not acceptable, because the chart is a legal document.

Karmaşık değişiklikler için tracing (ase.en: For complex changes, the tracing technique (acetate copy) is used: the tracing attached to the NtM is aligned with reference points on the chart (e.g. a lat/long intersection or a prominent light), and the new symbols are transferred to the chart by pressing through with a pencil. This is the most reliable method of avoiding position errors.

Düzeltme tamamlandığında haritanın sol a.en: When the correction is complete, the year and number of the notice (e.g. "2026-1542") are added to the correction line in the bottom left-hand corner of the chart. This line is the official record showing up to which correction the chart is up to date, and it is the first place looked at during a PSC check.

Bazı düzeltmeler manuel çizilemeyecek ka.en: Some corrections are too extensive to be drawn by hand; in this case the NtM issues a printed "block correction" (a self-adhesive or cut-and-paste piece of chart). The Second Officer cuts out this block carefully, positions it according to the alignment marks (register marks) and pastes it onto the chart, then enters it in the log.

Değişiklikler bir bloğun ötesine geçtiği.en: When the changes go beyond a block, the UKHO publishes a "New Edition" of the chart; the old edition becomes invalid, and the chart cannot be corrected until the new edition has been obtained. The Second Officer reports this to the Master and starts a folio renewal request.

New Edition ile \"Reprint\" farklıdır: r.en: A New Edition is different from a "Reprint": a reprint is a reissue that contains only the existing corrections and may not need any further correction, whereas a New Edition contains new navigational information and requires the old edition to be withdrawn from use.

ECDIS, IHO S-57 standardında üretilen ve.en: ECDIS works with ENC cells produced to the IHO S-57 standard and encrypted with S-63. Updates arrive through weekly ENC update services (such as the Admiralty Vessel ENC Service / AVCS) on CD-DVD or online (e-mail, broadband), and the update files for each cell (.001, .002 ...) are loaded in sequence.

İkinci Zabit, sefere ait tüm hücrelerin.en: The Second Officer verifies that all cells for the voyage are licensed (permits) and loaded and that the update status is 100%. ECDIS reports the last update date of each cell and any missing updates; in a PSC inspection, this report is the digital equivalent of the paper log.

Güncelleme sırasında \"base CD\" (taban.en: When updating, the distinction between the "base CD" (base data) and the "update CD" (weekly changes) is important: base data arrives at set intervals, updates every week. Loading in the wrong order or a missing permit results in cells not being loaded and the navigation area appearing blank.

Admiralty Information Overlay (AIO), ENC.en: The Admiralty Information Overlay (AIO) is an additional layer that can be displayed over the ENC; it shows Admiralty T&P notices not yet included in the ENC and the differences between the ENC and the paper chart (ENC Preliminary Notices, EP). In this way, ECDIS-only ships can also see the temporary dangers that are known on paper charts.

Otomatik güncellemelerin yetişmediği aci.en: For urgent situations that the automatic updates do not cover in time (e.g. a new NAVAREA warning, a danger not yet included in the ENC), points, lines, areas and text can be added with the ECDIS manual update function. The Second Officer records these manual entries with their date and source and deletes the temporary ones when they expire.

AIO'nun açık tutulması ve manuel update.en: Keeping the AIO switched on and maintaining discipline with manual updates make up, on ECDIS-only ships, for the loss of the paper T&P advantage. If this layer is left switched off, temporary dangers are missed.

Dünya, World-Wide Navigational Warning S.en: Under the World-Wide Navigational Warning Service (WWNWS), the world is divided into NAVAREAs; a coordinator for each area issues the NAVAREA warnings. Below this level come national coastal warnings and local warnings at port/VTS level. Throughout the voyage, the Second Officer follows the warnings for the NAVAREAs the ship passes through.

Uyarılar; söndürülen fenerler, sürüklene.en: Warnings report temporary/urgent dangers such as extinguished lights, drifting buoys, wrecks, military training areas, seismic survey ships and ice. This information may not yet have been included in the NtM or the ENC updates; for this reason it may need to be entered manually on the chart/ECDIS.

NAVTEX (518 kHz uluslararası İngilizce,.en: NAVTEX (518 kHz international in English, 490/4209.5 kHz national) and EGC SafetyNET (Inmarsat) are the main channels for receiving these warnings. The Second Officer filters the warnings received according to whether they are relevant to the voyage and transfers the relevant ones to the plan/chart.

Sefere ilişkin bir uyarı alındığında İki.en: When a warning relevant to the voyage is received, the Second Officer assesses its position, period of validity and nature and, if necessary, enters it on the paper chart in pencil and in ECDIS as a manual update or with reference to the AIO. When a cancellation is received, the mark is erased.

Aktif uyarıların bir listesi köprüüstünd.en: A list of active warnings is kept on the bridge; warnings that have not been canceled are considered to be in force. At the watch handover, active warnings are passed on verbally and in writing; otherwise a critical temporary danger may drop out of the monitoring chain.

Folio, geminin ticaret sahasına göre düz.en: A folio is a group of charts arranged according to the ship's trading area. The Second Officer selects from the folio the charts required for the planned voyage (passage chart, approach chart, harbor chart and suitable scales); if a scale or coverage is missing, a folio renewal request is raised.

Route-based folio yönetiminde, geminin t.en: In route-based folio management, a "standard folio" is defined for the ship's typical routes; if a new voyage goes outside this standard, additional charts are obtained. In AVCS this is handled as digital folio and cell permit management; license periods and renewal dates are monitored.

Folio yönetimi, harita \"yeterliliği\" (.en: Folio management is directly linked to chart "adequacy": in critical areas, the largest-scale (most detailed) up-to-date chart must be used, not the smallest-scale chart. The Second Officer ensures that the chart of the correct scale is available and corrected for each leg of the passage plan.

Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List o.en: Publications such as Sailing Directions (Pilot Books), List of Lights and List of Radio Signals are updated through the "Updates to Admiralty Sailing Directions / Lists" sections of the weekly NtM. These updates are entered on the relevant pages of the publication or kept as an attached sheet (supplement).

İkinci Zabit, yayın envanterini bir kayı.en: The Second Officer tracks the publication inventory in a register (publication record): the number, edition year, last correcting NtM and validity status of each publication are listed. For publications that have expired or for which a new edition has been issued, a supply request is raised.

ENC'lerde derinlik verisinin güvenilirli.en: In ENCs, the reliability of depth data is expressed by CATZOC (Category of Zone of Confidence); it is classified from A1 (most reliable) to D and U (unassessed). A low CATZOC indicates that the depths are based on old/inadequate surveys and that the water may in reality be shallower.

İkinci Zabit, passage plan'da kritik sah.en: The Second Officer checks the CATZOC value of the critical areas in the passage plan and adds an uncertainty allowance to the UKC calculation. For example, in a CATZOC C/D area a wider safety margin must be left for the same paper/ECDIS depth.

CATZOC, ECDIS'te ZOC sembolleriyle (yıld.en: CATZOC can be displayed in ECDIS with ZOC symbols (number of stars). Querying this layer creates awareness of the risk that "the chart looks right, but the data may be old"; this is vital especially in rarely navigated waters with old surveys.

ECDIS'te ENC'yi kendi derleme ölçeğinin.en: Enlarging an ENC in ECDIS beyond its own compilation scale (over-zoom / over-scale) is misleading; the data does not become visibly more detailed, only the symbols get larger, and detail that is missing is taken as not existing. ECDIS indicates this with an "over-scale" warning.

İkinci Zabit, her saha için uygun derlem.en: For each area, the Second Officer uses the ENC/paper chart with a suitable compilation scale; for approaches and maneuvering, larger-scale cells (usage band 5-6) are preferred. Using a chart of the wrong scale leads to no-go areas and dangers being missed.

Chart correction log (NP133A veya elektr.en: The chart correction log (NP133A or electronic equivalent) is the official record showing up to which NtM each chart has been corrected. Each entry contains the chart number, the notice number applied, the date and the signature/initials of the person who made the correction. In a PSC inspection, this log is the primary evidence that the charts are up to date.

ECDIS tarafında bu kanıt; güncelleme dur.en: On the ECDIS side, this evidence is the update status report, the license/permit list and the date of the last update. The Second Officer ensures that both the paper and the digital records are consistent and complete and that no corrections are outstanding.

Kayıtlar, yalnızca uyum için değil, soru.en: Records matter not only for compliance but also for responsibility: in an investigation after an accident, these logs show which correction the chart was up to date with on which date. A blank, late or backdated log is a serious weakness.

İkinci Zabit periyodik iç kontrol (self-.en: The Second Officer carries out periodic internal checks (self-audit): for randomly selected charts, the log is compared with the last correction line on the chart, and the ENC update percentage and the edition years of the publications are checked. This catches gaps proactively before a PSC inspection or a company audit.

Tespit edilen eksiklikler (eksik harita,.en: Deficiencies found (missing charts, outstanding corrections, expired publications) are reported to the Master and the company DPA, and supply requests are raised. Under the SMS (Safety Management System) this process is documented and followed up until closed.

En yaygın hatalar; hafta atlayarak veya.en: The most common errors are making corrections with weeks skipped or in the wrong order, entering T&Ps in ink (indelible), loading ENC updates incompletely or in the wrong order, leaving the AIO layer switched off and navigating on an over-scaled ENC.

Diğer hatalar; yıllık yayınların (ATT) e.en: Other errors are using an old edition of the annual publications (ATT), not having a chart of adequate scale in the folio for a critical area, trying to correct a chart for which a New Edition has been published, and not keeping the chart correction log at the same time as the corrections are made.

Düzeltme rutini sabit bir güne bağlanır.en: The correction routine is tied to a fixed day (e.g. every Friday) and kept up without interruption; the incoming edition is processed in the same week. The log is signed at the same time as each correction; after an ECDIS update has been loaded, the 100% status and the cell list are verified.

Sefer öncesi, passage plan ile folio çap.en: Before the voyage, the passage plan and the folio are cross-checked; for each leg, the chart of the correct scale, up to date and corrected, is confirmed. CATZOC and over-scale conditions are noted in the passage plan. This discipline cuts the risk of chart-related grounding right at the start.

Harita ve nautikal yayın yönetimi, seyir.en: Chart and nautical publication management is one of the invisible but most fundamental layers of navigational safety; a correct route is worthless when it is drawn on a chart that is not up to date. The Second Officer's task is not only to apply corrections but to keep all navigational information, paper and digital, complete, traceable and ready for the voyage. A correction routine carried out with discipline, promptly and completely, is the quiet but strongest defense that breaks, right at the start, the "uncorrected chart" and "unreliable source data" chain that recurs in grounding statistics.

Universal Time Coordinated (UTC), modern.en: Universal Time Coordinated (UTC) is the basis of all international time reference in modern seafaring and in practice is considered equivalent to Greenwich Mean Time (GMT). UTC is based on atomic clocks and is a continuous, fixed reference; wherever the ship is, UTC does not change. When managing clock changes, the Second Officer works on one golden rule: although ship's time (zone time) changes many times during the voyage, the UTC reference never moves.

GMDSS radyo kayıtları, distress/urgency/.en: GMDSS radio records, distress/urgency/safety messages, EGC messages and navigational warnings are always time-stamped in UTC. In this way, whatever time zone the ship is in, records can be compared worldwide on a single time axis. Although events in the deck logbook are entered in zone time, it is good seamanship practice to also note the UTC equivalent for critical events.

Astronomik seyirde (celestial navigation.en: In celestial navigation, all observations are timed in UTC, because the Greenwich Hour Angle (GHA) and declination values in the Nautical Almanac are based on UTC. Since even an error of seconds causes a position error of the order of a nautical mile, the accuracy of the chronometer and of the UTC reference is vital.

Local Mean Time (LMT), belirli bir boyla.en: Local Mean Time (LMT) is the mean solar time at a given meridian; it changes by 4 minutes for each degree of longitude (360° / 24 hours = 15°/hour = 4 minutes/degree). LMT is used for sunrise/sunset, twilight and moon observations. When planning star sights for night navigation, the Second Officer works from LMT, because twilight times depend on longitude.

Zone time ise idari kolaylık için 15° ge.en: Zone time, on the other hand, is time based on standard time zones 15° wide for administrative convenience, linked to UTC by whole-hour differences. Ship's time is usually kept as zone time, so that a whole-hour difference from UTC is used instead of fractions in minutes. The difference between LMT and zone time can reach at most half an hour (about 7.5°), depending on how far the ship is from the central meridian of the zone.

Dünya, Greenwich'i (0° boylam) merkez al.en: The world is divided into 24 standard time zones centered on Greenwich (0° longitude); each zone is 15° wide and differs from UTC by a whole hour. The Zone Description (ZD) shows the sign and value that must be applied to ship's time in that zone to obtain UTC. In east longitude the ZD is negative (e.g. ZD −5), in west longitude it is positive (e.g. ZD +5); the rule is: "in east longitude, zone time is ahead of UTC".

ZD'yi hesaplamak için boylam 15'e bölünü.en: To calculate the ZD, the longitude is divided by 15 and rounded to the nearest whole number. For example, 67° W divided by 15 gives 4.47; since the nearest whole number is 4, the ZD is +4. The zero zone centered on Greenwich covers ±7.5°; the boundary zones (±172.5° to 180°) are half zones and meet at the date line.

İkinci Zabit, gemi saatini ZD esas alara.en: The Second Officer sets ship's time on the basis of the ZD. When going from UTC to zone time, the ZD is added in east longitude and subtracted in west longitude (Zone Time = UTC − ZD, with the signed ZD). This mechanical consistency ensures that the clock change plan is made in the right direction and by the right amount.

Zone time tamamen coğrafi 15°'lik diliml.en: While zone time is based purely on geographical 15° zones, the legal standard time of a country (standard / legal time) is set according to administrative boundaries and usually does not coincide exactly with the 15° zones. Some countries use a single time zone (e.g. China is run on a single ZD), while others apply half-hour (e.g. India UTC+5:30) or quarter-hour (e.g. Nepal UTC+5:45) offsets.

Yaz saati uygulaması (Daylight Saving Ti.en: Daylight Saving Time (Summer Time) moves standard time forward by one hour according to the season. For the port approach and the ETA calculation, the Second Officer must work from the legal time in force at the port rather than the ship's zone time; otherwise the pilot station appointment, the VTS reporting time or the start of the cargo operation will be out by one or more hours.

Gemi doğuya doğru seyrederken boylam art.en: When the ship is steaming east, longitude increases (towards E), and zone time must be advanced by one hour for every 15° crossed (advance / put clocks forward). In this case the ship "loses time": the day has 23 hours instead of 24, and the time available to the crew that day is one hour shorter. For this reason, rest-hour planning is more delicate on eastbound voyages.

Saat ileri alındığında, ileri atlanan sa.en: When the clocks are advanced, the skipped hour is not actually "lived"; for example, if ship's time is put forward from 02:00 to 03:00, the period 02:00–03:00 is lost for that day. The Second Officer arranges the watch schedule and the rest periods accordingly; the advanced hour must not be applied in a way that shortens the watch concerned by one hour or squeezes a crew member's rest period.

Gemi batıya doğru seyrederken boylam aza.en: When the ship is steaming west, longitude decreases (towards W), and zone time must be put back by one hour for every 15° crossed (retard / put clocks back). In this case the ship "gains time": the day has 25 hours instead of 24. Westbound voyages are easier in terms of rest hours, because an extra hour is created.

Saat geri alındığında, geri alınan saat.en: When the clocks are retarded, the hour that is put back is lived twice; for example, if ship's time is put back from 03:00 to 02:00, the period 02:00–03:00 is passed through twice. This must be stated clearly in the deck logbook, and a note made for the second pass, so that events in the repeated hour are not confused. The Second Officer usually distributes the gained hour among the night watches to improve rest.

Uzun bir okyanus geçişinde gemi birden ç.en: On a long ocean passage the ship crosses several time zones; for example, a ship crossing the Atlantic westbound may build up a total difference of 5–6 hours. Applying this difference all at once seriously disrupts both the watch routine and rest. The Second Officer spreads the total difference over the days of the voyage and plans a change of no more than one hour per day.

Saat değişimi, mürettebatın en az etkile.en: So that the crew is affected as little as possible, the clock change is usually split between the night watches (00:00–04:00 and 04:00–08:00). A common practice is to divide a one-hour change into two half-hours over two night watches; for example, half an hour in the 00–04 watch and half an hour in the 04–08 watch. In this way no single watchkeeper carries the whole burden, and the rest periods are preserved in a more balanced way.

Saat değişim planı yazılı hazırlanır ve.en: The clock change plan is prepared in writing and submitted to the Master for approval. The plan states clearly the amount of change for each day (e.g. +30 min × 2 watches), on which night and over which watches it will be distributed, the ZD of the new ship's time relative to UTC, and when it will be announced to the crew.

Saat değişim planı, gemi saatinin varış.en: The clock change plan is calculated backwards so that, at the end of the voyage, ship's time matches the legal time of the arrival port exactly. The Second Officer establishes the standard time of the arrival port (including DST), finds the total difference from the current ship's time and divides it over the remaining days of the voyage. In this way, when the ship arrives in port, the crew's body clock is close to port time and the ETA and operation times are consistent.

Eğer varış limanı zone time'dan farklı y.en: If the arrival port uses a half-hour legal time that differs from zone time (e.g. UTC+5:30), the last change is made with a half-hour correction. The pilot station ETA, VTS reporting and cargo readiness times are always reported in the port's legal time; they must not be confused with the shipboard zone time.

MLC 2006 Standard A2.3 ve STCW Code A-VI.en: MLC 2006 Standard A2.3 and the STCW Code A-VIII/1 set two basic limits for seafarers' rest hours: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and at least 77 hours of rest in any 7-day period. The 10 hours of rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted; the interval between two consecutive rest periods must not exceed 14 hours.

Saat değişimi bu limitleri doğrudan etki.en: Clock changes directly affect these limits, because rest hours are calculated not on the basis of "actual elapsed time" but from records kept in ship's time. When the clocks are advanced on an eastbound passage and the 24-hour window is effectively reduced to 23 hours, it becomes harder for a crew member to complete 10 hours of rest in that window. The Second Officer must anticipate this squeeze in the plan and distribute the change so that the rest periods are protected.

Dinlenme saati kayıtları (IMO/ILO format.en: Rest-hour records (Records of Rest in the IMO/ILO format) are kept in ship's time. On days with a clock change, the record form must state clearly that the day had 23 or 25 hours instead of 24; otherwise the rest totals will look inconsistent at an inspection. For the day of the change, the Second Officer enters the direction and amount of the clock change as a footnote on the record form.

Bazı şirketler ve ekipler, dinlenme hesa.en: Some companies and crews check rest on clock-change days on a UTC basis, to make sure the rest-hour calculations are correct. When preparing the plan, the Second Officer verifies on the schedule that every watchkeeper still has 10 hours of rest in 24 hours after the change; if there is a clash, the change must be moved to another watch or split over two days.

SOLAS V/28, seyirle ilgili tüm faaliyetl.en: SOLAS V/28 makes it mandatory to record all navigational activities and incidents; a clock change is also a navigational event that must be recorded. The Second Officer enters the clock change in the deck logbook with these elements: the moment of the change (old ship's time and new ship's time), the amount and direction of the change (e.g. "Clocks retarded 30 min"), the new zone description and the reference of the Master's approval.

Saat geri alındığında (retard) aynı saat.en: When the clocks are retarded, the same hour is passed through twice, so a note such as "2nd time" is made against the second pass, or the UTC equivalent is written, to avoid confusion in the log entries. When the clocks are advanced, no blank line is left for the skipped hour; the entries continue without a break and the line of the change is clearly marked.

GMDSS radyo kaydı (radio log), distress/.en: The GMDSS radio log, distress/urgency/safety communications and test records are always kept in UTC and are not affected by clock changes. This is critical so that, in investigations after an accident, the timeline can be built correctly on a single reference axis. The Second Officer or the person responsible for GMDSS ensures that the UTC axis of the radio log runs without interruption, however many times the ship's zone time changes.

Köprüüstündeki saatlerden en az biri (ma.en: At least one of the clocks on the bridge (master clock or GMDSS console clock) must be kept set to show UTC at all times; the other clocks show zone time. NAVTEX and SafetyNET messages from the EGC receiver are time-stamped in UTC; assessing them against UTC rather than ship's time is necessary for interpreting the validity windows of navigational warnings correctly.

Pratikte hat 180° boylamını birebir izle.en: In practice the line does not follow the 180° meridian exactly; it zigzags because of the administrative choices of countries (e.g. there are deviations for Kiribati and some Pacific islands). On Pacific crossings, the Second Officer confirms from ALRS and the almanac exactly where the line crosses the ship's route, because the date change is a separate, additional step from the clock change.

Tarih hattı geçişinde seyir defterine ta.en: When crossing the date line, the date change is entered clearly in the deck logbook: "Crossed International Date Line, date advanced/retarded by one day". Because skipping or repeating a day can cause confusion in the rest-hour records and in pay/working-day calculations, the records are cross-checked against the UTC axis.

Tarih hattı geçişi GMDSS UTC kaydını etk.en: Crossing the date line does not affect the GMDSS UTC record, because UTC is continuous; only the ship's date is affected. The Second Officer treats the line crossing as an item separate from the clock change plan; if the date change and a required zone time change fall on the same day, each of them is documented separately in the logbook.

Saat değişimi, onaylandıktan sonra tüm g.en: Once approved, the clock change must be announced to the whole ship; otherwise confusion arises on the bridge, in the engine room and in the catering department. The common practice is to announce the direction, amount and time of the change with a "Notice to Crew" on the previous day or on the morning of the change. The notice is posted in the mess room and on the notice boards, and is also entered in the bridge night order book.

Duyuru özellikle vardiya devri için krit.en: The announcement is particularly critical for the watch handover; when the clocks are put forward or back, the relieving officer must know the new ship's time and the engine room must update its watch schedule. The Second Officer coordinates the change so that it is applied by all departments at the same time; setting all the clocks on board (bridge, engine room, cabins) at the same time is good practice.

Kaptanın night order book'una saat değiş.en: The clock change is written clearly in the Master's night order book: in which watch, by how many minutes and in which direction. The night watchkeeper applies the change on the bridge clock and enters it in the deck logbook. At the briefing, the Second Officer tells the officer on the night watch clearly how and when the change is to be made.

Vardiya devrinde devreden zabit, saat de.en: At the watch handover, the officer being relieved has the relieving officer confirm whether the clock change has been made and what the new ship's time is. A clock change that is missed or applied twice (e.g. two watchkeepers both making the same change) corrupts both the time record and the rest-hour calculation; for this reason, at handover there must be a single, clear verification that the change has been applied.

ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival), liman,.en: The ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) is binding information for the port, the agent, VTS and the charterer, and the time reference in which it is given must always be stated. The Second Officer usually calculates the ETA in UTC (from distance/speed) and then converts it to the legal time of the arrival port when reporting it. To avoid confusion, a dual presentation in reports such as "ETA pilot station 0600 LT (0030 UTC)" is good practice.

Sefer boyunca biriken saat değişimleri E.en: The clock changes accumulated during the voyage have no indirect effect on the ETA, because the ETA is calculated on a UTC basis; however, if the ship's zone time has not yet been synchronized with port time as the ship approaches the port, time discrepancies can arise in onboard planning. For this reason, the clock change plan must be completed so that ship's time is brought to port time before arrival.

En yaygın hatalar; saat değişiminin yanl.en: The most common errors are making the clock change in the wrong direction (such as retarding the clocks when steaming east), loading the change onto one person so that rest hours are violated, not entering it in the logbook, and mistakenly converting the GMDSS log to zone time. Another error is to confuse the date line crossing with a clock change and skip the date correction.

Önlem olarak İkinci Zabit; her sefer baş.en: As a precaution, at the start of each voyage the Second Officer calculates the total time difference and its direction, divides the change over the days, obtains the Master's approval, announces it to the crew and enters every change consistently in the logbook and the rest records. Keeping the UTC reference fixed and noting the UTC equivalent in critical records prevents the great majority of errors from the outset.

Saat değişimi yönetimi, denizci dinlenme.en: Managing clock changes is a task that looks simple but has a high margin for error, because it affects seafarers' rest, record integrity and operational timing at the same time. The Second Officer's job is not just to put the clocks forward or back; it is to run a disciplined process that protects the MLC 2006 rest limits and does not break the continuity of the navigational record, by keeping the UTC reference fixed, distributing the change fairly and documenting every change consistently. A well-planned clock change both reduces fatigue-related errors by the crew and presents a flawless chain of records in PSC inspections and company audits.

TRS, sıcak tropikal denizler üzerinde ge.en: A TRS is a violent system with a low-pressure center and closed circulation that develops over warm tropical seas. In the Northern Hemisphere it rotates counterclockwise, in the Southern Hemisphere clockwise. Wind and sea increase rapidly towards the center; the eyewall around the eye is the most destructive zone.

Barometredeki kararlı düşüş, uzun periyo.en: A steady fall of the barometer, long-period swell, unusual cloud systems and wind that departs from the normal pattern are the classic signs of an approaching TRS. The Second Officer combines instrumental data (official warnings) with these natural signs.

İkinci Zabit; ilgili RSMC/uyarı merkezle.en: The Second Officer monitors the relevant RSMCs/warning centers (JMA, NHC, JTWC, etc.), NAVTEX/EGC messages and weather fax/GMDSS bulletins. Each warning gives the position of the center, the pressure, the maximum wind, the direction/speed of movement and the forecast cones. The position and the forecast are updated continuously.

Fırtınanın ilerleme yönüne göre bir tara.en: Relative to the storm's direction of travel, one side is the "dangerous semicircle" and the other the "navigable semicircle". In the dangerous semicircle the wind pushes the ship towards the storm track, whereas in the navigable semicircle it pushes the ship away from it. In the Northern Hemisphere, the right-hand side relative to the direction of travel is the dangerous semicircle.

Geleneksel kural; tehlikeli yarımdaysanı.en: The traditional rule is: if you are in the dangerous semicircle, keep the wind on the starboard bow (in the Northern Hemisphere) and move away from the center; if you are in the navigable semicircle, bring the wind on the quarter and pass through quickly. The aim is always to stay as far as possible from the center and from the forecast track.

Tahmin yörüngesi belirsizlik taşır; bu y.en: The forecast track carries uncertainty; for this reason, with approaches such as the "1-2-3 rule", safety radii (e.g. 100/200/300 NM) are added around the 24/48/72-hour forecast positions, and the ship tries to stay outside these "limit lines". This gives a buffer against unexpected turns of the storm.

İkinci Zabit, analizini (merkez konumu,.en: The Second Officer presents the analysis (position of the center, movement, semicircle, limit lines, alternative routes) clearly to the Master. The options may be altering course, adjusting speed, seeking shelter or waiting. The final decision rests with the Master; if a weather routing service is available, its recommendation is also considered.

Kaçınma her zaman tam mümkün olmayabilir.en: Avoidance may not always be fully possible; when heavy seas are expected, lashing/securing is checked, movable equipment is secured, watertight closures are made and the crew is briefed. The risk of parametric rolling and synchronous rolling is managed by adjusting speed/course.

Tropikal fırtına kaçınması, denizcilik a.en: Tropical storm avoidance is maritime analysis in its purest form: reading the data, respecting uncertainty and making early, cautious decisions. The Second Officer's careful monitoring and clear analysis enable the Master to keep the ship away from the destructive core of the storm.

SOLAS V, seferin tamamını kapsayan, günc.en: SOLAS V requires the ship to carry official charts that cover the whole voyage, are up to date and are of adequate scale. On ships using ECDIS, this is achieved by subscribing to an official ENC service (UKHO ADMIRALTY, NOAA, Primar, etc.) and updating regularly. The Second Officer is the person actually responsible for keeping them up to date.

ENC (vektör) veri, ECDIS'in alarm/uyarı.en: ENC (vector) data makes full use of the alarm/warning capabilities of ECDIS (safety contour, anti-grounding). The Second Officer verifies that ENC coverage at suitable scales (folio) is complete along the route; a missing cell means that the safety functions will not work in that area.

Resmi ENC güncellemeleri (weekly update).en: Official ENC updates (weekly update) are received online or on media and loaded into ECDIS. The Second Officer verifies that the update has been applied successfully, that the cell status is "up to date" and that the digital certificates/licenses remain valid. The update dates are recorded.

ENC lisansları süreli ve hücre/folio baz.en: ENC licenses are time-limited and based on cells/folios. The Second Officer checks in advance that the cells required for the voyage plan are licensed; expired or missing licenses are renewed/added in time, otherwise "no permit" gaps appear along the route.

T&P notları; geçici (örn. tatbikat sahas.en: T&P notices contain temporary information (e.g. a training area, a temporary buoy) or advance information that has not yet become a permanent correction. Although the ENC updates include some of them, those not covered are entered by hand in the ECDIS Manual Update (Manual Correction) layer. The Second Officer assesses the effect of these notices on the route.

Elle yapılan düzeltmeler ECDIS'te kayıt.en: Corrections made by hand are recorded in ECDIS, and which notice has been entered is tracked. At an inspection, this record is the evidence that the charts have really been kept up to date.

ECDIS'in birincil sistem arızasına karşı.en: ECDIS must have a suitable backup against failure of the primary system: a second, independent (separate power/data) approved ECDIS or a suitable paper chart backup. The Second Officer ensures that the backup is operational and up to date; otherwise a single failure leaves the ship without charts.

Safety contour, safety depth ve alarm ay.en: Correct configuration of the safety contour, safety depth and alarm settings is critical for safe navigation. The ECDIS software version and the ENC Presentation Library must also be up to date; an old version may display some new symbols incorrectly.

PSC ve vetting, ENC güncelliğini, lisans.en: PSC and vetting inspections check ENC status, the license situation, T&P handling and the backup arrangement. The Second Officer keeps the update records, cell status reports and manual correction records in order and ready to present. Missing chart updates are a frequent PSC finding.

ECDIS güncelliği, görünmeyen ama hayati.en: Keeping ECDIS up to date is an invisible but vital discipline; a single out-of-date cell or an unapplied T&P can hide a real danger behind a screen that looks correct. The Second Officer's regular update cycle is the foundation of reliable electronic navigation.

GMDSS, gemiyi tek bir cihaza değil dokuz.en: GMDSS equips the ship not around a single device but according to nine basic communication functions: ship-to-shore distress alerting, shore-to-ship distress alerting, ship-to-ship distress alerting, SAR coordinating communications, on-scene communications, locating signals (SART/RADAR transponder), broadcast of Maritime Safety Information (MSI), general communications and bridge-to-bridge communications. The Second Officer verifies that the equipment on board provides all of these functions.

Deniz bölgeleri, kıyı istasyonlarının ka.en: Sea areas are defined according to the coverage range of coast stations and satellite access. A1 is the area within continuous alerting coverage of at least one VHF DSC coast station (about 20-30 NM); A2 is MF DSC coverage (about 100-150 NM); A3 is Inmarsat geostationary satellite coverage (about 70°N-70°S); A4 is the entire area outside these, including the polar regions (HF DSC mandatory).

İkinci Zabit, sefer rotasının hangi bölg.en: The Second Officer must know which sea areas the voyage route passes through and verify the equipment and reserve power requirements accordingly. For example, a ship going into A4 (polar voyage) cannot rely on Inmarsat alone; HF DSC and MSI reception must be operational.

DSC, her geminin benzersiz 9 haneli MMSI.en: DSC is a digital calling system in which every ship is identified by its unique 9-digit MMSI (Maritime Mobile Service Identity). There are distress, urgency, safety and routine call types. A distress alert is sent with a single button (the red distress button under a protective cover); the ship's position, the MMSI and, if possible, the nature of distress (fire, sinking, collision, etc.) are transmitted automatically.

DSC distress alert'in en kritik verisi p.en: The most critical item of data in a DSC distress alert is the position. If the equipment is not connected to a GNSS (GPS) receiver or the connection is lost, the position must be entered manually and updated regularly; otherwise the distress alert will transmit an old/wrong position. The Second Officer checks that the GNSS interface is working and that the position time stamp is current.

Manuel pozisyon girilen cihazlarda en ge.en: On equipment where the position is entered manually, the position must be updated at least every 4 hours. In A2/A4 areas, this is a point that is often skipped in practice on MF/HF DSC equipment but is questioned at inspections.

VHF DSC controller, her gün dahili self-.en: The VHF DSC controller is checked every day with the built-in self-test (internal test). This test checks the transmit/receive modules of the equipment without an actual transmission and shows the result on the display/in the log. The Second Officer carries out the test and records the result in the GMDSS Radio Log with the date/time (UTC).

Channel 70 (DSC kanalı) sürekli dinleme.en: Channel 70 (the DSC channel) must be in continuous watch mode; this channel is not for voice communication but only for DSC alerting. CH16 is monitored as the voice distress and calling channel.

İkinci Zabit, portable VHF'lerin aylık o.en: The Second Officer carries out the monthly operational test of the portable VHFs, monitors the expiry date of the primary batteries and keeps the sets accessible near the boat station.

MF/HF DSC cihazları da günlük dahili tes.en: MF/HF DSC equipment also requires a daily internal test. The distress and safety frequencies (2187.5 kHz MF DSC, 8414.5 kHz and the other HF DSC bands) are monitored continuously in scan/watch mode. The Second Officer verifies that the scanning receiver scans the correct set of frequencies.

HF, A4 bölgesinde tek güvenilir uzun men.en: In sea area A4, HF is the only reliable long-range alerting method; on polar voyages outside satellite coverage, the distress alerting function is lost if HF DSC is not kept operational.

MF/HF performansı büyük ölçüde anten ve.en: MF/HF performance depends largely on the integrity of the antenna and the earthing (earth/ground). The Second Officer visually checks the tension of the antenna wires, salt/dirt build-up on the insulators, the antenna tuner connections and the earth connection. Corrosion or a loose connection reduces transmit power dramatically.

Whip ve wire antenlerde fiziksel hasar (.en: If physical damage (a break, a cracked insulator) is found on whip or wire antennas, it is reported and repaired immediately. An antenna fault is usually a silent danger of the "you think the alert has gone out, but it does not get through" type.

Internal test cihazın iç devrelerini kon.en: The internal test checks the internal circuits of the equipment; a weekly DSC test call is made to verify the actual transmit and receive chain. The MF/HF DSC sends a routine test call to a coast station and waits for an automatic acknowledgement (ACK). Receiving the ACK proves that the whole chain, including the antenna, is working.

VHF DSC test call ise başka bir gemiye v.en: A VHF DSC test call can be made to another ship or to a coast station. The Second Officer enters the date/time of the test call, the station called and the result (ACK received/not received) in the GMDSS Radio Log. If no ACK is received, the fault is investigated and reported to the technical service.

Test call yalnız test/routine amaçlı ve.en: Test calls are made only for test/routine purposes and in the proper way; any action that could block distress-priority traffic or be mistaken for a distress alert is avoided. The Second Officer confirms that the "test" mode of the equipment has been selected correctly and that the real distress button has not been activated by accident.

Test call'lar ITU prosedürlerine ve kıyı.en: Test calls are made in accordance with ITU procedures and the test protocol accepted by the coast station (as listed in ALRS). Some coast stations give an automatic ACK while others reply manually; the correct station and frequency are selected using ALRS NP286.

EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Rad.en: The EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon) is a life-saving device that floats free automatically (with a hydrostatic release) when the ship sinks and transmits a distress signal and a coded identity (Hex ID) on 406 MHz to the Cospas-Sarsat satellites. The Second Officer checks the monthly self-test, the hydrostatic release expiry date, the EPIRB battery expiry and the bracket mounting.

EPIRB Hex ID, ülke SAR otoritesinin veri.en: The EPIRB Hex ID must be registered in the database of the national SAR authority (e.g. the national beacon registry), and the ship's details (name, MMSI, contact) must be kept up to date. If the registration is not up to date, the SAR response is delayed.

SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), ra.en: A SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) is either a radar SART or an AIS-SART. A radar SART responds to the 9 GHz radar of a searching ship and produces a line of 12 dots (blip line) on the PPI display. An AIS-SART transmits its position as an AIS target. The Second Officer carries out the monthly self-test and monitors the battery expiry.

Survival craft'ta erişilebilir, can fili.en: It is kept accessible for survival craft and in a form that allows it to be mounted high in the lifeboat; its range depends on its height. During testing, a short, controlled self-test is carried out so as not to mislead real SAR units in the vicinity.

NAVTEX, 518 kHz (uluslararası İngilizce).en: NAVTEX broadcasts navigational warnings, weather reports and SAR information by NAVAREA/METAREA on 518 kHz (international, in English), 490 kHz (national language) and 4209.5 kHz (tropical). The Second Officer verifies that the correct NAVAREA stations and message categories (A=navigational, B=met warning, D=SAR, etc.) are selected.

Kritik kategoriler (A, B, D, L) reddedil.en: The critical categories (A, B, D, L) are non-rejectable; they cannot be switched off. The Second Officer makes sure that the bridge team sees the NAVTEX printer/display output and that important warnings are reflected in the passage plan.

A3/A4 bölgelerinde NAVTEX kapsamı dışınd.en: In sea areas A3/A4, outside NAVTEX coverage, MSI is received through Inmarsat EGC (Enhanced Group Call) / SafetyNET. The Second Officer checks that the EGC receiver is subscribed (programmed) to the correct NAVAREA and coastal areas and that the ocean region selected is consistent with the ship's position.

Inmarsat terminalinin (FleetBroadband vb.en: Commissioning of the Inmarsat terminal (FleetBroadband, etc.), its subscription status and the distress priority test are also items the Second Officer must monitor. The procedure for sending a distress alert via Inmarsat must be clearly accessible from the terminal menu.

İkinci Zabit, reserve battery'nin haftal.en: The Second Officer follows the weekly voltage check (hydrometer/voltmeter), the monthly measurements and the annual capacity (discharge) test of the reserve battery. The battery cells are checked for corrosion, electrolyte level (if lead-acid) and ventilation.

Battery charger'ın çalıştığı ve aküyü ta.en: It is verified that the battery charger is working and keeping the batteries fully charged. Automatic (uninterrupted) changeover to the reserve battery when main power is lost is tested; during the changeover, the equipment must not reset and the listening watch must not be interrupted.

İkinci Zabit, akü değişim/servis tarihle.en: The Second Officer tracks the battery replacement/service dates and the date of the next annual capacity test in a planning table. An aging battery can put the GMDSS out of action at the worst possible moment (a real blackout).

GMDSS Radio Log (Radio Record), zorunlu.en: The GMDSS Radio Log (Radio Record) is a mandatory ship's document. A summary of distress, urgency and safety communications, the daily/weekly/monthly test results, the reserve battery status, equipment failures and repairs, and the operator signatures (designated operator and Master's approval) are entered in it.

İkinci Zabit, log'u zamanında ve eksiksi.en: The Second Officer keeps the log on time and complete. The most frequent PSC finding is tests that have been carried out but not entered in the log; at an inspection, "done but not recorded" counts as "not done".

GMDSS teçhizatını işletmek için geçerli.en: Operating GMDSS equipment requires a valid GMDSS operator certificate (GOC — General Operator's Certificate, or ROC depending on the sea area). The Second Officer must hold this certificate and be fully familiar with the distress traffic procedures (alert, acknowledge, relay).

Distress alert alındığında doğru eylem z.en: When a distress alert is received, the correct chain of actions is critical: the alert is confirmed, coordination is made with the MRCC and, if necessary, a distress relay is sent. A wrong procedure can cause loss of life; for this reason the bridge team carries out periodic GMDSS drills.

GMDSS, gemi battığı an \"çalışmazsa hiç.en: GMDSS is a system that "is meaningless if it does not work" at the moment the ship sinks; this is why its value stays invisible as long as it is never used. The Second Officer's task is not only to test the equipment but to make sure that every test proves the real transmission chain, that the power supplies will hold up in a blackout and that the records will be complete at an inspection. Disciplined GMDSS routines are the only guarantee that, at the worst moment, the distress signal actually reaches the other side.

SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 5, akit devle.en: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 5 obliges Contracting Governments to provide weather warnings, synoptic analyses and forecasts, and ships to receive and assess this information. The Second Officer ensures that the gale/storm warnings issued for the METAREA the ship is in are received and passed to the bridge.

Regulation 31/32 ise gemi kaptanına, tro.en: Regulations 31/32 place on the Master the obligation to report dangers such as tropical storms, dangerous ice, sub-freezing air temperatures and winds of Beaufort 10 or above to ships in the vicinity and to the authorities (danger message). The Second Officer prepares the necessary observations and reports.

Her gemi hava koşullarına farklı tepki v.en: Every ship responds differently to weather conditions; a container ship is more susceptible to parametric rolling, a bulk carrier to deck flooding, a tanker to green water, and a ro-ro to list and cargo shift. The Second Officer knows the thresholds for wind, wave height (Hs), wave period and swell direction set by the company/for the ship type and interprets the forecasts against these thresholds.

Wave encounter period ile geminin natura.en: Coincidence (resonance) of the wave encounter period with the ship's natural roll period is dangerous. The Second Officer prepares a recommendation by assessing which heading/speed combination avoids resonance for the given swell direction and period.

NAVTEX (518/490/4209.5 kHz), kıyıya yakı.en: NAVTEX (518/490/4209.5 kHz) broadcasts gale warnings, storm warnings and forecasts for areas near the coast (category B = met warning, E = met forecast). In the open sea, outside NAVTEX coverage, Inmarsat EGC/SafetyNET provides the same METAREA information. The Second Officer verifies that both sources are programmed for the correct area.

Mesajlar genelde standart bir yapı izler.en: Messages usually follow a standard structure: warning type, area affected, position/movement of the system, expected wind and sea state. The Second Officer transfers these messages to the passage plan and passes the critical ones to the Master and the officers of the watch.

Weather fax (HF radyofaks), sinoptik yüz.en: Weather fax (HF radiofacsimile) provides synoptic surface analyses, 24/48/72/96-hour forecast charts, wave (wave height/period) charts and ice charts. In addition, modern ships also use commercial weather routing services (shore-based) and GRIB-based numerical forecasts.

İkinci Zabit, farklı kaynakların tutarlı.en: The Second Officer cross-checks the consistency of the different sources; if two independent forecasts show the same system in different positions, planning is based on the more cautious (worse) scenario. Relying blindly on a single source is dangerous.

Sinoptik yüzey haritasında izobarlar (eş.en: On a synoptic surface chart, isobars (lines of equal pressure) show the pressure systems and the wind distribution. Closely spaced isobars (an increased pressure gradient) mean strong winds. The Second Officer distinguishes low-pressure (depression/low) centers, high-pressure (anticyclone/high) ridges, warm/cold fronts and occlusions.

Kuzey yarımkürede rüzgar, alçak basınç e.en: In the Northern Hemisphere, the wind blows counterclockwise and inward around low pressure, and clockwise and outward around high pressure (the reverse in the Southern Hemisphere). Buys Ballot's law: in the Northern Hemisphere, with your back to the wind, low pressure is on your left. This is the basic tool for finding the direction of a storm center.

24/48/72 saatlik prognostik haritalar, s.en: The 24/48/72-hour prognostic charts show the forecast movement of the system. The Second Officer overlays the ship's planned position and the system's forecast position on a time axis (time-space diagram) to check the ship against the worst quadrant.

Hızlı derinleşen alçak basınç (bomb cycl.en: A rapidly deepening low (bomb cyclogenesis — a fall of ≥24 hPa in 24 hours) is very dangerous; it produces sudden, violent wind and sea. The Second Officer checks whether the forecasts are coming true by continuously monitoring the pressure tendency with the barometer/barograph.

Toplam deniz durumu; lokal rüzgarın üret.en: The total sea state is the combination of the "sea" generated by the local wind and the "swell" coming from a distant system. Significant wave height (Hs) is the mean of the highest one third of the waves; a single maximum wave can reach about 1.8-2 times Hs. When interpreting this statistic, the Second Officer does not neglect the possibility of a "rogue wave".

Swell yönü ve periyodu, geminin rezonans.en: The swell direction and period determine whether the ship will go into resonance. Long-period swell (e.g. 12-16 s) coinciding with the ship's roll period can produce dangerous rolling even at a relatively low wave height.

Parametric rolling (özellikle container.en: The main dangers are parametric rolling (especially in container ships, in head/following seas), synchronous rolling (in beam seas, when the roll period coincides with the wave period) and broaching (loss of steering control in following seas). IMO MSC.1/Circ.1228 recommends changes of speed and heading to avoid these situations.

İkinci Zabit, swell verisi ile gemi roll.en: At the Master's briefing, the Second Officer compares the swell data with the ship's roll period and presents which heading/speed combinations are dangerous. The general principle: to get out of the resonance zone, change either speed or heading.

Weather routing; en kısa mesafe yerine,.en: Instead of the shortest distance, weather routing selects the fastest (least-time) or least-damage/least-risk route, considering weather and sea conditions. The Second Officer compares alternative routes using the ship's speed loss curve (loss of speed against waves/wind) and the ship-specific constraints.

Shore-based routing servisi öneri sağlas.en: Although a shore-based routing service provides recommendations, the final decision rests with the ship's team; the service does not know the ship-specific sensitivities or the real-time loading condition. The Second Officer confirms the service's recommendation with an independent analysis or rejects it with justification.

Bazen en güvenli karar, fırtınanın geçme.en: Sometimes the safest decision is to reduce speed and wait for the storm to pass (heave to / riding out), or to alter the route and pass ahead of or behind the system. The Second Officer presents the balance between ETA pressure and safety clearly to the Master; commercial pressure must never take precedence over safety.

Voluntary speed reduction, sadece hava d.en: Voluntary speed reduction is assessed not only for weather but also for structural fatigue (slamming, green water) and fuel efficiency. In the CII/EEXI era, a lower speed can be an advantage for both safety and the environment, but weather safety always comes first.

Tropical revolving storm (TRS), fırtına.en: A tropical revolving storm (TRS) is a destructive system rotating around the storm center. In the Northern Hemisphere, the right-hand side of the center is the "dangerous semicircle" (the wind pushes the ship towards the center) and the left-hand side is the "navigable semicircle". The Second Officer determines which semicircle the ship is in from the wind direction and how it changes.
