Bu konunun tam ayrıntısı (1-2-3 kuralı,.en: The full detail of this subject (1-2-3 rule, JMA/NHC/JTWC reports, maneuvering directions) is covered in the "Tropical Revolving Storm and typhoon avoidance" task; here the emphasis is on the Second Officer's ability to detect a TRS early as part of daily monitoring.

İkinci Zabit, barometre eğilimini (mevsi.en: By assessing together the barometric tendency (corrected for season/geography), anomalies in the swell direction and the cloud patterns, the Second Officer can sense a TRS before an official warning arrives. This early detection gains extra hours for avoidance.

TRS sezildiğinde gözlemler (basınç, rüzg.en: When a TRS is suspected, the observations (pressure, wind, swell, position) are reported as a danger message and the Master is informed. In areas with a seasonal TRS risk (Indian Ocean, Pacific, Atlantic), monitoring is intensified.

Ağır hava beklendiğinde, fırtına gelmede.en: When heavy weather is expected, preparations must be completed before the storm arrives: checking and tightening the lashings, securing deck equipment, hatch covers and weathertight closures dogged, freeing ports (water drainage openings) clear, anchors secured and sounding pipe caps closed. The Second Officer coordinates this checklist with the Chief Officer.

İç mekanlarda gevşek eşyaların sabitlenm.en: Measures such as securing loose items inside the ship, instructions to the crew on moving about safely and restrictions on going out on deck (green water risk) are applied on the Master's instructions. Preparations cannot be made after the storm has started; timing is critical.

Fırtınada heave to (rüzgara karşı minimu.en: In a storm, the decision to heave to (holding head to wind at minimum speed), run before the sea (taking the sea from astern) or alter course is made according to the ship type and the direction of the sea. The Second Officer assesses the minimum steerage way needed to keep steering/propulsion capability, and the risks of slamming/racing.

Vardiya zabiti, ağır havada pozisyon doğ.en: In heavy weather, the officer of the watch verifies the position continuously; set & drift (deviation caused by current and wind) increases and leeway grows. Near land/shoals this deviation can be dangerous.

Pek çok gemi Voluntary Observing Ship (V.en: Many ships contribute to the Voluntary Observing Ship (VOS) scheme; observations of pressure, wind, temperature, sea state and visibility are reported in a standard format. The Second Officer monitors the calibration of the observation instruments (barometer, anemometer, thermometer) and the accuracy of the readings.

Doğru gözlem, hem küresel tahmin modelle.en: Accurate observations both feed global forecast models and improve the ship's own short-term forecast. A wrongly calibrated barometer can mislead the pressure tendency analysis and delay recognition of a TRS.

İkinci Zabit'in hava analizi, ancak köpr.en: The Second Officer's weather analysis is of value only when it is passed on clearly to the bridge team and the Master. The daily weather brief must include the current situation, the 24/48-hour forecast, the critical thresholds and the recommended measures. Any uncertainty is stated openly.

Vardiya devrinde hava durumu, beklenen d.en: At the watch handover, the weather situation, expected changes and the criteria for calling the Master are passed on. If weather information stays in one person's head, the risk is missed when that person is not on watch.

En yaygın hatalar; eski/tek hava verisin.en: The most common errors are relying on old or single-source weather data, failing to allow for swell-roll resonance, heading towards a storm under ETA pressure, starting preparations late, and mistaking significant wave height for the maximum wave height.

Bir diğer hata, routing servisi önerisin.en: Another error is to follow a routing service's recommendation without questioning the ship-specific sensitivities. The service gives recommendations; it is the team that knows the ship. Blind obedience is as dangerous as blind rejection.

El Faro (2015): kasırga gelişimini yeter.en: El Faro (2015): inadequate monitoring of the hurricane's development, old data and a late decision → loss of the ship. Lesson: keep the weather data continuously updated and act early on the worst-case scenario.

Birçok container kaybı vakası (parametri.en: Many container loss cases (parametric/synchronous rolling): navigating at high speed in head/following seas without monitoring the swell period → stack collapse. Lesson: assess swell-roll resonance continuously and change speed/heading when necessary.

Hava takibi, geminin ne zaman gideceğini.en: Weather monitoring is the discipline that tells not when the ship should go but when she should wait. The Second Officer's task is not just to read forecasts but to translate the data into the ship's specific sensitivities, see the worst-case scenario early and give the Master a clear, reasoned recommendation. Good weather monitoring is less about getting through a storm than about never entering it; this is the strongest safety strategy.

STCW Kod A-VIII/2, vardiya zabitinin (OO.en: STCW Code A-VIII/2 states clearly that the officer of the watch (OOW), as the Master's representative, is primarily responsible for the safe navigation of the ship. The officer remains solely responsible for the watch until the Master comes to the bridge and formally takes over the con; the Master's presence alone does not relieve the officer of responsibility, and this handover must be made clearly and verbally and entered in the deck logbook.

Zabit, COLREG'e tam uyumu sağlamak, emni.en: The officer is obliged to ensure full compliance with COLREG, maintain a safe speed, keep a continuous lookout and call the Master immediately in case of doubt. STCW stresses that "if in any doubt" the officer must call the Master without hesitation; a late call is the most frequently seen link in the accident chain.

Vardiya zabiti aynı anda hem seyir sorum.en: The officer of the watch carries the navigational responsibility and other duties on board (GMDSS listening watch, responding to alarms) at the same time; however, no additional duty may take precedence over the lookout and safe navigation duties. Fatigue management (STCW rest hours) is therefore an integral part of watch safety.

04-08 vardiyası şafağı, 16-20 vardiyası.en: Because the 04-08 watch covers dawn and the 16-20 watch covers dusk, the sole lookout arrangement on these watches must be reassessed as the light conditions change. During the transition to darkness, it may not be enough for the officer alone to monitor the steering and keep a lookout at the same time; for this reason, calling a lookout before nightfall is good seamanship practice.

COLREG Kural 5, her geminin her zaman gö.en: COLREG Rule 5 requires every ship at all times to maintain a proper and continuous lookout by sight and hearing as well as by all available appropriate means (including radar, ARPA and AIS). Lookout is not just looking ahead; it covers scanning ahead, astern, both quarters and 360 degrees around the ship, listening for sound signals and continuously assessing the instrument data.

Vardiya zabiti, gözcülüğü ekran başında.en: The officer of the watch must keep the lookout without letting their attention be absorbed by the screens. In many accidents, the officer becoming absorbed in the radar or ECDIS display and failing to look out of the window (single-point fixation) has been identified as a root cause. Good lookout means continuously comparing the visual scan outside with the instrument data.

Gece gözcülüğünde köprüüstü aydınlatması.en: For the lookout at night, the bridge lighting is dimmed (red night lighting) and the eyes adapt to the darkness; this adaptation takes about 20-30 minutes. Exposure to white light spoils the adaptation, so controlling bright screens and lighting on the night watch is a direct part of keeping a lookout.

Yoğun trafik, kısıtlı görüş, dar sular v.en: In heavy traffic, restricted visibility, narrow waters and at night, the officer has an additional lookout posted. The lookout's only job is to look out; the lookout must not be given the helm or any other task, otherwise the lookout duty is compromised. The lookout is expected to report every target seen to the officer (e.g. "two points on the starboard bow, light in sight").

Otomatik dümen (autopilot) kullanılırken.en: Even when the autopilot is in use, the officer must ensure that it is possible to change over to manual steering immediately when there is a risk of collision or a maneuver is required. SOLAS V/24 and V/26 require prompt changeover to manual control and regular testing of the steering systems.

COLREG Kural 6, her geminin çatışmayı ön.en: COLREG Rule 6 requires every ship to proceed at all times at a safe speed so that she can avoid collision and be stopped within a distance appropriate to the prevailing conditions. Safe speed is not a fixed value; it is determined by factors such as the state of visibility, traffic density, the ship's maneuverability, stopping distance, background lights at night, wind/sea/current and depth of water.

Radar kullanan gemiler için Kural 6 ek f.en: For ships using radar, Rule 6 lists additional factors: the range and limitations of the radar, the range scale in use, the effect of sea/rain clutter, the possibility that small craft/ice will not be detected by radar, and the number and position of the targets detected by radar. If the officer relies on the radar and keeps up speed in poor visibility, Rule 6 is violated.

Büyük bir geminin durma mesafesi (stoppi.en: The stopping distance and turning circle of a large ship can be measured in kilometers; a VLCC may run more than a mile when stopping from full speed. Safe speed must be a speed at which the officer, knowing these maneuvering characteristics, can stop or turn away in time on seeing a danger.

Görüş bozulduğunda Kural 19 gereği hız \.en: When visibility deteriorates, under Rule 19 the speed is reduced "as far as is practicable"; if necessary, the ship takes all way off. The officer coordinates the decision to reduce speed with the engine room (stand-by engine request) and records it in the deck logbook.

COLREG Kural 7, çatışma riskinin var olu.en: COLREG Rule 7 requires all available means to be used to determine whether risk of collision exists. The basic principle: if the compass bearing of another ship does not change appreciably, risk of collision is deemed to exist. This "constant bearing, decreasing range" (CBDR) situation is the classic indicator of collision.

Radar varsa, riski erken belirlemek için.en: If radar is fitted, long-range scanning is carried out to get early warning of risk, and the targets detected are systematically plotted or tracked with ARPA. Rule 7 explicitly prohibits assumptions based on scanty information, especially scanty radar information; CPA/TCPA values must not be assessed on their own but only after the trend has been confirmed.

COLREG Kural 8, çatışmayı önleyici manev.en: COLREG Rule 8 requires action to avoid collision to be taken in ample time, to be positive and to be made with due regard to good seamanship. The action must be large enough to be readily apparent to the other ship, even by radar; a succession of small alterations of course/speed is avoided, because it can lead the other ship to misinterpret the situation.

Mümkünse rota değişimi (alter course) te.en: If possible, an alteration of course is preferred, because it is more readily apparent on radar and visually than a change of speed; however, if there is enough sea room, a change of speed can also be used. After the maneuver, it is monitored that the ship passes at a safe distance until the danger is completely past, and further action is taken if necessary.

ARPA hedefleri en az üç dakika izlendikt.en: ARPA targets give reliable vectors only after they have been tracked for at least three minutes; the vectors cannot be fully trusted before then. The officer must know what each of the true vector and relative vector modes shows: the relative vector shows the CPA, the true vector shows the target's true course. After an avoiding maneuver, the way the vectors change is confirmed.

Şirket veya kaptan talimatıyla belirlenm.en: If the minimum CPA set by company or Master's instructions (e.g. 2 miles in the open sea, less in restricted waters) looks like being infringed, the officer takes early action. The CPA margin is assessed not just as a number but together with the ship's maneuverability and the traffic density.

AIS (Automatic Identification System), h.en: AIS (Automatic Identification System) gives the target's identity, course, speed, draft and intentions (destination, navigational status); however, AIS is not a collision avoidance device. IMO Resolution A.1106(29) stresses that AIS data must be confirmed by radar/ARPA and that AIS must not be used on its own for maneuvering decisions. Incorrectly entered AIS data (e.g. wrong ROT, wrong position) is misleading.

Zabit, AIS hedefini radar hedefiyle eşle.en: The officer correlates the AIS target with the radar target; if the AIS and radar positions do not coincide, priority is given to the real-time radar data. Small craft without AIS, fishing boats and targets with a weak radar echo can be picked up only by visual and radar lookout; relying on AIS and missing them is dangerous.

COLREG Kural 9, dar bir kanal veya su yo.en: COLREG Rule 9 requires a ship proceeding along a narrow channel or fairway to keep as near to the outer limit of the channel on her starboard side as is safe and practicable. Ships of less than 20 meters in length, sailing vessels and fishing vessels must not impede the passage of a ship that can navigate only within the channel.

Kanal dönüşlerinde, görüşün engelli oldu.en: At bends in the channel and in areas where the view is obscured, the ship proceeds with caution and sounds one prolonged blast in accordance with Rule 34(e). Anchoring in a narrow channel is avoided. For overtaking within the channel, the officer applies the Rule 9(e) signal arrangement and agreement with the other ship.

COLREG Kural 10, IMO tarafından kabul ed.en: COLREG Rule 10 requires a ship in an IMO-adopted traffic separation scheme (TSS) to proceed in the appropriate traffic lane in the general direction of traffic flow and to keep as far as practicable clear of the separation line/zone. A lane is joined or left at its termination where possible; when joining from the side is unavoidable, it is done at as small an angle to the direction of traffic flow as practicable.

Trafik şeridini kesmek (crossing) zorunl.en: If crossing a traffic lane is unavoidable, the ship crosses on a heading as nearly as practicable at right angles to the direction of traffic flow; this shortens the crossing time and makes it easier for other ships to understand her intention. The Second Officer marks the TSS crossing in the passage plan in advance and complies with the VTS reporting requirements.

Kural 15 (crossing / kesişme), iki makin.en: Rule 15 (crossing) states that when two power-driven vessels are crossing, the vessel which has the other on her own starboard side is the give-way vessel and shall, if possible, avoid crossing ahead of the other. The give-way vessel takes early and substantial action; the stand-on vessel keeps her course and speed in accordance with Rule 17.

Kural 18, gemiler arası öncelik hiyerarş.en: Rule 18 defines the hierarchy of priority between ships: it determines who gives way to whom among power-driven vessels, sailing vessels, vessels engaged in fishing, vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver (RAM), vessels not under command (NUC) and vessels constrained by their draft (CBD). The officer applies the Rule 18 priority by correctly identifying the type of the other ship from her lights/shapes.

COLREG Kural 19, kısıtlı görüş (restrict.en: COLREG Rule 19 applies to ships navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility; in this case the ship must proceed at a safe speed, keep her engines ready for maneuvering (engines ready for immediate manoeuvre) and, if radar is fitted, make systematic observations. Under Rule 19 conditions there is no "stand-on / give-way" distinction; every ship carries her own responsibility for maneuvering.

Kural 35, kısıtlı görüşte verilecek ses.en: Rule 35 governs the sound signals to be given in restricted visibility. A power-driven vessel making way sounds one prolonged blast every two minutes; a vessel that is stopped and making no way (stopped, no way) sounds two prolonged blasts every two minutes. Vessels restricted in their ability to maneuver (RAM), NUC, CBD, sailing vessels, fishing vessels and vessels engaged in towing sound one prolonged blast followed by two short blasts (one prolonged + two short).

Zabit, kısıtlı görüşe girer girmez sis i.en: As soon as the ship enters restricted visibility, the officer starts the fog signals, switches on the navigation lights, calls a lookout, puts the engine on stand-by and informs/calls the Master. The fog signal can be sounded automatically or manually; it must be confirmed that the automatic signal system operates at the correct interval.

04-08 ve 16-20 vardiyaları, ışık koşulun.en: The 04-08 and 16-20 watches cover transition periods in which the light conditions change rapidly. At dawn the officer must correctly determine the time to switch off the lights (lights off), and at dusk the time to switch them on (lights on); lights are shown "from sunset to sunrise" and at all times in restricted visibility. Switching off early or switching on late leads other ships to misjudge the ship's status.

Alacakaranlıkta gözlerin karanlığa adapt.en: At dusk, because the eyes have not yet fully adapted to darkness, small targets are harder to detect, and background lights (shore lights) can be confused with ships' lights. At dawn, targets can be lost visually when looking towards the sun (sun glare). For this reason, on the dawn/dusk watches the radar lookout and the visual lookout are intensified together, and an additional lookout is posted as night begins/ends.

Bu vardiyalarda İkinci Zabit ayrıca seyi.en: On these watches, the Second Officer also has the opportunity to take star sights (celestial fix) in the short window (civil/nautical twilight) when the navigational stars are visible; this window, when the horizon and the stars can be seen at the same time, is the classic time for obtaining an astronomical position. The priority of duties always remains safe navigation and lookout.

Vardiya devri, devralan zabit durumu tam.en: The watch handover is not complete until the relieving officer has fully assessed the situation and accepted the duty. The officer being relieved gives clear information on the ship's position, course and speed, the surrounding traffic and plotting status, the critical points ahead in the passage plan, the Master's special instructions, the weather and any maneuvers in progress. An officer does not take over the watch while a maneuver is in progress or before their eyes have adapted to the dark.

Kaptanı çağırma kriterleri (calling the.en: The criteria for calling the Master (calling the master) are applied clearly and without hesitation: entering or approaching restricted visibility, failure to achieve the planned CPA, traffic density becoming unmanageable, an unexpected danger (drifting object, distress signal), equipment failure, uncertainty about the position, deteriorating weather and any situation of "any doubt". The officer must never hesitate to call the Master and must not put off the decision to call.

Bridge Resource Management (BRM); açık i.en: Bridge Resource Management (BRM) covers open communication, task sharing, cross-checking, situational awareness and a "speak up / challenge and response" culture. Everyone on the bridge — including the helmsman, the lookout and junior officers — must speak up when they notice a risk, and the hierarchy must not prevent this. Most collisions arise from an error chain that develops because someone in the team did not share a risk they had seen.

İkinci Zabit, vardiyayı paylaşılan bir m.en: The Second Officer runs the watch on a shared mental model: the whole team knows the same traffic picture, the same plan and the same maneuvering intention. Fatigue, over-reliance on automation (automation complacency) and distraction are the greatest enemies of BRM; the officer manages them actively.

Köprüüstü vardiyası, gemideki en yüksek.en: The bridge watch is one of the duties carrying the highest responsibility on board; on this watch, as the Master's representative, the Second Officer carries the safety of hundreds of lives and of cargo worth millions of dollars. Complying with the letter and spirit of COLREG, maintaining a safe speed, keeping a continuous lookout and calling the Master the moment there is any doubt ("if in doubt") are the disciplines that prevent, from the outset, the collisions and groundings that keep recurring in the statistics. An officer of the watch who knows the particular risks of the dawn and dusk transitions, relies on judgment rather than on equipment and has internalized the BRM culture is the ship's strongest safety defense.

SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19, gemi tona.en: SOLAS Chapter V Regulation 19 lists the navigational equipment that must be carried according to the ship's tonnage and area of operation (gyro compass, magnetic compass, radar/ARPA, ECDIS, AIS, echo sounder, speed/distance log, GNSS, BNWAS, VDR). The Second Officer monitors that this equipment is not only on board but also working in a condition that meets the performance standards.

Donanımın bakımı genelde elektro-teknik.en: Although maintenance of the equipment is usually carried out by the electro-technical officer (ETO) or a service company, monitoring of operational accuracy (error, deviation, calibration records) on the bridge is the Second Officer's responsibility. These records are among the first documents requested in PSC and flag State inspections.

Her cihaz tipi için IMO bir performans s.en: IMO publishes a performance standard (Resolution) for each type of equipment; for example A.424(XI) for the gyro compass and MSC.333(90) for the VDR. Equipment must be type approved to these standards and carry the "wheelmark". The Second Officer verifies that the equipment approval certificates and calibration documents are on board.

IEC 60945 (A.694(17)), tüm köprüüstü cih.en: IEC 60945 (A.694(17)) sets the environmental and EMC durability requirements for all bridge equipment. Retesting equipment after servicing and recording the result is part of a traceable maintenance chain.

Gyro compass, gerçek kuzeyi (true north).en: The gyro compass is designed to indicate true north; however, a small error (gyro error) may always be present. The error is expressed as "high" (the reading is greater than the true value) or "low", and is found from the difference between the true bearing and the gyro bearing. The Second Officer makes this check regularly and records it in the gyro error book.

En yaygın yöntemler; transit (iki sabit.en: The most common methods are a transit (two fixed objects in line), azimuth/amplitude (comparing the calculated true azimuth of a celestial body with its gyro azimuth) and a known transit bearing. The error must be checked at least once a day in the open sea, and always before entering restricted waters.

Tespit edilen gyro error tüm gyro bearin.en: The gyro error found is applied to all gyro bearings and headings: the true value is obtained with the logic "error east, compass least; error west, compass best". Because ECDIS and radar are fed from the gyro, the error directly affects position and target calculations.

Error sürekli artıyor veya sıçramalar gö.en: If the error keeps increasing or shows jumps, this is a sign of a fault; the Second Officer reports the situation to the Master and the technical department. It is also checked regularly that the repeaters are synchronized with the master gyro.

Manyetik pusula, geminin çelik gövdesi v.en: The magnetic compass deviates from magnetic north (deviation) because of the local magnetic field created by the ship's steel hull and electrical equipment. This deviation is different for each heading and is shown on the "deviation card" (deviation table). Total compass error = variation + deviation.

İkinci Zabit, deviation'ı düzenli olarak.en: The Second Officer checks the deviation regularly (usually at a suitable opportunity on every watch and on change of heading) and enters it in the deviation book. Variation is taken from the ENC/chart or from a magnetic model; deviation is found by observation.

Deviation, gemi büyük tamir/kuru havuz s.en: Deviation is redetermined by an authorized compass adjuster by "swinging" the ship after major repairs/dry-docking, when the cargo distribution has changed permanently, or when the reliability of the deviation card is in doubt. The Second Officer records the date of the swing and the new card.

Gyro arızasında manyetik pusula tek head.en: If the gyro fails, the magnetic compass may remain the only heading reference; for this reason, an up-to-date and reliable deviation is a redundancy safeguard. It is also checked that no magnetic material is placed near the compass.

Speed log; doppler (su/zemin referanslı).en: A speed log may be of the Doppler (water/ground referenced), electromagnetic (EM) or pitometer type. A Doppler log gives dual-axis ground/water speed; an EM log measures speed through the water. Each type is affected by current, shallow water, fouling and transducer alignment.

Log hatası, ECDIS dead reckoning, ETA he.en: Log error affects ECDIS dead reckoning, the ETA calculation and squat estimates. The Second Officer monitors consistency by regularly comparing the log readings with the GNSS SOG and records any discrepancies.

Log kalibrasyonu genelde üretici/servis.en: Log calibration is usually carried out by the manufacturer/service company on a measured mile or by comparison with GNSS. The Second Officer carries out a verification by comparing log speed with GNSS SOG in open, calm water; a large difference is a sign of transducer fouling or a fault.

Distance log (cumulative) makine perform.en: The distance log (cumulative) is also used for engine performance and fuel monitoring; for this reason, jumps or freezes are reported immediately. The calibration certificate and verification notes are kept in the log book.

Echo sounder, transducer altındaki su de.en: The echo sounder measures the depth of water below the transducer and is the last independent line of defense for UKC monitoring and the prevention of grounding. The Second Officer verifies that the draft/transducer offset setting is correct, that the gain and range settings are appropriate and that the shallow water alarm is set.

Gösterge \"depth below keel\" mi yoksa \.en: It must be made clear whether the display shows "depth below keel" or "depth below transducer/waterline"; if the offset is wrong, the depth reading becomes dangerously misleading. On dual-frequency sounders, the appropriate frequency is selected.

Kısıtlı sularda echo sounder sürekli çal.en: In restricted waters the echo sounder is run continuously and a depth recorder/log is kept (mandatory in some waters). The shallow water alarm is set according to the planned minimum UKC, and its audible alarm is tested.

İkinci Zabit, sounder'ın transducer kirl.en: The Second Officer watches that the sounder is not giving false readings because of transducer fouling, air bubbles (aeration) or false echoes (second reflection). A doubtful reading is confirmed immediately by another method.

Radar performance monitor (PM), radarın.en: The radar performance monitor (PM) is a built-in test arrangement that shows whether the radar's transmitted power and receiver sensitivity are normal. At the start of each watch and before entering critical waters, the Second Officer runs the PM to verify that radar performance has not deteriorated, and records the result.

Tune, gain, sea/rain clutter ve gerekirs.en: Tune, gain, sea/rain clutter and, where necessary, the manual settings are tested. It is checked that the ARPA functions (target acquisition, CPA/TCPA, vector mode) work and that the gyro/log inputs are fed correctly; otherwise the target speeds will be calculated wrongly.

SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), ca.en: The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder) is a device carried in a liferaft/lifeboat which, when triggered by a 9 GHz radar, produces a line of 12 dots on the display. The Second Officer keeps a record of the SART battery expiry date and, where required, of the periodic test (against a radar).

ECDIS'in birincil seyir aracı olduğu gem.en: On ships where ECDIS is the primary means of navigation, continuous and correct operation of the system is vital. The Second Officer regularly verifies ENC currency, the safety contour/depth settings, the sensor inputs (GNSS, gyro, log) and alarm management. The system software version must be approved (compliant with IHO S-52/S-57/S-63).

İki bağımsız ECDIS'li gemilerde her ikis.en: On ships with two independent ECDIS units, it is checked that both have the same up-to-date ENCs and settings; otherwise the backup cannot be relied on if the primary fails.

AIS statik verileri (MMSI, çağrı işareti.en: AIS static data (MMSI, call sign, ship's name/type, length/beam) and dynamic data (position, SOG, COG, heading, navigational status) are verified regularly; in particular, the navigational status (under way, at anchor, NUC) must be kept up to date manually. Wrong AIS data leads to misunderstandings in traffic.

VDR/S-VDR, kaza sonrası delil için kriti.en: The VDR/S-VDR is a critical "black box" for evidence after an accident. The Second Officer monitors that the VDR records all channels (bridge audio, VHF, radar image, sensor data), that the APT (Annual Performance Test) certificate is valid and that the capsule battery is in order. After an incident, the recording must be preserved before it is overwritten.

Seyir cihazlarının bakımı genelde gemini.en: Maintenance of navigational equipment is usually tracked as jobs defined in the ship's Planned Maintenance System (PMS). The Second Officer ensures that the test and calibration records for the bridge equipment (gyro error book, deviation book, radar PM log, magnetic compass swing, SART/EPIRB tests) are kept up to date and complete.

Servis raporları, kalibrasyon sertifikal.en: Service reports, calibration certificates and type approval documents are filed. A traceable chain of records is essential from both a safety and an inspection point of view.

Bir cihaz arızalandığında İkinci Zabit;.en: When equipment fails, the Second Officer records the failure, informs the Master and the technical department, brings in an alternative method if one is available and, if required, considers whether flag/class need to be notified. For example, on an ECDIS-only ship, a single ECDIS failure may result in navigational restrictions.

Yedek/alternatif düzenlemeler (manuel pl.en: Backup/alternative arrangements (manual plotting, magnetic compass, a second position source) are kept ready. Navigation with defective equipment is carried out with additional measures that reduce the risk (reduced speed, an extra lookout).

En yaygın hatalar; gyro error'un düzenli.en: The most common errors are not checking the gyro error regularly, an out-of-date deviation card, an incorrectly set echo sounder offset, skipping the radar performance monitor and never comparing the log with GNSS.

AIS navigational status'ün güncellenmeme.en: Not updating the AIS navigational status and letting the VDR APT expire are deficiencies frequently found at inspections. Trusting a single position source (GNSS) blindly and neglecting to cross-check the equipment can lead to grounding.

Royal Majesty (1995): GPS anten bağlantı.en: Royal Majesty (1995): the GPS antenna connection came apart, the positioning fell back to DR mode and the ship deviated for hours without the team noticing; because there was no confirmation with the echo sounder and independent fixes, she ran aground. Lesson: cross-check the equipment and do not rely on a single source.

Genel denetim bulgusu: kalibre edilmemiş.en: A general inspection finding: navigational equipment that is not calibrated or whose records are not kept is a regular cause of PSC detentions. Lesson: the chain of records is as important as the equipment itself.

Seyir cihazlarının düzenli bakım ve kali.en: Regular follow-up of the maintenance and calibration of navigational equipment is the invisible foundation of an accurate position and safe maneuvering. The Second Officer's task is not only to operate the equipment but to cross-check its readings, record discrepancies and catch silent failures early. A disciplined routine of records and verification both breaks the accident chain right at the start and ensures that the ship is found ready at every inspection.

Astronomik seyirde boylam hatası doğruda.en: In celestial navigation, a longitude error arises directly from a time error: a time error of about 4 seconds corresponds to a longitude error of ~1 nautical mile at the equator. Even in the GPS era, the chronometer and accurate time remain important, both as a backup navigation method and for the consistency of records.

Ayrıca tüm gemi kayıtları (deck log, ORB.en: In addition, all ship's records (deck log, ORB, GMDSS log, rest hours) carry time stamps. Inconsistent or wrong time undermines the reliability of the records at an inspection and creates serious problems in an investigation after an incident.

Geleneksel kronometre, UTC'ye göre bir h.en: A traditional chronometer has an error relative to UTC (chronometer error), and this error changes regularly from day to day (daily rate). The Second Officer measures the error by comparison with a time signal (radio time signal/GPS UTC), records it in the chronometer journal and monitors that the daily rate is stable. A sudden change in rate is a sign of a problem with the chronometer.

Köprüüstü, makine, GMDSS ve VDR saatleri.en: The bridge, engine room, GMDSS and VDR clocks must be kept consistent (usually referenced to UTC or ship's time). The time source of the VDR must be correct; otherwise the event record will not match real time. The Second Officer checks clock synchronization periodically.

Doğuya seyirde saatler ileri, batıya sey.en: When steaming east the clocks are advanced, and when steaming west they are retarded. The Second Officer plans the zone changes in advance according to the progress in longitude and usually spreads them evenly over the night watches. A sudden or large single clock change disrupts the crew's rest hours and alertness.

Deck log, ORB, GMDSS log ve diğer kayıtl.en: The time stamps of the deck log, ORB, GMDSS log and other records must be consistent both within each record and with each other. The Second Officer makes sure that the time reference used (UTC/ship's time) is clear and consistent in the logs. This consistency is the basis of trust in PSC inspections and incident investigations.

Sekstant rasadında gök cisminin yüksekli.en: When the altitude of a celestial body is measured in a sextant sight, the exact second is noted, because the calculated position depends on this time. The Second Officer keeps celestial navigation skills and the discipline of taking accurate time alive, in case of a GPS failure scenario.

Zaman, seyrin sessiz omurgasıdır. İkinci.en: Time is the silent backbone of navigation. The Second Officer's chronometer monitoring, UTC discipline and careful time zone management protect navigational accuracy, the reliability of records and the crew's rest pattern together.

STCW sertifikası bir zabitin generic (ge.en: An STCW certificate documents an officer's generic competence; however, every ship has a different make of ECDIS, a different radar/ARPA interface and a different bridge layout. For this reason, STCW Regulation I/14 and ISM Code Section 6 require seafarers to receive ship-specific familiarization before taking up their duties. The Second Officer carries out the navigational equipment part of this familiarization and records it.

Familiarizasyon ile eğitim (training) fa.en: Familiarization and training are different concepts: familiarization means "getting to know this equipment on this ship", while training is the process of "developing and maintaining competence". The Second Officer manages both together; a newly joined officer is given basic familiarization within the first 24 hours, and skills are reinforced with regular drills throughout the voyage.

Eğitim faaliyeti onboard training record.en: Training activity is documented with an onboard training record / familiarization checklist. Undocumented training counts as "not done" in Port State Control (PSC) inspections and internal company audits; in investigations after an accident, the absence of these records also increases the liability of the ship and the company.

İkinci Zabit, seyir cihazlarının (ECDIS,.en: Because the Second Officer is responsible for the maintenance, updating and correction of the navigational equipment (ECDIS, radar/ARPA, GPS, AIS, gyro, echo sounder), the Second Officer has the deepest practical knowledge of this equipment. As the person who prepares the ENC updates, the ECDIS safety settings and the passage plan, the Second Officer is in the best position to provide the training.

Ayrıca İkinci Zabit, kariyer basamağında.en: In addition, on the career ladder the Second Officer is the closest superior to the cadets and junior officers, so a mentoring relationship develops naturally here. While the Master and the Chief Officer provide strategic oversight, day-to-day practical training and follow-up of the Training Record Book (TRB) fall to the Second Officer.

Familiarizasyon; safety settings (safety.en: The familiarization covers the safety settings (safety contour, safety depth, shallow/deep contour), setting the display modes (base/standard/all), alarm management, route planning and the route check function, the manual update layer, S-52 symbology and the S-57/S-63 ENC loading and updating processes. Each make presents these functions with a different menu logic; what must be taught is the logic of each function, not blind memorizing of menus.

ECDIS'in en kritik ayarı safety contour'.en: The most critical ECDIS setting is the safety contour. The Second Officer must teach the officer the anti-grounding function of the safety contour, that if the required value is not available in the ENC the system rounds up to the next deeper contour, and that the actual value must therefore be verified.

İkinci Zabit, yeni zabit için yapılandır.en: For a new officer, the Second Officer uses a structured ECDIS familiarization checklist. This checklist verifies not merely that a function was "shown" but that the officer can carry it out on their own (demonstrated competence). The table below summarizes a typical familiarization scope.

Familiarizasyon tamamlandığında, kayıt z.en: When the familiarization is complete, the record is signed by the officer and the Second Officer and placed in the ship's training file. Additional sessions are planned for items found insufficient; an incomplete item is not considered passed.

Radar eğitimi, cihazın doğru ayarlanması.en: Radar training starts with setting up the equipment correctly: gain, sea clutter (STC), rain clutter (FTC), tuning, pulse length and range selection. The Second Officer demonstrates hands-on to the cadet that a wrong clutter setting can suppress real targets (e.g. small craft, growlers) and that excessive gain fills the screen with noise. Correct setting-up is not a static procedure but a skill that is continuously optimized for the conditions (sea state, precipitation).

Head-up, course-up ve north-up gösterim.en: The difference between the head-up, course-up and north-up display modes, and between true and relative motion, is taught. In relative motion, own ship is fixed and the targets move; in true motion, both show their true movement. In assessing collision avoidance, reading the relative motion and the relative track is essential.

ARPA (Automatic Radar Plotting Aid), hed.en: ARPA (Automatic Radar Plotting Aid) acquires targets, calculates their vectors and gives the CPA (Closest Point of Approach) and TCPA (Time to CPA) values. The Second Officer teaches the difference between the vector modes (true/relative), the trial manoeuvre function and the use of guard zones. The trial manoeuvre shows in advance how a planned maneuver will change the CPA; however, the maneuver parameters must be entered realistically.

ARPA'nın sınırlamaları kritik öneme sahi.en: The limitations of ARPA are critically important: target swap, loss of tracking at low SNR, the instability of the vector of a newly acquired target in the first minutes, and errors in the sensor inputs (gyro, log) corrupting the CPA calculation. The Second Officer stresses that ARPA is a decision support tool and does not replace the lookout or plotting.

COLREG kurallarını ezbere bilmek yetmez;.en: Knowing the COLREG rules by heart is not enough; the ability to make fast and correct decisions on a real bridge is needed. The Second Officer sets up scenarios using radar/ECDIS simulation or real traffic situations: head-on (Rule 14), crossing (Rule 15), overtaking (Rule 13) and restricted visibility (Rule 19) situations are worked through separately. In each scenario the questions are: "stand-on or give-way, which maneuver, when, and under which COLREG rule".

COLREG Kural 8, çatışmadan kaçınma manev.en: COLREG Rule 8 requires action to avoid collision to be taken early (in ample time), to be substantial (readily apparent) and, if necessary, to include a change of speed. The Second Officer teaches junior officers the most common mistake: small, gradual course alterations (e.g. 2-3 degrees) are not noticed on the other ship's radar and leave the intention unclear. Instead, a clear alteration of at least 20-30 degrees is made.

Bridge Resource Management; köprüüstünde.en: Bridge Resource Management is the discipline of ensuring safe navigation through the effective use of all resources on the bridge (people, equipment, information). The error chain concept describes the small errors and ignored signs that line up one after another on the path to an accident; an intervention that breaks any link in the chain prevents the accident. The Second Officer teaches the team to recognize the typical warning signs of the chain.

Bu belirtiler arasında; belirsizlik (amb.en: These signs include ambiguity, differing mental models among team members, skipped procedures, communication breakdown, excessive workload on one person, neglect of the horizon/lookout, and failure to voice the feeling that "something is wrong but I'm not sure". In training, a concrete example is given for each of these signs.

Challenge and response; bir ekip üyesini.en: Challenge and response is a culture in which any team member can question anyone's decision, including a superior's, in the interest of safety. The Second Officer teaches junior officers and helmsmen that "the courage to say what you see is wrong" is a duty; a bridge silenced by the authority gradient is dangerous. Even with a pilot on board, the pilot's advice must be questioned against the plan.

Closed-loop (kapalı çevrim) iletişim; bi.en: Closed-loop communication is completed by giving an order, the receiver repeating it (read-back) and confirmation that the order has been carried out (e.g. the helmsman saying "Midships, rudder amidships"). This loop prevents a misunderstood helm order from turning into an accident. In training, helm and engine orders are always practiced using closed-loop communication.

Durumsal farkındalık (situational awaren.en: Situational awareness consists of three levels: perceiving the surroundings (perception), making sense of them (comprehension) and anticipating the future (projection). The Second Officer teaches junior officers to keep asking not only "what is happening?" but also "what does this mean?" and "what will happen in 5-10 minutes?". Position, traffic, depth and the weather trend must together form one picture in the mind.

Durumsal farkındalık kaybının tipik nede.en: Typical causes of loss of situational awareness are excessive workload, distraction (e.g. fixation on a single device — task fixation), fatigue and the assumption that "everything is fine". Training builds the officer's habit of regularly stepping back to the "big picture" throughout the watch and rescanning the horizon and all sensors.

Modern köprüüstü; ECDIS, track control (.en: The modern bridge is highly automated, with ECDIS, track control (autopilot), ARPA and an integrated bridge system. This creates the risk of automation complacency: assuming the system is working correctly, the team relaxes its monitoring. In this complacency, GPS spoofing/jamming, an ENC error or a sensor failure progresses unnoticed. The Second Officer stresses that automation is a tool and that responsibility always remains with people.

Bu riske karşı pratik panzehir; bağımsız.en: The practical antidote to this risk is independent cross-checking. Even in track control mode, the position is verified by radar/visual bearings and the depth by echo sounder. Training builds the officer's habit of periodically "questioning" the automation: "ECDIS is showing me this — is it correct when checked independently?"

Stajyer eğitimi, görevleri yapma fırsatı.en: Cadet training cannot happen without giving the cadet the opportunity to carry out tasks. Following the principle of supervised responsibility, the Second Officer gives the cadet progressively greater tasks: first taking fixes and keeping the logbook, then radar plotting, ECDIS route monitoring and, in suitable conditions, supervised watchkeeping practice. Each task is assessed according to the level achieved, and feedback is given.

İyi mentorluk; hata yapıldığında suçlama.en: Good mentoring means not blaming when a mistake is made, but turning the mistake into a learning moment. By asking "why did you do it this way, what would the result have been, what would have been the right way?", the Second Officer develops the cadet's judgment. The aim is not rote learning of procedures but seamanship judgment.

Training Record Book (TRB), stajyerin ST.en: The Training Record Book (TRB) is the official record documenting that the cadet has achieved the competences required by STCW. On most ships, as the cadet's shipboard training officer or immediate superior, the Second Officer oversees completion of the TRB tasks, observes the cadet and signs off the tasks in which the cadet is judged competent. The TRB is the link between the maritime school and the ship, and if it is not filled in completely, the cadet cannot progress to the next stage.

İkinci Zabit, TRB'yi pasif bir imza deft.en: The Second Officer uses the TRB not as a passive signature book but as an active training plan: which tasks have been completed, which are outstanding, and how the voyage can be planned to close these gaps. For example, if the cadet's anchoring drill is outstanding, the procedure is taught to the cadet in a planned way before the next anchoring.

İkinci Zabit, sefer boyunca düzenli köpr.en: The Second Officer plans regular bridge drills throughout the voyage. These include drills for a GPS loss (loss of position) scenario, steering gear failure and changeover to emergency steering, bridge management after a blackout, the man overboard (MOB) maneuver (Williamson/Anderson turn), navigation in restricted visibility, and changeover to the backup on failure of the primary ECDIS. Each drill must be realistic and planned in advance.

Tatbikatlar, gerçek seyri tehlikeye atma.en: Drills are carried out without endangering actual navigation — in open sea and in suitable conditions. Some scenarios can also be run as simulations/table-top sessions; for example, in a grounding scenario the team is asked to discuss "what would you do?". A debrief is always held after the drill; what went well and what needs improvement are noted.

Her tatbikat tarih, katılımcılar, senary.en: Each drill is recorded with the date, participants, scenario, observations and lessons learned. As required by the ISM Code, this record is entered in the company safety management system (SMS) and presented at internal/external audits. Recurring deficiencies (e.g. the team hesitates to reduce speed in restricted visibility) become the focus of the next drill.

İkinci Zabit, tatbikatları \"yapılmış gö.en: The Second Officer manages drills not as "a formality that must be seen to have been done" but as a real tool for measuring and developing team competence. Once realism is lost, the drill loses its value; if the team does not take the scenario seriously, no automatic reflex will develop for a moment of crisis.

Eğitim, \"anlatıldı\" ile değil, \"yetki.en: Training is complete not when "it has been explained" but when "competence has been gained". The Second Officer measures competence through observation, practical tasks and scenario tests. An officer's ability to use ECDIS safely is considered verified only when the officer can independently enter the correct safety contour and interpret the route check output.

Geri bildirim somut, zamanında ve yapıcı.en: Feedback must be concrete, timely and constructive. Instead of "that was good", specific feedback such as "Your maneuver in the crossing scenario was correct, but you were 3 minutes late; earlier action would have given a much safer CPA" speeds up learning. The Second Officer conveys strengths and areas for improvement in a balanced way.

En yaygın eksiklikler; familiarizasyonun.en: The most common deficiencies are reducing familiarization to a "checklist signed" formality, confusing type-specific ECDIS training with generic training, COLREG remaining a memorized pattern that is not applied to real scenarios, and drills being carried out without realism. Another deficiency is failing to develop the junior team's courage to challenge.

İkinci Zabit ayrıca kendi bilgisini günc.en: The Second Officer must also keep their own knowledge up to date; ECDIS software updates, COLREG interpretations and changes to company procedures must be reflected in the training content. On a bridge where the trainer has fallen behind, the trainee falls behind too.

Köprüüstü ekibinin seyir eğitimi, İkinci.en: Navigation training of the bridge team is the Second Officer's most lasting contribution; a passage plan makes one voyage safe, whereas a well-trained team makes hundreds of voyages safe. A Second Officer who does not reduce familiarization to a formality, who applies COLREG to real scenarios and who instills the BRM culture and the courage to challenge in the team ensures that the error chain is broken at its very first link. As automation increases, the human responsibility for monitoring and questioning does not decrease; on the contrary, the value of training becomes more critical every year.

Doktorsuz bir gemide tıbbi bakım; eğitim.en: On a ship without a doctor, medical care rests on a triangle of a trained officer (usually the Second Officer), the medical guides and the ship's medical chest, and radio medical advice from ashore (TMAS). The Second Officer must hold the "medical care" competence under STCW A-VI/4 and carry this role seriously.

Revir; hasta/yaralı bakımı için ayrılmış.en: The sick bay is a space set aside for the care of sick or injured persons; it must be hygienic, heated/ventilated and provided with the necessary equipment. The Second Officer ensures that the sick bay is clean, tidy and ready for use; the berth, oxygen, stretcher and first-aid equipment are kept accessible.

Tıbbi sandık, bayrak devleti/IMGS listel.en: The medical chest contains specified medicines and supplies according to flag State/IMGS lists. The Second Officer keeps the inventory up to date, monitors expiry dates, adds used-up items and items nearing expiry to the port supply order, and ensures that controlled drugs (narcotics) are recorded and kept locked.

Narkotik/kontrollü ilaçlar kilitli, ayrı.en: Narcotic/controlled drugs are kept locked, recorded separately (controlled drugs register) and generally used under the supervision of two persons. The use, quantity and reason are recorded; missing stock or unrecorded use is a serious legal problem.

İkinci Zabit, ilk yardımda ABCDE (Airway.en: In first aid, the Second Officer assesses the patient systematically using the ABCDE (Airway-Breathing-Circulation-Disability-Exposure) approach, and measures and records the vital signs (pulse, respiration, blood pressure, temperature, level of consciousness). The guide (IMGS) leads from symptoms to diagnosis; however, in serious cases TMAS must always be consulted.

TMAS (Telemedical Assistance Service), g.en: TMAS (Telemedical Assistance Service) are shore-based centers that provide ships with free 24/7 medical advice. The Second Officer passes on the patient data (vital signs, symptoms, history, current medication) clearly and follows the doctor's instructions. A good TMAS consultation decides between correct treatment on board and medevac.

Hastanın gemide tedavi edilemeyeceği dur.en: When the patient cannot be treated on board, medevac (by helicopter or by diversion to the nearest port) is planned on TMAS advice. The Second Officer contributes to coordination with the MRCC, preparation of the patient, documentation and, if applicable, deck preparation for the helicopter operation. The decision rests with the Master; coordination is carried out together with the team.

Her tıbbi olay, tedavi ve ilaç kullanımı.en: Every medical incident, treatment and use of medicine is entered in the medical log book. The Second Officer also organizes first-aid and medical emergency drills; skills such as CPR, bleeding control, fracture immobilization and stretcher carrying are refreshed regularly.

Bulaşıcı hastalık şüphesinde IHR 2005 ka.en: If an infectious disease is suspected, isolation, hygiene measures and notification to the port health authority are required under IHR 2005. The Second Officer supports the Master and the health authority with patient isolation, contact tracing and hygiene measures.

Gemide tıbbi sorumluluk, nadiren kullanı.en: Medical responsibility on board is a form of preparedness that is rarely used but saves lives when it is. The Second Officer's up-to-date medical chest, refreshed skills and effective use of TMAS are a crew's only medical safeguard in the middle of the ocean.

Buz; gövdeye, dümene ve pervaneye hasar.en: Ice can damage the hull, rudder and propeller, restricts maneuvering, reduces speed and creates the risk of besetment. Low temperatures freeze equipment, visibility drops and rescue resources are far away. For this reason, entering ice-covered waters requires a separate risk assessment and preparation.

Geminin ice class'ı (Polar Class veya Fi.en: The ship's ice class (Polar Class or Finnish-Swedish ice class) determines in which ice conditions and with what support (unescorted / under icebreaker escort) she may navigate. The Second Officer provides the Master with data to verify that the planned route is within the capabilities of the ship's ice class.

WMO egg code, buz haritalarında konsantr.en: On ice charts, the WMO egg code summarizes concentration, stage of development (thickness) and floe size. By reading this code, the Second Officer interprets the ice severity along the route and reflects it in the planning.

Buz verisine göre passage plan; en az bu.en: Based on the ice data, the passage plan is revised to give the least ice-covered and safest transit. Open-water leads, icebreaker escort points and escape/refuge areas are identified. The plan is dynamic; the route is updated as the ice moves.

Düşük sıcaklıkta donabilecek hatlar izol.en: Lines that could freeze at low temperatures are insulated, or heated/drained: BWMS, fire main, deck wash, bilge, ballast vents and external lines. The Second Officer checks this preparation in coordination with the engine and deck crews; a frozen fire main is useless in an emergency.

Üst yapı buzlanması (icing/superstructur.en: Superstructure icing (icing) can adversely affect the center of gravity and stability; ice removal on deck is planned. Personnel use suitable PPE and take precautions against frostbite/slipping; work on open deck is restricted.

Buz seyrinde radar (ice detection ayarla.en: In ice navigation, radar (ice detection settings), searchlight, binoculars and careful visual lookout are used together. Small but dangerous pieces of ice such as growlers and bergy bits give weak radar echoes; visual lookout and low speed are therefore critical.

Buzkıran refakatinde belirlenen mesafe v.en: Under icebreaker escort, the specified distance and speed are maintained; communications and signals with the icebreaker are agreed in advance. A safe following distance is kept against the risk of a sudden stop. The Second Officer enters the escort plan and communications in the passage plan.

Buz seyri, hazırlığın seyir emniyetini e.en: Ice navigation is one of the areas in which preparation most directly determines navigational safety. The Second Officer's meticulous ice monitoring, realistic route revision and cold-weather preparation make the ship resilient to the unpredictable conditions of ice.

Kamarot, vardiyaya başlamadan önce sorum.en: Before starting duty, the steward turns their area of responsibility into a clear "cleaning route". A typical route starts with the officer cabins, continues with the alleyways and stairways, covers the messhall and pantry, and then ends with the common toilets/showers (common sanitary) and the dayroom/recreation room. To prevent cross-contamination, the basic principle is to work from clean areas towards dirty areas (cabin → toilet); work is never done in the reverse direction.

Görev dağılımında genellikle subay yaşam.en: In the allocation of duties, officers' accommodation and ratings' accommodation are usually kept to different standards and frequencies, but the level of hygiene must be equal in both. The cabins of the Master, Chief Officer and Chief Engineer and the common areas may be put on a daily program, and some ratings' cabins on a weekly deep-clean program. The steward follows this program using a checklist and records it by signing.

MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1, gemideki yaşam.en: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 requires the accommodation and recreational spaces on board to be of a "decent" standard and to be kept clean and healthy at all times. Standard A3.1 requires an accredited person (usually the Master or an officer authorized by the Master) to inspect the accommodation at regular intervals and the results to be recorded. The steward is the front-line implementer for this inspection; the quality of cleaning directly determines MLC compliance.

Flag state ve PSC denetiminde kirli kama.en: In flag State and PSC inspections, a dirty cabin, a moldy shower, a blocked drain, poor ventilation or signs of pests are recorded directly as a deficiency and, in serious cases, can lead to the ship's detention. The steward's work is therefore not "cosmetic"; it is the front line of regulatory compliance.

Kamarotun temel ekipmanı; mikrofiber bez.en: The steward's basic equipment consists of a set of microfiber cloths, a mop and bucket system (preferably with two buckets, separating clean and dirty water), a broom, a vacuum cleaner, a squeegee, a set of brushes, a garbage trolley and personal protective equipment (gloves, apron and, when necessary, a mask). The equipment itself is also a hygiene factor: dirty cloths and mops become carriers of bacteria. Cloths and mop heads are washed and dried after each use and are not left to go moldy in damp, closed lockers.

Elektrikli süpürge filtresi düzenli temi.en: The vacuum cleaner filter is cleaned regularly; a clogged filter both reduces performance and blows dust and allergens back out. Buckets and brushes are disinfected weekly. Equipment is kept tidy and labeled in the cleaning locker; this locker is one of the areas checked during inspections.

Profesyonel gemi temizliğinde renk kodlu.en: In professional shipboard cleaning, color-coded cleaning is the standard method of preventing cross-contamination. A cloth used for the toilet is never used on a galley worktop or a dining table. This separation is the primary barrier against the spread of norovirus and other fecal-oral pathogens.

Sistem basittir ve hatırlaması kolaydır:.en: The system is simple and easy to remember: each area is assigned a color, and the cloths, buckets and gloves for it are kept in that color. The system stays consistent even when personnel change. The steward applies this discipline without exception.

Her temizlik kimyasalının bir Safety Dat.en: Every cleaning chemical has Safety Data Sheet (SDS) information, and the steward must know the dilution ratio, contact time and incompatibilities of each product used. The most critical rule: never mix bleach (sodium hypochlorite) with acid-based descaler; this mixture releases toxic chlorine gas and is life-threatening in confined areas such as a closed bathroom.

Dezenfektanlar etiketteki temas süresi (.en: Disinfectants are not effective unless they are applied for the contact time stated on the label (the surface generally has to stay wet); a "spray it, wipe it" approach is not disinfection. Chemicals are stored in their original labeled containers, in a ventilated locker away from food.

Sık dokunulan yüzeyler (high-touch surfa.en: High-touch surfaces are the critical points of hygiene: door handles, washbasin taps, toilet seat lids and light switches. These surfaces are not just wiped; they are disinfected. During outbreaks, the frequency of cleaning these points is increased.

Çarşaf, nevresim, yastık kılıfı ve havlu.en: Sheets, duvet covers, pillowcases and towels are changed on a regular schedule; the typical standard is once a week, and immediately if soiled or in case of illness. Used linen goes straight into the laundry trolley/bag; it is never put on the floor or shaken out (shaking spreads dust and microorganisms into the air). When making up the bunk, the corners are folded neatly and the pillow is placed tidily; this is a sign of both comfort and good order during inspections.

Hasta mürettebatın veya bulaşıcı şüphesi.en: The bedding of a sick crew member, or of a person suspected of having an infectious disease, is collected separately, handled with gloves and washed at high temperature without being mixed with other laundry. Mattresses and pillows are aired periodically; damp and mold are the most frequent complaints.

Messhall (yemek salonu) ve dayroom (dinl.en: The messhall and the dayroom are the most heavily used common areas and need cleaning several times a day. Tables are disinfected before meals; after meals, leftovers are cleared, tables are wiped again and the floor is mopped. Shared touch points in these areas, such as the TV, game tables and armchairs, are part of infection control.

Dayroom genellikle mürettebatın dinlendi.en: As the dayroom is usually where the crew relax, cleaning is planned with respect for rest hours. Under the MLC, providing recreational space is the employer's obligation; by keeping this space usable and hygienic, the steward is the one who fulfills this obligation in practice.

Gemi ofisi (ship's office) ve kaptan/zab.en: When the ship's office and the Master's/officers' working areas are cleaned, documents and equipment are not touched; only surfaces and the floor are cleaned. Alleyways and stairways are critical for both hygiene and safety: a wet-mopped floor creates a slipping hazard, so a "wet floor" sign is put out and, where possible, half the width is left dry to allow passage.

Merdiven korkulukları (handrail) sık dok.en: Stair handrails are high-touch surfaces and are disinfected. When emergency exit signs, fire equipment lockers and lighting are cleaned, care is taken that they are never blocked by materials/equipment.

Yaşam mahallinden çıkan çöp; gıda atığı.en: Garbage from the accommodation is separated into food waste, plastics, paper/cardboard, glass, metal and domestic waste. The steward separates this waste in accordance with the ship's approved Garbage Management Plan and the color/label-coded bin system. MARPOL Annex V strictly prohibits, in particular, the discharge of plastics into the sea; all plastics are retained on board and delivered to the port reception facility.

Çöp poşetleri ağzı bağlı, sızdırmaz şeki.en: Garbage bags are carried tied and leak-tight; they are not left standing in alleyways or escape routes. As food waste causes odors and attracts pests, it is emptied as a priority. By separating correctly, the steward also makes accurate entries in the Garbage Record Book possible (responsibility for the record usually lies with a deck officer, but the data from the spaces comes from the steward).

Atık disiplini doğrudan haşere kontrolün.en: Waste discipline is directly linked to pest control. A bin with food scraps left in it, or one emptied late, invites cockroaches, rodents and flies. Garbage trolleys and bins are washed and disinfected after each emptying. The garbage storage area (garbage station) is kept tidy and odor-free.

Ortak sıhhi alanlar (common heads / show.en: Common sanitary areas (common heads/showers) are the areas with the highest infection risk and are disinfected at least twice a day. The inside of the toilet bowl is cleaned with red-coded equipment, and washbasin and shower surfaces with yellow-coded equipment. Particular attention is paid to toilets, shower trays, taps and door handles. The disinfectant is left on the surface for the contact time stated on the label.

Duş alanlarında küf (mould) ve kireç bir.en: Mold and limescale build-up are common in shower areas; a damp environment breeds mold. Ventilation is provided after showers, and moldy grout joints are cleaned with a special product. A blocked drain is both a hygiene and an odor problem; hair/soap blockages are cleared regularly, and serious blockages are reported to the engine/deck crew.

Sıhhi alanlarda tuvalet kâğıdı, kâğıt ha.en: In sanitary areas, toilet paper, paper towels, hand soap and disinfectant are kept stocked at all times; an empty soap dispenser is the weakest link in hygiene because it prevents hand washing. Through stock control, the steward ensures that these consumables never run out.

Gemide tatlı su sınırlı bir kaynaktır. T.en: Fresh water is a limited resource on board. Unnecessary water consumption is avoided during cleaning; in particular, in toilets supplied by the seawater system, the flushing and the lines are checked. Wasting water means both cost and load on bunkers/generators.

Temizlik, hiçbir koşulda emniyet bariyer.en: Cleaning must never, under any circumstances, compromise safety barriers. Fire doors are divisions in the accommodation that delay the spread of fire and smoke; the steward does not hold these doors open with a wedge or chair to make cleaning easier. A fire door left open can have fatal consequences in a real fire.

Kaçış yolları (escape routes) ve acil çı.en: Escape routes and emergency exits are kept clear at all times; cleaning trolleys, mop buckets or garbage bags are not left in these routes. Access to fire extinguisher lockers, hydrants, EEBDs and lifejacket stowage positions is never obstructed. These points are inspected under SOLAS and ISM.

Kamarot çoğu zaman yaşam mahallinde tek.en: The steward often works alone in the accommodation and during quiet hours; the steward is therefore often the first person to notice smoke, a burning smell, abnormal heat or a water leak. Any abnormality is reported immediately to the officer of the watch/bridge; even a smell that seems "minor" is never ignored without being investigated.

Yangın detektörlerinin (smoke detector).en: Smoke detectors are not covered during cleaning and must not be coated with paint/dust. Unauthorized electrical appliances or uncontrolled multi-socket adapters found in cabins and common areas are reported.

Yaşam mahallinin hava kalitesi konfor ve.en: Air quality in the accommodation is fundamental to comfort and health. Ventilation grilles (HVAC grilles) collect dust; a clogged grille both restricts airflow and spreads dust and allergens back into the room. The steward cleans these grilles periodically and reports excessive dust/mold to the engine crew (filter replacement is usually the engine department's responsibility).

Kapalı, nemli kamaralar küf ve kötü koku.en: Closed, damp cabins produce mold and bad odors. Ventilation is provided whenever possible, damp textiles are not put in lockers before being dried, and signs of mold are dealt with by early action.

Tropik ve yüksek nemli bölgelerde küf en.en: In tropical and highly humid regions, mold is the most common problem; bathroom grout joints, the area behind curtains, corners of lockers and the undersides of mattresses are risk points. As mold is both a cosmetic and a respiratory health problem, it is checked regularly and cleaned with an antifungal product.

Denetimde (MLC inspection, PSC, vetting).en: In inspections (MLC inspection, PSC, vetting), the accommodation is the most visible reflection of the ship's operating standards. The inspector checks cabin cleanliness, toilet/shower hygiene, the order of the messhall, garbage management, ventilation and general tidiness. A poor impression leads the inspector to view the whole ship with suspicion, whereas well-kept accommodation builds confidence.

Kamarot, denetim öncesi son kontrolde öz.en: In the final check before an inspection, the steward reviews in particular the high-touch surfaces, the stock of consumables, the cleanliness of the garbage bins and the integrity of escape routes/fire doors. Order must be continuous; the essential thing is to maintain the standard every day rather than doing a one-off clean because "an inspection is coming".

Temizlik programı bir checklist üzerinde.en: The cleaning program is recorded by signing it off on a checklist. During an MLC inspection, this record is the evidence for the claim that "cleaning is done regularly". An incomplete or blank form makes even work that has been done appear "not done".

Kamarotun yaşam mahalli temizliğindeki b.en: The steward's success in cleaning the accommodation directly determines the health and dignity of the environment in which the crew rest, eat and work every day. This work, which demands unseen meticulousness, is the cornerstone of the ship's quality of life, from infection control to fire safety and from MLC compliance to crew morale. Maintaining the standard every day, not just on "inspection day", is the most fundamental professional principle of the steward's job.

Gemide mess, sadece beslenme değil aynı.en: On board, the mess is not only a place to eat but also a place to socialize and relax. A well-prepared messhall and attentive service make the crew feel valued; a mess that is untidy, dirty or serves cold food quickly becomes a source of complaints and low morale. The steward therefore treats service not as a mechanical task but as a service that looks after the crew's welfare.

Gemilerde genellikle subay messi (office.en: On ships, the officers' mess and the crew mess are usually separate; the same standard of hygiene and service is provided in both. Because of watchkeeping, meals are taken at different times; the steward also coordinates keeping a night meal/standby meal ready for those coming off night watches.

MLC 2006 Regulation 3.2, mürettebata ücr.en: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.2 requires the crew to be provided, free of charge, with food that is sufficient in quantity, nutritious and suitable in quality and variety, and with clean drinking water. Standard A3.2 requires food to be provided with respect for religious and cultural diversity and catering staff to be trained. The steward implements this standard on the ground; the quality of service is the visible face of MLC compliance.

Denetimde (MLC inspection) mess düzeni,.en: During an MLC inspection, the order of the mess, hygiene of service, food temperature, cleanliness of drinking water and menu variety are checked. A dirty mess or a breach of hygiene results directly in a finding.

Servisten önce mess \"mise en place\" ma.en: Before service, the mess is prepared on the "mise en place" principle: everything in its place and nothing missing. Tables are disinfected and covered with a clean tablecloth or placemats; cutlery, plates, glasses, napkins, condiments (salt and pepper), water jugs and bread baskets are laid out neatly. The jugs are filled with fresh water. The hot drinks (tea/coffee) station is checked and replenished.

Çatal-bıçak diziminde standart düzen izl.en: A standard layout is followed when setting the cutlery, and the cutlery is kept spotless and clean; a stained fork makes the whole preparation look careless. Depending on the season and the voyage, the setting is kept simple, but the attention to detail never drops.

Servis kapları (chafing dish, bain-marie.en: Serving equipment (chafing dish, bain-marie, cold counter) is prepared according to the type of meal. For hot dishes, the bain-marie/chafing dish is preheated; cold dishes and salads are kept on the cold line. Having this equipment at the correct temperature is the basis for avoiding the "danger zone" (Section 4).

Servis kaşıkları, maşalar ve servis araç.en: Serving spoons, tongs and other serving utensils are kept separate for each dish; using the same spoon in different containers causes cross-contamination (particularly regarding allergens and the separation of raw and cooked food). Working in coordination with the cook, the steward plans the order and layout in which dishes are served.

Servis akışı düzenli ve nazik olmalıdır..en: The flow of service must be orderly and courteous. In a buffet (self-service) layout, dishes are arranged in a logical order: plates → main course → side dishes → salad → bread → dessert → drinks. Personnel must be able to move along without crowding. In messes with table service (usually the officers' mess), attention is paid to the left/right serving rule and to quiet professionalism.

Modern mürettebat çok uluslu ve farklı b.en: Today's crews are multinational, with different dietary needs: religious requirements (halal, vegetarian, pork-free/alcohol-free), allergens (nuts, gluten, seafood) and medical diets (diabetes, low salt) are taken into account during service. Together with the cook, the steward keeps track of these special needs and clearly labels/separates dishes that contain allergens.

Alerjen yönetimi ciddi bir emniyet konus.en: Allergen management is a serious safety issue; a nut or seafood allergy can turn into a medical emergency on board. Cross-use of serving utensils is therefore prohibited, and dishes containing allergens are served separately.

Gıda güvenliğinin kalbi sıcaklık kontrol.en: Temperature control is at the heart of food safety. Bacteria multiply rapidly in the "danger zone" between 5°C and 60°C; food left in this range for a long time carries a risk of food poisoning. Hot food is kept at 60°C or above, and cold food at 5°C or below. Bain-marie and cold counter temperatures are checked throughout service.

\"Soğuk zincir\" ve \"sıcak tutma\" serv.en: The "cold chain" and "hot holding" are basic principles of service: cooked food is quickly brought to serving temperature and is not left in the danger zone until it is served. The longer service lasts, the greater the risk; food that has been left out for a long time is discarded, and a "that'll do" attitude is not accepted.

Çapraz bulaşma (cross-contamination); çi.en: Cross-contamination is the transfer of pathogens from raw to cooked food, from dirty equipment to clean surfaces or from dirty hands to food. Serving utensils are kept separate, surfaces are disinfected and raw and cooked food are kept apart. The WHO "Five Keys to Safer Food" (keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep food at safe temperatures, use safe water and raw materials) form the framework of service discipline.

Kişisel hijyen kritiktir: el yıkama (öze.en: Personal hygiene is critical: hand washing (especially after using the toilet and before service), short clean nails, removal of jewelry, a hairnet and a clean uniform. A steward who is ill or has symptoms of infection (diarrhea, vomiting) must not serve food and must report the condition; a foodborne outbreak can paralyze the ship.

Servis sırasında buffet sürekli izlenir:.en: During service, the buffet is monitored continuously: dishes running low are replenished, spills are cleaned up and water/drinks are topped up. An empty dish or bread that has run out is a failure of service. The steward stays in constant contact with the galley and warns the cook in advance when food is running low.

Vardiyalı düzen nedeniyle herkes aynı an.en: Because of the watch system, not everyone comes to eat at the same time. For watchkeepers who come late, the steward ensures that food is kept hot/suitable or is plated and stored. The night meal arrangement is decisive for the morale of those working at night.

Mess, dinlenme ve sosyalleşme alanıdır;.en: The mess is a place to relax and socialize; the steward ensures that it stays clean, tidy and welcoming. Dirty plates piling up around the tables are cleared promptly, and spills are wiped up immediately. Temperature, ventilation and lighting are kept comfortable.

Servis bittiğinde toplama düzenli yapılı.en: When service is over, clearing is done in an orderly way: first, food leftovers are separated according to the MARPOL Annex V categories (food waste separately), dirty plates are taken to the dishwashing area and the tables are cleared. Because of the risk of odors and pests, food waste is dealt with without delay. Serving dishes are emptied and taken for washing.

Artan yemeğin değerlendirilmesi gıda güv.en: Using leftover food is subject to food safety rules: food that has been in the danger zone for a long time is discarded; food that has been properly and rapidly cooled and stored can be used under specific rules and reheated once only. Keeping unsafe food with the idea of "let's not waste it" is a food poisoning risk.

Masalar ve sandalyeler dezenfekte edilir.en: Tables and chairs are disinfected, the floor is swept and mopped, and condiment sets and jugs are cleaned and refilled. The mess is set up again in mise en place for the next meal, so that the next service always starts ready.

Çatal-bıçak ve servis araçları yıkanıp k.en: Cutlery and serving utensils are washed, dried and put away in a clean cupboard; cutlery put away damp picks up stains and germs. This cycle is repeated at every meal.

İçme suyu (potable water), MLC ve gemi s.en: Drinking water (potable water) is as critical as food under the MLC and ship sanitation requirements. Water jugs and drinks stations are kept clean, and water taps/dispenser nozzles are disinfected. Water quality (chlorination, quality tests) is usually the responsibility of the deck/engine departments, but cleanliness at the point of service belongs to the steward.
