Buz makinesi (ice machine) sık ihmal edi.en: The ice machine is a frequently neglected source of contamination; if it is not cleaned regularly, it breeds bacteria/mold. Ice is taken with a clean scoop, never directly by hand or with a glass.

Mess'teki sürekli açık çay/kahve istasyo.en: The tea/coffee station in the mess is always open and accessible to the crew 24/7. The steward keeps this station clean, stocked and working; the machines are cleaned regularly, and milk, sugar and other consumables are never allowed to run out. These small details make a big difference to morale.

Limanda gelen surveyor, PSC/vetting insp.en: In port, service to visiting surveyors, PSC/vetting inspectors or guests creates the first impression of the ship. The meeting room/saloon is prepared, and refreshments are served neatly and hygienically. The standard of the mess and service offered to inspectors gives an impression of the ship's general discipline.

Ağır havada (heavy weather) mess servisi.en: In heavy weather, mess service carries a safety risk: hot food and boiling water can be knocked over by the ship's rolling and cause serious burns. In these conditions, fiddles (table-edge rails) and non-slip mats are used, jugs are only partly filled, hot drinks are carried covered and service is simplified. Personnel move carefully to avoid slipping and falling.

Yemek servisi, kamarotluğun mürettebatla.en: Meal service is the part of the steward's job in most direct contact with the crew. A hot, hygienic, varied and carefully served meal is the most valuable service there is: it eases the fatigue of long voyages, holds the team together and keeps up the ship's morale. Temperature control and hygiene discipline are the non-negotiable safety foundation of this service.

Çamaşırhane/depo iki risk taşır: yanlış.en: The laundry/store carries two risks: toxic gas/corrosion from chemicals mixed incorrectly, and fire caused by lint from the dryer/washing machine igniting. Because the steward uses these areas frequently, the steward is the natural lookout for both risks and prevents them through correct practices.

Kamarot; çamaşır deterjanı, ağartıcı, de.en: The steward stores laundry detergent, bleach, disinfectants and cleaning chemicals in accordance with the SDS information. Incompatible groups (acids/alkalis, oxidizers) are kept apart, containers are correctly labeled and chemicals are kept in their original containers. A chemical stored unlabeled or in the wrong container is a serious accident risk.

Kimyasal elleçlerken kamarot uygun KKD (.en: When handling chemicals, the steward uses suitable PPE (gloves and, if necessary, goggles) and ensures ventilation. A spill is cleaned up in accordance with the SDS. Concentrated chemicals are diluted in the correct ratio; incorrect use causes both skin/respiratory harm and surface damage.

Çamaşırhane havalandırmasındaki fire dam.en: The fire damper in the laundry ventilation and the smoke/heat detectors limit the spread of a fire and give early warning. The steward makes sure this equipment is not obstructed and takes part in the checks/tests. A damper/detector that does not work is reported immediately.

Çamaşırhane ve depo düzenli, temiz ve ya.en: The laundry and store are kept tidy, clean and free of combustible accumulations. A cluttered area increases the risk of both fire and accidents. The steward keeps these areas in order at all times and does not allow combustible waste to accumulate.

Çamaşırhane ve depo kimyasal güvenliği,.en: Chemical safety in the laundry and store is an important task in which the steward manages two serious risks — chemical accidents and fire — in a "seemingly harmless" area. Storage in accordance with the SDS, regular lint cleaning and working fire equipment keep these silent risks under control and protect the ship and crew.

Galley'de aşçı pişirmeden, kamarot ise t.en: In the galley, the cook is responsible for cooking, and the steward for cleaning, dishwashing and preparation support; this division of work determines the flow of service. On the cook's instructions, the steward draws ingredients from the stores, does simple preparation (washing/chopping vegetables, weighing ingredients) and takes on all the dishwashing and cleaning after service. Good coordination allows two people to work efficiently in a small galley.

Galley, geminin en yüksek gıda riski taş.en: The galley is the area of the ship with the highest food risk; hot surfaces, sharp tools, boiling liquids and the risk of pathogens all come together there. In this environment, the steward constantly maintains both hygiene and occupational safety discipline.

Kirli veya yetersiz yıkanmış tabak-çatal.en: Dirty or inadequately washed plates and cutlery are a direct route of contamination to the mouth. A cutting board washed incorrectly can carry pathogens from raw meat to cooked food. Dishwashing is therefore not just "removing dirt" but a food safety process, and it must be done by the correct method (wash → rinse → sanitize).

MLC denetiminde galley hijyeni, bulaşık.en: During an MLC inspection, galley hygiene, the order of the dishwashing area, equipment cleanliness and storage are checked. A greasy, dirty or untidy galley results directly in an MLC finding and undermines confidence in the ship's food safety management.

Profesyonel bulaşık, üç aşamalı sistemle.en: Professional dishwashing is done with a three-stage system: (1) pre-scraping and washing in hot water with detergent (grease and residue are dissolved), (2) rinsing in clean hot water (detergent residue is removed), (3) sanitizing (killing germs with high-temperature water or a chemical sanitizer). A single-stage "wipe with detergent and leave" is not hygienic dishwashing.

Elde yıkamada genellikle üç gözlü evye (.en: For washing by hand, a three-compartment sink (wash–rinse–sanitize) is generally used. Sanitizing is done either with very hot water (≈82°C) or with an approved chemical sanitizer. When sanitizing with hot water, gloves are worn because of the risk of burns. Air-drying is preferred to drying with a tea towel; a dirty cloth recontaminates.

Bulaşık makinesi varsa, doğru kullanım k.en: Where a dishwasher is fitted, correct use is critical: plates are first roughly scraped and loaded correctly (the water jets must reach every surface), the correct detergent and rinse-aid dosage is ensured and the machine's wash/rinse temperature is checked. In industrial machines, the rinse water should be about 82-85°C; this temperature provides sanitization.

Makine her gün sonunda boşaltılıp temizl.en: At the end of each day, the machine is drained and cleaned; cleaning the filter, checking for scale and emptying the strainer are routine maintenance. A clogged filter both impairs washing and produces odors and bacteria. A machine fault (not heating, not filling with water) is reported immediately; dishes washed at low temperature are not sanitized.

Çapraz bulaşmanın en tehlikeli yolu, çiğ.en: The most dangerous route of cross-contamination is preparing raw meat/poultry/fish and cooked food or salad with the same board/knife. Professional kitchens use color-coded cutting boards (e.g. red: raw meat, blue: raw fish, green: vegetables/fruit, white: cooked food/dairy). In preparation support, the steward applies this separation meticulously.

Çiğ tavuk ve et, Salmonella ve Campyloba.en: Raw poultry and meat carry serious pathogens such as Salmonella and Campylobacter; if these pathogens pass to cooked food, they cause an outbreak on board. After each use, the board and knife are washed and sanitized, and hands are washed after handling raw products.

Bıçak emniyeti, gemi mutfağında en sık i.en: Knife handling is one of the most frequent sources of occupational accidents in the ship's galley. A blunt knife is more dangerous than a sharp one because it needs more pressure and slips. Knives are kept sharp and clean and are stored correctly (knife block/magnetic strip); they are never left in the sink under the suds — a hand reaching in blindly gets a serious cut.

Doğrama sırasında \"köprü tutuş\" ve doğ.en: When chopping, the "bridge hold" and correct cutting technique are used, and fingers are kept clear of the blade. In heavy weather, chopping is postponed or reduced where possible; knife control becomes difficult when the ship is rolling. In the event of a cut, the food is contaminated and first aid is given.

Kamarot, aşçının talimatıyla basit ön ha.en: On the cook's instructions, the steward does simple preparation: washing, peeling and chopping vegetables and fruit, weighing ingredients and taking them out of the refrigerator. Vegetables are washed thoroughly to remove dirt and any residues; this is part of food safety. Chopping is done to the size and arrangement the cook requires.

Hazırlanan malzeme, kullanılana kadar uy.en: Prepared ingredients are kept at a suitable temperature until they are used; ingredients left at room temperature for a long time enter the danger zone. Raw meat/poultry is prepared last or in a separate area, and surfaces are sanitized afterwards.

Buzdolabı ve dondurucu düzeni gıda güven.en: The organization of refrigerators and freezers is fundamental to food safety. Raw food is always stored on the bottom shelf (so that drips do not contaminate cooked food), and cooked/ready-to-eat food on the top shelf. Storage follows the "FIFO" (first in, first out) principle: what arrives first is used first, and older stock is moved to the front. Opened food is transferred to a covered container and labeled (with the date).

Buzdolabı sıcaklığı (0-5°C) ve dondurucu.en: Refrigerator (0-5°C) and freezer (≤ -18°C) temperatures are checked regularly; doors are not left open for long. Products that are past their expiry date or spoiled are set aside and reported to the cook. A well-organized cold store prevents both safety problems and waste of stock.

Servis ve hazırlık sonrası tüm çalışma y.en: After service and preparation, all work surfaces (worktops, cutting area), the area around the range, the sink and touch points are cleaned and sanitized. Food-contact surfaces are cleaned with green-coded equipment. Grease build-up is removed; accumulated grease is both a hygiene and a fire risk.

Mikrodalga, fırın, mikser, et kıyma maki.en: Equipment such as the microwave, oven, mixer and meat mincer is cleaned after use; equipment that can be dismantled is taken apart and washed. Care is taken with hot surfaces, and electrical equipment is unplugged before cleaning.

Davlumbaz (galley range hood) ve yağ fil.en: The galley range hood and grease filters are cleaned regularly; accumulated grease is the most common cause of galley fires. A greasy filter can catch fire and carry the fire into the ventilation duct. This cleaning is done weekly/on a schedule and is never neglected.

Yer giderleri (floor drains) ve evye süz.en: Floor drains and sink strainers are cleared regularly; a blocked drain causes odors and standing water (slipping hazard) and attracts pests. Pouring grease down the drain causes blockages; grease is collected separately.

Galley iş kazaları açısından geminin en.en: The galley is one of the riskiest areas of the ship for occupational accidents: hot surfaces, boiling liquids, hot oil and sharp tools all come together. Hot pans are carried with gloves, boiling water is poured off carefully, and water is never poured onto hot oil. The floor is not left wet/greasy; non-slip shoes are worn.

Ağır havada galley operasyonu özel riskt.en: Galley operation in heavy weather is a particular risk: a pot of boiling liquid tipped over by rolling causes serious burns. In bad weather, range fiddles (pot clamps) are used, pans are only partly filled and high-risk cooking/chopping is reduced. In these conditions, the steward moves more slowly and uses grab rails/handrails.

Galley'de yağ/fritöz yangınına asla su i.en: In the galley, water is never used on a cooking oil/deep-fryer fire; water makes the hot oil erupt, spreading the fire and causing serious burns. In a cooking oil fire, the heat source is cut off, a fire blanket or an extinguisher of the appropriate class is used (a special extinguisher is usually provided in the galley) and the alarm is raised immediately.

Yıkanan ve kurutulan tabaklar, bardaklar.en: Washed and dried plates, glasses, cutlery and serving dishes are put away in their correct places in tidy, clean cupboards. Items put away damp pick up stains and germs; thorough drying is essential. Well-organized crockery storage allows the next service to start quickly and hygienically.

Servis kaşıkları, maşalar ve özel servis.en: Serving spoons, tongs and special serving utensils are cleaned and kept separate. Broken/cracked plates and glasses are removed from use; a cracked surface carries the risk of both injury and harboring bacteria.

Bulaşık alanı her vardiya sonunda temizl.en: The dishwashing area is cleaned at the end of each working period; the sink, worktop and floor are sanitized. Food waste is separated in accordance with MARPOL Annex V and emptied without delay. Cooking oil and grease are collected separately and are not poured down the drain. A tidy dishwashing area is the measure of the galley's overall hygiene.

Bulaşık ve mutfak desteği görünürde sıra.en: Dishwashing and galley support may look ordinary, but they are in fact the cornerstone of food safety on board. A correctly washed plate, a correctly separated cutting board and a clean galley quietly prevent an outbreak. Doing this task meticulously protects both the health of the crew and the ship's uninterrupted voyage.

Gemi çamaşırhanesi (ship's laundry) tipi.en: The ship's laundry typically contains industrial or semi-industrial washing machines, a tumble dryer, an iron/ironing board, laundry trolleys and a bag system that keeps dirty and clean laundry apart. The steward sets up a one-way workflow: "dirty in → sorting → washing → drying → folding/ironing → clean out". The paths of dirty and clean laundry never cross; this is the basic principle for preventing cross-contamination.

Çamaşır toplama programı genellikle yata.en: The laundry collection schedule is usually weekly for bedding and as needed for uniforms and personal laundry. Depending on the ship's practice, officers' and ratings' laundry may be tracked with separate schedules or labeling, but the hygiene standard is the same for both. The steward applies the labeling/bagging system meticulously so as not to mix up which laundry has come from which cabin.

MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 ve Standard A3.1.en: MLC 2006 Regulation 3.1 and Standard A3.1 require suitable facilities on board for the crew to wash their laundry and maintain personal hygiene. Keeping the laundry working, clean and accessible is the employer's obligation; the steward is the one who delivers this facility on the ground. A broken washing machine or a dirty laundry is a direct finding (deficiency) in an MLC inspection.

Temiz yatak takımı ve havlu sağlamak, sa.en: Providing clean bedding and towels is not just a matter of comfort but of health. Textiles that are not changed regularly, are poorly dried or are moldy cause skin infections, allergies and respiratory problems. The steward manages these risks by keeping the laundry cycle running without interruption.

Yıkama öncesi ayrıştırma, hem çamaşırın.en: Sorting before washing determines both the life of the laundry and the standard of hygiene. Whites and light colors are separated from dark colors; otherwise color bleeding spoils the whole load. Fabric types are also separated: delicates, towels, sheets and uniforms require different programs and temperatures. Heavily soiled or oily work clothes are never washed in the same load as clean textiles.

Kirlilik düzeyi ayrıştırmanın kritik boy.en: The degree of soiling is a critical aspect of sorting. Laundry from sick crew members, textiles contaminated with blood/body fluids and oily clothes from the galley/deck are collected separately and processed separately. This separation prevents cross-contamination and the spread of infection. Pockets are checked before items go into the washing machine; a forgotten lighter, pen or metal object can ruin both the laundry and the machine.

Bazı lekeler (kan, çay/kahve, yağ, mürek.en: Some stains (blood, tea/coffee, oil/grease, ink) do not come out in a normal wash; pre-treatment is required. The type of stain is identified and the appropriate pre-treatment is applied: protein-based stains (blood) are treated with cold water, because hot water coagulates the protein and sets the stain. Oil-based stains, on the other hand, need pre-treatment and a higher temperature.

Ön işlem kimyasalları da kontrollü kulla.en: Pre-treatment chemicals are also used in a controlled way; too much bleach wears out fabric and causes yellowing/thinning. The steward avoids the "bleach for every stain" approach, applies the right product to the right stain and follows the washing instructions on the fabric care label.

Deterjan dozajı, su sertliği ve çamaşır.en: Detergent dosage is adjusted according to water hardness and the amount of laundry. Too much detergent is not fully removed in rinsing; it leaves residues in textiles, irritates the skin and damages the machine. Too little detergent weakens cleaning and disinfection. The steward follows the dosage instructions on the product label and the machine capacity; measured use, rather than "guesswork", is essential.

Yumuşatıcı (fabric softener) konfor sağl.en: Fabric softener adds comfort but, as it reduces the absorbency of towels, it is used sparingly on towels. Bleach (sodium hypochlorite) is used in a controlled way, only on whites and where disinfection is needed; it fades colors and wears out fabric. The most critical rule: bleach is never used together with acid-based products, as toxic chlorine gas is released.

Çamaşır makinesi ne aşırı doldurulur ne.en: A washing machine is neither overfilled nor underloaded. An overfilled machine does not wash or rinse properly; too small a load wastes water and energy. Laundry is put in loosely, not packed in. The program is selected according to the fabric type and degree of soiling; a high temperature disinfects but damages delicate textiles.

Gemide tatlı su ve enerji sınırlı kaynak.en: On board, fresh water and energy are limited resources. The steward avoids starting unnecessary cycles before a full load has been collected; this means saving water/energy and reducing the generator load. When washing is complete, laundry is not left in the machine; it produces damp and odors.

Kurutucu (tumble dryer), çamaşırı hızlı.en: The tumble dryer dries laundry quickly, but incorrect use puts both the textiles and the machine at risk. Excessive heat shrinks delicate fabrics and damages the fibers; an overfilled dryer dries unevenly and wastes energy. The temperature is selected according to the fabric type, and delicate textiles are dried at low heat or hung up.

Kurutucudan çıkan çamaşır tamamen kuruma.en: Laundry from the dryer is not folded and put in lockers until it is completely dry; damp textiles produce mold and odors. The steward checks that laundry is dry before folding it and processes again any items that are still damp.

Çamaşırhanedeki en ciddi yangın riski, k.en: The most serious fire risk in the laundry is the combustible fluff that builds up in the dryer's lint filter and exhaust duct. Accumulated lint can be ignited by the dryer's heat and lead to a fire on board; P&I and loss prevention records frequently report laundry fires caused by lint. The lint filter is therefore cleaned after EVERY cycle, and the exhaust duct is checked periodically.

Ütüleme, kumaş tipine göre sıcaklık ayar.en: Ironing requires the temperature to be set according to the fabric type: cotton is ironed at high heat and synthetics at low heat; the wrong temperature melts synthetic fabric or yellows and scorches cotton. The ironing board is set up properly, the iron is left standing upright, and it is never left switched on and unattended while hot. The risk of burns with a steam iron is high; care is taken with the water reservoir and steam vents.

Ütü, kullanılmadığında mutlaka fişten çe.en: When not in use, the iron is always unplugged and left to cool. A hot iron forgotten on fabric or a combustible surface is one of the common causes of laundry fires. After ironing, the steward makes sure the iron is switched off and unplugged and is not put away until it has cooled completely.

Temiz, kuru çamaşır düzgün katlanır ve s.en: Clean, dry laundry is folded neatly and returned correctly to its owner/cabin. The labeling or bagging system ensures that laundry does not get mixed up; it is particularly important for privacy and trust that personal laundry reaches the right person. Bedding is distributed to the relevant cabins, and the surplus is stored neatly in the clean linen locker.

Temiz çamaşır, kirli çamaşırın bulunduğu.en: Clean laundry is kept covered and separate from the area where dirty laundry is kept. Clean laundry is not put next to the dirty laundry trolley; this causes cross-contamination. The linen locker is kept clean, dry and tidy; clean laundry stored in a damp environment goes moldy.

Çamaşırhane ekipmanı, hijyen kaynağı old.en: Laundry equipment is a factor in hygiene, and it also needs maintenance. The washing machine drum is cleaned periodically with an empty high-temperature cycle or a machine cleaner; otherwise detergent residue, mold and bad odors build up. The detergent drawer and the door seal (door gasket) are cleaned regularly; these are the most common places for mold to grow.

Kurutucu lint filtresi her çevrimde, egz.en: The dryer lint filter is cleaned after every cycle and the exhaust duct periodically. If abnormal noise, vibration, a water leak or overheating is noticed in the machines, they are not operated, and this is reported to the engine crew/the person responsible for technical matters. The steward is responsible for basic cleaning and filter maintenance; electrical/mechanical faults are left to the authorized team.

Çamaşırhane mahalli her gün temizlenir;.en: The laundry space is cleaned every day; the floor is swept and mopped, worktops are wiped and lint/dust deposits are removed. Lint accumulating on the floor is both a slipping hazard and fuel for a fire. Drains and water outlets are checked for blockages; a blocked drain causes flooding and odors.

Çamaşırhane havalandırması önemlidir; ne.en: Ventilation of the laundry is important; a damp, hot environment produces mold and stuffy air. Ventilation grilles are kept clean, and moisture is removed by leaving the door/vent open. Laundry trolleys and bags are washed and disinfected regularly; equipment that carries dirty laundry is a carrier of bacteria.

Çamaşırhanenin kesintisiz çalışması, det.en: Uninterrupted operation of the laundry depends on detergent, softener, bleach, stain remover and pre-treatment products being kept in stock at all times. The steward sets a minimum stock level for these products and raises a resupply request when stock approaches that level. "Reporting when it runs out" is too late; running out of stock on long voyages stops the laundry cycle.

Stok takibi basit bir envanter listesiyl.en: Stock is tracked with a simple inventory list: product name, quantity on hand, rate of consumption and reorder point. By monitoring consumption, the steward forecasts how much is needed for a typical voyage and passes the resupply request to the person responsible for provisions (usually the chief cook or the Chief Officer).

Çamaşırhane kimyasalları (özellikle çama.en: Laundry chemicals (especially oxidizers such as bleach, and acid-based products) are stored separately and labeled, in accordance with the SDS information. Oxidizers (hypochlorite) and acids are kept on separate shelves; accidental contact between them causes a dangerous reaction. Chemicals are kept in their original labeled containers; decanting them into unlabeled containers is both misuse and a legal violation.

Depo havalandırılmış, gıdadan ve ısı kay.en: The store is kept ventilated and away from food and heat sources. In the event of a spill, the response instructions in the SDS are followed. The steward must know the dilution ratio, contact time and incompatibilities of every chemical used.

Bulaşıcı hastalık şüphesi olan veya kan/.en: Laundry from a suspected infectious case, or contaminated with blood/body fluids, is collected and processed separately without being mixed with other laundry. These textiles are handled with gloves, kept in a separate bag and washed at high temperature (above 60°C where possible) so that they are disinfected. Shaking them out is prohibited; shaking spreads microorganisms into the air. Afterwards, hands are washed and the equipment used is disinfected.

Norovirus, deri enfeksiyonları ve solunu.en: Norovirus, skin infections and respiratory pathogens spread easily via contaminated textiles. During outbreaks (COVID, norovirus, etc.), the laundry handling protocol is tightened: separate collection, high temperature, extra disinfection and increased use of personal protective equipment.

Kamarot, kirli çamaşır ve kimyasallarla.en: When working with dirty laundry and chemicals, the steward uses personal protective equipment: gloves and, when necessary, an apron and mask. Hands are always washed after handling laundry, and especially after contact with contaminated textiles. The laundry is kept physically and operationally separate from food preparation; the steward pays attention to hand hygiene when moving between the two.

Renk kodlu temizlik mantığı çamaşırhaney.en: The color-coded cleaning principle extends to the laundry as well: equipment used for contaminated textiles is not mixed with clean items. Laundry bags and trolleys are disinfected regularly; this equipment is an unseen but critical link in the hygiene chain.

Gemide tatlı su (fresh water) sınırlı ve.en: On board, fresh water is a limited and valuable resource; it is either bunkered or produced by the fresh water generator. Washing laundry consumes a lot of water, so running full loads, avoiding unnecessary cycles and choosing the correct program are the basis of saving water. Excessive rinsing wastes water; the correct detergent dosage gives adequate cleaning with less rinsing.

Çamaşır makinesi ve kurutucu yüksek ener.en: Washing machines and dryers draw a lot of power, and this power comes from the generators. Saving energy means saving fuel (bunkers) and reducing emissions. By planning laundry runs around the high-load periods of the bridge/engine room, the steward can help balance the electrical load.

Çamaşırhaneden çıkan ambalaj atığı (dete.en: Packaging waste from the laundry (detergent drums, plastic, cardboard) is separated in accordance with MARPOL Annex V. Plastic waste is never discharged into the sea; it is retained on board and landed in port. Empty chemical containers are handled according to the SDS instructions; some may fall into the hazardous waste category and are collected separately.

Lint atığı da düzenli toplanır; çöpe atı.en: Lint waste is also collected regularly; when it is disposed of, it is borne in mind that it is combustible, and it is kept away from heat/sources of ignition. By separating waste correctly, the steward contributes to the ship's compliance with the Garbage Management Plan.

Çamaşırhane hizmetleri, kamarotun mürett.en: Laundry services are among the steward's tasks that most directly affect crew welfare: clean bedding, dry towels and neat uniforms are a quiet but decisive part of the ship's quality of life. This task also has a serious safety dimension; the risk of lint fires and chemical mixing makes the laundry one of the hidden fire points on board. When correct sorting, chemical discipline, lint control and stock tracking come together, the laundry becomes a reliable part of both MLC compliance and fire safety. Maintaining the standard every day is the fundamental professional principle of the steward's job.

Sarf malzeme, hijyenin görünmeyen lojist.en: Consumables are the unseen logistics of hygiene. By ensuring that supplies are replenished before they run out, the steward guarantees that the accommodation stays clean and comfortable at all times. An item that is not requested in time may be unavailable for the whole voyage.

Kamarot; temizlik kimyasalları (deterjan.en: The steward monitors cleaning chemicals (detergent, disinfectant, glass/surface cleaner), paper products (toilet paper, paper towels), soap/hand sanitizer, laundry supplies and general accommodation consumables. The current stock (ROB) and rate of consumption of each item are recorded.

Stok minimuma yaklaşan kalemler için kam.en: For items whose stock is approaching the minimum, the steward prepares a requisition and passes it to the responsible officer (usually the Chief Officer/Master). The requisition contains the item, current stock, quantity required and urgency. Accurate forecasting prevents both shortages and unnecessary overstocking.

Temizlik kimyasalları, SDS bilgisine uyg.en: Cleaning chemicals are stored in accordance with the SDS information; incompatible chemicals (acids/alkalis, oxidizers) are kept apart and stored in labeled containers. The steward oversees safe storage and the integrity of labels; incorrect mixing can cause a dangerous reaction.

Kamarot, stok hareketlerini (ikmal, tüke.en: The steward records stock movements (resupply, consumption). This record shows the consumption trend and makes planning the next resupply easier. A regular inventory prevents both waste and shortages.

Sarf malzeme stok takibi, kamarotun yaşa.en: Tracking consumable stock is the unseen logistics that allows the steward to maintain hygiene in the accommodation without interruption. Knowing consumption, requesting in time and storing chemicals safely together protect hygiene, crew comfort and safety.

Gemi, kalabalık ve kapalı bir ortamdır;.en: A ship is a crowded, closed environment; an infection can spread quickly and is difficult to manage with limited medical facilities. By maintaining hygiene, the steward prevents illness at the outset. Clean accommodation is critical for health, morale and inspections alike.

Kamarot; banyo/tuvaletleri, ortak alanla.en: The steward regularly cleans and disinfects bathrooms/toilets, common areas (mess, saloon, alleyways) and high-touch surfaces (door handles, handrails, switches). The correct disinfectant is used with the correct contact time; a hasty wipe does not disinfect.

Yaşam mahalli çöpü ayrıştırılır ve MARPO.en: Garbage from the accommodation is separated and managed in accordance with MARPOL Annex V; food waste, plastics and other garbage are handled differently. The steward ensures that garbage is collected hygienically and delivered to the correct disposal point (incinerator/shore reception). Accumulated garbage creates both a hygiene and a pest risk.

COVID, norovirus gibi bulaşıcı hastalık.en: During periods of infectious disease risk such as COVID or norovirus, the frequency and intensity of cleaning are increased; high-touch surfaces are disinfected more often and, if there is isolation, the areas concerned are cleaned under a separate protocol. The steward applies these enhanced protocols meticulously; in an outbreak, hygiene is the first line of defense.

Salgın döneminde veya izolasyon alanı te.en: During an outbreak or when cleaning an isolation area, the steward uses suitable PPE (gloves, mask) and also protects their own health. Contaminated waste is collected separately. The steward's health is important for continuity of service.

Hijyen, haşere (hamamböceği, kemirgen) k.en: Hygiene is the basis of pest control (cockroaches, rodents); food scraps and dirt attract pests. The steward prevents pests through cleaning and reports any signs seen (droppings, tracks, live pests). The steward supports the pest management program (traps, bait).

Hijyen ve sağlık standartlarının korunma.en: Maintaining hygiene and health standards is the steward's direct contribution to the health of the crew. Regular cleaning, correct disinfection, garbage management and outbreak protocols are the most effective defense for preventing illness in a closed environment and keeping the accommodation healthy.

Acil durumda kamarot \"servis personeli\.en: In an emergency, the steward is not "service staff" but a crew member with assigned duties. The steward knows and carries out the role defined in the Station Bill. As one of the people who know the accommodation best, the steward can play a valuable role in evacuating it and in the head count.

Alarm çaldığında kamarot, can yeleğiyle.en: When the alarm sounds, the steward goes to the muster station with a lifejacket and carries out the assigned duty. The steward knows where the lifejacket is and how to put it on correctly, the alarm signals and the muster point. These basic skills are reinforced by repetition in drills.

Yaşam mahallindeki yangın kapıları (fire.en: Fire doors in the accommodation are kept closed; wedging them open allows fire/smoke to spread. Escape routes must be kept clear and unobstructed at all times. The steward follows these rules while working and corrects/reports violations (wedged doors, blocked routes).

Kamarot, Station Bill'e göre yaralı bakı.en: In accordance with the Station Bill, the steward may assist the casualty care party (stretcher, first-aid support) or the head count. As the steward knows the accommodation well, the steward plays a valuable role in checking cabins and confirming that no one has been left behind.

Kamarot yaşam mahallinde çok dolaştığı i.en: Because the steward moves around the accommodation a great deal, the steward may be the first person to notice signs of fire (smoke, smell, heat). In such a case, the steward raises the alarm immediately and acts according to the procedure. Early detection and a quick alarm prevent a fire from growing.

Emniyet ve acil durum görevleri, kamarot.en: Safety and emergency duties are among the steward's most important responsibilities on board; beyond the service role, the steward contributes to saving lives as a crew member. Knowing one's duty, following fire door/escape route discipline and the reflex to raise the alarm early make the difference in a real emergency.

Bir denetçi gemiye geldiğinde, ilk gördü.en: When an inspector comes on board, the condition of the accommodation, which is the first thing seen, creates an impression of the ship's general maintenance culture. A clean, tidy environment inspires confidence, whereas an untidy one may trigger a stricter inspection. The steward plays a direct role in forming this impression.

Kamarot; gelen surveyor, denetçi, acente.en: The steward provides courteous and professional service to visiting surveyors, inspectors, agents and guests. Drinks/refreshments are prepared, the meeting area is set up and the guests' comfort is ensured. Professional hospitality reflects the ship's corporate image.

Denetim/toplantı öncesi kamarot, toplant.en: Before an inspection/meeting, the steward prepares the meeting room/saloon: cleanliness, tidiness, the necessary items (water, coffee, seating) and general comfort. A ready, tidy room helps the meeting run efficiently and the ship appear professional.

Ziyaretçi yönetimi, ISPS güvenlik kurall.en: Visitor management must comply with the ISPS security rules; visitors are registered, escorted and restricted to authorized areas. During service, the steward follows the security rules and reports unauthorized access/suspicious situations to the responsible officer.

Yaşam mahallinin denetim standardına uyg.en: Keeping the accommodation up to inspection standard is a job done every day, not only on the day of a visit. By keeping the environment consistently tidy, the steward ensures that the ship is ready even for an unannounced inspection. Living conditions under the MLC are also part of this order.

Ziyaretçi ve misafir yönetimi desteği, k.en: Supporting visitor and guest management is the steward's contribution to the ship's corporate image and to successful inspections. Tidy accommodation, professional hospitality and security awareness strengthen the impression that the ship is well managed and pave the way for inspections to go well.

Revir, hasta/yaralı bakımı için ayrılmış.en: The sick bay is a space set aside for the care of sick/injured persons and must be clean, tidy and ready for use at all times. A dirty or untidy sick bay both puts patient care at risk and results directly in an MLC non-conformity finding during inspections. The steward ensures this readiness of the sick bay every day.

Kamarot; revirin zemini, yatak/yatak tak.en: The steward regularly cleans and disinfects the sick bay floor, berth/bedding, worktop, washbasin and instruments. Sanitation checks (ventilation, odor, hygiene) are carried out. Medical instruments and surfaces are kept clean so as to reduce the risk of infection.

Revirde yatan hasta mürettebata kamarot;.en: For sick crew members confined to the sick bay, the steward brings meals, drinks and basic necessities and ensures the comfort of the room (temperature, ventilation, cleanliness). Suitable food for the patient (light/diet food if necessary) is coordinated with the cook. This support contributes to the patient's recovery and morale.

Bulaşıcı hastalık şüphesinde kamarot, ar.en: If an infectious disease is suspected, the steward applies enhanced disinfection protocols: frequent and intensive disinfection, particularly of toilets, shared surfaces and the patient's room. The steward uses suitable PPE (gloves, mask), collects contaminated waste separately and works in a way that prevents cross-contamination.

Kamarot, hasta bakımı ve revir temizliği.en: During patient care and sick bay cleaning, the steward also protects their own health, using PPE and paying attention to hand hygiene. The steward's health is important for continuity of service and for protecting the rest of the crew.

Kamarot, tıbbi sorumlu zabit (genelde İk.en: The steward works in coordination with the officer responsible for medical care (usually the Second Officer/Medical Officer) and reports changes in the patient's condition (not eating, fever, deterioration). Cleanliness of the sick bay and patient comfort are teamwork that complements medical care.

Revir temizliği ve tıbbi yardım desteği,.en: Sick bay cleaning and medical support is a task through which the steward contributes directly to the recovery of sick crew members and to the ship's MLC compliance. A sick bay that is always ready, attentive patient care and meticulous infection control protect both the individual's health and the hygiene of the whole ship.

Yaşam mahalli yangınları çoğu zaman küçü.en: Accommodation fires often start from a small moment of carelessness — an unextinguished cigarette, an overloaded socket, an unauthorized heater — and grow rapidly. Because the steward sees these areas constantly, the steward can spot risks early. Fire safety is a natural part of the steward's daily work.

Sigara yalnızca izin verilen alanlarda i.en: Smoking is permitted only in designated areas; the steward checks the cleanliness of these areas and the correct use of ashtrays (ones that fully extinguish embers). If the steward notices signs/smell of smoking in a bunk or in an unauthorized area, the steward reports it. Smoking is one of the main causes of accommodation fires.

Yaşam mahalli yangın kapıları kapalı (ve.en: Fire doors in the accommodation are kept closed (or self-closing); wedging them open allows fire and smoke to spread. The steward applies this rule while working and corrects/reports a wedged door. This common violation has fatal consequences in a real fire.

Yangın detektörlerinin (duman/ısı) önü k.en: Fire detectors (smoke/heat) must not be obstructed; a detector that is covered or painted over does not work. The steward makes sure that the detectors in the accommodation remain uncovered and functional; an obstructed detector is reported.

Kamaralarda izinsiz elektrikli alet (ısı.en: If unauthorized electrical appliances (heaters, high-power devices), uncontrolled multi-socket adapters or naked flame sources are found in cabins, the steward reports them immediately. These devices can cause overloading and fire. Company policy usually prohibits certain appliances.

Tek başına çalışırken kamarot, bir yangı.en: Working alone, the steward may be the first person to notice signs of fire (smoke, smell, heat). In such a case, the steward raises the alarm immediately and acts according to the procedure. Early detection saves lives in an accommodation fire.

Kamara ve ortak alanlarda yangın/sigara.en: Fire/smoking safety in cabins and common areas is a valuable monitoring task that arises from the steward's constant presence in the accommodation. Ashtray discipline, fire door and detector awareness, reporting of risky appliances and early alarm protect the accommodation from being the area where fires most often start.

ISM Code'un 5. maddesi, şirket SMS'inde.en: Section 5 of the ISM Code requires the Master's duties to be clearly defined in the company SMS, the Master to be given the authority to implement the SMS on board and to report deviations to the company, and the "overriding authority" to be confirmed in writing. Every Master joining a ship brings on board the company's Master's Standing Orders and Master's Review procedures in signed form; these documents are looked for during internal audits.

Master's Review, ISM'in kalp atışıdır. Y.en: The Master's Review is the heartbeat of the ISM system. At least once a year (generally every 6 months), the Master evaluates the effectiveness of SMS implementation on board and sends the deficiencies found and suggestions for improvement to the company in writing. These reports are examined by the DPA (Designated Person Ashore) and are an input to the company's management review meeting.

Manila değişiklikleriyle birlikte STCW T.en: With the Manila amendments, STCW Tables A-II/1 and A-II/2 made Bridge Resource Management and Bridge Team Management competences mandatory for Masters and officers. These competences are not purely theoretical knowledge; they are behavioral competences in maintaining the hierarchy without undermining safety, the "challenge & response" culture, sharing situational awareness and human factor risks.

Köprüüstü kaynak yönetiminin başarısız o.en: In many accidents in which bridge resource management failed (Royal Majesty 1995, Sea Empress 1996, Costa Concordia 2012), the common pattern is this: the officer of the watch or the pilot had doubts but did not speak up because of the Master's authority. While using their hierarchical power, the modern Master must at the same time build a bridge culture that encourages "challenge".

Appraisal, sefere ait tüm verilerin topl.en: Appraisal is the gathering and evaluation of all information relevant to the voyage. Publications (Sailing Directions, List of Lights, Tide Tables, Routeing Charts), electronic charts (ENC) and the necessary T&P NM corrections are checked. Weather forecasts (long and short range), ice reports, piracy areas (HRA, VRA), war risk areas and health authority warnings (yellow fever, malaria, COVID-like outbreaks) are compiled at this stage.

Kaptanın bu aşamadaki rolü, 2. Zabit'in.en: The Master's role at this stage is to read critically the appraisal prepared by the Second Officer (usually the navigation officer). It is the Master's duty to find the points where the route requested by the charterer clashes with the seasonal safe route, and to notify the company and the charterer of these with reasons. For example, in a North Atlantic winter a great circle may look economical, but in the light of sentinel buoy data and the weather routing service (e.g. WNI, AWT) it may be necessary to deviate further south.

Planning aşamasında waypoint'ler belirle.en: In the planning stage, waypoints are set, and the course alteration points, parallel index lines, contour-following lines and XTD (cross-track distance) limits are defined. There are three critical points to which the Master must pay particular attention: the abort point, the contingency anchorage and the point of no return.

Abort point, geminin manevrayı iptal edi.en: The abort point is the last point at which the ship can abort the maneuver and withdraw to safe water. Beyond it, the maneuver can no longer be reversed. The point of no return, on the other hand, is the point beyond which turning back is no longer possible because of fuel, tide or the weather window. Failure to mark these points clearly on the plan is one of the most frequently repeated findings in MAIB reports.

Execution, planın gerçek seyir koşulları.en: Execution is the carrying out of the plan in actual navigation conditions. Minor revisions to the plan may be needed because of weather changes, the traffic situation or VTS instructions. These revisions must be entered in the log book and on the passage plan; the officer of the watch cannot change the basic logic of the plan without the Master's decision.

Yakıt yönetimi (slow steaming, eco speed.en: Managing fuel (slow steaming, eco speed), CII performance and the ETA committed to the charterer at the same time is the modern Master's daily arithmetic. If the weather deteriorates, tactical decisions such as reducing speed, shifting to a safer route or a heave-to affect the commercial ETA; but the safety decision always takes priority.

Monitoring, gerçek pozisyonun planlanan.en: Monitoring is comparing the actual position with the planned route and detecting deviations early. Route monitoring alarms, XTD alarms, anti-grounding and depth alarms in ECDIS must be set correctly. At every watch handover, a situation briefing must be given; standard phrases such as "I have the conn" and "you have the conn" are used.

Kaptan kendisini köprüüstüne çağırma kri.en: The Master clearly writes the criteria for calling the Master to the bridge in the Master's Standing Orders. Typical criteria: if visibility falls below 2 miles, if the CPA closes to less than 1 mile, if ECDIS fails, if bad weather develops differently from what was expected, in the event of any equipment failure, before a narrow passage, before the expected pilot boarding, etc. This list must be tailored to each ship and voyage.

Manevra sırasında \"double watchkeeping\.en: During maneuvering, the "double watchkeeping" principle is applied: the position is checked by ECDIS, by radar parallel indexing and by taking visual bearings. Relying on a single device is flagged in MAIB reports as a "single point failure".

Ağır havada (Beaufort 8 ve üzeri) gemi y.en: In heavy weather (Beaufort 8 and above), ship-handling tactics change: heave-to, scudding, riding it out, seeking shelter. The Master assesses the rolling period and the risks of parametric rolling and synchronous rolling. Based on the GM and the wave period, the Master alters course and speed.

Pilot köprüüstüne çıkar çıkmaz Master-Pi.en: As soon as the pilot arrives on the bridge, the Master-Pilot Exchange card is completed: the pilot's intended route, speed profile, number/arrangement of tugs, tug positions, expected UKC, weather and current, contingency plan and communication channels are confirmed. This card is not just a bureaucratic form but written evidence of shared situational awareness.

Kaptan komutayı pilota devretmez. Pilotu.en: The Master does not hand over command to the pilot. The pilot's advice is assessed professionally; advice contrary to safety is rejected. The pilot is an adviser who does not know the ship; the Master is the person who knows the ship best.

Weather routing servisleri (örn. AWT, WN.en: Weather routing services (e.g. AWT, WNI, StormGeo) provide daily route recommendations. These recommendations are not binding; the Master assesses them and accepts or rejects them. A decision to reject is always entered in the log with the reasons. If the contract with the charterer contains a "weather routing follow" clause, any deviation is reported to the company and the charterer.

Kaptanın yorum becerisi, ham sinoptik ha.en: The Master's interpretive skill lies in translating raw synoptic weather data (500 hPa pattern, jet stream, polar vortex position) into ship performance. The modern bridge displays weather and wave data as an ECDIS overlay; however, the data are updated every 6 hours and can be wrong on a small scale.

Tropik siklon yönetiminin temel kuralı \.en: The basic rule of tropical cyclone management is summarized in Bowditch's "Avoiding the Storm" section: in the northern hemisphere, the right-hand half (dangerous semicircle) is dangerous and the left-hand half (navigable semicircle) is relatively safe. In the southern hemisphere it is the other way round. To locate the center of the cyclone, the Master uses Buys Ballot's law, the rate of pressure fall, the direction from which the swell arrives and the cloud signature.

Modern uydulardan elde edilen besttrack.en: Best-track data obtained from modern satellites make the Master's job easier, but uncertainty is high in forecasts beyond 72 hours. Using the "1-2-3 rule", the Master adds a safety margin of 100/200/300 NM to the 24/48/72-hour forecast radius.

ECDIS, kâğıt haritanın yerini almıştır a.en: ECDIS has replaced the paper chart, but it is also a potential "single point of failure". The Master confirms that all officers have received type-specific training for the make/model of ECDIS on board. ENC updates (weekly), consistency between the official chart catalogue and the ENCs for the voyage, and the safety contour, safety depth, shallow contour and deep contour settings are reviewed before the voyage.

ECDIS'in over-reliance riski MAIB tarafı.en: The risk of over-reliance on ECDIS has been reported repeatedly by the MAIB (CFL Performer 2008, Ovit 2013). The Master requires ECDIS to be used not on its own but with cross-checks by radar parallel indexing, visual bearings and GPS.

AIS, COLREG manevra yorumu için tek başı.en: AIS alone is not sufficient for interpreting maneuvers under COLREG; it must be verified by radar. In areas where AIS spoofing or erroneous data are frequently encountered (Black Sea, Persian Gulf), the Master requires extra vigilance.

Overriding authority; charterer'in fast.en: Overriding authority is used in situations such as a charterer's request for fast steaming, cost pressure from the company, a terminal operator rushing the ship, a charterer's order to an unsafe port, an incorrect pilot maneuver, or pressure to sail with deficient equipment. The decision is justified as "professional judgement" and notified to the company in writing.

Bu yetkinin kullanılması nadiren popüler.en: Using this authority is rarely a popular decision; however, a Master failing to back down when they should is a common pattern in fatal accidents. In ISM internal audits, companies examine "records of the use of overriding authority" as samples; even the fact that it has never been used is sometimes regarded as a sign of a "culture of fear".

Ders: planlanmamış manevra yapılmaz. Yap.en: Lesson: no unplanned maneuvers. If one is to be made, a written risk assessment is prepared and approved by the company.

Mauritius açıklarında karaya oturma, doğ.en: Grounding off Mauritius: approaching the coast for a birthday celebration + an unplanned route to get a Wi-Fi signal. Lesson: any deviation from the passage plan requires written justification; "small" personal motives trigger major accidents.

Standing orders, kaptanın gemi süresince.en: Standing orders set out in writing the conduct that the Master expects from the officers of the watch on a standing basis throughout the Master's time on the ship. All officers sign them. Typical content: criteria for calling the Master, rules for using the autopilot, when to call the helmsman, conditions for posting an additional lookout, log book entry discipline, alarm management, GMDSS test schedule.

Her akşam kaptan, ertesi 24 saatlik sefe.en: Every evening, the Master writes specific instructions for the next 24 hours of the voyage in the night order book: expected course alteration points, expected weather, traffic information, when to call the Master, ETA updates. Night orders are the most practical tool supporting the officer of the watch's decisions at night.

Mevzuat sürekli güncellenir (IMO MSC ve.en: Regulations are constantly updated (IMO MSC and MEPC meetings are held twice a year). The Master regularly follows amendments to SOLAS, MARPOL and STCW, IMO circulars, P&I bulletins, and MAIB and TSB reports. Company bulletins, vetting reports (RightShip, OCIMF SIRE) and class technical bulletins are the Master's daily reading list.

Seyir emniyetinin nihai sorumluluğu, kap.en: Ultimate responsibility for navigational safety places both great authority and a great burden on the Master. This authority is not a "privilege of rank"; it is a professional position that must be earned anew every day, with every decision. SOLAS V/34, ISM 5.2 and STCW define this authority not to protect the Master but to protect safety at sea. A prudent Master builds a bridge culture in which the Master "never has to use" that authority, but uses it without hesitation the moment it is needed.

ISM Code 16 madde üzerine kuruludur; bun.en: The ISM Code is built on 16 sections; they cover headings such as company policy (section 2), company responsibilities (section 3), the Designated Person Ashore — DPA (section 4), the Master's responsibility and authority (section 5), resources and personnel (section 6), development of plans for shipboard operations (section 7), emergency preparedness (section 8), reporting of non-conformities, accidents and hazardous occurrences (section 9), maintenance (section 10), documentation (section 11) and company verification, review and evaluation (section 12). For the Master, section 5 (Master's Responsibility and Authority) and section 9 (reporting) are the backbone of daily practice.

Madde 5, şirket SMS'inde kaptanın görevl.en: Section 5 requires the Master's duties to be clearly defined in the company SMS, the Master to be given the authority to implement the SMS on board and to report deviations to the company, and the "overriding authority" to be confirmed in writing. In other words, the company must explicitly give the Master the authority to place safety and environmental protection above all commercial considerations. This written confirmation is among the first pieces of evidence looked for in internal and external audits.

Document of Compliance (DOC) şirkete ver.en: The Document of Compliance (DOC) is issued to the company and covers the ship types the company operates (bulk, oil tanker, chemical tanker, gas carrier, container, passenger, etc.). The Safety Management Certificate (SMC) is issued to the ship and shows that the ship is operated in accordance with the company SMS. The ship must carry a copy of the DOC, because the SMC is valid only on the basis of a valid DOC. The Master always verifies that the ship's type is listed on the DOC; otherwise the SMC may be considered invalid.

SMS, gemide somut olarak bir dizi el kit.en: On board, the SMS lives in concrete form as a set of manuals, checklists, forms and records: the Safety Management Manual, critical operation procedures (enclosed space entry, hot work, mooring, bunkering, navigation), risk assessment templates, the permit-to-work system and the records archive. The Master's task is to confirm that these documents on board are at the latest revision (controlled document register), that old revisions have been withdrawn from use and that the crew have access to the relevant procedures.

Kaptan, gemiye yeni katılan her personel.en: The Master checks that the familiarization process for every person joining the ship is carried out in accordance with the SMS; this is a direct requirement of ISM section 6. A person cannot be assigned to a watch or a critical operation until familiarization has been completed. This check is an area that PSC and vetting inspections frequently look at, especially on ships with high crew turnover.

Modern SMS, \"her kritik ve rutin dışı o.en: The modern SMS is based on the principle of "a written risk assessment before every critical and non-routine operation". The common methodology is the 5x5 risk matrix: likelihood (1-5) multiplied by severity (1-5) gives the risk score. High-scoring jobs (generally >12) are either canceled or reduced to an acceptable level with additional barriers (control measures). The Master checks that the risk assessment team is made up of the right people (including those who will actually do the job) and that the "as low as reasonably practicable — ALARP" principle is observed.

Dinamik risk değerlendirmesi (dynamic ri.en: Dynamic risk assessment, on the other hand, is the immediate reassessment of a job on site when conditions change (the weather deteriorates, equipment fails, the team becomes tired). The toolbox talk (a short pre-job briefing) is the practical tool for this. The Master builds a just culture which clearly establishes that "stop work authority" is given to all crew members and that a person who uses this authority will not be penalized.

Management of Change (Değişim Yönetimi),.en: Management of Change (MOC) ensures that any permanent or temporary change on board (equipment, procedures, crew composition, software, structure) is assessed in a controlled way. For example, the MOC process is triggered if the type of a critical valve is to be changed, if a procedure is to be bypassed or if an experienced officer is to be replaced by someone new. The aim is to prevent a change that "looks small" from creating hidden risks.

MOC formu; değişikliğin tanımı, gerekçes.en: The MOC form includes a description of the change, its justification, a risk assessment, the required approvals (the Master and usually the company/DPA), the implementation steps and a post-change review. TMSA 3 (the OCIMF self-assessment for tankers) explicitly measures MOC as a performance indicator. Through MOC discipline, the Master prevents a temporary solution (e.g. a workaround for faulty equipment) from becoming a permanent norm.

Permit-to-Work (PTW) sistemi; enclosed s.en: The Permit-to-Work (PTW) system is mandatory for high-risk work such as enclosed space entry, hot work (welding/grinding), aloft work (working at height), overboard work and electrical isolation (LOTO — lock out tag out). The permit bears the signatures of the person authorizing the work (usually the Master or an officer designated by the Master), the person doing the work and the person verifying it; its validity is limited, and it is closed when the work is finished.

ISM madde 12, şirketin SMS'i en az yılda.en: ISM section 12 requires the company to verify the SMS by internal audit at least once a year. These audits are carried out by (trained) internal auditors who are independent of the area being audited. On the ship's side, the Master ensures that records are ready for the audit, procedures have been implemented and the team can answer questions. The internal audit must be positioned as a tool for "improvement", not "punishment"; otherwise findings are hidden and the system is left blind.

Denetim bulguları üç kategoriye ayrılır:.en: Audit findings are divided into three categories: observation, non-conformity (NC) and major non-conformity (Major NC). For each finding, a root cause analysis (e.g. 5 Whys, fishbone diagram) is carried out, and corrective action and preventive action are defined. Superficial close-outs of the "crew member warned" type are rejected by the auditor.

Uygunsuzluk (NC), SMS'in bir gerekliliği.en: A non-conformity (NC) is an observed situation in which a requirement of the SMS has not been fulfilled (e.g. a missing drill record). A major non-conformity is a serious finding that poses a serious threat to safety or the environment, indicates a systematic failure, or results from several minor NCs taken together (e.g. emergency equipment not working, a critical procedure not being applied at all). A Major NC directly endangers the validity of the DOC or SMC.

Major NC, denetim bitmeden veya çok kısa.en: A Major NC must be closed before the audit ends or within a very short time; otherwise the certificate may be suspended and the ship may be prevented from sailing. In the event of a major NC, the Master informs the DPA immediately, takes immediate containment measures and implements the permanent corrective action plan within the set time. In a PSC inspection, a serious ISM-related finding is flagged as an "ISM-related detention" and brings additional inspection pressure on the company's whole fleet.

Near-miss (ramak kala olay), bir kazaya.en: A near miss is an event that could have led to an accident but passed without consequence. MSC-MEPC.7/Circ.7 encourages near-miss reporting, because beneath every serious accident lie dozens of near misses and hundreds of unsafe acts (Heinrich/Bird pyramid). The Master creates a no-blame environment that encourages the crew to report near misses; a high number of near-miss reports is not bad but, on the contrary, a sign of a healthy safety culture.

Düzeltici aksiyon döngüsü PDCA (Plan-Do-.en: The corrective action cycle works on PDCA (Plan-Do-Check-Act) logic: the event is reported, the root cause is found, the action is defined and implemented, and its effectiveness is verified (effectiveness check). If the effectiveness check is skipped, the same event recurs. The Master is the person who follows up whether closed actions have really solved the problem; this tracking log is examined during audits.

Kaptan, müster listesinin (muster list —.en: The Master confirms that the muster list (SOLAS III/8) is up to date, that each crew member knows their emergency duties (fire party, rescue party, first aid, liferaft preparation) and that equipment assignments (radios, EEBDs, hoses) are correct. When the crew changes, the muster list is updated immediately.

Drill kalitesi, kaptanın imzasını taşır..en: The quality of a drill bears the Master's signature. An effective drill includes a realistic scenario, an unexpected complication (e.g. "this liferaft is unserviceable, use an alternative"), timing and a debrief afterwards. "What went well / what to improve" is written in the drill records, and deficiencies are turned into corrective actions. Beyond seeing the record, a PSC inspector may test actual competence by saying "show me".

ISPS Code iki bölümden oluşur: Part A zo.en: The ISPS Code consists of two parts: Part A contains mandatory requirements and Part B contains recommendations of a guidance nature (although many flag States also make Part B mandatory). The key actors in the system are the CSO (Company Security Officer, ashore), the SSO (Ship Security Officer, usually a deck officer) and the PFSO (Port Facility Security Officer). The Master is the SSO's superior and has ultimate responsibility for the ship's overall security.

Kritik bir prensip: ISPS, kaptanın emniy.en: A critical principle: ISPS confirms the Master's primacy in safety and security decisions. SOLAS XI-2/8 clearly provides that, if security and safety conflict, the Master has the authority to give priority to safety. In other words, if a security request (e.g. carrying out a particular search) would endanger the ship's safety, the Master may refuse it.

Ship Security Plan (SSP), her gemi için.en: The Ship Security Plan (SSP) is a document prepared for each ship on the basis of the Ship Security Assessment (SSA) and approved by the flag State (or an authorized RSO). The SSP defines access control, restricted areas, security equipment, the measures to be taken at each security level, the SSAS procedure and the response to security incidents. The SSP is a confidential document; even a PSC inspector cannot see certain parts of it (only certain operational provisions may be shown).

Kaptan ve SSO, SSP'nin güncel, manipülas.en: The Master and the SSO ensure that the SSP is up to date and protected against tampering (with authorized access if it is electronic), and that the ship's security equipment (CCTV, lighting, access barriers, metal detector) is in working order. The Continuous Synopsis Record (CSR — SOLAS XI-1/5) keeps the ship's "identity history" (flag, name, owner, ISM/ISPS certificate history) and is kept on board.

ISPS üç güvenlik seviyesi tanımlar. Sevi.en: ISPS defines three security levels. Level 1 (normal): minimum protective measures are maintained at all times. Level 2 (heightened): additional protective measures are maintained for a period of time because of an increased threat. Level 3 (exceptional): specific protective measures are maintained for a limited period when a security incident is probable or imminent. The security level is set by the flag State or port State authorities; the ship applies the higher of the level of the port she is in and the level set by her own flag.

Seviye yükseldiğinde kaptan ve SSO, SSP'.en: When the level is raised, the Master and the SSO put into effect the measures defined in the SSP for that level: reducing access points, tightening identity checks, increasing baggage/cargo searches, more frequent patrols and intensified seaward monitoring (anti-piracy/anti-stowaway watch). Changes of level and the measures applied are recorded; these records are reported to the port authority and the company.

Declaration of Security (DoS), gemi ile.en: A Declaration of Security (DoS) is a document confirming in writing how security responsibilities are shared between the ship and the port facility (or another ship). A DoS is requested in particular when security levels differ, when the ship berths at a facility that does not apply ISPS, during a high-risk operation (e.g. STS — ship-to-ship transfer) or after a security incident. The SSO or the Master has the authority to request a DoS when necessary.

DoS; her tarafın hangi güvenlik önlemini.en: The DoS includes which security measures each party undertakes (access control, cargo inspection, patrols, etc.), its period of validity and the signatories. At a facility that does not apply ISPS or applies it poorly, the Master clarifies the limits of responsibility with a DoS and takes additional measures on the ship's side. DoS records are among the security records that the ship must keep for a specified minimum period.

Ship Security Alert System (SSAS), SOLAS.en: The Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) is mandatory on certain ships under SOLAS XI-2/6. In the event of a security threat (piracy, terrorism, hijacking), the SSAS sends a silent alert directly to the company security contact and/or the flag State authority without sounding an alarm on board and without alerting nearby ships. There are at least two activation points: one on the bridge and the other in a concealed location. Activation points are protected to prevent false alerts.

Kaptan ve SSO, SSAS test prosedürünü (ge.en: The Master and the SSO know the SSAS test procedure (usually coordinated with the authorities in advance) and test the system periodically. An SSAS alert triggered by mistake must be canceled immediately by notifying the relevant centers; otherwise an unnecessary search and rescue or military response may be triggered. The SSAS message contains the ship's identity, position and the security threat status.

Citadel, mürettebatın saldırı anında çek.en: The citadel is a protected space, with means of communication, to which the crew withdraw during an attack and which cannot be entered from outside. The citadel principle is this: military rescue cannot be initiated until all crew members are inside and accounted for by a head count, and secure communication with the outside has been established. Carrying armed private security (PCASP) is subject to flag and port State permission, company policy and strict rules for the use of force; the Master implements this framework on board.

Bir güvenlik olayı (yetkisiz erişim giri.en: In the event of a security incident (attempted unauthorized access, suspicious package/person, bomb threat, stowaway, attack), the Master implements the response steps in the SSP, coordinates with the CSO and PFSO, and notifies the relevant State authorities (flag/port) and, where necessary, alerts via the SSAS. After the incident, a detailed record is kept and the root cause is assessed; the SSP or procedures may be updated to prevent recurrence (this is where ISM and ISPS come together).

Pratikte bir olay hem emniyet hem güvenl.en: In practice, an incident may have both a safety and a security dimension: for example, an unauthorized person entering the engine room is both a security breach and a safety risk. The Master manages the reporting flow and the response from both perspectives. The annual management review assesses the performance indicators of both systems together (KPIs: number of NCs, drill quality, near-miss rate, number of security incidents).

DPA (Designated Person Ashore), ISM madd.en: Under ISM section 4, the DPA (Designated Person Ashore) is a direct link between the Master and the highest level of company management. When there is a safety or environmental concern, the Master can bypass the hierarchy and contact the DPA directly; this access cannot be obstructed under any circumstances. Similarly, the CSO is the Master's counterpart ashore on security matters. The Master ensures that these two channels operate openly, quickly and on record.

Master's Review (kaptanın SMS değerlendi.en: The Master's Review (the Master's evaluation of the SMS) is the Master's periodic feedback on the effectiveness of the system on board and a critical input to the management review. Here the Master honestly reports gaps of the "exists on paper but doesn't work in practice" type; this honesty is the only way for the system to truly improve. A Master's Review that hides the reality on board is one of the most dangerous management failures.

Port State Control (Paris MOU, Tokyo MOU.en: The Port State Control (Paris MOU, Tokyo MOU, USCG, etc.) inspector tests the ship's ISM and ISPS compliance both through documents and on board. For ISM: validity of certificates, drill records, equipment maintenance records and whether there are any open NCs; for ISPS: validity of the ISSC (International Ship Security Certificate), gangway watch and access control, security records and the presence of the CSR are examined. If there are "clear grounds", a more detailed inspection is carried out.

Kaptan, denetim öncesi bir self-assessme.en: Before an inspection, the Master carries out a self-assessment (PSC self-assessment) and closes out in advance the frequently found detention items (LSA/FSS equipment defects, missing records, emergency equipment not working, security gaps). A serious systemic ISM-related finding leads to the ship's detention and to the company falling into "targeted" status; this brings an additional inspection burden on the whole fleet.

Tankerlerde OCIMF SIRE 2.0 vetting denet.en: For tankers, OCIMF SIRE 2.0 vetting inspections and the company-level TMSA 3 self-assessment are extensions of ISM/ISPS that have become de facto mandatory in commercial life. Despite valid certificates, a tanker may fail to find cargo because of a poor SIRE report. The Master has a thorough command of the SIRE question bank and ensures that the records and practices on board are consistent with the TMSA elements (e.g. MOC, risk management, navigation safety).

Kuru yük tarafında RightShip değerlendir.en: On the dry cargo side, the RightShip assessment performs a similar gatekeeping function. The Master's daily discipline (up-to-date records, working equipment, a competent team) is reflected directly, through these external inspections, in the fleet's commercial competitiveness. In other words, ISM/ISPS is not only a legal matter but a matter of commercial survival.

ISM ve ISPS, denetimde \"kağıt göstermek.en: ISM and ISPS live on board not as a way to "show paper" at inspections but as a living system that protects the crew, the ship and the environment when an accident or security incident occurs. The strength of this system comes from the Master owning it not as a bureaucratic burden but as a discipline and just culture that supports the Master's decisions. Certificates may hang on the wall; but what really makes ISM/ISPS work is the honesty in reporting, the document discipline and the culture rewarding the courage to "stop work" that the Master builds every day.

MLC içeriği beş Title altında düzenlenir.en: The content of the MLC is organized under five Titles: Title 1 — minimum requirements for work on board (minimum age, medical certificate, training, recruitment); Title 2 — conditions of employment (SEA, wages, hours of work/rest, leave, repatriation, compensation for loss of the ship, manning, career); Title 3 — accommodation, recreational facilities, food and catering; Title 4 — health protection, medical care, welfare and social security; Title 5 — compliance and enforcement (DMLC, survey, complaints, PSC). In each of the five Titles, the Master is the "supervisor on the ground".

Kaptanın rolü, standartları yalnızca \"b.en: The Master's role is not only to "know" the standards, but to ensure that they are actually applied on board, to prove it and to correct deviations. As the philosophy of the MLC is "decent working and living conditions for seafarers", the Master's leadership style directly determines whether these rights are realized.

Her MLC kapsamındaki gemi, Maritime Labo.en: Every ship covered by the MLC carries a Maritime Labour Certificate and the Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance (DMLC) attached to it. DMLC Part I is issued by the flag State and summarizes the relevant requirements of national legislation. DMLC Part II is prepared by the shipowner and describes the concrete measures applied on board for each item in Part I; the flag State approves it.

Kaptan, DMLC Part II'yi günlük yönetimin.en: The Master uses DMLC Part II like a "user manual" for day-to-day management: it sets out which procedure and which form are applied, and how often, for each subject. If a PSC inspector finds a contradiction between the practice observed on board and the DMLC Part II declaration, this counts as a "non-conformity". Even if the certificate is valid, the ship may be detained if there is an actual violation.

MLC, gemide çalışmak için asgari yaşı 16.en: The MLC sets the minimum age for working on board at 16; for seafarers under 18 there are restrictions on night work and hazardous work. Every seafarer must hold a valid medical fitness certificate (generally valid for 2 years, 1 year for those under 18); a separate validity period applies to color vision for duties that require it. The Master personally verifies the validity of the medical and STCW certificates of every seafarer joining the ship.

Süresi dolmuş medikal veya eksik STCW se.en: An expired medical certificate or a missing STCW certificate is a violation of both the MLC and STCW and a ground for PSC detention. The Master tracks certificate expiry dates in crew change planning; if a seafarer's certificate will expire during the voyage, renewal/relief is coordinated in advance.

MLC, denizcilerin ücretsiz işe alınmasın.en: The MLC guarantees that seafarers are recruited free of charge: no fee may be charged to a seafarer for finding employment (a manning agency commission cannot be passed on to the seafarer). The use of licensed/regulated recruitment & placement services is essential. The Master observes that the seafarers joining the ship have been employed through a lawful and transparent process and have not arrived in situations resembling "debt bondage".

Modern slavery ve insan kaçakçılığı risk.en: The risk of modern slavery and human trafficking is real in shipping; violation of the principle of free recruitment is its first sign. In a suspicious case, the Master coordinates with the DPA and CSO; holding a seafarer's passport without their consent (passport retention) is a violation of the MLC and of human rights.

Her denizci, imzalı bir Seafarers' Emplo.en: Every seafarer must hold a signed Seafarers' Employment Agreement (SEA); one copy is kept by the seafarer and one on board. The SEA includes the identity of the parties, the start date and duration, the position, wages, hours of work, annual leave, repatriation entitlements, health and social security, and termination conditions. The Master verifies that the SEA of every seafarer on board is available, legible and valid; it is one of the first documents PSC asks for.

Toplu iş sözleşmesi (CBA, örn. ITF/IBF k.en: If there is a collective bargaining agreement (CBA, e.g. ITF/IBF coverage), the SEA refers to it and the CBA is kept on board. The Master ensures consistency between the SEA and actual practice (wages, position, hours of work); if a seafarer is employed in a position different from that stated in the SEA or is underpaid, this is an MLC violation.

Kaptan, vardiya planını (watch system) b.en: The Master sets up the watch system in the light of these limits and has rest hours records kept daily. Port operations, drills, PSC/vetting and emergencies carry a high risk of disrupting rest hours. Fatigue is among the leading causes of accidents in MAIB reports; the Master plans honestly so as not to create a crew that is "compliant on paper but tired in reality".

Ödenmemiş maaş (wages outstanding), PSC.en: Unpaid wages (wages outstanding) are regarded by PSC as a serious MLC violation and may lead to the ship's detention; the ITF also inspects ships in port for unpaid wages and, if necessary, has the ship arrested. When the Master notices a payment problem, the Master reports it immediately to the DPA; the shipowner's financial difficulties cannot delay a seafarer's wages, and this situation is an early sign of the risk of "abandonment".

MLC, denizcinin belirli durumlarda ücret.en: The MLC guarantees the seafarer's right to be repatriated free of charge to their home country (or an agreed place) in certain circumstances: expiry of the SEA, illness/injury, loss of the ship, justified termination of the SEA by the shipowner or the seafarer, the seafarer being sent to a war zone, etc. The maximum period of service (the repatriation entitlement generally arises after 11 months) is set by flag legislation. Recovering repatriation costs from the seafarer (making deductions in advance) is prohibited, except where the seafarer is in serious default.

Kaptan, repatriation hakkı doğan denizci.en: The Master coordinates with the agent and the company for a seafarer who becomes entitled to repatriation; the flight ticket, visa, transit and final wage settlement are arranged. During COVID-19, hundreds of thousands of seafarers were stranded on ships because of the "crew change crisis"; this was a period in which the MLC's repatriation provisions were tested on a global scale, and joint IMO/ILO statements emphasized seafarers' "key worker" status.

MLC 2014 değişiklikleri (2017'de yürürlü.en: The 2014 amendments to the MLC (in force in 2017) introduced two new mandatory forms of financial security: (1) insurance/security covering repatriation, unpaid wages and essential needs in the event of the seafarer's abandonment; (2) financial security for contractual compensation arising from occupational injury, illness or death. The ship must carry the certificates proving this security (usually from the P&I Club) and post them in a conspicuous place.
