Abandonment, armatörün denizciyle bağı k.en: Abandonment is defined as the shipowner severing ties with the seafarer (failing to cover repatriation costs, failing to pay wages for at least 2 months or abandoning the seafarer). When a risk of abandonment appears on board (delayed wages, supplies cut off, the company going silent), the Master detects it early and informs the seafarers of their right to apply to the insurer named in the financial security certificate; the ILO tracks these cases in a publicly accessible database.

MLC Title 3, kamara büyüklüğü, havalandı.en: MLC Title 3 sets concrete standards for cabin size, ventilation/air conditioning, lighting, noise and vibration limits, berths, sanitary facilities (ratio of toilets/showers), laundry, hospital/sick bay and recreational facilities. These standards are largely met at the construction/refit stage, but the Master is responsible for maintaining them (maintenance, cleanliness, function). Air conditioning that does not work, noise above the limits or an insufficient number of toilets/showers is a real welfare problem that can arise.

Kaptan, periyodik konaklama denetimi (ac.en: The Master carries out periodic accommodation inspections; the MLC requires these inspections to be carried out frequently (generally at least weekly, on a regular basis in most SMSs) and to be recorded. The inspection covers cleanliness, working facilities, insect/rodent control, and the condition of the laundry and sick bay. Findings are closed with corrective action.

İçme suyu kalitesi (potability) sağlık a.en: Drinking water quality (potability) is critical for health; tank chlorination, periodic water testing and cleaning of the hydrophore system are followed up. Galley hygiene is managed on HACCP principles: prevention of cross-contamination, temperature control (refrigerator < 4°C, freezer < -18°C), date tracking and personal hygiene of staff. A foodborne mass illness (gastroenteritis) can paralyze operations on a ship.

Kaptan, ilaç dolabının envanterini, son.en: The Master checks the medical chest inventory, expiry dates and narcotics records; missing/expired medicines are replaced in port. In a serious case, TMAS is consulted and, if necessary, a MEDEVAC (by helicopter or by diverting to the nearest port) is arranged; this decision falls within the Master's overriding authority and is taken despite commercial loss.

Zihinsel sağlık ve denizci intiharı, sek.en: Mental health and seafarer suicide are serious issues for the industry; isolation, fatigue and insufficient communication with family are the main risks. The Master observes the crew's psychological state, creates an open communication environment and, if necessary, activates the company's EAP (Employee Assistance Program)/crisis line. Social security protection (health, invalidity, old age) is also covered by the MLC and is generally provided through the flag State/State of origin.

MLC, her gemide adil, etkili ve hızlı bi.en: The MLC requires every ship to have a fair, effective and expeditious on-board complaint procedure. A seafarer has the right to raise a complaint first with their immediate superior and, if it is not resolved, step by step up to the Master and, if necessary, to the authorities ashore (DPA / company / flag State / port State official). The procedure is given in writing to every seafarer (together with the SEA), and victimization of a seafarer for making a complaint is strictly prohibited.

Kaptan, şikâyetleri kayda geçirir, taraf.en: The Master records complaints and deals with them impartially and promptly, protecting the seafarer's right to be accompanied or represented. The procedure includes the flag State contact details and the details of the port State official; PSC checks whether the complaint procedure includes these final levels. A well-managed complaint procedure prevents small problems from turning into a major crisis (ITF intervention, PSC detention).

Gemide disiplin, keyfi değil belgeli ve.en: Discipline on board is carried out not arbitrarily but through a documented and fair process. The Master applies warnings, records, the sanctions defined in the SEA/CBA and, in serious cases, repatriation/termination proceedings in accordance with the principle of proportionality. The seafarer's right of defense, a written record of the process and witness statements are important. Excessive or arbitrary discipline is both an MLC violation and a source of future employment law claims.

Alkol/uyuşturucu politikası (drug & alco.en: The drug & alcohol policy is safety-critical and is generally based on zero tolerance or a low limit (e.g. 0.05 BAC or below); a violation calls for severe disciplinary action. The Master conducts random and for-cause tests in accordance with the SMS, with confidentiality and dignity. Maintaining the line between discipline and bullying is the Master's leadership responsibility.

MLC ve ILO ilkeleri; ırk, renk, cinsiyet.en: MLC and ILO principles prohibit discrimination on the basis of race, color, sex, religion, political opinion and national/social origin. Guidance developed since 2016 (ICS/ITF Guidance on Eliminating Harassment & Bullying) explicitly addresses the prevention of harassment and bullying on board. In multinational crews, cultural sensitivity, discipline in using a common language (working language) and equal treatment are part of the Master's daily management.

Kaptan, taciz/zorbalık iddialarını ciddi.en: The Master takes allegations of harassment/bullying seriously and investigates them confidentially and fairly, protecting the victim and preventing retaliation. With the increasing presence of women seafarers, sexual harassment and a safe environment have come to the fore; many companies now provide a clear "zero tolerance" policy and reporting channels (including off-ship and anonymous lines). Good welfare management depends on creating a safe climate in which problems are not hidden.

Kaptan, denetim öncesi kendi MLC dosyası.en: Before an inspection, the Master keeps the ship's own MLC file ready (certificate, DMLC I/II, sample SEAs, rest hours records, payroll, accommodation inspection records, complaint procedure). Consistent and honest records speed up the inspection; contradictory or incomplete records create a risk of detention. Rectifiable findings are closed in port; serious/recurring violations lead to the ship being detained.

MLC'de kaptanın savunması \"kayıt\"tır..en: Under the MLC, the Master's defense is "records". Rest hours schedules are kept daily and acknowledged by the seafarer; when back-filling is detected, the credibility of all records collapses. Accommodation inspection, water test, medical chest inventory, payroll and complaint records are kept dated and signed. These records are evidence for PSC, for the flag State and for any future employment law case.

Kaptan, kendi \"Master's Review\" (ISM).en: The Master also includes MLC compliance in the Master's own "Master's Review" (ISM) process and reports the deficiencies found and the corrective actions to the DPA. The MLC becomes sustainable when it is managed in an integrated way with ISM; keeping the two systems separate creates duplicate records and gaps.

Yorgunluk, denizcilik kazalarının en yay.en: Fatigue is the most common human-factor root cause of maritime accidents (it has been identified in the Exxon Valdez, the Cosco Busan and countless groundings/collisions). MSC.1/Circ.1598 (Guidelines on Fatigue) addresses factors such as sleep debt, circadian rhythm, monotony and workload. The Master's most critical responsibility is to close the gap between rest hours that "look compliant on paper" and a seafarer who is "actually rested".

Yetersiz manning (eksik personel) yorgun.en: Inadequate manning (insufficient personnel) is a structural cause of fatigue; if the Master finds that manning is not sufficient for the operation, the Master reports this to the DPA ("under-manning" is a safety and MLC issue). Intensive port rotations, frequent PSC/vetting, drills and emergencies put pressure on rest hours; the Master plans according to this reality and, if necessary, takes the decision to slow down operations using the overriding authority.

Modern gemilerde mürettebat çoğunlukla ç.en: On modern ships, crews are mostly multinational and multicultural (Filipino, Indian, Ukrainian, Chinese, Indonesian, etc.). The Master's welfare management covers clear communication in the common working language (usually English), respect for religious/cultural practices (menu, prayer times, religious holidays), equal treatment and preventing cliques and exclusion. Cultural sensitivity is a leadership skill that reduces tension on board and strengthens the safety culture.

Dil bariyeri, emniyet brifinglerinde ve.en: A language barrier is a serious risk in safety briefings and emergencies; the Master confirms that critical instructions are understood by everyone and, if necessary, uses visual/multilingual material. Welfare and safety feed each other in a multinational team: a crew that feels valued works more safely.

MLC 2006, kaptanın \"iyi niyetle\" değil.en: MLC 2006 is an area that the Master must manage "with documents", not "with good intentions": every right, from rest hours records to the payroll and from accommodation inspections to the complaint procedure, must be visible through a record. But the real spirit of the MLC lies not on paper but in the people on board; keeping compliant records while creating a crew that is tired, unpaid and feels worthless is contrary to the purpose of the MLC and will sooner or later turn into a safety accident. A prudent Master knows that by protecting the crew's rights they are at the same time making the strongest investment in safety: a rested, paid, healthy crew whose dignity is protected is the most reliable line of defense at sea.

Sea protest, geminin uğradığı veya yol a.en: A sea protest is a formal declaration that, in respect of damage the ship has suffered or may have caused, the circumstances (e.g. storm, force majeure) were beyond the control of the ship/crew. It establishes an early basis of evidence against claims that may be made later and protects the ship's position.

Ağır hava ve yük hasarı, çatışma, karaya.en: Situations such as heavy weather and cargo damage, collision, grounding, damage to shore facilities/berths, dragging anchor, unexpected delay or a dispute during cargo discharge may require a protest. When in doubt, noting a protest on the advice of the P&I Club/company is the safe course.

Protest, genellikle limana varıştan sonr.en: The protest is generally made before the competent authority/notary as soon as possible after arrival in port (often within 24 hours). Delay weakens the value of the declaration. Where necessary, a protest can be noted "with reservation to extend" before the full extent of the damage is known, and extended later.

Protest, deck/official log book kayıtlar.en: The protest is based on deck/official log book entries, weather data (barometer, wind, sea state), navigation records and, where necessary, witness statements. The Master clearly documents the timeline of the incident, the measures taken and the conditions.

Protest metni, log ve diğer kayıtlarla b.en: The text of the protest must be fully consistent with the log and other records. A contradiction damages the credibility of both the protest and the ship in general. The declaration is therefore prepared carefully on the basis of the records.

Olay sonrası P&I Club (sorumluluk sigort.en: After the incident, the P&I Club (liability insurance) and, where necessary, the H&M underwriter are informed as soon as possible. The Club gives guidance on the appointment of a surveyor, legal representation and protest strategy. The Master acts in coordination with the Club correspondent.

Geminin ve yükün ortak kurtarılması için.en: If a deliberate sacrifice was made for the common safety of the ship and cargo (general average), the process runs under the York-Antwerp Rules, and the protest contributes to the chain of evidence for this process. The protest and the records are also critical in cases such as salvage and towage.

Sea protest, noter/makam huzurunda yapıl.en: A sea protest is a formal declaration made before a notary or authority. A Letter of Protest (LOP), on the other hand, is a letter given to the terminal, charterer or other party, objecting to a specific situation (slow loading, damaged cargo, measurement dispute). The Master does not confuse the two and uses each of them where and when appropriate.

Deniz protestu, krizin sıcak anında gele.en: In the heat of a crisis, the sea protest is a quiet precaution that secures the legal position for the future. A timely protest by the Master that is consistent with the records, together with prompt P&I coordination, protects the ship and crew against unjust liability.

B/L üç temel işlev taşır: (1) yükün beli.en: A B/L has three basic functions: (1) a receipt confirming that the cargo was received in the stated condition and quantity, (2) evidence of the contract of carriage, (3) a negotiable document of title representing delivery of the goods. This triple function makes the statement of the Master who signs the B/L extremely binding.

Kaptan, B/L imzalanmadan önce yükün mikt.en: Before the B/L is signed, the Master has the quantity and apparent condition of the cargo checked against the documents. The Chief Officer's records and tally records, draft survey/ullage measurements and the Mate's Receipt are the basis of this verification. If there is visible damage, shortage or nonconformity, the B/L is "claused" (a remark is entered).

Görünür kusur yoksa \"clean\" B/L imzala.en: If there are no visible defects, a "clean" B/L is signed. If there are defects, the actual condition is documented by writing it on the B/L (claused/dirty). Pressure to present damaged cargo as clean is a serious legal and ethical trap.

Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye fiilen alın.en: The Mate's Receipt is the internal record documenting that the cargo has actually been received on board and its condition; the B/L is issued on the basis of this receipt. "Remarks" (damage notes) on the Mate's Receipt must be carried over to the B/L. The Master checks that this chain is consistent.

Kaptan; Notice of Readiness (NOR — gemin.en: The Master approves or authorizes the Notice of Readiness (NOR — notice that the ship is ready to load/discharge, which starts the laytime clock), the Statement of Facts (SOF — timeline of the operation), the Cargo Manifest and the related customs documents. These documents are evidence in demurrage and commercial disputes.

Bazı durumlarda B/L'yi acente \"for and.en: In some cases the agent signs the B/L "for and on behalf of the Master"; this authority may only be used with the approval of the Master/company and within the instructions given. The Master is responsible for the accuracy of documents signed on the Master's behalf.

B/L'de tarih değiştirme (ante/post-datin.en: Altering the date on a B/L (ante/post-dating), misstating quantity or condition, or issuing a false document has serious legal consequences and may invalidate insurance cover. Despite commercial pressure, the Master signs only a document that reflects the truth.

Bill of Lading, kaptanın imzasının doğru.en: The Bill of Lading is the most serious commercial document, one in which the Master's signature directly binds the company. An honest signature, given only after the cargo has been verified and the facts have been claused, and without yielding to pressure, protects the ship both commercially and legally.

ISM Code, şirketten emniyetli işletim iç.en: The ISM Code requires the Company to establish "safe practices" and a "safe working environment" for safe operation (Section 1.2.2). A person under the influence of drugs or alcohol is a direct danger both to themselves and to the ship; for this reason almost every company's SMS contains a separate Drug & Alcohol Policy. The Master is the "person in charge" responsible for the actual implementation of this policy on board; under ISM Section 5, the Master is obliged to implement the SMS on board and to report deviations to the DPA.

Politika tipik olarak \"zero tolerance\".en: The policy is typically built on the "zero tolerance" principle: possessing or using drugs on board, or performing duties under their influence, is strictly prohibited and usually results in immediate dismissal (summary dismissal). For alcohol, most modern companies apply a "dry ship" policy (completely dry ship, 0.00 BAC) or an upper limit consistent with the OCIMF recommendation. The Master confirms that every person newly joining the ship has read this policy and signed for it (familiarisation).

STCW ayrıca alkol ve uyuşturucu kötüye k.en: STCW also deals with the prevention of alcohol and drug abuse together with "fatigue" management under the heading of fitness for duty. A typical rule for alcohol consumption before going on watch is an abstinence window of at least 4 hours counted back from the start of the watch; under dry ship policies, however, this is not even a matter for discussion, because possessing alcohol on board is prohibited.

D&A politikası yalnızca alkolü değil; ba.en: The D&A policy covers not only alcohol but also, in particular, cannabis (THC), cocaine, amphetamine/methamphetamine, opiates (morphine, codeine, heroin), benzodiazepines and synthetic substances (NPS — new psychoactive substances). Prescription medicines are not excluded either: personnel using prescription medicines that may affect performance, alertness or judgment must declare this to the Master and to the ship's doctor/company medical department. This declaration is recorded and, if necessary, duty restrictions are applied.

Politikanın kapsamı tüm mürettebat, kapt.en: The policy covers all crew members, every rank including the Master, and also contractors, repair personnel and riding squad personnel who board the ship. The Master is not exempt from the zero-tolerance policy; the principle of leading by example requires the Master to be both the person who enforces the policy and the person who complies with it.

Dry ship politikası uygulayan şirketlerd.en: In companies with a dry ship policy, bringing alcohol on board, possessing it and consuming it are prohibited; there is no alcohol in the bond store, or it is kept sealed under lock. The Master has authority defined in the SMS for periodic searches of cabins and common areas (cabin search); these searches are carried out with respect for privacy, preferably in the presence of the person concerned and a witness.

Sınırlı alkole izin veren şirketlerde (ö.en: In companies that allow limited alcohol (e.g. on certain days, in controlled quantities), the Master keeps a record of the alcohol stock and may prohibit consumption completely during critical port/navigation periods (maneuvering, narrow passages, cargo operations). In any case, the basic rule is that alcohol must not affect watchkeeping performance; in case of doubt, the Master may require a test (for-cause testing).

Pre-employment test, personel gemiye kat.en: A pre-employment test is carried out before the person joins the ship (usually by the manning agency or a clinic), and a negative result is a condition of sign-on. A sign-on/joining test is a test carried out on joining the ship or shortly after joining, which provides a "clean start". The Master verifies that every person newly joining has arrived with a valid, negative D&A test certificate; if there is no certificate or it is doubtful, the Master has an onboard test carried out.

Bu testler genellikle idrar (urine) bazl.en: These tests are usually carried out with urine-based multi-panel immunoassay test kits, which are kept on board. If a preliminary positive result (presumptive positive) is obtained, the sample is sealed and sent to an accredited laboratory for confirmation (GC-MS/LC-MS method). The preliminary test result alone is not conclusive; this is why chain of custody and laboratory confirmation are critical.

Random testing, programın caydırıcılığın.en: Random testing is the heart of the program's deterrent effect, because nobody can know in advance when they will be tested. The company SMS usually sets an annual target rate (e.g. at least 25% of the crew to be randomly tested once a year; some tanker companies require a higher rate). The Master ensures that the selection process is genuinely random and unbiased — for example, a numbered list + random number, drawing of sealed capsules, or selection by the company's central software.

Random test \"unannounced\" (habersiz) o.en: A random test must be "unannounced"; the essential point is that the selected person is not given a long interval between notification and providing the sample (generally the sampling process starts immediately). The Master records the test date and the selection method; during PSC or vetting inspections, evidence of the random program (records, selection method, results) may be requested.

For-cause (reasonable suspicion / for-ca.en: A for-cause (reasonable suspicion / for-cause) test is applied when a person's behavior, speech, odor or performance gives rise to reasonable suspicion. Where possible, the observations giving rise to suspicion are recorded by two persons (the Master + an officer); what is written down is not a subjective "I don't like it" but concrete signs (unsteady gait, slurred speech, smell of alcohol, bloodshot eyes). In most SMSs, refusing a for-cause test leads to the same disciplinary outcome as a positive result.

Post-incident (serious marine incident s.en: A post-incident test (after a serious marine incident) is applied to the personnel involved after events such as collision, grounding, fire, serious injury/death or significant pollution. In USCG waters, under 46 CFR 4.06, after a "serious marine incident" the alcohol test must be carried out within 2 hours and the drug test within 32 hours; missing these time windows counts as a separate violation. The Master plans the logistics of post-incident testing (test kit, witness, records) in advance as part of emergency management.

Alkol testi gemide genellikle kalibre ed.en: On board, the alcohol test is usually carried out with a calibrated breathalyser (breath alcohol meter). The device's calibration date must be valid, and the calibration interval specified by the manufacturer (typically 6-12 months) must be observed. Before the test, the person is expected not to have taken anything by mouth for at least 15-20 minutes (to prevent contamination from residual mouth alcohol or food); if the result is positive, a second measurement is taken after a short wait.

Sonuç ekran değeri olarak kaydedilir ve.en: The result is recorded as the displayed value and shown to the person tested. The Master keeps a form containing the device serial number, calibration date, time of measurement and result. Since breathalyser results are instantaneous evidence that cannot be repeated later, the maintenance of the device and the stock of spare (single-use) mouthpieces are the Master's responsibility.

Uyuşturucu testi gemide multi-panel idra.en: Drug testing on board starts with a multi-panel urine test kit (presumptive screen). The kit indicates the presence of substances above certain cut-off values. A sample that gives a presumptive positive is sealed on the split-sample principle and confirmed at an accredited laboratory by GC-MS or LC-MS/MS. Only a result confirmed by the laboratory ("confirmed positive") is accepted as a definitive positive.

Cut-off değerleri madde başına farklıdır.en: Cut-off values differ for each substance and are based, for reference, on SAMHSA/international standards. For example, roughly: amphetamines ~500 ng/mL (confirm 250), cocaine metabolite ~150 ng/mL (confirm 100), opiates ~2000 ng/mL, cannabis (THC-COOH) ~50 ng/mL (confirm 15), phencyclidine ~25 ng/mL. These values are set to distinguish between environmental/passive exposure and actual use; for this reason, "I was exposed accidentally" defenses are usually refuted by the cut-off logic.

Chain of custody (CoC), örneğin alınması.en: Chain of custody (CoC) is the chain in which every point of contact, from collection of the sample to the laboratory result, is recorded, and it is the basis of the legal validity of the test. The sample is collected in the presence of the person tested; for a urine sample, a temperature check (32-38°C) is made to prevent "substitution" and "dilution". The sample is sealed, the person and the witness sign across the seal, and the CoC form travels with the sample.

CoC'deki bir kopukluk (mühürsüz örnek, e.en: A break in the CoC (unsealed sample, missing signature, untraceable storage) makes a positive result legally indefensible. For this reason, the Master conducts sample collection with an impartial witness and fills in every field of the form completely. If samples have to be held on board, they are stored locked and under suitable temperature conditions, and are sent to the laboratory by courier at the first suitable port.

Doğrulanmış pozitif sonuçta kaptanın ilk.en: After a confirmed positive result, the Master's first priority is safety: the person concerned is immediately removed from safety-critical duties (watchkeeping, maneuvering, cargo operations). The company (DPA / crew/HR department) is then notified immediately; most SMSs classify a positive result as a "non-conformity / reportable event". The decision process is not left to the Master alone; the company's disciplinary procedure and legal department become involved.

Çoğu zero-tolerance politikasında doğrul.en: Under most zero-tolerance policies, a confirmed positive results in summary dismissal and sign-off at the first suitable port. Repatriation is governed by the MLC; however, the contract and the policy may provide that repatriation costs can be charged to the seafarer in the event of a positive result. The Master makes sure that the entire process is documented and that the person's rights (for example, to request a confirmation test) are not violated.

D&A test sonuçları hassas kişisel ve tıb.en: D&A test results are sensitive personal and medical data; the principle of confidentiality is observed. Results are not shared beyond those who "need to know" (the Master, the person concerned, the company official), and gossip or stigmatization on board is prevented. The Master is responsible for ensuring that the process is conducted impartially and with respect for human dignity; acting otherwise is contrary to the MLC's expectation of "fair treatment" and also creates legal risk.

Adil süreç (due process), pozitif sonucu.en: Due process means that a positive result is not an automatic conviction, but is applied together with the right to confirmation and review. MRO review, declaration of prescription medicines and the possibility of retesting with the split sample are parts of this process. The Master files all steps (observation, test, result, removal from duty, notification, sign-off) time-stamped and signed; this file is decisive in any later employment law disputes.

USCG, kendi sularında 46 CFR Part 16 (ch.en: In its own waters, the USCG inspects D&A programs under 46 CFR Part 16 (chemical testing) and 33 CFR Part 95 (alcohol), and when necessary boards the ship to examine the testing and the program. On US-flagged ships or ships operating in US waters, the MEC (Marine Employer) program, random rates and records may be decisive. In a USCG inspection, missing program records may result in a serious finding and operational control.

Paris MOU ve diğer MOU rejimlerinde D&A.en: In the Paris MOU and other MOU regimes, D&A is not a separate inspection area as such, but it is assessed indirectly under fitness for duty, rest hours and ISM implementation. The PSC officer will want to see a D&A policy in force on board, familiarisation records and test records. If "clear grounds" arise, a more detailed inspection may be carried out.

Tanker sektöründe OCIMF SIRE/VIQ denetim.en: In the tanker sector, OCIMF SIRE/VIQ inspections question the D&A program in detail: is there a written policy, are limit values defined, is the random rate adequate, are records kept, is the breathalyser calibrated? In vetting, a weak D&A program directly affects the ship's acceptability for charter; this requires the Master to run the program rigorously, not only for "compliance" but also for commercial sustainability.

Kaptan, vetting öncesi bir iç denetimle.en: Before vetting, the Master closes the gaps in the program through an internal audit (self-assessment): expired calibration, missing familiarisation signatures and unrecorded random tests are the most common findings. This preparation significantly reduces the stress on the day of the inspection and the number of observations.

Etkili bir D&A politikası yalnızca test.en: An effective D&A policy does not consist only of testing and penalties; it also includes prevention and training. In periodic safety meetings, the Master explains D&A risks, the scope of the policy and how testing works. When personnel see the policy not as a "trap to catch people" but as a framework that protects everyone's safety, voluntary acceptance of the program increases.

MLC 2006'nın mürettebat refahı (welfare).en: The emphasis of MLC 2006 on crew welfare encourages treating alcohol/drug dependence as a health problem as well as a disciplinary one. Some companies offer a "self-referral" option: if a person asks for help before any positive test result, they are referred for rehabilitation. The Master supports the existence and the confidentiality of such a channel.

Gemide uzun seferler, izolasyon, monoton.en: Long voyages, isolation, monotony and fatigue on board are factors that increase the risk of escaping into alcohol or drugs. By managing these environmental risks (social activities, means of communication, reasonable rest), the Master takes indirect preventive measures. The D&A policy and fatigue management (rest hours) complement each other; both are part of fitness for duty.

İçki sorunu olan bir personelin tespiti.en: A person with a drinking problem is usually identified not suddenly but through gradual signs (lateness, falling performance, social withdrawal). The Master's power of observation makes it possible to detect the problem early, before a for-cause test. Early intervention is the most effective defense for the safety of both that person and the ship.

Kaptan, D&A programının tüm ayak izini k.en: The Master keeps a record of the complete footprint of the D&A program: signed policy and familiarisation forms, the random test selection method and results, observation reports for for-cause/post-incident tests, breathalyser calibration documents, records of test kit stock and expiry dates, and correspondence concerning positive results. These records must be ready both for internal audits and for PSC/vetting.

Kayıtların gizliliği ve saklama süresi ş.en: Confidentiality and retention periods of the records follow company procedure; since they are personal data, access is restricted. Summary results (number of tests, number of positives) may be reported in anonymized form; individual results, however, are shared only with authorized persons.

Pozitif sonuç, for-cause test kararı vey.en: A positive result, a decision to carry out a for-cause test or a policy violation is reported to the DPA in good time under the ISM Code. The report includes a summary of the event, the immediate action taken (removal from duty), the test details and the proposed action. The DPA and the company HR/legal department coordinate sign-off and repatriation logistics, the provision of a replacement and the legal steps.

Kaptan, bu sürecin \"tek karar verici\".en: The Master understands that in this process the Master is not the "sole decision-maker" but the "on-site manager and reporter". The immediate safety decision (removal from duty) belongs to the Master; termination of employment and the handling of legal matters, however, are carried out jointly with the company. This clarity protects the Master and also ensures that the person's rights are protected.

D&A politikasının uygulanmasında kaptanı.en: The Master's success in implementing the D&A policy is not "never having a positive result", but the program running consistently, impartially, in a documentable way and with respect for human dignity. Zero tolerance is a strong deterrent; its strength, however, comes from the legal soundness of its implementation and from the crew's trust in this framework. A well-managed D&A program is an invisible line of defense that may one day prevent an accident; a badly managed program leaves safety exposed and the company legally vulnerable.

H&M poliçesi, geminin kendi gövdesine ve.en: An H&M policy is a property insurance that covers physical damage to the ship's own hull and machinery (hull and machinery damage). It is typically based on standard sets of clauses such as the Institute Time Clauses (Hulls). Deformation of the hull resulting from a collision, fire damage in the engine room, bottom plating damage after a grounding, or propeller/shaft damage fall within H&M cover. Through the "running down clause" (RDC/3/4ths collision liability), H&M may also cover a certain proportion of the damage caused to the other ship in a collision.

H&M poliçesinde bir muafiyet (deductible.en: An H&M policy includes a deductible; small damage falling below this deductible is borne by the ship/company. The "sue and labour" clause (Marine Insurance Act 1906) provides for the assured to incur reasonable expenses to minimize the loss and for these expenses to be paid by the underwriter — the Master's efforts to limit damage after an incident are important in this respect.

P&I, geminin üçüncü taraflara karşı soru.en: P&I is a mutual insurance system that covers the ship's liabilities to third parties (third party liabilities); it operates through clubs formed by shipowners. P&I cover typically includes: liability for cargo damage/loss, injury/death of crew and third parties, pollution (oil pollution) liability, wreck removal, the 1/4 collision liability not covered by H&M, port/dock damage, fines, and expenses such as those for stowaways/repatriation.

Birçok kulüp, ayrıca FD&D (Freight, Demu.en: Many clubs also offer FD&D (Freight, Demurrage & Defence) protection as a separate cover; this covers legal costs in contractual disputes (charter party, freight, demurrage). In practice, the Master's task is to assess quickly whether an incident concerns H&M, P&I or both, and to inform both channels in good time, because a single collision can at the same time give rise to damage to the Master's own ship (H&M), liability to the other party (P&I) and a cargo claim (P&I).

P&I kulüp kuralları ve H&M poliçeleri, s.en: P&I club rules and H&M policies require the assured to report the incident "without undue delay". Late notification may weaken the cover to the extent that the club/underwriter has been prejudiced. As soon as the incident occurs, the Master informs the company (DPA/operations); the company in turn formally notifies H&M and P&I. Many companies keep an emergency contact list from which the Master can call the P&I correspondent directly.

Bildirim, soğukkanlı ve olgusal olmalıdı.en: The notification must be calm and factual. The Master avoids statements admitting liability ("we made a mistake"), because early and ill-considered admissions later become evidence against the ship. The notification includes the position and time (UTC) of the incident, weather/visibility conditions, the condition of the ship, whether there are any injured, dead or pollution, and the immediate actions taken.

Kaptan, olaydan hemen sonra delilleri si.en: Immediately after the incident, the Master systematically preserves and collects the evidence: deck/engine log book entries (time-stamped, accurate), bell book / movement book, ECDIS and radar records, "saving" and preserving the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) data, the GMDSS log, weather reports, photographs and video, and the crew's eyewitness notes. If the VDR record is not saved immediately after the incident, it may be overwritten and lost; for this reason, securing the VDR data is a priority in the first minutes.

Kargo, kirlilik veya yaralanma içeren ol.en: In incidents involving cargo, pollution or injury, the scene is preserved as far as possible until the surveyor arrives. The Master photographs the damaged areas, records measurements (sounding, draft, ullage) and gathers all documents in a single "casualty file". This file is the basic source for later P&I claims, the GA adjustment and court proceedings.

Bir olayın ardından birden çok surveyor.en: After an incident, several surveyors may attend the ship, each with a different principal. The H&M underwriter appoints its own surveyor (to assess hull/machinery damage); the P&I club appoints its own surveyor (for liability/cargo); the other party (for example, the other ship in the collision, cargo interests) may send its own surveyor; and the class (classification society) assesses the condition of class. The Master must know which surveyor represents whom and adjust the level of cooperation accordingly.

Kendi sigortacı/kulüp surveyor'larıyla t.en: Full cooperation is given to the surveyors of the ship's own underwriter/club. The other party's surveyor is given reasonable access, but statements and documents are shared under company/P&I guidance; giving uncontrolled statements to the other party's surveyor can create evidence against the ship. The Master records each surveyor visit: whom the surveyor represents, what was examined and what was documented.

Hasar tespit raporları (survey reports),.en: Damage survey reports are the basis of compensation and of the apportionment of liability. The Master also independently documents the extent and nature of the damage observed by the surveyor; consistency is sought between the surveyor's report and the ship's own records. Whether damage is "pre-existing" or results from this incident is frequently disputed; for this reason, the ship's regular maintenance/class records (to prove the condition before the damage) are critical.

Kargo hasarında, hasarın gemiye yüklenme.en: In cargo damage, distinguishing whether the damage occurred before loading on board (clausing / Mate's Receipt remark) or during carriage determines liability for compensation. The Master documents damage observed during loading/discharging with a Letter of Protest and a survey. These records are used directly by P&I in defending the cargo claim.

Gemi tehlikedeyse (oturmuş, yangın, maki.en: If the ship is in danger (aground, on fire, drifting after an engine failure) and outside salvage assistance is needed, the most common contract is Lloyd's Open Form (LOF). LOF is based on the "no cure - no pay" principle: if the salvor is successful, it receives an award; if unsuccessful, there is no payment. The greatest advantage of LOF is that it can be signed quickly in an emergency without lengthy price negotiation; the amount of the award is determined later by Lloyd's arbitration.

Kaptan, tehlike (peril) durumunda LOF im.en: In a situation of danger (peril), the Master has authority to sign LOF; if possible, however, the Master first contacts the company and P&I/H&M. If time is critical and there is no communication, the Master signs LOF for the safety of the ship and crew — this authority is supported by the safety priority of SOLAS and by maritime custom. After signing, the company and the underwriters are informed immediately.

SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Clause).en: SCOPIC (Special Compensation P&I Clause) is a mechanism that can be added to LOF and comes into effect particularly in salvage operations involving environmental risk. Under the classic "no cure - no pay" logic, the salvor may suffer a loss when salving a ship that poses an environmental threat but has low commercial value; SCOPIC pays the salvor reasonable expenses + a certain margin, regardless of success. SCOPIC compensation is typically paid by P&I.

SCOPIC devreye alındığında, P&I'ın atadı.en: When SCOPIC is invoked, an SCR (Special Casualty Representative) appointed by P&I joins the operation and monitors the salvage expenses. The Master works in coordination with the SCR and the salvage master; the ship's crew usually gives practical support to the salvage operation (for example, towing connection, pumping, damage control). Throughout this period, safety and environmental protection take priority.

Her dış yardım salvage değildir. Gemi ac.en: Not all outside assistance is salvage. If the ship is not in immediate danger but needs assistance (for example, being towed to port after an engine failure, dead tow), this is carried out under a towage contract. BIMCO's standard Towcon (lump sum) and Towhire (daily hire) contracts are used for this purpose. The distinction between salvage and towage matters, because a salvage award can be much higher than a towage fee.

Kaptan, durumu doğru sınıflandırır: gerç.en: The Master classifies the situation correctly: if there is no real danger (peril) and negotiation is possible, a towage contract is preferred, because it has a known and fixed cost. However, if the situation deteriorates during a towage operation and a real danger arises, it may turn into salvage. The Master coordinates the type of contract and the basis of remuneration with the company/P&I.

General Average (GA), örneğin yangını sö.en: General Average (GA) is the sharing of sacrifices made to escape a common danger, such as wetting cargo to extinguish a fire, throwing cargo overboard (jettison) to refloat a grounded ship, or salvage/towage costs. When GA is declared, the contributions of all saved parties (shipowner + all cargo owners) to the losses are calculated under the York-Antwerp Rules (commonly the 2016 version).

GA'yı ilan etme kararı genelde gemi sahi.en: The decision to declare GA is usually taken by the shipowner/company, which appoints an average adjuster; the Master, however, is responsible for fully documenting all details of the event giving rise to GA (jettison, firefighting, salvage). The Master's records (which cargo was sacrificed, when and for what reason) are the basis of the GA adjustment.

GA ilan edildiğinde, kargo sahiplerinden.en: When GA is declared, documents securing their contributions are required from the cargo owners: an Average Bond (an undertaking signed by the cargo owner) and an Average Guarantee (a guarantee given by the cargo underwriter), or a cash deposit. The cargo is not delivered until this security is complete, because collecting the contribution becomes very difficult once the cargo has been delivered. This process often delays delivery and requires careful coordination.

Average adjuster (örneğin Richards Hogg.en: The average adjuster (for example, firms such as Richards Hogg Lindley) draws up the "general average statement", which sets each party's contribution by calculating the value of all saved interests and the amount of the sacrifices. This process may take months or years. The Master's task is to provide the adjuster with accurate and complete documents; missing documents both delay the adjustment and may result in items in the shipowner's favor being left out of GA.

Kaptan, gemi ve şirket adına hukuki süre.en: The Master is the primary on-site point of contact in legal proceedings on behalf of the ship and the company. After an incident, court/administrative papers (writ, arrest warrant, subpoena), investigation requests from the port/coastal State and legal correspondence from the other party reach the Master first. Before signing or replying to these documents, the Master must contact the company and the P&I FD&D/legal department. A hasty signature or statement may weaken the ship's legal position.

Sworn statement (yeminli ifade), affidav.en: Sworn statements, affidavits or investigation statements directly affect the legal outcome of the incident. The Master obtains legal advice before giving a statement; the statement must be based on facts, consistent and in line with the ship's records. Relying on the records rather than saying "I don't recall", avoiding contradictions and avoiding speculation are the basic principles.

Sea Protest (Note of Protest), kaptanın.en: A Sea Protest (Note of Protest) is a declaration by which, after an unusual event (heavy weather, grounding, risk of cargo damage, collision), the Master formally places on record that neither the Master nor the ship was at fault and that the damage resulted from external causes. It is made before a notary or consul at the first suitable port, generally within a reasonable time after arrival (often within 24 hours). A Sea Protest strengthens the ship's position against later cargo claims and in GA proceedings.

Her büyük limanda P&I kulübünün bir corr.en: In every major port, the P&I club has a correspondent (local representative). The correspondent acts as the Master's eyes, ears and hands in that port: arranges surveyors, engages local lawyers, negotiates security, handles communication with the authorities and collects the necessary documents. When an incident occurs, one of the Master's first calls (with company approval) should be to the P&I correspondent at the port concerned; the correspondent list is kept up to date on board.

Correspondent ile çalışırken kaptan, olg.en: When working with the correspondent, the Master is factual and transparent; legal strategy and the assessment of liability, however, are directed by the correspondent + the club lawyer. The Master meets the correspondent's requests (documents, statements, access) in coordination with the company. This cooperation ensures that the process runs both quickly and with legal protection.

Bir ciddi olay, eş zamanlı olarak birçok.en: A serious incident sets many parties in motion at the same time: the company (DPA/operations), the H&M and P&I insurers, the classification society (condition of class), the flag State and, if necessary, the coastal State (accident investigation, pollution authority). ISM Code Section 9 requires non-conformities and accidents to be reported to the company and analyzed, with corrective action. At the center of this multi-party communication, the Master presents a single, consistent factual account.

Koordinasyonun anahtarı, tek bir \"casua.en: The key to coordination is a single "casualty file" and a single set of facts: telling different stories to different parties is disastrous. The Master records all correspondence and keeps track of who asked for what and what was shared. This discipline speeds up insurance recovery and also eliminates the risk of contradictions in legal proceedings.

Sigorta ve hukuki muhataplıkta kaptanın.en: In insurance and legal matters, the Master's strength comes not from taking decisions alone, but from bringing in the right party at the right moment and documenting the facts flawlessly. In a marine casualty, what determines the financial outcome is often not the event itself, but the quality of the evidence collected and the timing of notifications in the first hours after the event. A well-managed casualty process ensures that the ship receives the full cover it is entitled to; a badly managed process can leave even a ship that is in the right uninsured and legally vulnerable.

Yorgunluk; tepki süresini uzatır, dikkat.en: Fatigue lengthens reaction time, distracts attention, impairs judgment and leads to dangerous conditions such as "microsleep". Fatigue plays a direct or indirect role in most bridge and engine room accidents. The Master regards fatigue not as a "weakness" but as a serious operational risk that must be managed.

Yetersiz uyku, bölünmüş dinlenme, ağır i.en: Insufficient sleep, fragmented rest, heavy workload, intensive operations in port, noise/vibration, disruption of the circadian rhythm (night watches, frequent time zone changes) and stress are the main factors. On ships with small crews, intensive port and maneuvering periods increase fatigue rapidly.

STCW/MLC; her 24 saatte en az 10 saat ve.en: STCW/MLC require a minimum of 10 hours of rest in any 24-hour period and 77 hours in any 7-day period. Rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted, and the interval between consecutive periods of rest must not exceed 14 hours. The Master ensures that these limits are not violated.

Acil durum ve drill'ler için sınırlı ist.en: Although limited exceptions are defined for emergencies and drills, they must not be abused; compensatory rest is given after an exception. The Master avoids having a crew that is "compliant on paper but tired in reality".

Rest hours kayıtları, gerçek dinlenmeyi.en: Rest hours records must reflect actual rest. Keeping false records to show compliance (record falsification) is both an MLC violation and a collapse of safety culture, because it hides real fatigue and makes the risk invisible. The Master insists on honest records.

Manevra, dar su geçişi, yoğun yük operas.en: Before maneuvering, narrow-water passages, intensive cargo operations or heavy weather, it is ensured that the personnel involved are rested. The Master plans the port schedule and the allocation of duties so as to reduce fatigue; if necessary, the operation is slowed down or additional rest is given.

Esneme, dikkat dağınıklığı, gecikmiş tep.en: Yawning, distraction, delayed reactions, irritability and an increase in errors are signs of fatigue. The Master builds a culture in which the crew can report fatigue without hesitation; saying "I am tired" is not punished but taken seriously.

Yorgunluk yönetimi, kaptanın hem yasal y.en: Fatigue management is both a legal obligation of the Master and one of the most effective accident prevention tools. Honest records, realistic workload planning and an open culture minimize the invisible risk that a fatigued crew can create.

Bir stowaway tespit edildiğinde öncelik.en: When a stowaway is found, the priority is human safety: the person's life is protected and basic needs (water, food, shelter, medical care) are provided. At the same time, for the security of the ship, the person is kept under supervision. The Master ensures that the person is treated humanely and in accordance with the regulations; ill-treatment is unacceptable.

Kaptan; kişinin bulunma koşullarını, kim.en: The Master documents the circumstances in which the person was found, identity details (if any), state of health and the supervision arrangements. The P&I Club is informed early (stowaway costs are covered by P&I). Disembarkation/repatriation is carried out in coordination with the States concerned and the agent.

Yüksek riskli bölgelerde (geçmişte Aden.en: In high-risk areas (historically the Gulf of Aden/Indian Ocean, the Gulf of Guinea, some SE Asian waters), BMP is applied. The Master carries out a risk assessment and prepares ship protection measures (physical barriers, razor wire, water spray), a speed/maneuvering plan and lookout arrangements. Crew awareness and drills are critical.

Saldırı durumunda mürettebatın korunaklı.en: In the event of an attack, the plan is for the crew to withdraw to a protected area (citadel); the citadel is kept ready with communications, water and food. Reports are made to UKMTO/MSCHOA and the relevant naval units; the SSAS (Ship Security Alert System) is activated when necessary. Crew safety always comes before the ship and cargo.

ISPS Code kapsamında gemi, güvenlik sevi.en: Under the ISPS Code, the ship implements the Ship Security Plan (SSP) according to the security level (1-2-3). The Master and the SSO organize access control, monitoring of restricted areas, security of cargo/stores and visitor management. Changes of security level are recorded.

Hırsızlık, sabotaj, izinsiz giriş, bomb.en: Security incidents such as theft, sabotage, unauthorized entry, a bomb threat or a suspicious situation are managed in accordance with the SSP and reported to the company/PFSO/authorities. The SSAS provides a covert alarm when life or the ship is threatened. The Master carries out the post-incident recording and corrective action.

Hem stowaway hem de gözaltına alınan şüp.en: Humane treatment is mandatory for both stowaways and detained suspects. The Master strikes the balance between ship security and human rights within the regulatory framework; excessive force, ill-treatment or endangering a person is unacceptable and creates serious liability.

Güvenlik olayları yönetimi, kaptanın hem.en: Managing security incidents is an area in which the Master uses command composure, humanitarian responsibility and regulatory knowledge together. A prepared ship — drilled, with plans in place and connected to the reporting network — turns these incidents into a controlled procedure instead of panic.

IHR 2005, hastalıkların uluslararası yay.en: IHR 2005 aims to prevent the international spread of disease without unnecessarily restricting travel and trade. Ships are at the center of this regime: port health authorities require a health declaration from the ship and, when necessary, carry out inspections and apply measures. The Master is responsible for the ship's compliance with this framework.

MDoH, geminin son uğraklarında ve seyir.en: The MDoH is the formal declaration that reports to the port authority any cases of illness or death at the ship's last ports of call and during the voyage, the sanitary conditions on board and known health risks. The Master prepares the declaration accurately and completely; concealment or a false declaration creates serious liability.

Ship Sanitation Control Exemption Certif.en: The Ship Sanitation Control Exemption Certificate (SSCEC) or Ship Sanitation Control Certificate (SSCC) documents the ship's sanitary conditions and pest/rodent control; it is generally valid for 6 months and is renewed at authorized ports. The Master monitors the validity of the certificate and plans the port of renewal; an expired certificate causes problems in port.

Bir mürettebatta bulaşıcı hastalık şüphe.en: When an infectious disease is suspected in a crew member, the patient is isolated, hygiene and contact precautions are taken, TMAS is consulted and the health authority of the port of arrival is notified under the IHR. The Master manages the risk of an outbreak transparently, without concealment; this protects both the crew and public health.

Sağlık serbestisi (free pratique) alınan.en: Until free pratique is granted, the "Q" flag is hoisted when required — the ship declares that it is healthy and requests free pratique. Until health authority approval (radio/face-to-face pratique) is obtained, movement of persons to and from the ship is restricted where required. The Master applies this signaling and procedure correctly.

Belirli bölge geçişlerinde (örn. sarı hu.en: For passage through certain regions (e.g. yellow fever endemic areas), vaccination and a valid vaccination certificate may be required. The Master monitors the crew's vaccination status. General hygiene, drinking water quality, food safety and pest control are the basic measures that prevent disease in the first place.

Gemi sağlık prosedürleri, mürettebatı ve.en: Ship health procedures are an invisible shield protecting the crew and the communities visited from infectious diseases. Up-to-date documents, a transparent declaration and sound sanitation discipline on the Master's part ensure both legal compliance and genuine protection of public health.

Acil durum komuta yapısı tipik olarak üç.en: The emergency command structure is typically built around three centers: the bridge (command center — the Master in command, overall coordination, navigation and communications), the scene (on-scene command — usually the Chief Officer, who directs the response teams) and the engine control room (Chief Engineer — management of machinery, fire pump, generators, steering and emergency power). The Master is not the person who runs to the scene, but the one who sees the whole picture, manages resources and handles external communications. This division prevents the error of "the Master getting lost at the scene".

Müster listesi (muster list — SOLAS III/.en: The muster list (SOLAS III/8) shows each crew member's duty in an emergency, muster station, assigned equipment and the meaning of the alarm signals. The general emergency alarm consists of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast. The Master continuously confirms that the muster list is up to date and that each person knows their duty (fire team, rescue team, first aid, liferaft preparation, bridge support).

Kriz kararları çoğu zaman eksik bilgi ve.en: Crisis decisions are often taken with incomplete information and under time pressure. An effective approach is the OODA loop of military origin (Observe-Orient-Decide-Act), or the "GRADE" logic common in shipping: Gather (information), Risk assess, Analyse (the options), Decide, Evaluate (the result). Rather than freezing while waiting for perfect information, the Master takes a "good enough" decision early and updates it as conditions change, because in a crisis the most expensive decision is no decision at all.

Kaptan, bilişsel tuzaklara (tunnel visio.en: The Master must be alert to cognitive traps (tunnel vision, plan continuation bias, fixation on a wrong picture of the situation). As in the El Faro case, clinging to the original plan when it is no longer valid is fatal. Keeping the "challenge & response" culture on the bridge during a crisis as well is the strongest safeguard covering the Master's blind spots; an officer being able to say "Master, shouldn't we reconsider this?" saves lives in a crisis.

GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safe.en: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) is regulated by SOLAS Chapter IV and recognizes three priority levels: Distress (MAYDAY — a ship or person is in grave and imminent danger and requires immediate assistance), Urgency (PAN-PAN — an urgent but not life-threatening situation concerning the safety of a ship or person, e.g. a serious medical case) and Safety (SECURITE — navigational or meteorological warning). The Master chooses the level that matches the real seriousness of the situation; a distress alert given too late is as dangerous as an unnecessary one.

Distress mesajı önce DSC (Digital Select.en: A distress message is first sent by DSC (Digital Selective Calling) (VHF Ch 70, MF/HF distress frequencies), followed by a MAYDAY voice call by radiotelephony (VHF Ch 16, MF 2182 kHz): MAYDAY x3, ship's name and call sign, position, nature of distress, assistance required, number of persons on board and other information. Multiple channels are used, via satellite (Inmarsat/Iridium) and, if necessary, the EPIRB. An accurate, up-to-date position determines how quickly rescue arrives.

EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Rad.en: The EPIRB (Emergency Position Indicating Radio Beacon) is activated automatically (hydrostatic release) when the ship sinks, or manually; it transmits the ship's identity and GPS position to the 406 MHz Cospas-Sarsat satellites. The SART (Search and Rescue Transponder), on the other hand, is a radar transponder in the liferaft; it appears on the radar display of a searching ship as a distinct line of dots. The Master writes into the muster procedure that the EPIRB and SART are to be taken along when abandoning ship.

Distress aldıktan sonra koordinasyonu MR.en: After a distress alert is received, the MRCC (Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre) takes over coordination. The MRCC may designate an OSC (On-Scene Coordinator); this role is taken by the first ship to arrive or the most capable ship, which directs the search pattern (expanding square, sector search, parallel track) according to the IAMSAR Manual. The Master must know IAMSAR procedures both when calling for assistance and when going to the assistance of another ship; SOLAS V/33 makes the obligation to assist persons in distress a legal requirement.

Yangın sınıfına göre söndürücü seçilir:.en: The extinguishing agent is selected according to the class of fire: class A (solids) water; class B (oil/fuel) foam or CO2; class C (gas) shutting off the source; electrical fires CO2/clean agent (with the power isolated). In an engine room fire, the fixed CO2 or water mist system is used as a last resort; however, before CO2 is released it must be confirmed beyond doubt that the space has been completely cleared of personnel and that a headcount has been taken. The Master personally obtains this confirmation that "all personnel are out".

Kaptan, müdahale ekibinin güvenliğini ya.en: The Master gives the safety of the response team as much importance as extinguishing the fire. SCBA air time is monitored (person in charge of air control — air control board), the team enters in pairs, and a withdrawal signal and a backup team are ready. Because of the risk of re-ignition, the area continues to be watched and its temperature monitored after the fire is out. The principle is a disciplined response from which the team can withdraw, not heroics by a single person.

Konteyner gemilerinde güverte üstü yangı.en: On container ships, on-deck fires (especially those caused by mis-declared DG) are very difficult: access to the stacks is limited, water may be insufficient and there is a structural risk. Cases such as Maersk Honam (2018) show that the Master may sometimes be unable to extinguish the fire completely, and that withdrawing the team and waiting for outside assistance (salvage, escort) may be the better course. The Master's duty is not to defeat the fire at the cost of losing the team, but to protect people.

Çatışma kaçınılmaz hale geldiğinde son d.en: When a collision becomes unavoidable, the aim is to minimize the angle and speed of impact by last-minute maneuvering (COLREG Rules 8 and 17) and use of the engine; if possible, the ship is maneuvered so that the impact is taken in the bow region (the strongest structure). Immediately after the collision, the Master simultaneously manages: checking for injured persons, assessing flooding, damage control, pollution risk and communication with the other ship. If the two ships remain embedded in each other, a decision to separate may increase flooding; this assessment is made carefully.

COLREG Rule 19 ve sınırlı görüş hükümler.en: COLREG Rule 19 and the provisions on restricted visibility feature in the root causes of a large proportion of collisions. After a collision, the Master has legal obligations: to assist the other ship and persons, to exchange the ship's name, port of registry and ports of departure and destination, and to record the event. SOLAS V/33 and international custom require assistance to be given to the other ship without endangering one's own ship.

Su alma durumunda kaptan ve Birinci Zabi.en: In a flooding situation, the Master and the Chief Officer use the damage stability information (the ship's damage stability booklet, compartment plans) to assess which compartments are flooded, the ship's tendency to sink or capsize, and whether counter-flooding is needed. Closing watertight doors, managing the bilge and ballast pumps and controlling the list are vital. Progressive flooding is the silent killer in the loss of many ships.

Kaptan, geminin kurtarılabilir mi yoksa.en: When deciding whether the ship can be saved or must be abandoned, the Master must judge the timing correctly: abandoning too early can cause unnecessary loss of life, and abandoning too late can be fatal. The guiding principle is "the ship carries the people, not the people the ship"; however, where staying on board is always safer than a liferaft (the ship remaining a rescue platform as long as it does not sink), the Master considers this as well.

Karaya oturma anında ilk refleks makiney.en: At the moment of grounding, the first reflex may be to try to get off by going astern on the engine; this is often a mistake. The Master first assesses the situation: where the ship is aground (bow, stern, full length), the type of seabed (sand, mud, rock), hull integrity, flooding, the state of the tide and the environmental risk. Going astern hastily can tear open the damaged area and multiply flooding and pollution; moreover, a damaged ship that slides off into deep water may sink.

Kaptan; tank ve bölme soundinglerini ald.en: The Master has soundings taken of the tanks and compartments (to detect flooding), compares the draft readings, calculates the high-water window from the tide tables and, if necessary, prepares a refloating plan with salvage/class advice. If there is a risk of pollution, the SOPEP is activated and the authorities are informed. A controlled and calculated refloating plan, rather than hasty decisions, protects both the ship and the environment.

Karaya oturmalar büyük çevre felaketleri.en: Groundings can turn into major environmental disasters (Exxon Valdez 1989, Wakashio 2020). The Master gives priority to the condition of the fuel tanks; if necessary, the pollution risk is reduced by internal transfer (moving cargo/fuel to intact tanks). The SOPEP/SMPEP includes the initial response equipment and the notification list. The port/coastal State, class and the P&I club are informed promptly, and a surveyor is appointed.

Kaptan, olayın tüm zaman çizelgesini (lo.en: The Master preserves the complete timeline of the event (log, ECDIS replay, lookout statements) and prepares for the formal sea protest. The lesson of the Wakashio case is clear: deviating from the passage plan for personal motives (approaching the coast) is a trigger for major accidents. Crisis management covers not only the moment of the event but also the post-event records and legal proceedings.

MOB anında ilk eylemler: \"MAN OVERBOARD.en: The first actions in a MOB situation: "MAN OVERBOARD" is shouted, a lifebuoy (with light/smoke signal) is thrown on the side the person fell, the MOB button is pressed (GPS position marking), the helm is put over to the side the person fell (to swing the propeller away from the person), and a lookout keeps the person in sight continuously, never losing sight of them. The Master is called to the bridge and selects the appropriate turning maneuver: Williamson turn (person out of sight, returning along the same track), Anderson turn (person in sight, fastest turn) or Scharnow turn.

Kurtarma botu/rescue boat hazırlanır, MO.en: The rescue boat is prepared and launched using the procedure rehearsed in MOB drills. Water temperature is a critical factor: in cold water, hypothermia sets in within minutes, so speed is vital. The Master also looks after the safety of the rescue team; to avoid further casualties, the rescue boat crew is assigned with lifejackets and the necessary equipment.

Kurtarılan kişiye hipotermi ve boğulma p.en: The recovered person is treated according to the hypothermia and drowning protocol; the ship's medical equipment and the personnel competent in first aid are brought in. In serious cases, a shore doctor is consulted through telemedicine (e.g. TMAS — Telemedical Maritime Assistance Service) and, if necessary, a MEDEVAC by helicopter is requested through the MRCC. The Master runs this chain quickly (including a PAN-PAN urgency call).

MOB olayları çoğu zaman güverte çalışmas.en: MOB incidents often arise from preventable causes such as deck work, seasickness or not wearing a safety harness. After the crisis, the Master investigates the root cause (overboard work permit, use of harnesses, maintenance of guardrails) to prevent recurrence; prevention is as much a part of crisis management as rescue.

Gemiyi terk, kaptanın verebileceği en ağ.en: Abandoning ship is the gravest decision a Master can take, and it is the last resort. Following the principle "abandon ship when the ship can no longer carry you", as long as the ship is afloat it is a safer platform than a liferaft. The Master must make the decision to abandon neither too early (abandoning a ship that could be saved) nor too late (disorderly abandonment as the ship sinks). Once the decision is taken, the abandon ship signal is sounded and the crew musters at the muster stations with lifejackets/immersion suits.

Tahliye, müster listesine göre düzenli y.en: Abandonment proceeds in an orderly manner according to the muster list: liferafts/boats are prepared and launched, the EPIRB and SART are taken, the necessary documents and water/provisions are loaded, and a headcount is made. The Master leaves the ship last and confirms that every crew member is present and counted. Cold water, darkness and bad weather make abandonment far more difficult; for this reason, the equipment must be familiar and rehearsed in drills.

Can salına/bota geçtikten sonra hayatta.en: After boarding the liferaft/boat, survival management begins: headcount, conservation of body heat (rafts are tied together, openings are closed), rationing of water and provisions, hydration (seawater is not drunk), management of seasickness, and morale. The Master or a senior officer continues to lead in the raft; course and detectability (flares, SART, signaling mirror) are managed. Cold is the greatest threat; hypothermia claims more lives than drowning.

Kurtarma gelene kadar düzen ve umut koru.en: Order and hope must be maintained until rescue arrives. In drills, the Master also rehearses this psychological dimension (panic management, allocation of tasks), because how people will behave in a crisis is as decisive as the equipment. A well-rehearsed crew remains orderly even in bad conditions.

SOLAS III/19, fire ve abandon ship drill.en: SOLAS III/19 requires fire and abandon ship drills every month (weekly on passenger ships), and enclosed space entry/rescue drills at least once every 2 months. In addition, the company SMS plans MOB, pollution (SOPEP), grounding, blackout, steering failure, helicopter operation and security drills. The Master fits the drill schedule into the voyage program and ensures that no drill is carried out only "on paper".

Gerçekçi bir drill; beklenmedik bir sena.en: A realistic drill includes an unexpected scenario (e.g. "this exit is blocked, find an alternative"), timing of actions, use of real equipment and a debrief afterwards. "Went well / to be improved" notes are written in the drill records, and deficiencies are turned into corrective action. A poor drill creates false confidence, which is more dangerous than no drill at all.

Krizde kaptan, içeride komutayı sürdürür.en: In a crisis, the Master must maintain command on board while managing accurate and timely communication with the outside. The company's Emergency Response Team (ERT) is activated; the Master coordinates with the DPA/CSO and the company crisis line. The communication flow is defined in advance: who calls, what information is given, who speaks to the media (generally not the Master but the company). An early, honest and regular flow of information speeds up outside support and prevents misinformation.

Kaptan, kriz boyunca bir olay günlüğü (i.en: Throughout the crisis, the Master keeps an incident log: time-stamped decisions, messages and changes in the situation. This record both facilitates operational coordination and is critical evidence for the subsequent investigation, insurance and legal proceedings. Memory is unreliable in a crisis; a written record is reliable.

Kriz atlatıldıktan sonra mürettebatın fi.en: Once the crisis is over, the physical and psychological care of the crew is given priority. The injured are treated and, if necessary, a MEDEVAC is arranged. Stress after a traumatic event (loss of crew members, having faced danger to life) can have serious effects; the Master arranges a debriefing and, if necessary, professional support (psychological first aid, counseling ashore). People are at the center of a crisis and remain so after the event is over.

Kaptan, mürettebatın dinlenme ve toparla.en: The Master looks after the crew's need for rest and recovery (including MLC rest hours). Returning to normal operations with an exhausted team after a crisis invites new errors; if necessary, additional personnel or port support is requested.

Olay, ISM madde 9 kapsamında raporlanır.en: The event is reported under ISM Section 9 and a root cause analysis is carried out. The VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) data is preserved (recording is stopped/backed up so that it is not overwritten), and logs, ECDIS replay and statements are archived. The Master provides honest and complete information to the flag State casualty investigation (Casualty Investigation Code), to the P&I/H&M process and, if necessary, to judicial proceedings.

Her ciddi olay, filo için bir öğrenme fı.en: Every serious incident is a learning opportunity for the fleet. Corrective actions are implemented not only on that ship but across the company. Modern safety culture focuses not on the question "whom shall we blame?" but on "how do we strengthen the system?". The Master's honesty after an incident is the foundation for preventing future accidents.

Acil durum komutası, kaptanlığın en saf.en: Emergency command is the purest test of a Master: being able to make the right decision amid uncertainty and time pressure, at the moment when human lives hang in the balance. This ability is not innate; it comes from well-rehearsed drills, procedures learned by heart, a sound command structure and a bridge culture that is open to "challenge". In a crisis, the Master must be the calmest, best-prepared and clearest-thinking person on board, because at that moment everyone looks to the Master. The best crisis management, however, is often the preparation that prevents a crisis before it starts.

Yük operasyonunun sahada yürütülmesi Bir.en: Conducting the cargo operation on site is the duty of the Chief Officer; however, under ISM Code Section 5 and the provisions of SOLAS Chapter VI, it is the Master's responsibility to verify that the operation has been planned safely and is being carried out within the strength/stability limits. The Master can delegate the task but cannot delegate accountability. In a loading accident, PSC, class and P&I always ask the Master first.

Kaptan, cargo plan'ı imzasıyla onaylar..en: The Master approves the cargo plan with a signature. This signature is not a formality; it is written evidence that the Master has actually reviewed the plan for consistency with the ship type, the charter party terms and the strength curves. In a dispute, the record that "the Master saw and approved the plan" is evidence that both protects the Master and places responsibility on the Master.

Bulk carrier'larda ana risk liquefaction.en: On bulk carriers, the main risks are liquefaction, structural overstress and hold flooding. On tankers, fire/explosion, static electricity, inadequate inert gas and pollution stand out. On container ships, the main hazards are lashing failure, mis-declared DG and parametric rolling. The Master knows the risk signature of the ship type and focuses supervision accordingly.

Ro-Ro ve PCC (Pure Car Carrier) gemileri.en: On Ro-Ro ships and PCCs (Pure Car Carriers), water ingress routes (bow/stern door), low GM and vehicle lashing are critical. The Estonia (1994) and Golden Ray (2019) cases show the importance of stability and door securing on this type of ship.

Pre-stowage plan, stabilite/mukavemet ya.en: The pre-stowage plan is entered into the stability/strength software (LoadMaster, Cargomax, BluePrint). The Master reviews whether GM, draft FP/AP/Mid, list, bending moment, shear force and, on container ships, torsion values are within limits at every loading stage. Stages exceeding 85% of a limit are revised.

Final cargo plan Birinci Zabit tarafında.en: The final cargo plan is signed by the Chief Officer, approved by the Master and handed to the chief stevedore, the terminal and the duty officer. In the event of last-minute changes (contaminated cargo, damaged trailer, reefer failure), the software is run again and the plan is updated. The approved printouts are kept; PSC and vetting inspections may ask for them.

2008 IS Code minimum intact stability kr.en: The 2008 IS Code sets the minimum intact stability criteria: area under the GZ curve, angle of maximum GZ, initial GM (≥0.15 m) and the weather criterion specific to the ship type. The Master verifies that these criteria are maintained throughout loading. An excessively small GM makes a "tender" ship (risk of list), while an excessively large GM makes a "stiff" ship (violent rolling, overloading of lashings).

Free surface effect (FSC), kısmen dolu t.en: The free surface effect (FSC) reduces the effective GM in partly filled tanks and holds. On tankers and during ballast operations, the number of slack tanks is minimized. The Master checks that the FSC correction has been entered correctly in the software.

Bending moment ve shear force, hold'lar.en: Bending moment and shear force depend on the distribution of cargo between the holds. Heavy cargo at the ends + light cargo amidships creates "hogging", and the reverse creates "sagging"; both lead to hull fatigue and cracks. On bulk carriers, staged discharging during grab discharge carries a risk of overstress; the Master also checks the discharge sequence.

Her gemi klas onaylı bir Cargo Securing.en: Every ship carries a Cargo Securing Manual approved by class; this manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment and the approved lashing patterns. CSS Code Annex 13 provides a method of calculating forces for non-standardized cargo. The Master checks that the lashing plan complies with the manual and is adequate for the expected weather conditions.

Container gemilerinde twist lock + lashi.en: On container ships, the twist lock + lashing rod + turnbuckle combination, tier limits and the rules for stowage on hatch covers are observed. Lashing failure is the main cause of container losses (ONE Apus 2020, Maersk Essen 2021).

Kaptan, sefer çıkışından önce lashing ti.en: Before departure, the Master confirms that lashing tightening has been completed and that the "lashing certificate" (where applicable) is ready. On voyages where bad weather is expected, the Master gives instructions for additional lashing. For heavy lift and project cargo, an engineering calculation and class approval are required.

IMDG Code 9 ana sınıf kullanır (1 patlay.en: The IMDG Code uses 9 main classes (1 explosives … 9 miscellaneous). The segregation table governs which classes may be stowed side by side, on top of each other or in an adjacent hold. The Master checks that the DG manifest, packing certificate, EmS (Emergency Schedules) and stowage position comply with the segregation rules. Mis-declared DG is a hazard for the whole industry; CINS circulars are followed.

Group A yükler (nickel ore, iron ore fin.en: Group A cargoes (nickel ore, iron ore fines, bauxite fines) may liquefy; the TML (Transportable Moisture Limit) and the cargo declaration are critical. If the TML is exceeded, the Master refuses loading; otherwise the ship may capsize due to liquefaction. Group B cargoes (DRI, sulfur, coal) carry risks of self-heating, off-gassing and CO; hold ventilation and gas measurement are required. Group C is low risk.

Kaptan, gerektiğinde \"can test\" (kompl.en: When necessary, the Master has a "can test" (complementary test) carried out and does not blindly trust the shipper's TML declaration.
