In the Bulk Jupiter (2015) case, bauxite was loaded with a moisture content above its TML, the ship capsized and 18 people died.

SOLAS VI/2 ve MSC.1/Circ.1475, her dolu.en: SOLAS VI/2 and MSC.1/Circ.1475 make a VGM declaration mandatory for every packed container. Without a VGM, a container may not be loaded on board. The VGM is obtained either by weighing (Method 1) or by an approved calculation (Method 2). The Master knows that a missing VGM or unreasonable values are grounds for stopping loading; a mis-declared weight corrupts the lashing and stability calculations (with reference to MSC Napoli 2007).

SOLAS VI/2 uyarınca shipper, yüklemeden.en: Under SOLAS VI/2, the shipper must provide accurate and sufficient cargo information before loading (IMSBC group, TML, MSDS, density/stowage factor, DG class). The Master does not accept this information passively; in the event of inconsistency, missing documents or a doubtful declaration, the Master requests additional verification, has a Letter of Protest issued and, if necessary, stops loading.

Kaptan; TML aşımı şüphesi, mis-declared.en: The Master may stop a cargo operation because of suspected TML exceedance, mis-declared DG, a missing VGM, exceedance of stability/strength limits, unsafe practice by the terminal, pollution risk or weather. This authority is the expression, in cargo operations, of the "overriding authority" in SOLAS V/34-1 and ISM 5.2.

Durdurma kararı her zaman gerekçeli ve y.en: The decision to stop is always reasoned and in writing: log book, Letter of Protest, e-mail to the company (DPA) and notification to the charterer through the SOF/NOR. This record trail protects both the ship and the company in demurrage disputes and legal proceedings.

Bulk gemilerinde BLU Code, ship-shore ch.en: On bulk carriers, the BLU Code requires the ship-shore checklist and the loading/unloading plan to be agreed and signed with the terminal. High loading rates can cause overstress in a short time; if the terminal increases the rate outside the plan, the Master uses the authority to slow down or stop the operation.

Yükleme/boşaltmada hose/manifold kaçakla.en: During loading/discharging, the risk of hose/manifold leaks, overflow and drips is monitored continuously. Even a single drop of spilled oil activates the SOPEP; the terminal and the port authority are informed immediately. On tankers, ISGOTT requires the Ship-Shore Safety Checklist to be confirmed at every watch.

Bulk Jupiter, bauxite'in TML üzerinde yü.en: Bulk Jupiter capsized as a result of liquefaction after bauxite was loaded above the TML (18 dead). MOL Comfort suffered a hull fracture due to cargo distribution and strength problems. Two lessons: the shipper's declaration is questioned, and strength limits are a line that is never compromised.

PCC gemisi, ballast/yük dağılımı kaynakl.en: The PCC capsized during a turning maneuver because of insufficient stability caused by the ballast/cargo distribution. Lesson: on vehicle carriers, the GM margin and the ballast calculation are under the Master's direct supervision; the software printout is signed before departure and kept.

Yük operasyonunda kaptanın başarısı, \"h.en: In cargo operations, the Master's success comes from disciplined approval, cross-checking and decisions to stop, which are invisible when "everything goes well" but are the only line of defense when "something goes wrong". The Master does not stow the cargo, but guarantees that the cargo does not endanger the ship and crew.

MARPOL Annex I yağı, Annex II zararlı sı.en: MARPOL Annex I regulates oil, Annex II noxious liquid substances, Annex III harmful substances in packaged form, Annex IV sewage, Annex V garbage and Annex VI air emissions. For each Annex, the ship carries the relevant record book, certificate and management plan (IOPP, ORB, GMP, SEEMP, etc.). The Master knows which Annexes the ship is subject to and whether its current certificates are valid.

Kayıt defterlerindeki kayıtların doğrulu.en: The accuracy of the entries in the record books is the Master's personal responsibility. In the USA, magic pipe cases are generally brought on the basis of false ORB entries (false statement), resulting in prison sentences for the Master and the Chief Engineer and million-dollar fines for the company.

IOPP (Annex I), ISPP (Annex IV), IAPP ve.en: The IOPP (Annex I), ISPP (Annex IV), IAPP and IEEC (Annex VI) and EIAPP (for engines) certificates are subject to the initial/annual/intermediate/renewal survey cycle. The Master makes sure that the certificates are valid for PSC inspection and that the supplement forms (equipment lists) match the equipment on board.

Kaptan, ORB kayıtlarını periyodik olarak.en: The Master signs the ORB entries periodically and checks the accuracy of every page. The "magic pipe" (OWS bypass) is the most serious environmental crime; the Master's duty is to guarantee that no such arrangement exists on board and that the records match the actual operations exactly.

2020 Carriage Ban uyarınca, scrubber'sız.en: Under the 2020 Carriage Ban, a ship without a scrubber is prohibited from having on board (even merely carrying) fuel with a sulfur content above 0.50%. The Master ensures that the fuel changeover is carried out in good time when entering/leaving an ECA and that the ORB Part I / fuel changeover record is kept.

2023'ten itibaren yürürlükteki EEXI (Ene.en: EEXI (Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index), in force since 2023, sets a one-off efficiency threshold for ships; CII (Carbon Intensity Indicator), on the other hand, measures annual operational carbon intensity with an A–E rating. A ship rated D for three consecutive years, or E once, prepares a corrective action plan (SEEMP Part III). The Master has a direct influence on the CII rating through slow steaming, trim optimization and hull/propeller performance.

Kimyasal tankerlerde NLS, X/Y/Z/OS kateg.en: On chemical tankers, NLS are divided into categories X/Y/Z/OS. Discharge of tank washing residues is managed with the P&A (Procedures and Arrangements) Manual and the Cargo Record Book. For cargoes requiring a prewash, the operation is carried out in the presence of a surveyor. The Master checks the accuracy of the Cargo Record Book entries.

Kaptan, BWMS'in çalışır durumda olduğunu.en: The Master checks that the BWMS is in working order, that D-2 compliance is achieved and that the BWRB is kept correctly. The USA (USCG) has its own approval regime; additional compliance is required for ships entering US waters.

AFS Convention, TBT içeren zararlı anti-.en: The AFS Convention prohibits harmful anti-fouling systems containing TBT; under recent amendments, cybutryne has also been prohibited. The ship carries an AFS certificate or declaration. After dry-dock, the Master verifies that the paints are compliant and that the certificate is up to date.

Hull biofouling, hem CII performansını h.en: Hull biofouling affects both CII performance and the risk of invasive species; some jurisdictions (New Zealand, California) require a biofouling management record. The Master finds out in advance the regional environmental rules for the area the ship is going to (ECA, EU ETS / EU Emissions Trading, regional speed limits) and plans for compliance.

ORB, GRB ve BWRB kayıtları PSC, klas ve.en: ORB, GRB and BWRB entries are the first documents examined in PSC, class and vetting (SIRE, CDI) inspections. An inconsistency between the records and the actual operations (e.g. a mismatch between the sludge quantity and the tank level) is grounds for a "deficiency" or detention. The Master guarantees that the records reflect the truth and that no retrospective "corrections" are made.

ABD APPS rejimi, kirliliği ihbar eden mü.en: The US APPS regime gives rewards (a portion of the fine) to crew members who report pollution. This means that it is impossible to conceal falsification of records. By building an open and honest environmental culture on board, the Master stays on the safe side both legally and ethically.

Bir döküntü veya ihlalde kaptan; SOPEP r.en: In the event of a spill or violation, the Master informs the nearest coastal State, the port authority, the company (DPA) and the P&I Club using the SOPEP reporting format. The response is documented with the log book and photographs/video. Early, honest and complete reporting is the most effective way to limit penalties and liability.

Çevresel uyumlulukta kaptanın gücü tekno.en: In environmental compliance, the Master's strength lies not in technology but in the honesty of the records and in the shipboard culture. A correctly kept ORB is the difference between a million-dollar fine and a PSC inspection lasting a few hours. The Master treats protection of the marine environment not only as a legal obligation but as part of professional honor.

Bayrak devleti, SOLAS Chapter I gereğinc.en: Under SOLAS Chapter I, the flag State confirms through certificates that the ship complies with the international conventions; it often delegates this authority to a Recognized Organization (RO — e.g. a classification society). Statutory surveys produce convention certificates such as IOPP, SafCon, SafEquip, ISSC and SMC. Class surveys, on the other hand, examine the structural integrity of the ship and the compliance of machinery and equipment with class rules, and maintain the Class Certificate.

İki katman pratikte iç içe geçer: bir kl.en: In practice the two layers overlap: a class surveyor can close out both statutory and class items during the same visit. The Master must know which item belongs to which regime, because a condition of class (CoC) or memorandum has a different timeline and consequence from a statutory deficiency. If a CoC is not closed in time, class is suspended (suspension), which automatically takes the ship out of service and out of insurance cover.

PSC, bir liman devletinin (Paris/Tokyo M.en: PSC is a legal enforcement mechanism through which a port State (Paris/Tokyo MOU, USCG, AMSA, Black Sea MOU, etc.) inspects foreign-flagged ships in its waters for compliance with international standards. PSC has sanctions: deficiency, detention, banning. The aim is safety and the environment; the outcome is public and visible on platforms such as Equasis.

Vetting ise ticari bir kabul sürecidir;.en: Vetting, by contrast, is a commercial acceptance process: a charterer or cargo owner (e.g. the major oil companies that are OCIMF members, or RightShip in dry bulk) carries out a risk assessment of the ship before chartering it. Vetting has no legal enforcement power, but its commercial sanction is very severe: a negative SIRE report or a low RightShip score can exclude the ship from an entire commercial segment. The practical consequence for the Master is this: in PSC the aim is "not to get the ship detained"; in vetting the aim is "to keep the ship charterable at all times".

Kaptanın kritik kavramı \"survey window\.en: A critical concept for the Master is the "survey window": a window running from 3 months before to 3 months after the anniversary date (±3 months for the annual survey). The renewal survey must be completed within the 3 months before the expiry date. Falling outside the window disrupts the harmonized survey regime, and a certificate falling "out of window" directly produces a deficiency at PSC. The Master must plan the port rotation with the company so as to meet the survey windows.

ISM rejiminde iki belge vardır: şirkete.en: There are two documents in the ISM regime: the Document of Compliance (DOC), which belongs to the company, and the Safety Management Certificate (SMC), which belongs to the ship. The SMC on board is valid only as long as it is linked to a valid DOC of the company; the Master must verify that a certified copy of the DOC is on board and that the ship type is listed in the scope of the DOC (e.g. if it says "bulk carrier", the ship cannot be operated as a tanker).

ISSC için de benzer mantık geçerlidir: g.en: The same logic applies to the ISSC: an approved ship security plan (SSP) and functioning CSO/PFSO coordination are the foundation of the ISSC. At PSC, an inspector who sees the SMC tests the question "is the SMS really working on board?" against near-miss records, drill records and the close-out rate of corrective actions. What is inspected is not the certificate hanging on the wall, but whether the system behind it is alive.

Paris MOU New Inspection Regime, her gem.en: The Paris MOU New Inspection Regime assigns each ship a Ship Risk Profile (SRP): Low Risk Ship (LRS), Standard Risk Ship (SRS) or High Risk Ship (HRS). The profile is calculated from the ship type and age, flag performance (black/grey/white list), class/RO performance, the company's previous deficiency and detention history and the findings of recent inspections. LRS ships are inspected every 24-36 months, HRS ships every 5-6 months.

Bir PSC denetimi tipik olarak initial in.en: A PSC inspection typically starts with an initial inspection: certificate check, the general condition of the ship (general impression) and first contact with the crew. If "clear grounds" arise — for example, a certificate is missing, equipment is visibly defective, or the crew do not know their basic duties — the inspection is escalated to a more detailed inspection. For certain ship types and ages, an expanded inspection is mandatory anyway.

Kaptan, \"general impression\" faktörünü.en: The Master must not underestimate the "general impression" factor: a rusty deck, lighting that does not work, an untidy lifeboat station, open watertight doors, a dirty engine room — all of these give the inspector the impression that "the system on this ship is weak" and deepen the inspection. The visual impression in the first 15 minutes sets the tone and duration of the inspection.

Her yıl Paris ve Tokyo MOU, belirli bir.en: Every year the Paris and Tokyo MOUs run a coordinated campaign (CIC) focused on a particular theme: in the past, themes such as STCW rest hours, MARPOL Annex VI, fire safety, ISM, crew familiarization and ballast water management have been chosen. During the CIC period, a CIC questionnaire is applied to every ship in addition to the standard inspection. The Master should find out the theme of that year's CIC in advance and specially prepare the relevant files, records and equipment tests.

CIC'in incelikli yanı, normalde detentio.en: The subtle aspect of a CIC is that a finding that would not normally be a ground for detention can become a deficiency when an item in the CIC questionnaire is marked "No". For example, in a ballast water CIC, failure to keep an approved operating record of the BWMS, or in a fire safety CIC, a missing maintenance record for the fixed CO2 system, is scrutinized far beyond the standard throughout the campaign.

Detention'lar genellikle \"emniyeti, çev.en: Detentions usually arise from findings that "directly threaten safety, the environment or life": inoperative lifeboat launching appliances or davits, a defective emergency fire pump, an oily water separator discharging overboard (15 ppm bypass), an invalid/missing main certificate, an inoperative standby steering gear system, open/obstructed watertight closures, serious rest hours violations and the crew's inability to demonstrate basic emergency duties.

SIRE 2.0, OCIMF'in 2024'te tam yürürlüğe.en: SIRE 2.0 is OCIMF's new tanker vetting regime, fully implemented in 2024. Instead of the old static VIQ, it works with a tablet-based, question-bank-based and vessel-specific risk profile. When the inspector arrives on board, the inspector sees the question set the system has selected for that ship; the questions are distributed across the Hardware, Process (procedures/records) and Human (crew competence) dimensions. The weighting given to the human factor has significantly increased the importance of the interviews with the Master and officers.

Kaptanın SIRE 2.0 hazırlığı, dosya düzel.en: The Master's SIRE 2.0 preparation goes beyond putting files in order: an officer must be able to describe the actual practice on their own ship when asked "how do you apply this procedure?". Because of photographic evidence and the real-time recording system, "showing it and putting it away" is not possible. In SIRE 2.0, negative findings are reported as "observations"; each observation must be closed out by the company with a root cause and corrective action, otherwise the way to the next charter is not open.

RightShip, ağırlıklı olarak dökme yük (b.en: RightShip is the platform through which charterers make ship acceptance decisions, mainly in the dry bulk segment (bulk; traditionally iron ore, coal, grain). It assigns a ship a Safety Score (similar to 1-5 stars) and also a GHG Rating (A-G, carbon performance based on EEXI/CII). A low safety score or a poor GHG rating causes the ship to drop off the nomination lists of the major mining and energy companies.

RightShip kabulü için RISQ (RightShip In.en: A physical inspection based on RISQ (RightShip Inspection and Survey Questionnaire) may also be carried out for RightShip acceptance. The Master's practical task is to ensure, together with the company, that the ship's data on the RightShip platform (survey dates, PSC history, accident/incident record) is current and correct, and to take every finding seriously, knowing in particular that PSC detentions pull the score down for months.

CDI (Chemical Distribution Institute), k.en: CDI (Chemical Distribution Institute) is a vetting/inspection regime for chemical and gas tankers, similar to OCIMF; the CDI-Marine report is decisive in the ship acceptance decisions of chemical cargo owners. SIRE for oil tankers, CDI for chemical/gas, RightShip for dry bulk — the Master must have a thorough command of the inspection logic and reporting cycle of the program for whichever segment the ship trades in.

Tüm bu programların ortak paydası şudur:.en: The common denominator of all these programs is this: vetting is not a snapshot of a "moment" but a continuous record and performance history. Even if a ship passes an inspection brilliantly, it may be rejected because of observations not closed out in its past reports. For this reason, the Master must manage vetting not as an "event" but as a "condition" maintained every day.

Kaptan, beklenen PSC veya vetting öncesi.en: Before an expected PSC or vetting inspection, the Master conducts a systematic internal audit using the ship's own VIQ/RISQ/PSC checklist. This audit covers the deck, the engine room, life-saving appliances (LSA), fire-fighting appliances (FFA), the bridge, paper/electronic records and crew competence. Findings are entered in a "snag list"; each item is assigned to a responsible person and a deadline.

İyi bir self-audit, \"denetçi gözüyle\".en: A good self-audit is carried out "through the inspector's eyes"; that is, the Master must learn to look at the ship as an outside inspector would. Familiarity with the team (familiarity bias) makes real findings invisible; for this reason, having the self-audit done by a different officer, or cross-auditing (the Chief Officer audits the engine room, the 2nd engineer audits the deck), reduces blind spots.

Kaptan, denetim öncesi bir \"tatbikat br.en: Before the inspection, the Master holds a "drill briefing": with crew members who face a language barrier, the English wording of key answers is refreshed, and the location and testing of critical equipment are gone over again. This is not, however, about imposing memorization but about reminding people of what they really know, because an answer that has been memorized but not understood falls apart at the first follow-up question and creates distrust in the inspector.

Denetçi gemiye geldiğinde kaptan veya gö.en: When the inspector arrives on board, the Master or a senior officer designated by the Master meets the inspector, gives a safety briefing (PPE, restricted areas, emergencies) and provides an appropriate escort throughout the inspection. The inspector is never left alone; in each area the person responsible for that department (the Chief Officer on deck, the Chief Engineer in the engine room) is present. The escort is not there to "watch" the inspector, but to direct questions to the right person and to put a finding into context immediately.

İletişimde altın kural: sorulmayanı söyl.en: The golden rule of communication: do not volunteer what is not asked; answer what is asked honestly and clearly. Crew members must not guess on a subject they do not know, but should say "let me check and give you the exact information". A lie or a contradictory statement is far more dangerous than a single finding, because it fundamentally shakes the inspector's trust in the ship and drags the inspection to a defensive depth.

Bir bulgu yanlış veya haksız görünüyorsa.en: If a finding appears wrong or unfair, the Master may discuss it during the closing meeting in a respectful, reasoned and documented manner; the discussion must not become personal and must be based on the regulations and evidence. If the inspector is convinced, the finding may be dropped before it enters the report; if not, the Master must sign the report, but the signature means "acknowledgment of receipt of the report", not "acceptance of the finding".

Her deficiency veya observation için ISM.en: Under ISM, a root cause analysis is carried out for every deficiency or observation. Using "5 Whys" or similar methods, the managerial/systemic cause underlying the surface technical failure is identified. For example, the root cause of the finding "emergency fire pump did not work" is often not the pump itself but a missing maintenance item in the PMS, untrained personnel or an inadequate stock of spare parts.

Kaptanın burada hassas olması gereken no.en: The point on which the Master must be careful here is the difference between "blame" and "root cause". "The AB was negligent" is not a root cause but an accusation; the real root cause may be "this item was not in the AB's job description" or "familiarization was inadequate". RCA based on just culture is a precondition for an honest reporting culture that does not hide the real cause.

RCA'nın çıktısı, bir düzeltici aksiyon (.en: The output of the RCA is a plan of corrective action (which eliminates the existing problem) and preventive action (which prevents recurrence). While the corrective action may be "repair the pump", the preventive action may be "add this test to the PMS every 3 months, train the personnel concerned, set a minimum stock level for the spare part". Each action is assigned to a responsible person, a deadline and close-out evidence (photo, test report, training record).

Kaptan, tüm bulgu-RCA-CA/PA döngüsünü şi.en: The Master enters the complete finding-RCA-CA/PA cycle into the company's SMS reporting system (usually a non-conformity/CAR form) and forwards it to the DPA. This record is not just a bureaucratic requirement; it is the concrete answer to the question "how did you close out your last finding?" at the next inspection, and it is an input to the company's management review meeting. Actions that are not closed out will come up again and again at vetting and PSC.

Denetçinin en sevdiği teknik, farklı kay.en: The inspector's favorite technique is to cross-check different records. A transfer in the Oil Record Book must be consistent with the engine room logs, the sounding records and the bunker delivery notes (BDN). The deck log, GMDSS log, ECDIS route history and passage plan must not contradict each other. One record contradicting another makes the inspector suspect that "something is being hidden here" and drags the inspection to a forensic depth.

Rest hours kayıtları özellikle hassastır.en: Rest hours records are particularly sensitive: meeting the STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC limits (≥10 hours in 24 hours, ≥77 hours in 7 days) "on paper" while violating them in reality is revealed when the inspector cross-checks them against the port log, gangway watch and cargo operation records. Rest hours tables that "look perfect but are unrealistic" are a red flag for the inspector.

Kayıt sahteciliği — özellikle ORB'de \"m.en: Falsification of records — especially the "magic pipe" in the ORB (concealing the discharge of oily water overboard bypassing the OWS) — is among the crimes most severely punished under maritime law. In the USA, under APPS (Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships), entering a US port with a false ORB is a crime in itself, even if the actual pollution did not take place in US waters; fines of millions of dollars, imprisonment of the Master and a sailing ban on the ship may follow.

Kaptan için temel ilke şudur: bir bulgu,.en: The basic principle for the Master is this: a finding that is honestly recorded is a manageable problem; when concealed, it turns into a crime that ends careers and liberty. Preparing for an inspection does not mean "making a bad reality look good" but "correcting the reality before the inspection and documenting it honestly". Falsification is a far greater risk than any deficiency could ever create.

Kaptan için \"denetime hazır gemi\", den.en: For the Master, a "ship ready for inspection" is not one that is hastily tidied up on the morning of the inspection, but one that is kept in an inspectable condition every day. Discipline in the certificate matrix, honesty in self-audits, depth in root cause analysis and genuine crew competence — when all of these come together, PSC and vetting are merely external confirmation of this continuous preparation. The best Master is the one who has seen and corrected what the inspector sees long before; for that Master, the inspection is not an exam but the confirmation of a result already known.

ISM Code madde 6, şirketin geminin \"uyg.en: ISM Code Section 6 requires the company to ensure that the ship is manned with "qualified, certificated and medically fit" seafarers. The person who implements this section on board is the Master: it is the Master's responsibility to verify that each crew member is competent for their duties, holds the necessary certificates and has been properly familiarized before taking up duties.

Madde 6 ayrıca, geminin emniyeti ve çevr.en: Section 6 also requires the company to ensure that duties critical to the safety of the ship and protection of the environment are understood by the personnel; this covers a common language (working language), the comprehensibility of instructions and the effectiveness of training. In a multinational crew, the adequacy of the common working language (usually English) is a subject questioned directly in ISM audits and accident analyses.

STCW Reg. I/14, şirketleri gemiye atanan.en: STCW Reg. I/14 holds companies responsible for ensuring that the certificates of seafarers assigned to the ship are valid and appropriate to their duties, that STCW-compliant records are kept on board, and that familiarization and emergency coordination are provided. The extension of this responsibility on board is the Master: the company establishes the policy, the Master implements it on board and reports deviations.

Pratikte bu, kaptanın her join eden müre.en: In practice, this means that the Master physically/electronically checks the STCW certificates of every crew member who joins (CoC — Certificate of Competency, CoP — Certificate of Proficiency, GMDSS, tanker endorsement, advanced fire fighting, medical first aid, etc.). If a missing certificate or one close to expiry is found, the company is notified immediately; employing a person without a certificate in a duty that requires one is both an STCW violation and a serious insurance risk.

SOLAS V/14 ve IMO Res. A.1047(27) uyarın.en: Under SOLAS V/14 and IMO Res. A.1047(27), every ship carries a Minimum Safe Manning Document issued by the flag State. This document defines the minimum manning — by position and certificate level — required for the safe navigation of the ship, safety of life, protection of the marine environment and safe operation. The Master must make sure that the actual manning on board never falls below this document.

MSMD bir \"yeterlilik\" değil \"asgari\".en: The MSMD is a "minimum" document, not an "adequacy" document; with heavy cargo operations, frequent port calls, canal transits or fatiguing routes, the minimum manning may in practice be insufficient. If the Master finds that the actual workload forces the minimum crew into rest hours violations, the Master must report this to the company with justification and request additional personnel or a change of rotation. A crew that is "compliant on paper" with minimum manning but "tired in practice" is the classic start of an accident chain.

Kaptan, kadronun yorgunluk seviyesini sü.en: The Master continuously monitors the crew's level of fatigue; the STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC limits (at least 10 hours of rest in 24 hours, at least 77 hours in 7 days) are only a lower limit, not a target. A busy port rotation, frequently broken watches and critical operations (cargo, anchoring, canal) increase fatigue cumulatively. Before critical operations, the Master actually verifies that key personnel are rested.

Manning planlaması ile rest hours yöneti.en: Manning planning and rest hours management are two sides of the same coin: inadequate manning makes rest hours violations mathematically unavoidable. If the Master has to choose between "making the records look clean" and "actually letting the crew rest", the Master must choose the latter and send the company a written request for the manning/rotation that would make the former possible.

STCW ve ISM gereği, gemiye yeni katılan.en: Under STCW and ISM, everyone newly joining the ship — whether seafarer or riding crew/contractor — goes through a basic safety familiarization before taking up duties: they learn their muster station, the alarm signals, the location and donning of the lifejacket and immersion suit, the escape routes, the watertight doors and the basic "do / don't" rules. This familiarization must be completed before the ship berths or before the first critical moments of the voyage.

Kaptanın sorumluluğu, bu tanıtımın \"for.en: The Master's responsibility is to ensure that this familiarization does not consist merely of "getting a form signed". The newcomer must really know where to go when the alarm sounds; for this reason, good familiarization includes a physical tour of the ship (walk-through): the person actually walks to the muster station, is shown the nearest exit and puts on a lifejacket there and then.

Genel tanıtımın ötesinde, her mürettebat.en: Beyond the general familiarization, every crew member is familiarized with the equipment specific to their duties: the officer of the watch is introduced to the make of ECDIS on board, the radar, the autopilot and the GMDSS console; the engineer officer to the ship's main engine, auxiliary systems and alarm panel. An officer keeping a watch alone without having received type-specific training is a recurring accident cause in MAIB reports.

Kaptan, göreve özgü familiarization'ı bi.en: The Master conducts duty-specific familiarization through a checklist and a responsible senior officer (the Chief Officer for deck, the Chief Engineer for the engine room). The critical point is timing: a person may take on a duty alone (e.g. a solo navigational watch) only after familiarization has been completed and their competence has been confirmed. The approach of "they will learn on the first watch" is unacceptable.

STCW sertifikası asgari standardı belgel.en: An STCW certificate documents the minimum standard; however, two officers with identical certificates can show very different competence in practice. From the first watches onward, the Master observes each officer's real level: position-fixing discipline, application of COLREG, command of the equipment, speed of decision-making and behavior under pressure. This observation amounts to drawing up a picture of real competence.

Bu değerlendirme yargılamak için değil,.en: This assessment is not for judging people but for identifying training needs. If an officer's radar plotting is weak, the Master treats this not as a "defect" but as an opportunity for targeted onboard training. The competence matrix determines who may work under supervision and who without supervision in which operation; this is the basis of the allocation of duties and of risk management.

Birçok şirket SMS'i, periyodik competenc.en: Many company SMSs provide for periodic competency assessment forms: a structured, observation-based tool in which specific competence items are scored and development areas are marked. Each period, the Master or a senior officer designated by the Master carries out this assessment, shares the results with the person and links them to a development plan.

Değerlendirmenin değeri, dürüstlüğüyle d.en: The value of the assessment is directly proportional to its honesty. A Master who gives "everyone high marks" both hinders that person's development and misleads the company about the real risk. Conversely, an assessment that only points out weaknesses damages morale. A good assessment is a balanced tool that records strengths and links each development area to a concrete action.

SOLAS Chapter III ve ISM madde 8, düzenl.en: SOLAS Chapter III and ISM Section 8 make regular drills mandatory: abandon ship and fire drills every month (within 24 hours of leaving port if more than 25% of the crew did not take part in drills in the previous month), enclosed space entry & rescue drills at least once every two months, and also damage control, oil spill (SOPEP), man overboard, steering gear failure, security (ISPS) and other scenarios. The Master keeps the schedule of these drills and records that they have actually been carried out.

Tatbikatın amacı kayıt doldurmak değil,.en: The purpose of a drill is not to fill in records but to build muscle memory for a crisis. For this reason a good drill is realistic: the scenario is changed (the same "launch the lifeboat" routine every month turns into rote), difficulty is added (one person is treated as "injured", one exit is assumed to be "blocked"), and an honest debrief is held afterwards. El Faro and similar accidents showed that rote, unrealistic drills do not work in a crisis.

Her tatbikatın asıl değeri debrief'tedir.en: The real value of every drill lies in the debrief: what went well, where time was lost, which equipment did not work as expected, which role remained unclear. The Master runs the debrief not as an "assessment exam" but as an open, no-blame learning session; junior crew members must be able to share mistakes rather than hide them. The lessons learned shape the scenario of the next drill.

Onboard training, drill'lerle sınırlı de.en: Onboard training is not limited to drills: junior personnel are developed continuously through toolbox talks, short training videos, CBT (computer-based training) modules, hands-on equipment-based lessons and "shadow watches" (supervised watches). The Master ties training to a schedule and records it, because PSC and vetting examine training records as evidence that the system is alive.

Bridge Resource Management ve Engine-roo.en: Bridge Resource Management and Engine-room Resource Management became mandatory competences with the STCW Manila amendments. The basic principles are: clear allocation of roles (who is the Master/has the conn, who is on navigation, who is lookout, who handles communications), closed-loop communication (an order given is confirmed by repeating it back), sharing of situational awareness within the team, and error-trapping mechanisms (cross-check, monitoring).

Kaptanın buradaki rolü çift yönlüdür: he.en: The Master's role here is twofold: to lead as head of the team, and to create an environment in which the team can "challenge" the Master. A junior officer being able to say "Master, the CPA looks close to me" is a sign that the team is really working. If this culture is not established, even the most competent team will miss a danger seen by a junior who stays silent.

Etkili ekip yönetimi, hatanın kaçınılmaz.en: Effective team management accepts that error is inevitable and focuses on catching it early. "Just culture" distinguishes between deliberate violation and human error: when a human error is reported, it is not punished but learned from; people are, however, held accountable for reckless risk-taking or deliberate rule violations. By striking this balance, the Master ensures that near-misses and errors are reported rather than hidden.

Near-miss raporlamasının canlı olması, b.en: Active near-miss reporting is the most reliable indicator of a ship's safety culture. A ship on which no near-misses are reported is not a ship where "everything is perfect", but one where "nothing is reported out of fear". The Master encourages reporting, protects those who report and draws a systemic lesson from every report.

Çoğu şirket, mürettebatın gemide kalış s.en: Most companies provide for an appraisal form completed at the end of a crew member's time on board or periodically. This form scores dimensions such as technical competence, safety awareness, teamwork, leadership, discipline and development potential, and forms the basis for promotion/re-employment decisions. The Master or a senior officer makes an assessment that is based on observation, supported by concrete examples and shared with the person.

Adil appraisal, kişiye yüz yüze geri bil.en: A fair appraisal is given to the person with face-to-face feedback; it should not come as a surprise. A Master who manages well gives feedback continuously throughout the period, so that the appraisal is merely a written summary of what has been said during the year. An unfair or arbitrary appraisal affects that person's career and also damages the sense of fairness on board, and therefore morale.

Appraisal yalnızca bir not değil, bir ge.en: An appraisal is not just a grade, but the start of a development plan. For a strong junior officer, the Master may plan the steps of preparation for promotion (e.g. more supervised maneuvering, responsibility for coastal navigation, mentoring in paperwork). Conversely, for a person who is struggling, concrete improvement targets and support are defined.

Kaptanın halefiyet (succession) perspekt.en: The Master is expected to have a succession perspective: today's Second Officer is tomorrow's Chief Officer; today's Chief Officer is tomorrow's Master. A good Master regards training people who can take the Master's own place not as a threat but as a professional duty. This is the only real source of sustainable competence for the fleet.

Disiplin, ceza değil, paylaşılan standar.en: Discipline is not punishment, but the upholding of shared standards. MLC 2006 and the company SMS provide for a fair procedure for disciplinary action (warning, investigation, right of defense, record); the Master applies this procedure consistently and without arbitrariness. Reacting differently to different people for the same violation is what destroys authority fastest.

Disiplinin amacı, bir kişiyi cezalandırm.en: The purpose of discipline is less to punish an individual than to remind the whole team how seriously the standard is taken. In serious cases (violence, drunkenness, leaving one's post, a positive D&A result), the Master coordinates with the company immediately; most everyday matters, however, are resolved through an early, private and fair conversation, without the need for formal action. A good Master uses formal discipline as a last resort.

Modern bir gemi mürettebatı genellikle ç.en: The crew of a modern ship is usually multinational and multicultural. The Master guarantees respect for differences of language, culture, religion and tradition, the prohibition of discrimination (MLC) and equal treatment. In an isolated environment, morale is maintained through food quality, rest, internet/communication facilities, a fair distribution of work and a respectful atmosphere. Low morale is an accident factor as dangerous as fatigue.

Kaptan, mürettebatın refahını (welfare).en: The Master should treat crew welfare — long contracts, missing family, isolation, mental health — as a visible priority. An open-door policy, a complaints procedure that really works and a person's ability to speak up safely when struggling are both an MLC requirement and the basis of operational safety. A happy and respected crew is a safe crew.

Mürettebat rotasyonu (crew change) sürek.en: Crew rotation (crew change) carries a constant risk of loss of information; the handovers of the Master, Chief Officer and Chief Engineer in particular are critical. A good handover covers a realistic transfer of open issues, findings not yet closed, ongoing maintenance items, charterer/company instructions, critical equipment characteristics and team dynamics. A written handover note is standard, and where possible the handover is done face to face (overlap).

Kaptan değişiminde, gelen kaptanın gemiy.en: When the Master changes, the first days are vital for the incoming Master to grasp the ship, the SMS, the team and the open risks quickly. An incomplete handover puts the new Master in the middle of a risk they do not know about; for this reason, the outgoing Master is obliged to make an honest and complete handover instead of hiding problems in order to "look good".

Kaptanın kadro ve eğitim yönetimi, tek b.en: The Master's management of manning and training goes beyond the boundaries of a single ship; the appraisals given, the officers trained and the competence gaps reported feed the company's fleet-wide human resources planning. By reporting training needs and certificate gaps to the company regularly, the Master ensures that the next rotation is better prepared.

Sonuçta gemideki insan kaynağı, en pahal.en: Ultimately, the people on board are a more critical resource than the most expensive equipment: even the most advanced ship is unsafe with a team that is not competent, rested and motivated. The Master's skill in manning and training management is measured by a team that works quietly, does not fall apart in a crisis and keeps improving.

Kaptanın kadro ve eğitim yönetimindeki b.en: The Master's success in manning and training management is not a polished list but a reality that shows itself in a crisis: everyone knowing their place when the alarm sounds, a junior officer being able to speak up about a danger they see, a tired team having been rested in advance, and an error being reported rather than hidden when it occurs. None of these results is a coincidence; all of them are the product of the disciplined competence tracking, genuine familiarization, realistic drills and fair leadership that the Master maintains every day. A good Master knows that the best equipment on board is its people, and regards developing those people as the most important duty.

Kaptan, geminin yasal temsilcisidir (mas.en: The Master is the legal representative of the ship (master as agent). A document the Master signs is not merely a confirmation; it is a legal commitment that binds the ship, the shipowner and, in some cases, the charterer. The signature on a bill of lading (B/L) triggers the contract of carriage, the signature on the NOR triggers the laytime clock, and a letter of protest triggers a declaration reserving rights against the other party. For this reason, the Master must know the legal consequence of every document the Master signs.

İmza atılırken \"for and on behalf of th.en: When signing, qualifications such as "for and on behalf of the Master" or "as agent only" may limit the Master's personal liability; however, these wordings must be used with care. If the Master signs documents prepared by the agent without reading them, this later leads to the presumption that "the Master approved", which is difficult to reverse.

Belgeler iki ana kategoriye ayrılır: (a).en: Documents fall into two main categories: (a) official books made mandatory by the flag State or international conventions (official log book, oil record book, garbage record book, rest hour records); (b) commercial/operational documents (NOR, SOF, mate's receipt, manifest). In official books, page numbers may not be skipped, erasures may not be made and entries may not be filled in retrospectively; errors are struck through with a single line and initialed.

Bu ayrım önemlidir çünkü resmi defterler.en: This distinction matters because falsification of official books falls under criminal law and may lead to PSC detention. In the USA, companies have received million-dollar fines for falsifying the Oil Record Book (magic pipe cases).

Ölüm, ciddi yaralanma, doğum, kaybolma (.en: Events such as death, serious injury, birth or disappearance (man overboard) are entered in the OLB immediately and usually require a witness signature. These entries are primary evidence in consular, insurance and judicial proceedings. A back-dated entry destroys its value as legal evidence and exposes the Master to personal liability.

Deck log, çatışma, karaya oturma veya ağ.en: The deck log is the main source for the sea protest and the P&I process after a collision, grounding or heavy weather damage. For this reason, log entries during and after an incident must be kept in as much detail as possible, and helm orders and engine orders must be recorded with time stamps. A log entry that contradicts the VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) data damages credibility in litigation.

Bayrak devletleri giderek elektronik kay.en: Flag States are increasingly permitting electronic record books (e-OLB, e-ORB); the 2020 amendment to MARPOL formally recognized the use of electronic record books. In a digital system too, tamper-proofing (audit trail), time stamps and authorized user identification are essential. The Master confirms that the system is approved (type-approved) and can produce readable printouts for inspections.

Deck log ile VDR/ECDIS kayıtları arasınd.en: Consistency between the deck log and the VDR/ECDIS records is critically important. In a dispute, the first documents the parties ask for are the VDR download, the ECDIS playback and the deck log. After a critical incident, the Master must ensure that the VDR data is preserved (save/lock) without being overwritten; otherwise evidence is lost.

NOR, geminin yükleme/boşaltma için her b.en: The NOR is the document notifying the charterer/receiver that the ship is ready in all respects to load/discharge, and it starts the laytime clock. For the NOR to be valid, the ship must be physically and legally ready (free pratique obtained, customs formalities completed, access to the cargo open). An NOR tendered too early or invalidly disrupts the laytime calculation and leads to demurrage/dispatch disputes.

Charter party'de \"WIPON, WIBON, WIFPON,.en: Clauses such as "WIPON, WIBON, WIFPON, WICCON" (whether in port/berth/free pratique/customs cleared or not) in the charter party determine when the NOR may be tendered. The Master must know these clauses and tender the NOR in writing at the right time and to the right party (usually the charterer and the agent). The time of tender (date and time) is very important.

SOF, limandaki tüm olayların (varış, dem.en: The SOF is a time-stamped chronological record of all events in port (arrival, anchoring, berthing, NOR tender, cargo commencement/completion, waiting times, weather delays, breakdowns). The agent prepares it; the Master checks and signs it. Through the time sheet, the SOF is the basis of the demurrage/dispatch calculation; for this reason, the reason for each delay (rain, no cargo, awaiting documents) must be stated clearly.

Kaptan, SOF'taki çelişkili veya gemi ale.en: Before signing, the Master corrects any entry in the SOF that is contradictory or against the ship's interest; if it is not corrected, the Master signs with the remark "signed under protest, time as per ship's log". This remark ensures that the ship's records are taken as the basis later in arbitration.

Mate's Receipt, yükün gemiye alındığını.en: The Mate's Receipt is the preliminary document showing that the cargo has been received on board, and it forms the basis of the B/L. Reservations about the cargo (clausing) are first entered on the mate's receipt; these reservations are carried over to the B/L. The Cargo Manifest, on the other hand, is a list of all cargo (per B/L) with port, consignee, quantity and description, and it is the basis of the customs declaration.

Manifestteki hata veya eksiklik, gümrükt.en: An error or omission in the manifest can lead to customs penalties, the cargo not being released and delays to the ship. The Master confirms that the manifest matches the B/Ls and the actual cargo.

IMDG yük için Dangerous Goods Declaratio.en: For IMDG cargo, a Dangerous Goods Declaration (DGD), a Container/Vehicle Packing Certificate and correct stowage/segregation documents are mandatory. For bulk cargo, the cargo declaration obtained from the shipper under the IMSBC Code (including TML/MC information) and, where necessary, a Trimming Certificate are required. Missing documents are grounds for refusing to load.

ORB tutarsızlığı (örn. sludge üretimi il.en: ORB inconsistencies (e.g. an imbalance between sludge generation and delivery/incineration) immediately draw suspicion in PSC and US Coast Guard inspections. Most "magic pipe" (illegal bypass) cases have come to light through a contradiction between the ORB and the actual situation.

Crew List, gemideki tüm mürettebatın kim.en: The Crew List is the official document containing the identity, rank, nationality and certificate details of all crew members on board; it is required by immigration and the port authority on arrival in port. Under MLC 2006 Standard A2.1, a signed SEA for every seafarer must be on board; the Master checks that the SEAs are complete and up to date.

Mürettebat sertifikaları (CoC, GMDSS, me.en: The Master keeps a tracking matrix for crew certificates (CoC, GMDSS, medical, STCW courses) and ship certificates (SMC, ISSC, class, statutory). Documents due to expire are included in port and class planning. Sailing with an invalid certificate carries the risk of both PSC detention and loss of insurance cover (P&I cover prejudice).

Letter of Protest, kaptanın karşı tarafa.en: A Letter of Protest is a document by which the Master formally notifies the other party (terminal, charterer, shipper, surveyor) of an objection to a situation and reserves rights. Typical subjects: cargo damage, draft survey discrepancy, slow loading/discharging rate, delay due to bad weather, terminal equipment failure, contaminated fuel (bunker dispute). The LOP is given in writing and, if possible, signed by the other party; even if it is refused, a "presented and refused" note is entered.

LOP, sea protest'ten farklıdır: sea prot.en: An LOP differs from a sea protest: a sea protest is a formal declaration made before a notary, whereas an LOP is a commercial instrument of objection between the parties. The two are complementary.

Kaçak yolcu tespitinde FAL Konvansiyonu.en: When a stowaway is found, the procedures of the FAL Convention and the IMO Res. FAL.13(42) guidelines are applied. The Master ensures the person's safety, enters the identity details and the circumstances of discovery in the standard stowaway report form, and notifies the flag State, the next port State, the company and the P&I Club. The stowaway is not included in the crew; humane treatment and safety are, however, provided.

Stowaway maliyeti (repatriasyon, fines,.en: Stowaway costs (repatriation, fines, detention) are usually within P&I cover; for this reason, early and complete notification is essential for the insurance to respond. Incomplete documentation puts the cover at risk.

ISM Code madde 11, SMS kapsamındaki tüm.en: ISM Code Section 11 requires all documents within the SMS to be current, valid and checked by authorized persons. The removal of invalid/obsolete revisions, the controlled document list and revision tracking are carried out under the Master's supervision. Document control discipline is a main focus area in internal and external ISM audits.

Her belge türünün yasal saklama süresi v.en: Each type of document has a legal retention period: ORB 3 years, garbage record book 2 years, deck/official log book generally a long period after the event, depending on the flag State. Completed books are handed over to the company and archived. At a change of Master (handover), all active and completed books, certificates and files on ongoing disputes are handed over to the new Master with a signed handover record.

Aşağıdaki liste, kaptanın günlük ve lima.en: The list below summarizes the Master's daily and port-by-port document discipline. The list should be tailored to the ship type, the nature of the voyages and the requirements of the flag State.

Belge yönetimi, denizciliğin görünmeyen.en: Document management is one of the invisible but most decisive disciplines of seafaring. A well-kept log book is the strongest shield protecting the Master and the company in court; a careless or falsified record, on the other hand, brings down even the best defense. The Master's aim is to turn the principle of "every document at the time it happens, as it happens and in legible form" into a lasting culture on board.

Pilotun gemiye çıkması, kaptanın sorumlu.en: The pilot boarding the ship does not remove the Master's responsibility. The pilot provides local expertise; however, the ship's maneuvering characteristics, condition and ultimate safety are within the Master's knowledge and authority. If the Master considers that a piece of advice from the pilot is endangering the ship, the Master intervenes.

Pilot köprüüstüne geldiğinde MPX kartı d.en: When the pilot arrives on the bridge, the MPX card is completed: the transit plan, speed profile, expected maneuvers, use of tugs, berth/anchorage information, UKC, weather/current and the emergency/abort plan are shared. The Master provides the pilot with the ship's maneuvering data (turning circle, stopping distance, draft, propeller/rudder characteristics).

Pilotun planı ile geminin passage plan'ı.en: If there is a significant difference between the pilot's plan and the ship's passage plan, it is clarified before the maneuver starts. "Starting without talking" is a recurring error pattern in bridge accident investigations.

Vardiya zabiti, pilotaj boyunca geminin.en: Throughout pilotage, the OOW independently monitors the ship's progress (position, speed, rate of turn, UKC) and reports any deviation from the plan to the Master. Helm/engine orders given by the pilot are repeated back (closed-loop) and their execution is confirmed. The team supports the pilot not with "blind trust" but with active monitoring.

Pilot biniş/inişi, SOLAS V/23 ve ilgili.en: Pilot embarkation/disembarkation is carried out with a pilot ladder/combination ladder complying with SOLAS V/23 and the related regulations. The Master verifies that the equipment is rigged correctly and that lighting, a lifebuoy, a line and the supervising crew are ready. Incorrectly rigged pilot ladders are a real and persistent cause of pilot deaths.

Pilotaj/manevra öncesi steering gear tes.en: Before pilotage/maneuvering, the steering gear test, the engine being ready for maneuvering, the anchor stations being ready, the tug line-handling team and communications are verified. The Master confirms that the bridge team and the forward/aft stations know their duties and are rested.

Kaptan, pilotun bir hareketinin gemiyi t.en: If the Master is convinced that an action of the pilot is endangering the ship, the Master intervenes immediately and, if necessary, takes direct control. This is not disrespect for pilotage but the Master's legal duty. The event is recorded.

Pilotaj, uzmanlık ile nihai sorumluluğun.en: Pilotage is a delicate process in which expertise and ultimate responsibility work hand in hand. The Master's MPX discipline, active bridge monitoring and, where necessary, decisive intervention turn the pilot's local knowledge into a safe passage.

ISM Code madde 4, her şirketin bir veya.en: ISM Code Section 4 requires every company to designate one or more Designated Persons Ashore (DPA). The DPA has two critical features: direct access to the highest level of management, and the duty of monitoring the safety and pollution prevention aspects of the ship's operation. The DPA forms the bridge between the Master and the company's highest level of management; it is a safety line independent of the commercial line (operations, chartering). This independence is designed to prevent commercial pressure from overriding safety decisions.

Kaptan, DPA'ya ulaşmak için hiçbir izne.en: The Master needs no permission to contact the DPA and can reach the DPA 24/7, day and night. The DPA's contact details (telephone, e-mail, satellite line) must be posted visibly on the bridge and in the SMS documentation. PSC inspectors often ask "who is the DPA and where is the number?"; the crew not knowing this is a cause of an ISM major non-conformity.

Overriding authority, kaptanın emniyet,.en: Overriding authority is the Master's authority to take any decision the Master considers necessary for safety, security and protection of the marine environment, regardless of the instructions of the company or the charterer. ISM Code 5.2 requires this authority to be confirmed in writing in the company's SMS. This turns the Master from a mere "order-taker of the company" into the final decision-maker on safety.

Bu yetki soyut bir hak değil, iletişim d.en: This authority is not an abstract right but a tool tied to communication discipline. When the Master uses overriding authority, the Master does so not simply by saying "I will not do it", but by notifying the DPA in writing of the reasons, the alternative plan and the risk. Companies review records of the use of this authority in internal ISM audits; the fact that it has never been used is sometimes regarded as an indicator of a "culture of fear".

Emniyet/kirlilik/security olayları emniy.en: Safety/pollution/security events go through the safety line (DPA); commercial matters (laytime, bunkers, ETA, speed) go through the operations/chartering line. The Master's most frequent mistake is to put a safety event into the commercial line, or a commercial matter into the safety line. This confusion causes both delays in response and a break in the legal chain of evidence.

Resmi yazışmalar (port authority, flag s.en: Official correspondence (port authority, flag State, class, customs) usually goes through the agent or directly under the Master's signature. Every statement made to third parties (terminal, the charterer's surveyor, inspector) must be measured and documented, as it may legally bind the company.

Denizcilikte sözlü iletişim kanıt değild.en: In shipping, verbal communication is not evidence. The Master's basic principle: "if you said it, write it down; if you did not write it down, it is as if you never said it." Every critical communication is recorded by e-mail, log book, SOF (Statement of Facts), Letter of Protest or telex. Telephone conversations are immediately confirmed in summary by e-mail ("as per our telcon at 0930 LT...").

Belge zinciri ileride doğacak demurrage,.en: The document chain is the strongest defense protecting the Master and the company in future demurrage, off-hire, cargo damage or accident disputes. Time stamps (UTC and LT together), position, weather and the counterpart must always be stated. Back-dating documents, however, is a serious disciplinary and legal offense; when courts detect it, the credibility of all the records collapses.

Time charter'da (örn. NYPE, SHELLTIME) c.en: In a time charter (e.g. NYPE, SHELLTIME), the charterer hires the ship for a certain period and directs its commercial use (employment). Under clause 8 of NYPE, the Master must comply with the charterer's instructions "as regards employment, agency or other arrangements"; however, this obligation does NOT extend to the safe navigation of the ship, navigation itself or the Master's overriding authority. The charterer determines the route, port and speed commercially; the Master remains responsible for navigational safety.

Time charter'da \"off-hire\" (kira durma.en: In a time charter, the concept of "off-hire" is critical: if the ship cannot perform because of breakdown, crew shortage or the Master's fault, the charterer may stop paying hire. For this reason, the Master's correct and timely reporting of situations such as delays, engine breakdown and deviation directly affects the company's revenue. The "safe port / safe berth" warranty also lies with the charterer; the Master objects to an instruction to go to an unsafe port and issues a Letter of Protest.

Voyage charter'da (örn. GENCON) armatör.en: In a voyage charter (e.g. GENCON), the ship is chartered to carry a specific cargo from A to B; commercial management remains largely with the shipowner. Here the Master's main contact with the charterer revolves around the NOR (Notice of Readiness), laytime and demurrage. A validly tendered NOR (the ship "in all respects ready") starts the laytime clock; early/invalid NORs are the main subject of demurrage disputes.

Kaptan, voyage charter'da SOF'u (Stateme.en: In a voyage charter, the Master keeps the SOF (Statement of Facts) meticulously: NOR tendered/accepted times, pilot on/off, all fast, hose connected, commenced/completed loading, weather stoppage, equipment breakdown. The demurrage/dispatch calculation is made entirely from these records. Every "remark" in the SOF signed with the charterer's surveyor can make a difference of thousands of dollars later.

Charterer'in voyage instructions'ı (rota.en: The charterer's voyage instructions (route, speed, ECO speed, weather routing service, bunker port) are commercially binding; however, no instruction that endangers safety is binding. When faced with an unsafe instruction, the Master asks for the instruction in writing, gives a reasoned refusal in writing, proposes an alternative and informs the DPA. Saying "no" protects the Master when done professionally and on record; when done argumentatively and verbally, it leaves the Master on their own.

Pratikte en sık çatışma \"unsafe port /.en: In practice, disputes most often arise over "unsafe port / unsafe berth", "meeting the ETA by excessive speed" and "continuing the voyage with deficient equipment". In these situations the Master gives priority to safety; the commercial consequences (off-hire, demurrage) are settled between the company's lawyers and the charterer, but the loss of life or of the ship cannot be undone.

Liman acentesi, gemiyi limanda temsil ed.en: The port agent is the party that represents the ship in port, arranges pilots/tugs, handles customs/immigration formalities and coordinates supplies (provisions, bunkers, fresh water), waste collection, crew changes and the flow of paperwork. The agent is sometimes appointed by the shipowner (owner's agent) and sometimes by the charterer (charterer's agent); this distinction matters where the parties' interests diverge. Since the charterer's agent is commercially tied to the charterer, the Master must not relax record-keeping discipline, in order to protect the interests of the ship/shipowner.

Kaptan, acenteye pre-arrival mesajı ile.en: In the pre-arrival message, the Master informs the agent of the ETA, draft, gross/net tonnage, last 10 ports, crew list, waste quantities, supply needs and special requests (MEDEVAC, repatriation, spare parts). The Master requires all expenses incurred by the agent to be documented transparently through the PDA/FDA (Proforma / Final Disbursement Account) and queries doubtful items.

IMO FAL Convention (Convention on Facili.en: The IMO FAL Convention (Convention on Facilitation of International Maritime Traffic) defines the standard documents: General Declaration, Cargo Declaration, Ship's Stores Declaration, Crew's Effects, Crew List, Passenger List, Dangerous Goods and Maritime Declaration of Health. The Master is responsible for the accuracy of these documents; incomplete/incorrect declarations lead to customs penalties and delays. As of 2024, many ports require electronic declarations through a Maritime Single Window.

Kaptan, acente aracılığıyla yürütülse de.en: Although the FAL documents are handled through the agent, the Master signs them personally and must therefore check their content. In particular, tobacco/alcohol/cash not declared in the Ship's Stores and Crew's Effects declarations leads to heavy fines ("manifest violation") in the USA and many other countries. Passport and seaman's book details in the Crew List are critical for immigration.

PSC denetimleri (Paris MoU, Tokyo MoU, U.en: During PSC inspections (Paris MoU, Tokyo MoU, USCG, etc.), the Master is the inspector's sole official point of contact. Open, honest and documented communication is essential; concealing documents or misleading the inspector makes a detention more severe. Every deficiency on the Form A/B issued at the end of the inspection is recorded with a code; code "30 — detainable" means the ship is detained. The Master reports the findings immediately to the DPA and the technical department and coordinates the corrective action plan with the company.

Kaptan, haksız gördüğü bir detention'a k.en: The Master may exercise the right of appeal, through the flag State and the company, against a detention considered unjustified; however, moving the ship during this process without the inspector's permission is a serious violation. An appeal, too, must be supported by documents and justification.

Kaptan, sertifikaların (Safety Construct.en: The Master tracks the validity dates and survey windows of the certificates (Safety Construction, Safety Equipment, Safety Radio, IOPP, ISM/SMC, ISSC, MLC/DMLC); an expired or conditional certificate is a ground for PSC detention. "Condition of class" (CoC) items identified in communication with the class surveyor are closed out on time.

Terminal ile iletişim emniyet kritiktir..en: Communication with the terminal is safety-critical. On tankers, the Ship-Shore Safety Checklist is completed after berthing in accordance with ISGOTT and reconfirmed every watch; at the pre-transfer conference, the loading rate, max pressure, ESD (Emergency Shut Down) signal, communication failure procedure and authority to stop are agreed. The Master uses the overriding authority to say "no" to an unsafe request from the terminal representative (e.g. starting the transfer before the checklist is completed).

Petrol/kimyasal tankerlerde OCIMF SIRE 2.en: On oil/chemical tankers the OCIMF SIRE 2.0 inspection, and in dry cargo the RightShip inspection, are decisive for the ship's commercial survival. The Master communicates with the vetting inspector in a professional and well-prepared manner and responds to observations with explanation and corrective action rather than defensiveness. Negative observations in the vetting report can lead to the charterer rejecting the ship (vetting rejection); this directly affects company revenue.

Cargo surveyor, draft surveyor, bunker s.en: Every joint measurement or signature made with the cargo surveyor, draft surveyor, bunker surveyor and P&I surveyor may bind the company. The Master endorses any disputed measurement or statement "for receipt only" / "under protest" and issues a Letter of Protest. Verbal admissions made to a surveyor may later be used as evidence against the ship.

Ciddi kazada (çatışma, oturma, yangın, k.en: In a serious casualty (collision, grounding, fire, pollution, loss of life, piracy), the communication sequence must be memorized in advance: first safety of life and MRCC/MAYDAY, then the DPA, then the flag State and P&I, then the charterer and the agent. The company's Emergency Response Plan (ERP) typically defines an Emergency Response Team (ERT) and a 24/7 hotline. The Master's task is to report the facts on scene quickly, accurately and without exaggeration, and not to speculate.

Kirlilik olayında SOPEP/SMPEP devreye gi.en: In a pollution incident, the SOPEP/SMPEP is activated; the coastal State, the port authority and P&I are informed immediately. In US waters, notification of the QI (Qualified Individual) and the OSRO under OPA 90 is time-critical; delay multiplies the penalty. In the initial report, the Master uses the framework "estimated quantity, source, action taken, assistance required".

Kaza sonrası kaptan ve mürettebat, medya.en: After a casualty, the Master and crew make NO statements to the media, shore surveyors, the other party's lawyers or on social media. All external communication goes through the spokesperson appointed by the company and the P&I club/lawyers. An early, careless sentence ("I think the speed was too high") becomes evidence against the ship in criminal and compensation proceedings. This discipline is explained to the crew in advance in a briefing.

Kaptan, resmi soruşturma (flag, coastal,.en: The Master is honest in statements given to official investigations (flag State, coastal State, MAIB) but knows the right to refrain from self-incriminating statements without legal counsel. In many countries, criminalization of the Master after a casualty (criminalization of seafarers) is a real risk; the P&I "loss prevention" department provides legal support in this respect.

Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) tetikl.en: When the Ship Security Alert System (SSAS) is activated, the signal goes silently to the CSO and the flag State; no alarm sounds on the bridge (so that pirates do not notice). The Master knows the SSAS test and activation procedure, the conditions for completing a Declaration of Security (DoS) and the reporting for high risk area (HRA) transits (UKMTO, MSCHOA).

Korsan saldırısı anında iletişim sırası:.en: Communication sequence during a pirate attack: UKMTO/MSCHOA, naval forces, CSO/DPA, flag State. The Master's decision to retreat to the citadel is the most effective way of protecting the crew's lives; however, the citadel's communication and resilience criteria must be tested in advance.

Kaptanın iletişim altyapısı GMDSS (DSC,.en: The Master's communication infrastructure covers GMDSS (DSC, Inmarsat-C, MF/HF/VHF, EPIRB, SART) and commercial satellite systems (FleetBroadband, VSAT, Starlink and similar). In distress, urgency and safety traffic, the correct channel and procedure are vital: MAYDAY (distress), PAN-PAN (urgency), SECURITE (safety). The VHF Ch16 listening watch and Ch13 (bridge-to-bridge maneuvering) discipline are daily routine at sea.

Ticari e-posta ve uydu hattının ucuzlama.en: Cheaper commercial e-mail and satellite links have made communication easier, but have also created pressure to "ask about everything instantly". The Master handles routine commercial traffic through economy/store-and-forward systems and urgent safety traffic through a real-time channel, and does not mix the two. For cybersecurity, the Master verifies messages against the risk of e-mail phishing and fake instructions (especially bunker/payment fraud).

Resmi yevmiye (Official Log Book), deck.en: The Official Log Book, deck log, bell book, GMDSS log, oil record book, garbage record book and rest hours records are the written backbone of the Master's communication discipline. These records are the "single source of truth" between the ship and the outside world and may be requested at any time by PSC, vetting inspectors or insurers. The VDR (Voyage Data Recorder) is the most reliable evidence after a casualty; preserving the VDR data (save/preserve) is one of the Master's first actions in a casualty.

Kayıtların tutarlılığı kritiktir: deck l.en: Consistency of records is critical: the position in the deck log, ECDIS, GPS and the SOF must not contradict each other. A contradiction leads an investigation to conclude that "the records are unreliable" and undermines the insurance defense. The Master periodically cross-checks the records for consistency.

Kaptanın iletişim becerisi, \"kibar yazı.en: The Master's communication skill is not "polite correspondence" but the discipline of delivering the right message to the right party at the right time, in documented form. Keeping the DPA line open, managing charterer pressure professionally and maintaining signature and statement discipline towards third parties protect the Master both legally and in terms of safety. The principle to remember is this: commercial pressure is temporary, but the casualty and legal consequences of poorly managed communication are permanent. A prudent Master is one who, even at moments when saying "yes" is easy, can say the "no" that safety requires, with reasons and in writing.

Stajyer, STCW A-III/1 yeterlilik kazanma.en: The cadet is a trainee engineer working towards STCW A-III/1 competence; however, legal responsibility for the watch always rests with the EOOW on duty. Under no circumstances may the cadet independently start/stop machinery, switch valves, close breakers or reset alarms. Before every action, the cadet states the intention to the EOOW, obtains approval and carries out the action under supervision.

Bu prensip \"challenge and response\" (s.en: This principle is part of the "challenge and response" culture. If the cadet notices an abnormality, the cadet is expected to report it to the EOOW immediately; an observation that seems minor (for example a leak at a flange or a rise in bearing temperature) may be an early sign of a serious failure. The cadet is expected to report, not to stay silent.

Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (Unattended Ma.en: Most modern ships are UMS (Unattended Machinery Space) certified; the engine room may be left unmanned at night and alarms are routed to the bridge and to the duty engineer's cabin. The cadet learns how the engine room is monitored in both attended (manned) and unattended periods.

Vardiya devri, EOOW'lar arasında yapılan.en: The watch handover is a formal transfer of information between EOOWs. By following this process closely, the cadet learns which information is critical: the status of running machinery, maintenance work in progress, isolated equipment (under LOTO), tank levels, transfers in progress (fuel, ballast, bilge) and outstanding alarms.

STCW, gelen mühendisin vardiyayı devralm.en: STCW requires the relieving engineer to be fully informed about the condition of the equipment, operations in progress and potential hazards before taking over the watch. If the relieving engineer feels physically or mentally unfit for duty, the watch is not taken over. By observing this, the cadet internalizes the professional discipline of this standard.

Engine Log Book, makine dairesinin yasal.en: The Engine Log Book is the legal memory of the engine room. Hourly parameters (RPM, exhaust gas temp, scavenge air pressure, jacket cooling temp, LO pressure, FO temp/viscosity), tank levels and significant events are recorded. The cadet first takes readings under supervision, then starts keeping the log personally under the EOOW's control.

Kayıtlar gerçek, zamanında ve düzeltilme.en: Entries must be true, timely and unaltered (no false data). If a parameter goes outside its limits, both the value and the action taken are recorded. These records have evidential value in Port State Control (PSC) inspections, insurance investigations and casualty investigations.

Tur, genellikle yukarıdan aşağıya veya b.en: The round is usually made in a logical order, from top to bottom or from one system to the next: the main engine and its surroundings, generators, boiler, purifier room, pump platforms, separators/clarifiers, air compressors, cooling systems, steering gear room and bilge wells. During the round, the cadet learns to use four senses: "look, listen, smell, touch" (by sight, by sound, by smell, by temperature).

Gözle: sızıntı, gevşek bağlantı, anormal.en: Look: leaks, loose connections, abnormal levels, vibration. Listen: unusual knocking, cavitation, rubbing noise. Smell: burnt insulation, oil/fuel vapor, exhaust gas leaks. Touch (carefully): bearing housing temperature, temperature differences between pipes. This sense-based diagnosis reveals early faults that panel readings cannot catch.

Bilge well seviyeleri turun kritik bir p.en: Bilge well levels are a critical part of the round. A rising bilge level may indicate a hidden leak (seawater, cooling water, FO/LO). The cadet learns the bilge alarm system, the Oily Water Separator (OWS) and the logic of the 15 ppm bilge alarm/oil content monitor; however, pumping out bilges is never within the cadet's independent authority.

MARPOL Annex I, makine dairesi sintine s.en: MARPOL Annex I requires that engine-room bilge water may be pumped overboard only through the OWS and at less than 15 ppm. Every bilge transfer is recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I. The cadet learns this recording logic; unlawful bilge discharge (magic pipe) is one of the most severely punished maritime offenses.

Stajyer, ana makinenin temel parametrele.en: The cadet learns the main engine's key parameters and their normal ranges: the exhaust gas temperature of each cylinder (cylinder exhaust deviation), scavenge air pressure, turbocharger RPM, jacket cooling water inlet/outlet, piston cooling oil outlet, LO inlet pressure/temp and fuel oil viscosity/temp. These values are interrelated; the trend is interpreted, not a single value.

Örneğin bir silindirin egzoz sıcaklığı d.en: For example, if the exhaust temperature of one cylinder deviates noticeably from the others (deviation), that cylinder may have a combustion problem, an injector fault or a fuel index imbalance. By learning these correlations, the cadet grasps the physical meaning behind the panel readings.

Jeneratör yükü, kazan buhar basıncı, hav.en: Generator load, boiler steam pressure, air receiver pressure, cooling water temperatures and the sea water cooling system differential pressure (an indicator of filter clogging) are read regularly. On modern ships, the Alarm and Monitoring System (AMS) logs these values continuously; the cadet learns to read the trend displays.

Trend analizi proaktif bakımın temelidir.en: Trend analysis is the basis of proactive maintenance: a slowly rising bearing temperature, a gradually falling LO pressure or an increasing differential pressure gives a warning days before a sudden failure. Instead of saying "it is within limits for now", the cadet learns to ask "which way is it going?"

Makine dairesi alarmları kademelidir: ön.en: Engine room alarms are graded: first a warning (alarm), then slow-down (automatic speed reduction) and finally shut-down (automatic stop). Critical alarms (LO low pressure, jacket water high temp, scavenge fire, overspeed) trigger automatic intervention to protect the engine. The cadet learns the meaning of each alarm and the action it triggers.

Bir alarm çaldığında stajyer paniğe kapı.en: When an alarm sounds, the cadet, without panicking, reads the alarm, informs the EOOW and verifies the relevant parameter on the panel and locally. The cadet does not silence/reset the alarm independently. With multiple alarms (alarm flooding), identifying the most critical one and finding the root cause is the EOOW's job; the cadet assists.

Oil Mist Detector (OMD) alarmı, krank ka.en: An Oil Mist Detector (OMD) alarm indicates that a bearing inside the crankcase has overheated and is producing oil mist; this is a precursor of a crankcase explosion. On this alarm the crankcase doors must never be opened; wait until the engine has cooled down (usually 20-30 min). The cadet must know this lethal risk.
