Scavenge fire ise scavenge boşluğunda bi.en: A scavenge fire is the ignition of oil accumulated in the scavenge space; the exhaust temperature rises, the load is reduced and the fixed smothering system (steam/CO2) is kept ready. These events are critical safety lessons on which the cadet must base the answer to the question "why do we wait on a crankcase alarm?"

ERRM, köprüüstündeki BRM'in (Bridge Reso.en: ERRM is the engine room counterpart of BRM (Bridge Resource Management) on the bridge. It is based on the principles of open communication, task sharing, situational awareness and breaking the error chain. The cadet is the most junior member of the team but an important part of the "speak up" culture.

Closed-loop communication (kapalı döngü.en: Closed-loop communication is essential: when an order is given, the receiver repeats it (read-back) and the sender confirms. The order "Put No. 2 generator on standby" is confirmed as "No. 2 generator on standby, understood". This prevents accidents caused by misunderstanding.

Manevra durumlarında (liman giriş-çıkış,.en: During maneuvering (entering/leaving port, narrow channels), the engine room goes to standby: an extra generator is put in parallel, the main engine is switched from UMS to manual control and the EOOW stands by in the control room. The cadet observes the coordination between telegraph orders, speed requests from the bridge and the "stand by engines / finished with engines" orders.

Tank seviyelerinin doğru takibi, makinen.en: Correct monitoring of tank levels ensures an uninterrupted fuel/oil supply to the engine and prevents overflow/spillage. The cadet learns why a service tank level is kept within a certain range (settling time, need for water draining).

FO/DO iç transfer, LO yenileme ve fresh.en: Internal FO/DO transfers, LO replenishment and fresh water transfers are operations in which the cadet takes part under supervision. Before the transfer, the valve alignment is verified and the overflow tank level is checked; throughout the transfer, the level is monitored continuously. An incorrect valve line-up or an uncontrolled transfer creates a risk of overflow and pollution.

Stajyer her transferde \"kaynaktan hedef.en: In every transfer, the cadet learns to build the complete line-up "from source to destination" mentally: which valve is open, which pump is running, which tank is filling. This discipline is the basic skill that will prevent wrong-transfer errors later, as an independent engineer.

Sıcak yüzeylere (egzoz manifoldu, buhar.en: Bare contact with hot surfaces (exhaust manifold, steam line), standing near a rotating shaft/coupling and careless movement on an oily floor are causes of accidents. The cadet learns to use ladders with "three points of contact", the correct lifting technique and the locations of the emergency stop buttons.

Stajyer, tank/sintine/cofferdam gibi kap.en: The cadet learns the importance of the enclosed space entry permit and atmosphere testing (O2, LEL, H2S, CO) for enclosed spaces such as tanks, bilges and cofferdams. Unauthorized enclosed space entry is one of the deadliest types of accident at sea. Under no circumstances does the cadet enter an enclosed space without a permit and without supervision.

Aynı şekilde sıcak iş (hot work — kaynak.en: In the same way, the cadet learns the purpose of the hot work (welding, grinding) and electrical lockout (LOTO) procedures. These procedures are covered in detail in later sections; during watch participation, the cadet observes how they relate to watch safety.

Her vardiya katılımı, Training Record Bo.en: Each watch participation is entered under the relevant competence area of the Training Record Book (TRB): "engineering watch keeping", "monitor machinery performance", "maintain safe engineering watch". The cadet records every task performed under supervision (keeping the log, rounds, transfers, observing alarm response) in the TRB and has it signed by the training engineer.

TRB'nin tamamlanması, OOW (Engine) yeter.en: Completion of the TRB is a legal prerequisite for sitting the OOW (Engine) certificate of competency examination. The cadet should therefore see watch participation not merely as "filling hours" but as a process of accumulating concrete evidence of competence.

Eğitmen mühendis, stajyerin gözlem keski.en: The training engineer regularly assesses the cadet's sharpness of observation, compliance with procedures and safety awareness. The cadet should actively ask for feedback: "What did I miss on this round?", "Did I respond correctly to this alarm?". This feedback loop is the basis of the progression from supervised participation to independent competence.

Makine stajyerinin vardiya katılımındaki.en: The engine cadet's success in watch participation comes not from moving fast but from observing correctly, reporting on time and respecting the limits of authority. The discipline learned under supervision today forms the basis of the safety culture of the engineer who will keep an independent watch tomorrow. A good cadet learns what is "normal" so well that he or she notices what is "abnormal" before anyone else.

Her planlı bakım, PMS yazılımında açılan.en: Every planned maintenance job starts with a work order opened in the PMS software. The work order contains the job to be done, the spare parts and tools required, the estimated duration and the OEM procedure reference. By reading the work order, the cadet understands the scope of the job, its critical steps and its safety requirements in advance.

Bakım öncesi risk değerlendirmesi (risk.en: A risk assessment and a toolbox talk are held before maintenance: the hazards of the job, the need for isolation, the PPE required and emergency measures are discussed. The cadet attends the toolbox talk, asks questions and understands the allocation of tasks. The principle "think before you start" prevents most maintenance accidents.

Bakıma başlamadan önce gereken tüm takım.en: Before maintenance starts, all the tools, spare parts, gasket/O-ring sets, cleaning materials and sealing elements required are prepared. The cadet learns to recognize the right tool: torque wrench, hammer, puller, feeler gauge, micrometer, dial gauge, Allen key/socket sets. Using the wrong tool harms both the job and the operator.

Yedek parçaların OEM orijinali veya onay.en: It is important that spare parts are OEM originals or approved equivalents; the wrong part leads to early failure. The cadet learns to lay out dismantled parts in order (labeling them according to the assembly sequence); this eliminates the risk of errors and missing parts during reassembly.

Hiçbir bakım, ekipman enerji altındayken.en: No maintenance starts while the equipment is energized. With Lockout-Tagout (LOTO), electrical, pressure, thermal and kinetic energy are isolated; the isolated valve/breaker is tagged and locked. The cadet learns to verify that the equipment to be worked on is actually isolated (zero energy state).

Sıcak iş veya kapalı alan gerektiren bak.en: For maintenance requiring hot work or enclosed space entry, the relevant permit (Permit to Work) is obtained. The cadet internalizes the principle "no work without a permit". Before any equipment is dismantled, it is confirmed that the system pressure has been released, the temperature has dropped and rotating parts have stopped.

Bakım alanı temiz, aydınlık ve düzenli o.en: The maintenance area must be clean, well lit and tidy. Dismantled parts are laid out in order on a tray/cloth, oily waste is collected in a suitable container and walkways are not blocked. A disorderly work area creates a risk both of slip/fall accidents and of lost parts/incorrect assembly.

Stajyer \"5S\" benzeri bir düzen disipli.en: The cadet learns a "5S"-type housekeeping discipline: put back what you use, segregate waste, leave the area clean. Good maintenance work shows itself when, on completion, the area is cleaner than before the work started.

Santrifüj pompa overhaul'unda; coupling.en: In a centrifugal pump overhaul, the coupling is removed, the casing is opened and the impeller, wear ring, mechanical seal and bearings are checked. The cadet learns the function of each part: the impeller creates the flow, the wear ring limits internal leakage and the mechanical seal prevents leakage along the shaft.

Aşınma ölçümleri yapılır: impeller-wear.en: Wear measurements are taken: impeller-to-wear ring clearance, shaft run-out, bearing clearance. The measurements are compared with the OEM tolerances; parts outside the limits are renewed. The cadet grasps the question "why do we measure": a part that looks good may be out of tolerance and cause a loss of performance/efficiency.

Mechanical seal montajı pompanın en hass.en: Fitting the mechanical seal is the most delicate operation on a pump: the seal faces must not be touched by hand, scratched or run dry. Incorrect fitting results in early seal failure and leakage. The cadet learns the importance of clean assembly, correct orientation and proper lubrication.

Montaj sonrası coupling alignment (laser.en: After assembly, coupling alignment is carried out (with a laser or dial gauge); misalignment leads to vibration, bearing wear and seal failure. The cadet learns that alignment is a measured value, not something that "looks aligned".

Gate, globe, butterfly, check (non-retur.en: Gate, globe, butterfly, check (non-return) and ball valves have different functions: gate valves for fully open/closed isolation, globe valves for flow control, check valves for one-way flow and butterfly valves for quick isolation. The cadet learns which valve is used where and why their maintenance differs.

Valf bakımında disc/seat lapping (alıştı.en: Valve maintenance includes disc/seat lapping, renewal of spindle/gland packing and a tightness test. Lapping is a grinding-in process carried out with lapping paste; it restores the contact surface between the disc and the seat. The cadet learns this manual skill by observing and assisting.

Gasket (conta), flanşlar arasındaki sızd.en: The gasket provides the seal between flanges. The correct material (suitable for the fluid and temperature), the correct thickness and correct cutting are critical. The cadet learns to cut a gasket from gasket sheet using the flange as a template, to position the bolt holes correctly and to cut the inner diameter so that it does not obstruct the flow.

Flanş montajında cıvatalar çapraz (star.en: When a flange is assembled, the bolts are tightened in a cross (star pattern) sequence and in torque stages; uneven tightening leads to crushing of the gasket and leaks. The cadet learns why the correct torque value and tightening sequence are important.

LO, FO ve hava filtreleri düzenli temizl.en: LO, FO and air filters are cleaned/changed regularly. A clogged filter shows itself by an increase in differential pressure; when this difference exceeds a set limit, an alarm is given or the bypass opens. The cadet learns why filters must be changed on time (insufficient supply, damage to equipment).

Duplex (çift) filtrelerde bir taraf çalı.en: On duplex filters, one side can be taken out for maintenance while the other is in service; the changeover is done carefully so that the supply is not interrupted and no air lock forms. The cadet learns the changeover sequence and the need for venting (air release).

Purifier (separator), yakıt ve yağdan su.en: The purifier (separator) separates water and solid sediment from fuel and oil by centrifugal force. Opening the bowl, cleaning the disc stack, selecting the gravity disc and renewing O-rings are parts of the maintenance. The cadet experiences that learning the order and fitting direction of the discs is critical (incorrect assembly impairs separation efficiency).

Bowl ağır ve hassas bir parçadır; doğru.en: The bowl is a heavy and delicate part; correct lifting technique and balanced assembly are important. An unbalanced bowl creates dangerous vibration at high speed. In purifier maintenance, the cadet sees the direct relationship of cleanliness and precision with efficiency.

Cıvataların doğru torkla sıkılması, hem.en: Tightening bolts to the correct torque is critical both for tightness and for structural integrity. Insufficient torque leads to leaks and loosening, while excessive torque leads to bolt failure and flange distortion. The cadet learns the correct use of the torque wrench and how to read the OEM torque table.

Büyük flanş ve ana yatak gibi kritik bağ.en: On critical joints such as large flanges and main bearings, stepwise and cross-pattern tightening is essential; in some cases a hydraulic tensioner or the angle-tightening method is used. The cadet learns why these methods differ.

Titreşimli ortamda cıvataların gevşememe.en: To prevent bolts from loosening in a vibrating environment, split pins, locking wire, lock washers or thread-locker are used. The cadet learns which locking device is used in which application and what kind of failure a forgotten locking wire can cause.

Bakım sırasında oluşan yağlı bez, kullan.en: Oily rags, used filters, waste oil and sludge generated during maintenance are collected separately under MARPOL Annex I/V and disposed of properly (burning in the incinerator or delivery ashore in port). The cadet learns the discipline of waste segregation (oily rags, contaminated waste, scrap metal).

Yağlı atığın denize karışması veya yanlı.en: Oily waste entering the sea or being wrongly segregated means serious pollution and penalties. The cadet also learns that solvents/chemicals used for cleaning must be used in accordance with the MSDS and require proper waste management.

Temizlik solventleri, pas sökücüler ve d.en: Cleaning solvents, rust removers and degreasers may be flammable and toxic. The cadet learns to read the MSDS, provide adequate ventilation, use gloves/a mask and keep these products away from sources of ignition. Incorrect use of solvents is both a health and a fire hazard.

Bakım desteğinin önemli bir kazanımı, ek.en: An important gain from assisting with maintenance is learning the correct English/technical names of equipment parts: impeller, gland, bushing, journal, liner, gasket, O-ring, sleeve, key/keyway, circlip. The cadet learns that using the correct term prevents communication errors (such as ordering the wrong part).

Teknik dil hem yedek parça siparişinde h.en: Technical language is critical for ordering spare parts, reading OEM manuals and working with a multinational crew. The cadet learns new terms on every maintenance job and enters them in the TRB notes.

Stajyer, \"yaklaşık\" değil \"ölçülen\".en: The cadet learns to work with "measured" rather than "approximate" values. In using the micrometer, feeler gauge and dial gauge, the cadet gains awareness of correct reading, parallax error, temperature effects and calibration. Precise measurement is the basic language of engineering.

Bakım biten ekipman devreye alınmadan ön.en: Before equipment that has been maintained is put back into service, it is checked: are all bolts torqued, have the tools been collected (tool count), has the isolation been removed, is the valve line-up correct? The first start (recommissioning) is done under supervision; leaks, vibration, abnormal noise and temperature are monitored.

Stajyer, \"monte ettik bitti\" değil \"t.en: The cadet learns the discipline not of "we assembled it, job done" but of "we tested it, verified it and recorded it". A small leak noticed on first start can be corrected without dismantling the equipment again; an error that is missed later turns into a major failure.

Bakım tamamlanınca PMS'te iş emri kapatı.en: When the maintenance is completed, the work order is closed in the PMS: the work done, spare parts used, values measured and observations are recorded. This record builds up the ship's maintenance history and forms the basis for future failure analysis. The cadet observes the logic of closing a work order.

Stajyer ayrıca katıldığı her bakımı TRB'.en: The cadet also enters every maintenance job taken part in under the "maintenance and repair" competence area of the TRB and has it signed by the training engineer. In this way, the practical skills acquired become part of the official record.

Makine stajyerinin bakım desteğindeki ge.en: The engine cadet's real gain from assisting with maintenance is not just dismantling and reassembling a pump, but experiencing planning, isolation, measurement, precision and documentation together. Manual skill is gained through repetition, technical language through curiosity and safety awareness through discipline. The meticulousness learned under supervision today is the signature discipline of the engineer who will carry out maintenance independently tomorrow.

Her makine sistemi bir girdi alır, dönüş.en: Every machinery system takes an input, converts it and gives an output. The main engine converts fuel energy into shaft power; the fuel system supplies it, the lubrication system reduces friction, the cooling system removes heat and the air system enables combustion. By making these connections, the cadet understands the engine room as a whole.

Bir sistem arızalandığında etkisi diğerl.en: When one system fails, the effect spreads to the others: if cooling is insufficient, the oil thins, the oil pressure drops, bearings are damaged and the engine stops. By learning these chain dependencies, the cadet lays the foundation for fault-diagnosis logic.

Stajyer, makine dairesini fiziksel olara.en: By walking around the engine room, the cadet memorizes where each piece of equipment is: main engine, generator flat, boiler, purifier room, pump platform, compressors, switchboard room, steering gear room, separators and tank locations. In an emergency, reaching the right equipment quickly may be vital.

Lokasyon öğrenimi, General Arrangement ç.en: Learning these locations is reinforced by matching the General Arrangement drawing with the actual spaces. The cadet develops the skill of "finding on site what I see on the drawing"; this is a true engineering competence.

Büyük ticari gemilerin çoğu, doğrudan pe.en: Most large merchant ships use two-stroke, low-speed, crosshead-type diesel engines directly coupled to the propeller. The cadet learns the scavenging, compression, combustion (expansion) and exhaust phases, the principle of uniflow scavenging and how the crosshead keeps the side thrust off the piston.

Ana makinenin alt sistemleri birbirine b.en: The main engine's subsystems are interconnected: fuel injection, scavenge air (turbocharger + air cooler), jacket cooling water, piston/crosshead LO, cylinder lubrication and exhaust. The cadet learns how each subsystem contributes to the healthy running of the engine.

Ana makine; overspeed trip, LO low press.en: The main engine is equipped with multi-layered protection such as the overspeed trip, LO low pressure shut-down, jacket water high temp slow-down, oil mist detector and scavenge fire alarm. The cadet learns what each protection prevents: the overspeed trip prevents the engine from breaking apart on loss of load, and the OMD prevents a crankcase explosion.

Crankcase relief valve (patlama kapağı).en: There are also mechanical protections such as crankcase relief valves (explosion doors) and the turning gear interlock (which prevents starting while the turning gear is engaged). The cadet learns that these devices must never be bypassed.

Gemi elektriği, dört zamanlı orta devirl.en: The ship's electrical power is supplied by four-stroke, medium-speed diesel generators. The cadet learns the logic of parallel operation of generators, load sharing, synchronization and preferential trip (disconnecting low-priority consumers on overload).

Şaft jeneratörü (PTO) ve emergency gener.en: The shaft generator (PTO) and the emergency generator are also sources of electrical power. The cadet learns how the electrical supply is managed in normal, maneuvering and emergency conditions, and why enough generators are kept in parallel to prevent the risk of a blackout.

Jeneratör; reverse power, over-current,.en: The generator has reverse power, over-current, over/under-voltage and over/under-frequency protection. The cadet learns how these protections safeguard the electrical system and the generator. In addition, cooling water, oil pressure and exhaust temperature alarms protect the engine side.

Auxiliary (oil-fired) boiler, port'ta ve.en: The auxiliary (oil-fired) boiler produces steam in port and at low load; the exhaust gas economizer produces steam at sea from the main engine exhaust heat (waste heat recovery). Steam is used for heating fuel/oil, tank heating and general services. The cadet learns how the two sources complement each other.

Su seviyesi kontrolü buhar kazanlarında.en: Water level control is vital in steam boilers: a low water level can lead to boiler damage and explosion. The cadet learns to read the gauge glass and learns the water level alarm and automatic feed water control.

Safety valve (emniyet supabı), kazan bas.en: The safety valve limits the boiler pressure; it opens at excessive pressure and releases steam. The cadet learns the set pressure of the safety valve and the requirement for periodic testing. The pressure gauge, water level controller and flame failure device are also part of boiler safety.

Ana makine basınçlı hava ile çalıştırılı.en: The main engine is started with compressed air (starting air, usually ~30 bar). Air compressors fill the air bottles (air receivers). In addition, control air (control/service air) supplies the pneumatic systems. The cadet learns the difference between the two air systems and why they are kept separate.

Hava şişelerinin doluluğu kritiktir: yet.en: The pressure in the air bottles is critical: without sufficient starting air the engine cannot be started, or maneuverability is lost. The cadet learns to monitor bottle pressure and the logic of automatic filling by the compressors.

Makine dairesinde santrifüj (cooling wat.en: The engine room has centrifugal pumps (cooling water, ballast), positive displacement pumps (FO/LO transfer, screw/gear) and eccentric screw pumps (sludge). The cadet learns which pump type is used in which system and why (according to pressure/flow/viscosity requirements).

Pompa sistemleri yedekli (duty/standby).en: Pump systems are designed with redundancy (duty/standby); if one pump fails, the standby pump cuts in automatically or manually. The cadet learns the auto-start logic and why critical services have redundancy.

Boru hatları renk kodlarıyla işaretlenir.en: Pipelines are marked with color codes (according to the type of fluid) and the flow direction is shown by arrows. By physically following a pipeline (line tracing), the cadet learns the path of a system from source to consumer; this is a basic skill for valve alignment and fault isolation.

Modern gemiler merkezi soğutma sistemi k.en: Modern ships use a central cooling system: sea water (low temp sea water) cools the fresh water circuit through a central cooler, and the fresh water (LT/HT fresh water) in turn cools the engine and auxiliary equipment. This keeps the corrosive effect of seawater away from the equipment. The cadet learns the difference between the LT and HT circuits.

Plate ve shell-and-tube tipi ısı değişti.en: Plate and shell-and-tube heat exchangers are used. The cadet learns that cooling efficiency drops because of fouling (clogging/deposits), and that the time for cleaning is determined by monitoring the differential pressure and the temperature difference.

Three-way thermostatic valve, soğutma ak.en: A three-way thermostatic valve keeps the engine temperature at the optimum by regulating the cooling flow. Running too cold (especially at low load) is also harmful because of wear and sulfuric acid corrosion. The cadet learns the balance of "warm enough, but not too hot".

Ağır yakıt (HFO) makineye girmeden önce.en: Before entering the engine, heavy fuel oil (HFO) passes through the settling tank → purifier → service tank chain; water and solid sediment are separated, and the fuel is heated and its viscosity adjusted. The cadet learns why this treatment chain is critical for healthy combustion in the engine.

LO da benzer şekilde sürekli purifier'da.en: Similarly, LO is kept clean by passing it continuously through the purifier. The cadet learns the purifier's separator (water separation) and clarifier (solids separation) modes and the importance of selecting the gravity disc.

Yakıt hazırlama sistemi, ana makine ve j.en: The fuel treatment system directly affects main engine and generator performance. Poorly purified fuel leads to injector clogging, liner wear and exhaust temperature imbalance. The cadet sees concretely that the output of one system determines the health of another.

P&ID (Piping and Instrumentation Diagram.en: A P&ID (Piping and Instrumentation Diagram) shows a system's valves, pumps, tanks, sensors and line connections with standard symbols. The cadet learns to read valve types, pump symbols, flow direction and instrument tags (PI, TI, LI, PT). The diagram simplifies the complexity of the plant in the mind.

Stajyer, bir P&ID'yi okuyup sahada doğru.en: By reading a P&ID and verifying it on site (finding on site the valve seen on the drawing), the cadet brings the two worlds together. This skill is the basis of valve alignment, fault isolation and operation planning.

Bir transfer veya switching işlemi önces.en: Before a transfer or changeover operation, the cadet learns to work out the line-up on the P&ID: which valve is open, which pump will run, which tank will be affected. This mental rehearsal reduces the likelihood of errors on site.

Makine sistemlerini öğrenmek, ekipman is.en: Learning machinery systems is not memorizing equipment names but understanding the path of the fluid, the conversion of energy and the dependencies between systems. When the cadet learns each system in terms of "purpose, flow, failure, protection", the engine room stops being a puzzle and becomes a meaningful whole. This holistic understanding lays a solid foundation for fault diagnosis and operational management later on.

STCW Bölüm A-III/1, makine vardiya mühen.en: STCW Section A-III/1 requires completion of a structured onboard training program in order to become an engineer officer in charge of a watch. The TRB is the evidence that this program has been implemented and assessed. The Administration (flag State) issues the candidate's certificate of competency only together with an approved TRB and valid sea service.

TRB; eğitim kuruluşu (akademi/MET instit.en: The TRB is a document that bridges the training institution (academy/MET institution), the company and the ship. It shows that the theoretical knowledge gained at the academy has been put into practice on board, that each competence area has actually been applied and that it has been assessed by an authorized engineer. For this reason, the TRB is also seen as "the contract between the school and the ship".

OOW (Engine) yeterlilik belgesine giden.en: On the way to the OOW (Engine) certificate of competency there are three chains of evidence: (1) approved sea service (Sea Service), (2) a completed TRB, (3) mandatory courses (firefighting, survival, medical first aid, security awareness, etc.), and finally the certificate of competency examination. The TRB is the middle link of this chain; if it is incomplete, the other links are not sufficient.

Stajyer, TRB'yi sınav dosyasının çekirde.en: The cadet should see the TRB as the core of the examination file. In the Administration's review, the answer to "how many months did you spend at sea?" is in the Sea Service record, and the answer to "what did you learn and what is your evidence?" is in the TRB. The two complement each other.

Standart bir Engine Cadet TRB; kişisel b.en: A standard Engine Cadet TRB consists of personal details, ship record pages (vessel record / particulars), familiarization checklists, task records, supervisor assessment pages and summary approval sections. On joining each ship, the ship's details (type, tonnage, main engine, class) are entered on the relevant page.

TRB'nin kalbi, STCW Table A-III/1 yetkin.en: The heart of the TRB is the task record section, which links the STCW Table A-III/1 competence areas to shipboard tasks. Here, the fields "what was done, when, which competence it corresponds to, trainer's assessment" are completed for each task. The familiarization section is completed on first joining the ship and documents the safety, escape route and equipment familiarization.

Table A-III/1 dört ana fonksiyon altında.en: Table A-III/1 defines competences under four main functions: Marine Engineering, Electrical/Electronic and Control Engineering, Maintenance and Repair, and Controlling Operation of the Ship and Care for Persons on Board. TRB tasks are distributed among these functions; the cadet must accumulate sufficient evidence in each function.

Örneğin \"Maintain a safe engineering wa.en: For example, the competence "Maintain a safe engineering watch" is filled with watch participation records, "Operate main and auxiliary machinery" with system operation observations and "Maintenance and repair of shipboard machinery" with maintenance participation records. Knowing which task supports which competence, the cadet progresses through the book in a balanced way.

Bir görev yapıldığı gün TRB'ye işlenmeli.en: A task must be entered in the TRB on the day it is done. An entry written while the memory is fresh is accurate in terms of date, equipment, work done and lesson learned. Entries written in bulk weeks later are vague and general and have weak evidential value; the training engineer also finds it difficult to approve such entries.

Stajyer, her vardiya veya bakım işi sonr.en: After each watch or maintenance job, the cadet takes a few minutes to record the task: which system, which operation, observations, tools used, safety points observed. This discipline both feeds the TRB and serves as the cadet's own learning journal.

İyi bir TRB kaydı şu sorulara yanıt veri.en: A good TRB entry answers these questions: What was done? On which equipment/system? Which procedure was followed? Which safety precautions were taken? What was learned? It must be concrete: not "I looked at the pump" but "I assisted, under the trainer's supervision, in replacing the mechanical seal of No. 2 transfer pump; LOTO was applied, the old seal was removed, a new gasket was cut".

Kaydın sahte veya abartılı olmaması esas.en: It is essential that entries are not false or exaggerated. Entering in the TRB a job in which the cadet did not actually take part is a serious disciplinary offense; these tasks are also questioned in the oral examination, and superficial entries are exposed. The TRB is the mirror of the cadet's real competence.

Gemide TRB sürecinden sorumlu kişi genel.en: The person on board responsible for the TRB process is usually the Chief Engineer or a senior engineer designated by the Chief Engineer (training officer). The trainer reads the cadet's entries, verifies that the task was actually done and performed to an appropriate standard, requests corrections if necessary and signs the entries found satisfactory.

Onay sadece bir imza atma işlemi değildi.en: Approval is not just a matter of signing; the trainer makes an assessment by observing the cadet's competence. The trainer looks for answers to the questions "Can the cadet do it, has the cadet understood it, is the cadet working safely?". For this reason, the cadet should submit entries for signature at regular intervals (e.g. weekly) and not leave them until the end of the voyage.

İdeal pratik, haftalık veya iki haftalık.en: The ideal practice is a weekly or two-weekly signing cycle. With this rhythm, the trainer assesses fresh entries and shows the cadet the areas for development. Signing hundreds of entries accumulated until the end of the voyage all at once both burdens the trainer and lowers the quality of the assessment.

Stajyer, her imza turunu bir geri bildir.en: The cadet should turn every signing round into a feedback opportunity: "In which competence am I weak, what should I focus on next month?" These questions turn the TRB from a passive record into an active development tool and strengthen the mentoring relationship with the trainer.

Her yeni gemiye çıkışta TRB'nin familiar.en: On joining each new ship, the familiarization section of the TRB is completed as a priority. This section covers the locations of safety equipment, escape routes, the muster station, lifejacket/immersion suit locations, emergency alarm signals, engine room emergency stop buttons and enclosed space entry points. The ISM Code requires every person joining the ship to receive familiarization before taking up duties.

Aşinalık sadece bir kutu işaretleme egze.en: Familiarization is not just a box-ticking exercise; it is the cadet loading a "mental picture" of the ship into memory so as to be able to act independently later. The cadet must reach the level of being able to find the escape route with eyes closed and of knowing where the emergency stop button is.

PSC (Port State Control) ve şirket denet.en: During PSC (Port State Control) and company inspections, whether the crew are familiar with the ship is questioned. The signed familiarization record in the TRB is the document showing that the cadet has received this training. A missing familiarization record is both an inspection finding and a lethal risk in a real emergency.

Stajyer, gemi değişikliklerinde (yeni ge.en: When changing ships (transferring to a new ship), the cadet must not forget to complete familiarization again. Each ship's layout, equipment and procedures are different; familiarization from the previous ship is not automatically carried over to the new one.

TRB'nin yaygın bir zaafı, bazı yetkinlik.en: A common weakness of TRBs is that some competences are over-filled while others are under-filled. If the cadet goes on watch every day, the "watchkeeping" record fills up, but "maintenance and repair" or "electrical systems" may remain weak. The cadet should periodically review the gaps in the book and turn to the incomplete areas.

Pratik yöntem, aylık bir öz-değerlendirm.en: The practical method is a monthly self-assessment: which STCW function has been sufficiently evidenced, and which has fallen behind? For the area that has fallen behind, the cadet asks the training engineer for opportunities ("may I take part in the electrical switchboard job in the coming maintenance plan?"). This proactive approach avoids being left with large gaps at the end of the voyage.

Staj birden fazla gemide tamamlanabilir..en: Cadet training may be completed on more than one ship. Although the ship record pages are completed separately for each ship, the evidence of competence accumulates in a single book. When changing ships, the cadet should plan to close on the new ship a gap left on the previous one; for example, if the tanker fuel system was not learned on the previous ship, priority is given to this opportunity on the new ship.

TRB'nin fiziksel güvenliği de süreklilik.en: The physical safety of the TRB is also critical for continuity. The book must not get wet or be lost, and its pages must not be torn. Many cadets keep a photo/scan backup of completed pages; if the original is lost, a trace of the approved entries remains. Nevertheless, official validity lies with the original bearing wet-ink signatures.

Sea Service Certificate \"ne kadar süre.en: The Sea Service Certificate answers the question "how long did you spend at sea", and the TRB the question "what did you learn in that time and what is your evidence". The Administration requires both together with the examination application. Sea service time alone is not sufficient; completion of structured training during that time must be proven by the TRB.

Stajyer, iki belgenin tarihlerinin tutar.en: The cadet must make sure that the dates in the two documents are consistent: the task dates in the TRB must match the periods on board documented in the Sea Service record. Inconsistent dates are questioned during review and undermine the validity of the documents.

Sınav başvurusundan önce stajyer, TRB'yi.en: Before applying for the examination, the cadet reviews the TRB from beginning to end: have all mandatory competences been evidenced, are all pages signed, are the familiarization sections complete for each ship, are the trainer's and the Master's approvals present? This final check prevents the application from being rejected for missing documents.

İdarelerin TRB tamamlanma kriterleri far.en: Administrations' criteria for TRB completion may differ; the flag State's guidance must be read. Some Administrations require a minimum number of repetitions of certain tasks, others look for minimum evidence in each function. The cadet should learn the specific requirements of their own flag at the start of the voyage.

En sık hata, TRB'yi sefer sonuna kadar b.en: The most common mistake is leaving the TRB blank until the end of the voyage and trying to fill it in all at once. This produces entries that are both poor in quality and difficult for the trainer to approve. The second mistake is writing tasks in a vague and general way ("I looked at the engine"); the third is recording only easily accessible tasks without regard to the balance of competences.

Dördüncü ciddi hata, fiilen yapılmamış i.en: The fourth serious mistake is entering in the TRB work that was not actually done. This is both a disciplinary offense and a risk that will be exposed in the oral examination. The TRB is also a test of the cadet's honesty; an exaggerated book creates distrust in the examination interview.

Doğru pratik şudur: günlük ve somut kayı.en: Correct practice is: daily and concrete entries, a weekly signing rhythm, a monthly gap analysis, a balanced spread of competences, repeated familiarization on every new ship and physical safety of the book. A cadet who adopts these disciplines will be ready for the examination file at the end of the voyage with a complete and strong TRB.

TRB ayrıca stajyerin kariyer boyu sürece.en: The TRB is also the first step in a learning habit that will last the cadet's whole career. Systematic recording, sharp observation and self-assessment are the basic professional disciplines of the engineer who will later become an OOW, and then Second/Chief Engineer.

TRB yönetimi, makine stajyerinin sertifi.en: TRB management is the most concrete responsibility in the engine cadet's certification journey. A well-managed book not only secures the right to sit the examination; it also documents the cadet's real competence, honesty and professional discipline. Daily recording discipline, balanced evidence of competence and regular approval are the three cornerstones of a complete TRB. A cadet who neglects this book risks the valuable months spent at sea being left without evidence.

Deniz kazalarının büyük çoğunluğu tek bi.en: Most marine casualties result not from a single error but from small overlapping omissions (error chain). Safety procedures are designed to break this chain at specific points: LOTO isolates energy, the PTW assesses the risk in advance and atmosphere testing reveals invisible hazards. Every procedure is a lesson from fatal accidents of the past.

Stajyer, prosedürleri \"bürokrasi\" deği.en: The cadet should see procedures not as "bureaucracy" but as "survival tools". The thought "I will cut corners this time" is the first link in the accident chain. Experienced engineers know that following the procedure even in the most routine job is the mark of professionalism.

Stajyer, emniyet prosedürlerine gözetiml.en: The cadet takes part in safety procedures under supervision: applies LOTO, reads the PTW form, observes atmosphere testing. However, under no circumstances does the cadet independently remove an isolation, enter an enclosed space without a permit or start hot work. Every safety-critical operation is carried out with the approval and under the supervision of an authorized person.

Stajyerin en güçlü emniyet aracı \"speak.en: The cadet's strongest safety tool is the right to "speak up". On seeing an unsafe situation — whatever the difference in seniority — the cadet must know to stop and report. In many accidents, a junior crew member's failure to voice a hazard they had noticed has ended in disaster.

LOTO, bir ekipman üzerinde çalışılırken.en: LOTO prevents equipment from starting unexpectedly, or stored energy (electrical, pressure, steam, hydraulic, mechanical) from being released, while work is being done on it. Before maintenance on a pump, fan, compressor or electric motor, the energy source is isolated, locked (lock) and tagged (tag).

Standart LOTO adımları: hazırlık ve bild.en: Standard LOTO steps: preparation and notification, stopping the equipment, isolating all energy sources, fitting locks and tags, releasing stored energy (pressure relief, capacitor discharge) and verification of zero energy (try-out: attempt to start, see that it does not run). Each worker fits their own lock; another person's lock may not be removed.

Stajyer, gözetimli bir bakım işinde kend.en: In a supervised maintenance job, the cadet learns to fit their own lock and learns the importance of zero energy verification. The attitude "we fitted the lock but did not test it" is dangerous; the proof of real isolation is attempting to start and seeing that the equipment does not run (try-to-start).

Stajyer ayrıca grup LOTO mantığını öğren.en: The cadet also learns the logic of group LOTO: if more than one person is working on the same equipment, everyone fits their own lock and removes it when their work is finished. The equipment cannot be energized until the last lock is removed. This ensures that nobody is "forgotten" and left in danger.

PTW, yüksek riskli işlerin başlamadan ön.en: The PTW is a formal permit system documenting that high-risk work has been systematically assessed and the necessary precautions taken before it starts. Work such as hot work, enclosed space entry, aloft work (working at height), electrical isolation and diving usually requires a separate permit. The permit defines the job, the risks, the precautions taken, the responsible person and the period of validity.

PTW süreci risk değerlendirmesini (risk.en: The PTW process makes a risk assessment mandatory: what hazards there are, who may be affected, what controls will be applied. When the job is finished, the permit is closed and the area returns to normal. Work cannot continue on an expired permit until it is renewed.

Stajyer, bir permit formunun nasıl doldu.en: The cadet learns how a permit form is completed, which questions are asked and which approvals are required. The cadet understands that a permit is not just a piece of paper; each line represents a concrete precaution. The line "Has the atmosphere been tested?" is the guarantee of a life.

Stajyer, kendi katıldığı işlerin permit'.en: The cadet should read the permit for the jobs they take part in and ask themselves "what is the risk in this job and how are we protected?" This habit forms the basis of the risk awareness of the responsible engineer who will sign permits in the future.

Kapalı alanlar (tanklar, cofferdam, ball.en: Enclosed spaces (tanks, cofferdams, ballast tanks, bilges, chain lockers, boilers) may contain invisible lethal atmospheres: oxygen deficiency, toxic gases (H2S), explosive vapors (LEL) and carbon monoxide. Human senses cannot detect most of these hazards; therefore atmosphere testing before and during entry is vital.

Giriş prosedürü: alanı izole et ve haval.en: Entry procedure: isolate and ventilate the space, test the atmosphere (O2, LEL, toxic gases), issue the permit, assign standby personnel, ensure continuous communication and monitoring, keep a rescue plan ready. Nobody may enter until the readings are within the safe range. Oxygen must be around 20.9%, LEL 0% and toxic gases below their threshold limits.

Stajyer için en katı kural budur: hiçbir.en: This is the strictest rule for the cadet: under no circumstances is an enclosed space entered without a permit, without testing and without supervision. Thoughts such as "I'll just take a quick look" or "I'm only going to get my tool" are fatal. Most enclosed space fatalities are people who went in "just for a moment".

Daha da önemlisi: içeride biri baygın gö.en: More importantly: if someone is seen unconscious inside, the cadet first raises the alarm and calls for help; the cadet does not rush into an unsupervised and unequipped rescue. The statistics of enclosed space accidents are painful: a significant proportion of those who die are rescuers who ran to save the first victim and were asphyxiated in the same atmosphere.

Hot work (kaynak, taşlama, kesme, açık a.en: Hot work (welding, grinding, cutting, open flame) significantly increases the risk of fire and explosion on board. Fuel vapor, oily surfaces and combustible materials can be ignited by a spark. For this reason, hot work requires a separate permit and the atmosphere is verified as "gas-free".

Önlemler: çalışma alanını yanıcılardan a.en: Precautions: clear the work area of combustibles, close nearby openings, have a fire extinguisher and a fire watch present, test the atmosphere, and keep the area under watch for a set time after the work is finished (risk of a spark starting a delayed fire). Hot work is particularly restricted on tankers and near flammable cargo.

Stajyer, hot work sırasında genellikle f.en: During hot work, the cadet is usually present as fire watch support or as an observer. The cadet learns how critical the fire watch is: a small spark can start a fire even minutes later. The cadet must know the location, type and use of the extinguisher.

Stajyer ayrıca \"neden bu işten önce tan.en: The cadet also learns the answer to the question "why was the tank made gas-free before this job?" In the past, many tankers and other ships have exploded, with loss of life, as a result of hot work carried out with inadequate preparation. Every step of the procedure is the lesson of a death.

Blackout, tüm ana güç kaynağının kaybedi.en: A blackout is the loss of all main power; the ship is plunged into darkness and left immobile. In this case, the emergency generator starts automatically and supplies the critical loads (emergency lighting, steering gear, communications, fire pump). The recovery procedure includes diagnosing the cause, manual/automatic start of the generators, stepwise load acceptance and restarting the main engine.

Stajyer, blackout recovery'yi gözlemleye.en: By observing blackout recovery, the cadet learns the prioritization of the power system: first the emergency switchboard, then the main generators, then heavy loads. A blackout during maneuvering or in confined waters creates a risk of collision/grounding, so the speed of recovery is critical.

Makine dairesi yangını en tehlikeli gemi.en: An engine room fire is one of the most dangerous fires on a ship; fuel, oil and hot surfaces are present together. The response includes the steps of shutting off the fuel supply (quick-closing valves), shutting down the ventilation (ventilation flaps), withdrawing personnel, closing off the space (boundary cooling) and activating the fixed smothering system (CO2/foam/water mist). A personnel count is always carried out before the fixed system is released.

Su basması (flooding) ise hull/boru hasa.en: Flooding may result from hull/pipe damage or failure of the sea water system. The bilge pumps, emergency bilge suction and damage control are brought into action. The cadet learns the bilge alarm system, the capacities of the bilge pumps and the early signs of flooding (rising bilge level).

Makine dairesinin en az iki bağımsız kaç.en: The engine room has at least two independent escape routes; one of these may be a protected (fire-protected) escape trunk. The cadet must know the escape routes well enough to find them with eyes closed, because in a real fire smoke can reduce visibility to zero. Emergency lighting and photoluminescent signs then show the way.

Muster station (toplanma yeri), acil dur.en: The muster station is the designated place where the crew assemble in an emergency. The muster list shows each person's duty in an emergency (fire party, liferaft, first aid, etc.). The cadet must know their own muster duty and station by heart; this is learned during familiarization and reinforced through drills.

Tatbikatlar (drills), acil durum prosedü.en: Drills ensure that emergency procedures become ingrained in muscle memory. The cadet takes an active part in abandon ship, fire, enclosed space rescue and man overboard drills. Treating a drill as a "formality" is dangerous; when a real incident occurs, people can only do what they have rehearsed.

Stajyer her tatbikattan sonra kendine so.en: After every drill, the cadet should ask: "Did I know my duty? Did I use the equipment correctly? What could I have done faster/more safely?" This self-assessment and the post-drill debrief determine performance in a real emergency.

PPE, riskin kaynakta giderilemediği duru.en: PPE is the last line of defense where the risk cannot be eliminated at source. Basic PPE in the engine room is safety shoes (steel toe cap), a boiler suit, ear protection (mandatory in zones above 90 dB), a hard hat, safety glasses and, depending on the situation, gloves (heat/chemical), a respirator and a face shield. Selecting PPE suitable for the work being done is critical.

Gevşek giysi, takı ve açık saç dönen eki.en: Loose clothing, jewelry and loose hair are a lethal hazard near rotating equipment; entanglement accidents result in serious injury or death. The cadet must get into the habit of checking clothing and accessories when entering the engine room.

PPE ancak doğru kullanıldığında korur. Y.en: PPE protects only when used correctly. Incorrectly fitted ear protection, a leaking mask or cracked goggles give a false sense of safety. The cadet must check their PPE before every use, replace it if damaged and learn to put it on and take it off correctly.

PPE bireysel sorumluluktur ama aynı zama.en: PPE is an individual responsibility, but it is also a visible sign of safety culture. A cadet who uses the full PPE both protects themselves and sets the right example for the team. The excuse "it's only a one-minute job" is the most frequent cause of injury.

Emniyet prosedürlerini öğrenmek, makine.en: Learning safety procedures is the engine cadet's most vital task at sea. LOTO, PTW, enclosed spaces, hot work and PPE are each lessons drawn from past deaths, and none of them is a "formality that can be shortened". The cadet must internalize that following procedures is the mark of professionalism and that stopping and speaking up in an unsafe situation is a right. The safety discipline learned under supervision today is the most valuable legacy of the engineer who will lead a team tomorrow.

Bir mühendis, bir sistemi sadece fizikse.en: An engineer cannot fully understand a system just by seeing it physically; where the pipes go, which valve isolates what and the design logic of the system can only be learned from the drawing. When a fault is being traced, an isolation is being planned or a transfer line is being set up, the drawing is the engineer's guide.

Stajyer, çizim okumayı sistem tanıma ile.en: The cadet learns to read drawings in parallel with learning the systems: tracing on site a line seen on the drawing, and finding on the drawing a valve seen on site. This drawing-to-site matching (drawing-to-deck verification) is the basis of true engineering understanding. Memorized equipment knowledge, combined with the ability to read drawings, becomes mastery of the system.

Piping diagram (P&ID benzeri boru devre.en: A piping diagram (a P&ID-type piping circuit diagram) shows the pipes, valves, pumps and instruments of a fluid system (fuel, oil, cooling water, ballast, bilge). An electrical diagram (single line diagram / wiring diagram) shows power distribution, the switchboard, breakers and motor supply lines. The general arrangement (GA) gives the general layout of the ship/engine room.

Bunların yanında capacity plan (tank yer.en: In addition, there are the capacity plan (tank layout), the fire control plan and OEM equipment drawings (sectional views, assembly drawings). The cadet learns which question each drawing answers: "where does the fluid go?" is answered in the piping diagram, "where does the power come from?" in the electrical diagram and "where is the equipment?" in the GA.

Piping diagram standart semboller kullan.en: A piping diagram uses standard symbols: different valve types (gate, globe, ball, butterfly, non-return/check, relief), pumps, filters, heat exchangers, tanks and instruments (pressure/temperature gauges). Lines are usually colored or labeled according to the type of fluid (FO, DO, LO, SW, FW, steam, air).

Çizimi okumak için stajyer \"akışı takip.en: To read the drawing, the cadet learns the method of "following the flow": tracing the line from the source (tank/pump) to the destination (equipment/tank) and identifying the valves and instruments along the way. A non-return valve indicates that the flow is one-way, a relief valve indicates overpressure protection and a three-way valve indicates diversion.

Bir ekipman üzerinde bakım yapılacaksa,.en: If maintenance is to be carried out on equipment, the valves to be closed are determined from the drawing. For isolating a pump, the cadet identifies on the drawing the suction and discharge valves and, if necessary, the bypass and drains. Incorrect valve isolation can leave a line thought to be isolated still under pressure and lead to an accident.

Stajyer, çizim üzerinde planladığı izola.en: The cadet verifies on site the isolation planned on the drawing: the valve number on the drawing must match the label on site, the valve must actually close and LOTO must be applied. This sequence of "from drawing to plan, from plan to site, from site to verification" is the basis of safe maintenance.

Tek hat şeması (single line diagram), ge.en: The single line diagram shows the backbone of the ship's power system: generators, main switchboard (MSB), bus-tie breakers, transformers, emergency switchboard and distribution boards. The cadet learns how power travels from the generator to the consumer and which breaker protects what.

Wiring/motor starter diagram ise bir mot.en: The wiring/motor starter diagram details the supply and control circuit of a motor: contactor, overload relay, start/stop buttons, interlocks. The cadet learns to use this diagram when finding out why a pump does not run: has the breaker tripped, has the overload tripped, has an interlock opened the circuit?

Elektrik şeması, izolasyonun nereden yap.en: The electrical diagram shows where the isolation is to be made. If maintenance is to be done on a motor, the relevant breaker is located, opened and locked (LOTO), and zero energy is verified by measuring the voltage. The cadet learns that saying "we switched off the breaker" is not enough; confirmation by measurement is essential.

Stajyer, elektrik işlerinin yetkili elek.en: The cadet learns that electrical work is done under the supervision of authorized electrical personnel (ETO/Electro-Technical Officer or an authorized engineer) and that high-voltage (HV) systems require special procedures. The cadet does not intervene in electrical systems independently.

General Arrangement planı, geminin tüm g.en: The General Arrangement plan shows the layout of all the ship's decks and the engine room. From this plan, the cadet learns which platform/deck each piece of equipment is on, as well as the escape routes, doors and passages. The GA provides quick orientation, particularly on joining a new ship.

Capacity plan ise tankların yerleşimini.en: The capacity plan shows the arrangement and volumes of the tanks; it is used in sounding and stability calculations. The fire control plan shows the fire zones, fixed systems, extinguisher locations and release points, and is an important part of PSC inspections.

Makine üreticisinin (OEM) bakım el kitap.en: The sectional and assembly drawings in the machinery manufacturer's (OEM) maintenance manuals show the internal construction of a piece of equipment part by part. In a pump overhaul, these drawings give the dismantling/assembly sequence of the parts, torque values and part numbers.

Stajyer, OEM çizimlerini bakım işiyle bi.en: The cadet learns to use OEM drawings together with the maintenance job: which part is dismantled in which order, which gasket goes where, which clearance is measured. These drawings also contain spare part codes; these codes are critical for ordering the correct part in the PMS.

PMS, gemideki tüm ekipmanların bakım per.en: The PMS is software that digitally manages the maintenance intervals, procedures and history of all equipment on board (examples: AMOS, TM Master, ShipManager, BASSnet). Maintenance intervals (running-hour or calendar based) are defined for each piece of equipment; the PMS generates the maintenance that falls due as a work order.

Sınıf kuruluşları (Class), bazı gemiler.en: For some ships, classification societies (Class) accept an approved PMS under a "Planned Maintenance Scheme" in place of traditional periodic survey. For this reason, the PMS is not just a convenience but a class and ISM requirement. A well-functioning PMS increases equipment reliability and reduces unplanned failures.

PMS'te bakım türleri tanımlanır: önleyic.en: Maintenance types are defined in the PMS: preventive (planned, periodic), condition-based (according to measurements) and corrective/breakdown (after failure). Preventive maintenance is done as planned, before any failure; condition-based maintenance is triggered by indicators such as vibration/oil analysis.

Bakım aralıkları çalışma saati (running.en: Maintenance intervals may be based on running hours or on the calendar. For example, a purifier requires maintenance "every 2000 hours" or a safety valve "once a year". The PMS generates work orders automatically from running hours entries or as the date advances.

Bir iş emri (work order), PMS'te bir bak.en: A work order represents a maintenance task in the PMS: which equipment, which job, which procedure, the spare parts and time required. The PMS generates work orders automatically for planned jobs; for an unplanned failure, a work order is opened manually. A work order passes through the stages of planning, material preparation, execution and close-out.

İş bitince iş emri kapatılır (close-out).en: When the job is finished, the work order is closed (close-out): the work done, hours spent, parts used, measurements (clearance, pressure) and observations are recorded. This close-out record builds up the equipment's maintenance history and is used in planning the next maintenance, as well as evidence in class surveys.

Stajyer, gözetimli olarak iş emri okumay.en: Under supervision, the cadet learns to read a work order and to find the relevant procedure and required parts in the PMS. When taking part in a maintenance job, the cadet opens the relevant work order, follows the procedure and observes how the close-out record is made at the end of the job. This is where drawing-reading and PMS skills come together with maintenance.

Stajyer, iş emri kapanış kaydının kalite.en: The cadet learns the importance of the quality of the work order close-out record: writing "done" is not enough; measured values, replaced parts and observations must be recorded. A good close-out record tells the next engineer the real condition of the equipment.

Her yedek parça, PMS/envanter sisteminde.en: Every spare part is identified in the PMS/inventory system by a code (part number / IMPA or OEM code). This code is critical for ordering the correct part; two parts that look similar may have different codes, and ordering the wrong part causes delay and cost. The part code is usually found in the OEM maintenance manual and the equipment drawing.

Stok kontrolü, kritik yedek parçaların m.en: Stock control ensures that the minimum stock level of critical spare parts is maintained. When a part is used, it is deducted from the inventory; when the level falls below the minimum, a reorder is triggered. Critical spares (for safety and the main engine) are always kept in stock; class may require them to be carried.

Stajyer, bir bakım işi için doğru parçay.en: The cadet learns to find the correct part for a maintenance job in the PMS, to match the part code with the drawing/manual and to deduct the part used from the inventory. Although this discipline may look like "shelf keeping", it is the basis of the ship's operational continuity: an incorrect record leads to a part not being found at a critical moment.

Stajyer ayrıca periyodik stok sayımının.en: The cadet also learns why periodic stocktaking is carried out: the physical stock and the system record must agree. A discrepancy shows either that the records have not been updated or that a part has been used without being recorded. Disciplined recording is the only way to a reliable inventory.

Teknik çizim okuma ve PMS kullanımı, mak.en: Reading technical drawings and using the PMS are the two basic skills that turn the engine cadet from an observer who "knows the equipment" into an engineer who "manages the system". The drawing shows the logic of the system and the route to safe isolation; the PMS makes maintenance planned, recorded and sustainable. As the cadet develops the discipline of finding on site what is seen on the drawing, confirming on the drawing what is seen on site and recording every maintenance job correctly in the PMS, the cadet becomes a reliable part of the ship's technical memory.

STCW, yeterlilik belgesi için \"qualifyi.en: STCW defines "qualifying seagoing service" for certificates of competency. This covers periods when the ship is actually at sea on voyages and the candidate serves in a position relevant to the duties. Time waiting in port, in the shipyard (lay-up) and periods without duties are generally not counted at the same rate; the rules of the flag Administration determine this distinction.

Makine stajyeri için deniz hizmeti, maki.en: For the engine cadet, sea service means the period of structured training and supervised duties in the engine room. This period is not just "being on board" but the active period during which the training program (TRB) is carried out. This is why Sea Service and the TRB complement each other: one proves the duration, the other the content.

Deniz hizmeti birden fazla belgeyle izle.en: Sea service is tracked by more than one document. The seafarer's book (seafarer's discharge book / service record book) officially records each signing on and signing off. The Seafarer's Employment Agreement (SEA — the employment contract required by MLC 2006) documents employment. The Sea Service Certificate confirms the summary of a given period with the Master's signature.

Stajyer, bu belgelerin tutarlı olmasına.en: The cadet must make sure that these documents are consistent: the sign-on/sign-off dates in the seafarer's book, the SEA periods and the periods in the Sea Service certificate must match. Inconsistencies are questioned in an Administration/inspection review and undermine the validity of the documents.

Geçerli bir Sea Service Certificate; gem.en: A valid Sea Service Certificate contains the seafarer's identity details, the ship's name, IMO number, flag, type and tonnage, main engine power (propulsion power — kW), rank/capacity, dates of joining and leaving and the total length of service. The certificate is signed by the Master and bears the ship's stamp.

Bu bilgiler tesadüfi değildir: ana makin.en: This information is not incidental: main engine power (kW) is related to the tonnage/power limitations of certain certificates; the ship type shows what kind of experience has been gained; the rank determines in which position the service will be counted. A missing field may lead to the certificate being rejected by the Administration.

Stajyer, her gemiden ayrılırken eksiksiz.en: The cadet should regard obtaining a complete Sea Service Certificate on leaving each ship as their own responsibility. If this certificate is forgotten or obtained incomplete in the rush of signing off, it can be very difficult to obtain later; the ship may have gone to another port, or the Master may have changed. The attitude "I'll get it later" is a serious risk.

Belgeyi alırken stajyer tüm alanları kon.en: When receiving the certificate, the cadet checks all fields: are the dates correct, are the ship's details complete, is the engine power stated, are the signature and stamp present? An incorrect certificate may become almost impossible to correct when it is noticed at the time of the examination application.

Deniz hizmeti, katılış ve ayrılış tarihl.en: Sea service is calculated as the number of days between the dates of joining and leaving; however, each Administration's acceptance rules differ. Some Administrations count watchkeeping days specifically, others count shipyard/lay-up periods partly or not at all. The cadet should learn, at the start of the voyage, the rules of their flag and of the Administration to which they will apply.

STCW, OOW (Engine) için belirli bir asga.en: STCW prescribes a minimum period of approved seagoing service for OOW (Engine) (within a structured training program accepted by the Administration). Knowing the target period, the cadet plans voyages and tracks the time still outstanding; before applying for the examination, the cadet makes sure the period has been completed.

Stajyer, farklı gemilerdeki Sea Service.en: The cadet must make sure that the dates of the Sea Service certificates from different ships do not overlap; service on two different ships on the same date cannot be shown. In addition, Sea Service dates must be consistent with the seafarer's book entries and the TRB task dates. This three-way consistency is the basis of the reliability of the document file.

Çakışma veya tutarsızlık, idare inceleme.en: An overlap or inconsistency raises the question of "document reliability" in the Administration's review and may lead to the entire file being subjected to further scrutiny. For this reason, each time a document is received, the cadet should enter the dates in a personal record sheet and check consistency continuously.

Watchkeeping Certificate (Engine) ve nih.en: For the Watchkeeping Certificate (Engine) and the final OOW certificate, Sea Service is not enough; all competence areas under STCW Table A-III/1 must have been completed in the TRB and approved by the training engineer. Sea Service answers the question "how long", and the TRB the question "what was learned and what is the evidence"; together they make up the examination file.

Stajyer, TRB'sini Sea Service süresiyle.en: The cadet should progress the TRB in parallel with the Sea Service period. If the evidence of competence is incomplete when the period runs out, even additional sea service will not secure the right to sit the examination. For this reason, the TRB gap analysis (see the TRB management section) is carried out together with sea service planning.

Sea Service belgesi kaptan onayı, TRB is.en: The Sea Service certificate requires the Master's approval and the TRB the approval of the training engineer (usually the Chief Engineer). The cadet must complete both approvals at the end of each period. A missing approval — for example unsigned TRB pages or an unstamped Sea Service certificate — may invalidate the application.

Onay sürecinde stajyer proaktif olmalı,.en: In the approval process, the cadet should be proactive and obtain signatures regularly without waiting for the end of the voyage. Trying to get hundreds of pages accumulated by the end of the voyage signed at the last minute is risky and also lowers the quality of the assessment.

OOW (Engine) Certificate of Competency (.en: An application for an OOW (Engine) Certificate of Competency (CoC) requires several documents to be brought together: approved Sea Service certificates, a completed TRB, mandatory STCW course certificates (Basic Safety, Advanced Firefighting, Survival Craft, Medical First Aid, Security Awareness, etc.), a valid medical certificate and the training institution's diploma/approval. A missing document holds up the application.

Stajyer, başvuru öncesi idarenin güncel.en: Before applying, the cadet should obtain the Administration's current list of requirements and check every item. Requirements may be updated over time (such as the STCW Manila amendments); relying on old information leads to an incomplete application. Early planning prevents last-minute gaps.

Belge dosyası kabul edildikten sonra ada.en: Once the document file has been accepted, the candidate enters the examination/assessment stage prescribed by the Administration; this may include written, oral and/or simulator assessment. In the oral examination, the tasks in the candidate's TRB may be questioned; honest and concrete TRB entries are therefore the best examination preparation.

Sınav başarısının ardından idare CoC'yi.en: After the examination has been passed, the Administration issues the CoC and adds the necessary endorsements. The cadet must learn the certificate's period of validity, the revalidation requirements and the tonnage/power limitations; it is a mistake to think a CoC has no expiry date, as it requires periodic revalidation and recent sea service.

Sea Service belgeleri, cüzdan ve TRB; yı.en: Sea Service certificates, the seafarer's book and the TRB are evidence accumulated over years and very difficult to reproduce. Their loss, theft or damage (getting wet, fire) may result in the training period not being recognized. The cadet should keep these documents in a waterproof, secure place and protect them carefully when traveling.

Pratik koruma yöntemi, tüm belgelerin yü.en: A practical method of protection is to make high-resolution digital copies (scans/photos) of all documents and keep them in secure cloud/backup storage. If the original is lost, the digital copy provides a reference for reissue; however, official validity always lies with the original bearing wet-ink signatures.

Stajyer, her gemiden döndüğünde belgeler.en: On returning from each ship, the cadet immediately adds the documents to their personal file and updates the service record sheet. Documents are kept in chronological order together with their digital backups. This discipline allows the file to be prepared within minutes when applying for the examination.

Belge yönetimi, sadece bir bürokratik gö.en: Document management is not just a bureaucratic task; it is the protection of the evidence of a career. Even years later, in an application for a higher certificate (Second/Chief Engineer), these early records may serve as a reference. Disciplined filing is the foundation of a habit that lasts a whole career.

En sık problem, eksik veya geç alınan Se.en: The most frequent problem is a missing or late Sea Service certificate; the certificate is not obtained when leaving the ship and cannot be obtained afterwards. The second problem is missing fields on the certificate (engine power not stated, no stamp, incorrect date). The third is inconsistency between the Sea Service dates and the seafarer's book/TRB dates.

Dördüncü problem, deniz hizmeti süresini.en: The fourth problem is sea service being calculated incorrectly under the Administration's rules, so that a period the candidate thought was sufficient turns out to be insufficient on the accepted basis. The fifth is that the validity of mandatory courses has expired at the time of application. Most of these problems are prevented by early planning and checks.

Bu sorunların çözümü reaktif değil önley.en: The solution to these problems is preventive, not reactive: obtain the complete certificate when leaving each ship, check the fields, enter the dates in your personal record sheet, learn the Administration's rules at the start of the voyage and track course validity with a calendar. Review the file months before applying for the examination.

Stajyer, belge sürecini \"sınav zamanı h.en: The cadet should regard the document process not as "a job to be dealt with at examination time" but as "a natural part of every period at sea". When each period is closed out properly, applying for the examination is simply a matter of bringing together documents that are already prepared.

Sea Service belgesi ve sertifika süreci,.en: The Sea Service certificate and the certification process are the point at which the valuable months the engine cadet has spent at sea become legal evidence. Complete certificates, consistent dates, a completed TRB and valid courses are the load-bearing pillars of the file leading to the OOW certificate. Obtaining certificates on time and correctly, keeping dates consistent and storing everything securely are the cadet's most basic responsibilities towards their own career. A poorly managed document process can leave even the most successful training period without evidence and invalid.

Yakıt sistemi, ham bunker yakıtını depol.en: The fuel system stores, heats and cleans (separator) the raw bunker fuel and delivers it to the engine at the correct viscosity/temperature. The lubrication system lubricates, cools and cleans moving parts and prevents wear. Both must operate continuously, cleanly and to the correct specification; otherwise the engine may stop or suffer serious damage.

Risk profili yüksektir: yakıt yanıcıdır.en: The risk profile is high: fuel is flammable (fire/explosion), hot fuel/oil carries a risk of spraying, and if either enters the sea it constitutes a pollution offense. When learning these systems, the cadet must understand both the technical operation and the safety and environmental aspects together.

Gemilerde başlıca yakıt türleri HFO (Hea.en: The main fuel types on ships are HFO (Heavy Fuel Oil), VLSFO (Very Low Sulphur Fuel Oil), MGO/MDO (Marine Gas/Diesel Oil) and, increasingly, alternative fuels such as LNG. Each has a different viscosity, sulfur content and treatment requirement. ISO 8217 defines marine fuel specifications; fuel received is expected to comply with this specification.

MARPOL Annex VI, ECA (Emission Control A.en: MARPOL Annex VI sets the sulfur limits in ECAs (Emission Control Areas) and in general waters (global limit 0.50% m/m, within an ECA 0.10% m/m). The cadet learns which fuel is used in which area, the fuel changeover procedure and the importance of the BDN (Bunker Delivery Note) record.

Bunkering, gemiye yakıt alınması operasy.en: Bunkering is the operation of taking fuel on board and carries a high risk of pollution/fire. Before the operation, the bunker plan is prepared, tank capacities and ullages are calculated, the line is checked, the valve alignment is verified, SOPEP equipment is kept ready and the scuppers (deck drain holes) are plugged. The ship-shore checklist is completed and communication is established.

Bunker sırasında sürekli izleme yapılır:.en: During bunkering, continuous monitoring is carried out: tank levels, flow rate (loading rate), overflow tank condition and line leaks. The emergency stop signal is agreed in advance. By following the bunkering operation under supervision, the cadet learns both the technical and the safety aspects; however, valve/pump control rests with authorized personnel.

Bunker tesliminde Bunker Delivery Note (.en: On bunker delivery, the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN) documents the quantity, density, sulfur content and delivery details of the fuel; under MARPOL Annex VI it is retained for a set period. During delivery, the MARPOL sample (representative sample) is taken and sealed; in a dispute or a PSC inspection, this sample is analyzed.

Yakıt kalitesi kritiktir: spesifikasyon.en: Fuel quality is critical: off-specification fuel (off-spec — water, solids, cat fines, high sulfur) can cause serious damage to the engine. The cadet observes the logic of sampling, sealing and checking the BDN. Suspect fuel should not be used in the engine before the laboratory analysis (fuel testing) result has been received.

Yakıt, depolama tankından (storage/bunke.en: Fuel flows from the storage tank (storage/bunker tank) to the settling tank and from there to the service tank. In the settling tank, the fuel is heated and allowed to stand; heavy water and sediment sink to the bottom and are drained off (settling). The service tank holds clean fuel that has passed through the separator, ready to be pumped to the engine. This chain cleans the fuel in stages.

Stajyer, bu tank zincirinin neden bu sır.en: The cadet learns why this tank chain is arranged in this order: the settling time allows water/sediment to separate, the separator removes the remaining impurities and the service tank holds the final clean reserve. If the settling tank water drain is not done regularly, water reaches the engine and combustion/injection problems arise.

Ağır yakıt (HFO/VLSFO) makineye doğru vi.en: Heavy fuel (HFO/VLSFO) must reach the engine at the correct viscosity; for this reason, heating (heating coils, trace heating) is fitted in the tanks and lines. The Viscotherm/viscosity controller automatically adjusts the temperature to bring the fuel to the optimum viscosity before injection (usually ~12-15 cSt). Incorrect viscosity causes poor atomization and combustion problems.

Stajyer, yakıt sıcaklık ve viskozite kon.en: The cadet learns the direct relationship between fuel temperature/viscosity control and engine performance: fuel that is too cold/viscous atomizes poorly, and fuel that is too hot can cause problems in the injection pumps. This balance is the basis of clean and efficient combustion in the engine.

Separatör (purifier/clarifier), yüksek h.en: The separator (purifier/clarifier) separates water and solid particles from fuel/oil by high-speed centrifugal force. In purifier mode, water and oil are separated (the water is discharged); in clarifier mode, only solids are separated. Separation, which is based on the difference in density, is balanced by gravity disc selection (in conventional separators) or by automatic water detection (in modern separators).

Stajyer, separatör operasyonunu gözetiml.en: The cadet follows separator operation under supervision: feed temperature (the optimum temperature for oil/fuel improves separation), throughput, water outlet (water seal) and periodic desludging (sludge discharge). The correct temperature and throughput determine the separation efficiency; excessive throughput impairs cleaning.

En sık separatör sorunu, yağ/yakıtın su.en: The most frequent separator problem is oil/fuel escaping through the water outlet (overboard); this may be caused by loss of the water seal, the wrong gravity disc or excessive throughput, and creates a risk of both fuel loss and pollution. Other problems are vibration (bowl imbalance), insufficient desludging and leaks.

Stajyer, separatörün \"normal\" çalışma.en: The cadet must learn the separator's "normal" running sound, vibration and appearance so as to be able to notice what is abnormal. Separator overhaul (bowl cleaning, gasket replacement) is a regular PMS job; by taking part in this maintenance, the cadet learns the internal construction. The sludge removed is managed subject to entry in the ORB.
