Ana makine yağlama sistemi; LO sump tank.en: The main engine lubrication system consists of the LO sump tank, LO pumps, LO cooler, filters and distribution lines. The oil lubricates and cools the main bearings, the crosshead/crankpin bearings, the piston (piston cooling oil) and the cam mechanism, then returns to the sump. Circulation is continuous and under pressure.

Stajyer; LO inlet pressure/temperature,.en: The cadet learns to monitor LO inlet pressure/temperature, sump level, filter differential pressure and cooler inlet/outlet temperatures. Falling LO pressure (pump/filter/leak) is a critical alarm and triggers slow-down/shut-down; for this reason, the LO system is under constant monitoring.

Büyük iki-zamanlı dizel makinelerde iki.en: Large two-stroke diesel engines have two separate oils: system oil (crankcase lubrication, cooling) and cylinder oil (lubrication of the cylinder liner wall, dosed by the lubricators). Cylinder oil is selected with a BN (Base Number) suited to the sulfur content of the fuel; the correct BN and feed rate are critical for neutralization of the sulfur.

Stajyer, cylinder oil feed rate'in (g/kW.en: The cadet learns why the cylinder oil feed rate (g/kWh) is adjusted according to fuel sulfur: insufficient lubrication causes liner wear and scuffing, while excessive lubrication causes deposits and cost. Scrape-down oil analysis is one way of monitoring cylinder condition. This balance is fundamental to engine life.

Yakıt ve yağ numuneleri düzenli alınır:.en: Fuel and oil samples are taken regularly: the MARPOL bunker sample, a fuel sample before use and periodic LO samples (used oil analysis). Samples must be representative and taken under clean conditions; a contaminated sample gives a false result. Samples are labeled and either tested quickly on board or sent to a laboratory.

LO analizi; viskozite, su içeriği, BN, a.en: LO analysis shows the condition of the oil in terms of viscosity, water content, BN, wear metals (Fe, Cu, Cr) and deposits. Increasing wear metals may be an early sign of a bearing/liner problem. By observing, the cadet learns sampling discipline and what the analysis results reveal.

Viskozite ve density (yoğunluk) ölçümü,.en: Viscosity and density measurements are key parameters for fuel quality and separator setting. Density affects the separator's density setting (and, in older separators, gravity disc selection); with very high-density fuels, water separation becomes difficult. Viscosity is the basis of heating/atomization control.

Stajyer, gemide bulunan ölçüm cihazlarıy.en: The cadet observes how measurements are taken with the instruments on board (viscometer, density meter / hydrometer) and learns how these values are reflected in operating settings. Measurement is not an abstract laboratory task; it is a practical tool directly serving the clean and safe operation of the engine.

MARPOL Annex I gereği, makine dairesi ya.en: Under MARPOL Annex I, engine-room oil operations are recorded in the Oil Record Book Part I: bunkering, internal fuel/oil transfers, pumping bilge water overboard through the OWS, sludge disposal (incinerator/ashore/tank) and tank cleaning. Each operation is recorded under specific code letters (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I) with the date, quantity and details, and signed by the responsible engineer.

Stajyer, ORB formatını okumayı ve her ka.en: The cadet learns to read the ORB format and what each type of entry means: why and how a bilge transfer is recorded, where sludge was sent, how separator sludge was managed. The ORB is one of the documents most frequently examined in PSC inspections; entries must be consistent with the actual tank levels and with machinery operation.

Bilge suyunu OWS'yi by-pass eden gizli b.en: Pumping bilge water overboard through a hidden line bypassing the OWS (magic pipe), or making false entries in the ORB, is among the most severely punished offenses at sea. Companies have been fined millions of dollars and crew members have been sentenced to prison. The cadet must learn why the ORB is taken so seriously and why honest recording is non-negotiable.

Stajyer ORB'yi imzalama yetkisine sahip.en: The cadet is not authorized to sign the ORB; this authority rests with the responsible engineer. However, the cadet learns the recording logic and internalizes the legal weight of this book, which one day will bear the cadet's own signature. Honesty in the ORB is part of the honor of the engineering profession.

Yakıt ve yağlama sistemleri, geminin kal.en: The fuel and lubrication systems are the arteries that feed and protect the heart of the ship. Bunkering safety, the tank chain, separator operation and LO circulation are the basis of reliable engine operation. At the same time, under MARPOL, these systems are among the most critical sources of marine pollution; honesty in the ORB and safe operation unite the technical and ethical dimensions of engineering. While learning these systems, the cadet must internalize the question "how are the environment and safety protected?" as much as the question "how is the engine fed and protected?"

Geminin ana güç ve kontrol sistemleri ar.en: When the ship's main power and control systems fail — blackout, fire, flooding — independent emergency systems with their own power sources are needed to maintain safety. These are located separately from the main systems (usually above the main deck, in a watertight compartment) and can operate without main power. The aim is to maintain basic safety functions even in the worst-case scenario.

Acil sistemler yalnızca var olmakla yetm.en: It is not enough for emergency systems simply to exist; they must be kept "ready to operate at any moment" by regular testing and maintenance. An emergency generator or fire pump that is not tested runs the risk of not working in a real emergency. For this reason, the regulations make periodic testing of these systems mandatory; the cadet learns by observing these tests.

Stajyer, acil sistem testlerine gözlemci.en: The cadet attends emergency system tests as an observer; the cadet does not start the system or intervene independently, but carefully follows the test procedure, the system's response and the success criteria. With each test, the cadet reinforces the answer to the question "when, why and how does this system cut in?"

Stajyer için acil sistem testleri çok de.en: For the cadet, emergency system tests are very valuable learning opportunities: scenarios not seen in normal operation (loss of power, automatic cut-in) are observed under controlled conditions. The cadet enters every test in the TRB and discusses the observations with the training engineer.

Emergency generator, ana güç (main gener.en: When main power (main generators) is lost, the emergency generator cuts in automatically and supplies the critical loads through the emergency switchboard: emergency lighting, navigation lights, steering gear, communications (GMDSS), fire detection, watertight doors and the emergency fire pump. It is usually located above the main deck, with its own fuel tank and starting system.

Blackout olduğunda emergency generator o.en: In a blackout, the emergency generator starts automatically (auto-start) and is usually ready to take load within 45 seconds (SOLAS requirement). Its starting source is independent (battery or compressed air). By observing the auto-start test, the cadet learns how the system detects the loss of power and cuts in.

Emergency generator testi, hem manuel st.en: The emergency generator test includes both a manual start (weekly trial) and an auto-start (simulated loss of power). During the test, starting success, achieving the required running time, voltage/frequency stability, load transfer to the emergency switchboard and the fuel/oil condition are observed. After the test, the system is returned to standby mode.

Stajyer, testte özellikle \"süre\" boyut.en: In the test, the cadet pays particular attention to the "time" dimension: how quickly was the generator ready to take load? Did the auto-start detect the loss of power correctly? Is the fuel tank sufficient (it is usually kept at a capacity for running for a set period)? These observations are indicators of the system's reliability in a real emergency.

Emergency fire pump, ana yangın pompalar.en: The emergency fire pump supplies firefighting water when the main fire pumps cannot operate (for example when an engine room fire has put the main pumps out of action). For this reason, it is located outside the engine room, in a separate compartment, and has its own independent power source (a motor supplied from the emergency generator, or an independent diesel).

Pompanın bağımsız konumu kritiktir: maki.en: The independent location of the pump is critical: in an engine room fire, the main pumps may be inaccessible; in this scenario, the emergency fire pump continues to supply pressure to the fire main. SOLAS specifies the pump's capacity and requires a minimum pressure at specified fire hydrants.

Stajyer, testte pompanın ne kadar sürede.en: In the test, the cadet observes how long the pump takes to supply pressure and observes the remote start mechanism. On most ships, the pump can be started remotely from outside the engine room; this makes it possible to respond to a fire without entering the engine room. The cadet learns where this remote start point is.

Ana makinenin başlatılması (start) genel.en: The main engine is usually started with compressed air; this air is stored in air bottles (air receivers) and filled by the main air compressors. The emergency air compressor is an independent capacity that provides enough air to restart the main engine when the main compressors cannot operate (as in a blackout); on some ships it may be driven by an independent diesel or supplied from emergency power.

Stajyer, blackout recovery'de emergency.en: The cadet learns the role of the emergency air compressor in blackout recovery: there must be enough starting air to start the main engine. Keeping the air bottle pressure at a set level and keeping the emergency compressor in working order are prerequisites for recovery after a blackout. The test verifies the compressor's ability to build up pressure.

Dümen sistemi (steering gear), geminin m.en: The steering gear is fundamental to the ship's ability to maneuver and avoid collision; for this reason it is designed with redundancy. If the main steering gear fails or power is lost, emergency steering mode is used: the second hydraulic pump is started or local/manual control is applied from the steering gear room. Communication (telephone) between the bridge and the steering gear room, and a rudder angle indicator, are provided.

Stajyer, emergency steering tatbikatını.en: The cadet observes the emergency steering drill: how control is transferred from the bridge to the steering gear room, how local control is carried out, how communication is maintained. SOLAS requires emergency steering drills to be held regularly; when a real steering failure occurs, the team must already have rehearsed.

Quick closing valve, yakıt/yağ tankların.en: Quick-closing valves are valves fitted at the outlets of fuel/oil tanks that can be closed remotely (usually from outside the engine room, from a control station). In an engine room fire, these valves are closed remotely to cut off the fuel supply to the fire; this is one of the most critical steps in preventing the fire from spreading.

Valfler genelde yay veya pnömatik/hidrol.en: The valves are usually closed by a spring or pneumatic/hydraulic mechanism, operated by a lever or button at a remote position. The cadet learns which tanks have quick-closing valves, where the remote closing position is and how the fuel supply is cut off after closing. Periodic testing of these valves (do they actually close?) is important.

Emergency stop butonları, makine dairesi.en: Emergency stop buttons stop fuel pumps, separators, fans and other critical equipment remotely from outside the engine room. In a fire, this stops the supply of fuel/oil and the circulation of air to the space and so makes firefighting possible. Ventilation flaps are closed remotely to cut off the entry of air (oxygen) into the engine room.

Fixed smothering system (CO2 veya benzer.en: Before the fixed smothering system (CO2 or similar) is activated, the ventilation flaps must be closed and the fans stopped; otherwise the extinguishing gas is expelled and the fire cannot be extinguished. The cadet learns the order of these remote controls in the firefighting chain: shut off fuel → stop equipment → close ventilation → count personnel → release the fixed system.

Blackout, tüm ana jeneratörlerin güç kay.en: A blackout is when all main generators lose power and the ship is left without electricity and immobile. Causes may be a generator trip (overload, fault), interruption of the fuel supply, an automation fault or a main switchboard problem. At the moment of blackout, the emergency generator cuts in automatically and supplies the critical loads; the recovery process starts immediately.

Recovery'nin ilk adımı nedeni hızlıca te.en: The first step in recovery is to diagnose the cause quickly: which generator tripped, and why? Then a generator is started manually/automatically, connected to the main switchboard and loaded in stages (critical consumers first, then heavy consumers). Rushing to take all the load at once may lead to a new trip (cascade blackout).

Blackout, özellikle dar suda veya manevr.en: A blackout is most dangerous in confined waters or during maneuvering; the ship rapidly loses maneuvering and steering capability, and a risk of collision/grounding arises. For this reason, the engine room is put on standby before maneuvering (an extra generator in parallel), and the speed of recovery is critical. Immediate coordination between the bridge and the engine room is essential.

Stajyer, blackout recovery tatbikatını v.en: The cadet treats a blackout recovery drill, or observing a real one, as a major learning opportunity: prioritization of the power system, paralleling of generators, the role of starting air and team communication are displayed intensively within a few minutes. The cadet follows each step, notes questions and discusses them with the training engineer.

Acil sistem testleri ve tatbikatları, IS.en: Emergency system tests and drills are recorded as required by ISM and SOLAS. The test date, result, abnormalities found and corrective actions are documented. These records are the evidence in PSC inspections and class surveys that the system has been tested regularly. A system that the records show has not been tested constitutes a serious inspection finding.

Stajyer, test kayıtlarının nasıl tutuldu.en: The cadet learns how test records are kept and enters every test/drill attended in the TRB. This supports both regulatory discipline and the TRB evidence of competence. A record is the only way to go beyond saying "the system exists" and to say "the system has been tested and works".

Acil sistemler, \"her an çalışmaya hazır.en: Emergency systems must be "ready to operate at any moment"; this requires regular maintenance. The emergency generator fuel/oil levels and battery, the fire pump priming system, the air compressor and the quick-closing valve mechanisms are checked periodically. The PMS manages this maintenance through planned work orders.

Stajyer, acil sistemlerin bakımına gözet.en: By taking part in the maintenance of emergency systems under supervision, the cadet both gets to know the system and grasps the question "why is this maintenance critical": a poorly maintained emergency system runs the risk of not working in a real emergency, which is even more dangerous than not having the system at all (a false sense of safety). An emergency system kept ready is the ship's insurance.

Acil sistemler, geminin \"en kötü gün\".en: Emergency systems are the ship's preparation for its "worst day"; they remain invisible in normal operation but determine the survival of the ship and crew in a crisis. The emergency generator, fire pump, air compressor and steering gear; quick-closing valves and remote controls; blackout recovery — none of them is reliable unless tested regularly. By observing these tests, the cadet learns the answers to "how does the system work, and does it really work?" together. The emergency system logic grasped today as an observer forms the basis of the composure and preparedness of the engineer who will manage a crisis tomorrow.

Reis, güverte bölümünün en kıdemli tayfa.en: The Bosun is the most senior rating in the deck department and works directly under the Chief Officer. The Bosun's authority is limited to interpreting the work order, allocating the team, ensuring safety on site and checking the quality of the work. Authority for planning and prioritization remains with the Chief Officer; the Bosun turns this plan into work on site. Knowing this distinction prevents taking unnecessary initiative and stepping outside safe limits.

Reis aynı zamanda tayfanın \"abisi\"dir;.en: The Bosun is also the "big brother" of the ratings, passing on technical knowledge, shipboard etiquette and safety culture. A good Bosun leads by example rather than by giving orders; the Bosun personally demonstrates the hardest job and stands at the front at the riskiest point. Team discipline comes not from fear but from this trust.

Tipik bir bakım gününde Reis, ekipten ön.en: On a typical maintenance day, the Bosun gets up before the team and reviews the weather, the ship's situation (in port/at sea), active work orders and work left over from the previous day. The Bosun holds a short synchronization with the Chief Officer: which job has priority today, which area is closed because of operations, which permit will be needed.

08:00'de güverte ekibi toplanır. Reis, g.en: At 08:00 the deck team assembles. The Bosun explains the day's work, the team allocation, the risks and the PPE requirements. This toolbox meeting is the most important 15 minutes of the day; a well-planned morning means an accident-free and productive day.

Birinci Zabit, PMS (Planned Maintenance.en: The Chief Officer gives the Bosun the work orders generated by the PMS (Planned Maintenance System) software. Each order contains the equipment, the work to be done, the materials list, the PPE required, the relevant risk assessment reference, the estimated duration and the evidence of completion (photo, measurement, signature). Before carrying out the order, the Bosun confirms that the materials and tools are available.

Reis emri yorumlarken sahanın gerçeğini.en: When interpreting the order, the Bosun brings in the reality on the ground: weather, sea state, the ship's port/sea schedule, the team's current fatigue and operations running at the same time. A plan that is perfect on paper cannot be carried out on deck in a storm; the Bosun sees this difference and gives feedback to the officer.

İşler; emniyet kritikliği, klas/PSC takv.en: Jobs are ranked according to safety criticality, the class/PSC schedule, the weather window and operational dependency. Safety equipment (liferaft servicing, fire main, LSA) and inspection preparation jobs always have priority. These are followed by voyage-critical jobs (lashing, hatch cover tightness), and then by cosmetic maintenance (painting, cleaning).

Her tayfanın yetkinliği, sertifikası ve.en: Each rating's competence, certification and experience differ. The Bosun matches qualified (AB - Able Seaman), general (OS - Ordinary Seaman) and novice (deck cadet/trainee) personnel to jobs according to the risk. High-risk work (working aloft, overside, enclosed space, hot work) is given only to trained personnel under supervision.

Reis, ekibi tanır: kimin yüksekte rahat.en: The Bosun knows the team: who works comfortably at height, who is meticulous with paint, who is quick with ropework. Putting the right person on the right job increases both safety and productivity; a wrong match means unfinished work or injury.

Bazı işler tek kişiyle yapılamaz: workin.en: Some jobs cannot be done by one person: working aloft requires a standby person at deck level, enclosed space entry a standby person plus atmosphere testing, and overside work a lookout ready for MOB. The Bosun sets the team size according to the minimum safe number of personnel for the job; risky work is not started with too few people.

Genç personel, deneyimli bir tayfa ile e.en: Young personnel are paired with an experienced rating and work within a "buddy system". This serves both teaching and safety; a novice is never left alone in a high-risk area.

Toolbox meeting (toolbox talk), iş başla.en: The toolbox meeting (toolbox talk) is a short safety briefing held before work starts. The Bosun explains what the job is, its steps, its risks, the precautions to be taken and what to do in an emergency. Participation is two-way; the ratings are asked to point out where they see hazards.

İyi bir toolbox; somut, kısa ve işe özel.en: A good toolbox talk is concrete, short and specific to the job. Saying "be careful" is not enough; specific instructions are given, such as "when changing the grinder disc, cut off the air, check the flange, put on the face shield". For important jobs, a job-specific risk assessment (JSA) is completed and the participants sign it.

Çok uluslu ekiplerde ortak çalışma dili.en: In multinational teams, a common working language (usually English + maritime jargon) is used. The Bosun confirms by read-back that the instruction has been understood. An order that is not understood is carried out wrongly on site, and that means an accident. Visual demonstration and showing by doing are the most effective ways to overcome the language barrier.

Reis, ekibin baret, emniyet ayakkabısı,.en: The Bosun checks that the team is wearing a hard hat, safety shoes, boiler suit, gloves, goggles, ear protection and job-specific equipment (harness, face shield, dust mask, lifejacket), complete and in good condition. Damaged PPE is replaced immediately. PPE is the last line of defense; it remains indispensable even after the risk has been eliminated at source.

Reis, sahada sürekli dolaşır; permit kap.en: The Bosun moves around the site continuously and immediately warns personnel who step outside the scope of the permit, work without PPE or take dangerous shortcuts. A small violation that is tolerated becomes normal and prepares the ground for a major accident. The principle "unsafe behavior that is ignored is unsafe behavior that is approved" applies.

STCW ve MLC 2006, mürettebatın asgari di.en: STCW and MLC 2006 regulate the minimum hours of rest for the crew: at least 10 hours of rest in any 24 hours and at least 77 hours in any 7 days; rest may be divided into no more than two periods, one of which must be at least 6 hours uninterrupted. The Bosun does not plan work in a way that would breach the team's work/rest hours records.

Yorgunluk, denizdeki kazaların başlıca i.en: Fatigue is the main human factor in accidents at sea. A rating who has worked long hours during a port/maneuvering period is not given risky work the following morning. By making sure the team actually rests, the Bosun both complies with the regulations and prevents accidents.

Reis; dikkat dağınıklığı, yavaşlama, sin.en: The Bosun spots signs of fatigue early, such as lack of concentration, slowing down, irritability and increasing errors. In such a case, the pace of work is changed, the team is rotated or the job is postponed. The most valuable quality of an on-site leader is the ability to "read" the team.

Reis, masaya oturup işi izlemez; sahada.en: The Bosun does not sit at a desk watching the work; the Bosun moves around the site and personally steps in on the technique and safety of the work. On seeing a job start wrongly, the Bosun stops it and shows the correct method. If more than one job is under way at the same time, the Bosun gives the most time to the riskiest one.

Reis, işin ilerlemesini takip eder ve ge.en: The Bosun follows the progress of the work and informs the Chief Officer in good time when a delay or obstacle arises (shortage of materials, change in the weather, equipment failure). Passing a problem on site to the officer late means a loss of productivity for the whole day.

Limanda yük operasyonu, bunkering, store.en: In port, cargo operations, bunkering, taking stores and maintenance may all run at the same time. The Bosun ensures that these jobs do not endanger each other — for example, no painting is done underneath a cargo crane while it is working, and no hot work is done during bunkering. Managing overlapping operations is one of the on-site leader's most critical skills.

Gün sonunda Reis, tamamlanan işleri, kul.en: At the end of the day, the Bosun reports to the Chief Officer on the jobs completed, materials used, jobs left unfinished and observations on site (new rust areas, failed equipment, stock running out). PMS work orders are closed with evidence of completion (photo, measurement).

Bu raporlama yalnızca bürokrasi değildir.en: This reporting is not just bureaucracy; it is the ship's technical memory. In an inspection, after an accident or when a new team arrives, these records are the only reliable answer to the question "what has been done, and what remains?"

Reis, ucuz atlatılan olayları (near-miss.en: The Bosun reports near-misses and unsafe conditions with an encouraging attitude. A near-miss culture is the strongest early warning system against major accidents. An instructive rather than punitive approach encourages the team to report.

Ekip disiplini, Reis'in adil ve tutarlı.en: Team discipline comes from the Bosun being fair and consistent. The same rule is applied equally to everyone; favoritism is what destroys team morale fastest. The Bosun criticizes in private and praises in public; this simple principle protects the team's health for years.

Zor koşullarda (kötü hava, uzun saatler,.en: In difficult conditions (bad weather, long hours, monotonous work), the Bosun's attitude is reflected in the team. A calm, determined Bosun who stands at the front carries the team; a Bosun who panics or constantly shouts breaks the team apart.

Gemilerde çok uluslu ekipler standarttır.en: Multinational crews are standard on ships. The Bosun brings ratings of different languages, religions and cultures together in a common safety and work culture. Respect and clear communication are the basic tools. Fairness in mess room arrangements, use of recreation areas and allocation of duties ensures team harmony.

Reis'in günlük yönetimdeki başarısı, \"k.en: The Bosun's success in daily management lies hidden in trouble-free days that "nobody notices". Well-allocated work, well-supervised safety and a well-motivated team keep the ship both productive and accident-free. As the on-site leader of the deck, the Bosun re-establishes this balance every day.

Çelik gemi gövdesi, deniz suyu, klorür,.en: A steel ship's hull is under intense attack from seawater, chlorides, oxygen and UV radiation. Once corrosion starts, it accelerates geometrically: a small rust spot can affect hundreds of square meters of surface in 6 months. The Bosun's basic task is to find and remove "small rust spots" before they grow and to maintain the integrity of the protective paint system.

Korozyonun tipleri farklıdır: uniform co.en: There are different types of corrosion: uniform corrosion (a thin layer over wide surfaces), pitting (localized deep pits — particularly in ballast tanks and in the middle of holds), galvanic corrosion (at joints between dissimilar metals), crevice corrosion (at tight intersections) and stress corrosion cracking (in fatigued areas). Each type requires different measures.

Reis sabah toolbox toplantısından sonra.en: After the morning toolbox meeting, the Bosun reviews the work orders with the Chief Officer. The work order contains the equipment, the work to be done, the materials list, the PPE required, the risk assessment reference, the estimated duration and the evidence of completion (photo, measurement). When allocating this order to the team, the Bosun combines job competence, team size, weather conditions and the port/at-sea situation.

Yüzey hazırlığı, boyanın ömrünü %60-80 o.en: Surface preparation determines 60-80% of the life of the paint. ISO 8501-1 defines practical standards for surface cleanliness. There are the levels SA 1 (light brush-off blast), SA 2 (thorough blast), SA 2.5 (very thorough — the industry norm) and SA 3 (white metal — for special applications). For mechanical cleaning, ST 2 (thorough manual cleaning) and ST 3 (very thorough) are used.

Gemide saha şartlarında SA 2.5 zor sağla.en: On board, under site conditions, SA 2.5 is difficult to achieve; most areas are prepared with hand tools to around ST 2 - ST 3. Using a visual reference (color chart), the Bosun records which standard the area to be painted has achieved; this is critical for the paint warranty period.

Pneumatic chipping hammer, needle scaler.en: Pneumatic chipping hammers, needle scalers, angle grinders and disc sanders are the most common tools. The Bosun checks the appropriate PPE (goggles, ear protection, mask, gloves, chaps), the daily check of electric/pneumatic tools, hose connections and grounding. Use of a grinder that requires a hot work permit (especially on a tanker deck) needs the approval of the Chief Officer + Master + Chief Engineer.

Tipik bir güverte boya sistemi: primer (.en: A typical deck paint system: primer (zinc rich epoxy, 75 µm DFT) → intermediate coat (epoxy, 125 µm) → topcoat (polyurethane, 50 µm). Total DFT (Dry Film Thickness) 250-300 µm. On exposed areas such as hatch tops, the main deck and the forecastle, a UV-resistant topcoat is essential.

Underwater hull için anti-fouling sistem.en: For the underwater hull, the anti-fouling system (usually applied in drydock): anti-corrosion epoxy + tie coat + self-polishing copolymer (SPC) anti-fouling. The exterior of the accommodation is painted with an enamel finish; intumescent (fire-retardant) paint is used in interior spaces.

Boya tatbiki için ortam koşulları kritik.en: Ambient conditions are critical for applying paint: the surface temperature must be at least 3 °C above the dew point, relative humidity below 85%, air temperature above +5 °C, and there must be no rain or salt spray. The Bosun measures these parameters with a psychrometer and a temperature probe. Paint applied in the wrong conditions comes off within 6 months.

Boya inceltme oranı (genelde max %5-10),.en: The thinning ratio (usually max 5-10%), mixing time, pot life (4-6 hours for epoxies) and application method (brush, roller, airless spray) are determined according to the product's TDS (Technical Data Sheet).

Modern gemilerde yüksek mukavemetli HMPE.en: On modern ships, high-strength HMPE (Dyneema) and polyester blend ropes are common. After every voyage, the rope is checked visually for chafe, glazing (heat damage), kinks, broken yarns and UV fading. Under OCIMF MEG4, ropes are kept on record with regard to LDBF (Line Design Break Force), MBL and the use of "tails".

Cargo wire, mooring wire ve crane wire i.en: Periodic greasing (OEM lubricant), broken wire counts and diameter measurements are carried out on cargo wires, mooring wires and crane wires. According to ISO 4309 and the company standard, >10% broken wires within a lay length, kinks, severe wear or visible bulging are reasons for retirement.

Hatch cover; rubber gasket, compression.en: The hatch cover consists of rubber gaskets, compression bars, cleats, hydraulic cylinders and drainage channels. Tightness tests (chalk test, hose test, ultrasonic test) are carried out by the Chief Officer + Bosun. Seawater ingress into the hold is a forerunner of major casualties such as the MOL Comfort.

Reis, kapanan hatch çevresinde rubber co.en: The Bosun checks the rubber compression marks around the closed hatch; if the compression is not even, the gasket or compression bar must be replaced. For the hydraulic system, checking the oil level and hoses and testing the lift/close function are routine.

Cargo crane periyodik load test (yıllık.en: Cargo cranes require periodic load tests (annual + 5-yearly at 1.25× SWL) under class survey. The Bosun carries out daily checks: oil level, hydraulic leaks, brake test, operation of the limit switches, wire rope condition, hook safety latch.

Windlass ve mooring winch bakımında; bra.en: In windlass and mooring winch maintenance, brake band wear, gear oil level, the pawl mechanism and brake holding capacity (annual test) are the critical points. Compliance with SOLAS Chapter II-1 and IACS UR A2 is checked.

Anchor ve chain cable, klas survey'inde.en: The anchor and chain cable are examined closely at the class survey; they are subject to a program under which, every 5 years, the whole cable is ranged out (extracted), inspected and, if necessary, turned end-for-end. Every day, the Bosun checks the chain locker ventilation, drainage of accumulated mud, the chain stopper, the bow stopper and the devil's claw.

Anchor windlass bakımı vinç bakımıyla be.en: Anchor windlass maintenance is similar to crane maintenance; in addition, the chain compressor (anchor secured at sea) and the riding pawl are tested periodically.

Limanda gürültülü ve toz yapan işler (ch.en: In port, noisy and dusty jobs (chipping, grinding, painting) take priority, because at sea a large part of the team is keeping watches. Roughly, 30% of port time is allocated to operations, 50% to maintenance and 20% to rest + documentation.

Seyirde havaya bağlı işler yapılamaz; bu.en: At sea, weather-dependent jobs cannot be done; instead, maintenance inside equipment (crane servicing, hatch hydraulics, workshop jobs), inventory taking and training activities come to the fore. If the weather permits, jobs such as touch-up paint, lashing inspection and lifeboat exterior maintenance are scheduled.

Çalışmalar; risk seviyesine göre permit.en: Depending on the level of risk, work may require a permit: hot work permit, enclosed space entry permit, working aloft permit, working overside permit, electrical isolation permit. Through supervision on site, the Bosun ensures that the team does not step outside the scope of the permit.

Working aloft (yüksekte çalışma) için ha.en: For working aloft, the requirements are a harness with double lanyard, a secondary attachment point, a cordon on the deck below, no passage permitted and suitable weather conditions. Working overside starts with a liferaft ready, MOB equipment and communication.

Her sabah Reis, ekibe günün işini, riskl.en: Every morning, the Bosun holds a toolbox meeting explaining to the team the day's work, the risks, the equipment to be used and the PPE. For important jobs, a job-specific risk assessment (JSA) is completed and the participants sign it. After an accident, this record is evidence of "due diligence".

Klasik bir baş gemi (forecastle) bakım p.en: A classic forecastle maintenance program: days 1-2 chipping (removing existing rust + flaking paint), days 3-4 finish surface preparation with ST 3 power tools, day 5 primer, day 6 intermediate coat, days 7-8 topcoat. Application is staged according to the weather and the likelihood of sea spray.

Hatch coaming, tuz suya en açık bölgeler.en: The hatch coaming is one of the areas most exposed to salt water. The Bosun plans periodic washing to remove salt/water accumulated in the drainage recesses. When the onset of rust is seen, a local touch-up is not applied straight away; surface preparation is done first (ST 3), then epoxy primer + topcoat are applied.

Reis sadece denetçi değil, eğitici rolün.en: The Bosun is not only a supervisor but also a trainer. The Bosun demonstrates in practice basic skills to young ratings, such as preparing ropes, tying knots, rope splicing, chipping and painting, hot work safety and enclosed space discipline. This training is recorded in the "deck training book"; it is an important part of the STCW familiarization requirements.

Güverte bakımı; sadece \"boya atmak\" de.en: Deck maintenance is not just "slapping on paint". It is a disciplined, systematic and continuous effort to prevent corrosion, extend the service life of equipment, pass inspections with credit and keep the team safe. The Bosun is the on-site leader of this effort; the Bosun's success keeps the ship upright, sound and certified for 10-15 years.

Ambar, bir sonraki yüke uygun temizlik s.en: The hold must be handed over at a level of cleanliness suitable for the next cargo; otherwise residues of the previous cargo (taint), moisture or odor will damage the new cargo. Independent inspections are carried out for grain cargoes; a failed hold inspection leads to rejection for loading and major delays/costs. The Bosun knows and applies these standards.

Operasyon; süpürme, deniz suyu yıkama, t.en: The operation consists of sweeping, washing with seawater, rinsing with fresh water (especially for salt/odor), drying and, if necessary, paint touch-up. The Bosun directs the team, sets the sequence and confirms that each stage has been completed. Dryness is critical, especially for grain/steel cargoes.

Hatch coaming, track, bilge well, hold l.en: Hatch coamings, tracks, bilge wells, hold ladders and light fixtures are cleaned separately; these details often make the difference in an inspection. Cleaning the bilge wells and strainers is important for water drainage and cargo safety.

Tahıl/konsantre hassas ve yüksek temizli.en: Grain/concentrates are sensitive and require a high level of cleanliness; if ferrous ore is to be loaded after coal, a different standard applies, and "hospital clean" is required for sensitive food cargoes. The Bosun knows which cargo requires which level and directs the team accordingly. Residues of the previous cargo (taint) can contaminate an incompatible next cargo.

Ambar kapalı mekandır; giriş enclosed sp.en: The hold is an enclosed space; entry is made with an enclosed space entry permit and atmosphere testing. High-pressure washing, slippery surfaces and working at height (hold ladders, edges) are additional risks. The Bosun ensures PPE, supervision and safe working practice.

Hazırlık tamamlanınca Reis, ambarın iste.en: When preparation is complete, the Bosun checks that the hold is up to the required standard and reports to the Chief Officer. The condition is documented with photos/video; in a cargo dispute, this record is the evidence that the hold was handed over clean.

Cargo hold preparation liderliği, Reisin.en: Leading cargo hold preparation is an operation in which the Bosun uses technical knowledge, team management and safety awareness together. The correct cleanliness standard, attention to detail points and safe working ensure that the hold is handed over fit to carry the cargo safely and that costly cargo disputes are avoided.

Hatch cover sızdırmazlığı, ambardaki yük.en: Hatch cover tightness protects the cargo in the hold from seawater and protects the ship's integrity against water ingress. A leaking cover leads to cargo damage (especially grain, steel, sensitive cargo), mold/wetting and large claims. The Bosun knows that the maintenance preserving this tightness is, directly, cargo safety.

Reis; rubber gasket'lerin temiz, esnek v.en: The Bosun ensures that the rubber gaskets are clean, flexible and undamaged, that the compression bars bear evenly on the gaskets and that the drain channels (water drainage channels) are kept open. A blocked drain lets water leak inside; a crushed/permanently deformed gasket impairs tightness.

Kapağı kapalı tutan cleating/securing me.en: The cleating/securing mechanism that keeps the cover closed (cleats, wedges, hydraulics) is lubricated and kept in working order. Cleating that does not hold may allow the cover to open in heavy weather and the hold to flood.

Sızdırmazlık; hose test (yüksek basınçlı.en: Tightness is verified by a hose test (high-pressure water) or an ultrasonic test. The Bosun prepares the covers before the test (gaskets/drains clean, cover correctly seated). The ultrasonic test shows the leak point numerically and provides assurance before loading.

Tank vent head, sounding pipe head ve ma.en: Deck openings such as tank vent heads, sounding pipe heads and manhole covers are checked periodically; the float/flame screen of the vent head, the sounding pipe cap and the manhole gaskets/bolts ensure watertightness. A defect in these can lead to water entering a tank/void space.

Hatch cover panelleri, coaming ve güvert.en: Hatch cover panels, coamings and deck openings are monitored for corrosion; advanced corrosion creates both a structural risk and a tightness risk. The Bosun includes corrosion spots in the painting program and reports serious deformation to the Chief Officer.

Hatch cover ve weather deck sızdırmazlık.en: Hatch cover and weather deck tightness maintenance is one of the Bosun's most concrete tasks in protecting the cargo and the ship from the sea. Clean gaskets, open drains, working cleats and sound deck openings ensure that the holds stay dry even in heavy weather and that the cargo is carried safely.

Deniz ortamı çeliği hızla korozyona uğra.en: The marine environment corrodes steel quickly; paint is the primary barrier against this corrosion. A well-managed coating extends the life of hull and deck steel by decades, whereas neglected corrosion leads to structural weakness and expensive steel renewal. The Bosun is the on-site leader of this fight.

Boyanın tutması, tümüyle yüzey hazırlığı.en: Paint adhesion depends entirely on surface preparation. The surface is cleaned by chipping, grinding and descaling (removal of scale/rust); loose rust, old paint and salt residues are removed. The Bosun ensures that the preparation level (e.g. Sa 2.5 blast cleanliness) is in line with the plan. On a poorly prepared surface, even the best paint will not hold.

Boya sistemi katmanlıdır: primer (yapışm.en: The paint system is layered: primer (adhesion/corrosion protection), intermediate (thickness/barrier) and topcoat (outer protection/appearance). The Bosun applies the coat sequence in accordance with the paint scheme, the dry film thickness (DFT) and the overcoating intervals between coats. The wrong sequence or insufficient thickness shortens the protection life.

Boya, hava ve yüzey koşulları uygun oldu.en: Paint is applied when the air and surface conditions are suitable. The surface temperature should generally be at least 3°C above the dew point; otherwise moisture condenses on the surface and the paint does not hold. Humidity, temperature and wind are measured. The Bosun plans the application according to these conditions.

Reis; boya stoğunu, karışım oranlarını (.en: The Bosun monitors the paint stock, mixing ratios (two-component paints) and batch number records. The coat applied, area, DFT and conditions are recorded. These records are valuable both for warranty/compliance and for planning the next maintenance.

Chipping/grinding göz/solunum riski, boy.en: Chipping/grinding carries eye/respiratory risks, and paint carries solvent vapor and fire risks. Suitable PPE (goggles, respirator, gloves), ventilation and distance from ignition sources are essential. Painting in an enclosed space is subject to the enclosed space and atmosphere rules.

Boya programı ve korozyon yönetimi, Reis.en: The painting program and corrosion management are tasks through which the Bosun contributes directly to the ship's structural life. Good surface preparation, the correct coating system and respect for weather conditions build a lasting defense that protects steel from corrosion and secures the ship's long-term health.

Bağlama operasyonunda halatlar geminin t.en: In a mooring operation, the lines carry the forces generated by the ship's entire tonnage; when a line is loaded close to its MBL, hundreds of kJ of energy are stored in it. When this line parts, the energy is released like a whip, creating the lethal recoil known as "snap-back". A rotating winch drum, a confined working area, a wet deck and restricted visibility increase the risk.

Reis; istasyondaki tüm tayfaların güvenl.en: The Bosun ensures that all ratings at the station stand in safe positions, use the correct technique and carry out the bridge's orders in full. The more routine an operation is, the more dangerous it is, because attention drops. The Bosun's task is to keep attention alive.

Reis genelde baş (forward) istasyonunu,.en: The Bosun usually runs the forward station and the Second Officer the aft station; or, depending on the arrangement, the Bosun is aft. At the station, the Bosun clearly assigns who will tend which line, who will operate the winch and who will act as lookout. The Bosun communicates with the bridge by radio and confirms every order by read-back.

Reis, güvertede kayma/takılma riski yara.en: The Bosun has anything that creates a slip/trip hazard on deck (oil, heaps of line, tools) cleared away. The snap-back zones are reviewed and the radio/communications are tested. The whole team knows what to do; the report "stations ready forward/aft" is given to the bridge.

Standart bağlama paterni; head line, bre.en: A standard mooring pattern includes head lines, breast lines and spring lines (forward and aft). The springs restrain longitudinal movement, the breast lines restrain transverse movement and the head/stern lines provide general holding. In coordination with the bridge and the pilot, the Bosun knows which line is to be sent first; usually a spring or a breast line is sent first.

Halat winch drum'a sarılırken \"turn\"la.en: When the line is wound onto the winch drum, the turns must lie evenly without riding over one another; a riding turn causes the winch to jam and leads to loss of control. The Bosun checks that enough turns (usually 3-4) are on the drum and that the line is able to render.

Bazı gemilerde wire + sentetik tail komb.en: Some ships use a wire + synthetic tail combination; the tail offsets the stiffness of the wire and absorbs the dynamic load. The Bosun checks that the MBL of the tail is compatible with the wire (usually 125-150% of the wire's MBL) and that the connecting shackle/cow hitch is sound. A worn tail increases the risk of parting.

Mixed mooring (aynı yönde hem tel hem se.en: Mixed mooring (using both wire and synthetic lines in the same direction) is not recommended by MEG4, because lines of different elasticity do not share the load equally and the stiffer one parts first. The Bosun prevents this error; lines of similar elasticity are used in the same service.

Winch freni, halatın MBL'sinin altında (.en: The winch brake must be set to render (slip and shed load) below the MBL of the line (usually around 60% of SDBF), so that the brake slips before the line parts and the energy is released in a controlled way. Brake holding capacity is tested periodically. The Bosun knows that this setting must be correct and monitors how tightly the brake is applied.

Aşırı yük altında halat koparmak yerine.en: Under excessive load, allowing the winch brake to slip in a controlled way (render) rather than letting the line part protects both the equipment and the people. When the Bosun notices that a line is overloaded (water squeezing out, noise, drum vibration), the Bosun intervenes immediately and, if necessary, warns the bridge: "line overloaded".

Manevra sırasında pilot, köprüüstüne kom.en: During maneuvering, the pilot gives orders to the bridge; the bridge passes them to the station by radio ("heave away forward spring", "slack head line", "make fast", "let go aft"). The Bosun confirms these orders by read-back and carries them out at the station. If an order is not understood, "say again" is used; no action is taken on guesswork.

Reis, sahadan köprüüstüne geri bildirim.en: The Bosun reports back from the station to the bridge: "forward spring made fast", "one line ashore", "all fast forward", "all gone aft, clear of propeller". The "clear of propeller/thruster" report is especially critical; if a line has fallen into the water, there is a risk of it fouling the propeller, and the engine is not used until the bridge has been warned.

Römorkör kullanılıyorsa Reis, tug line'ı.en: If tugs are used, the Bosun ensures that the tug line is taken on board safely and made fast to the correct bitt/SPM point, and that the crew keep clear while it is under tension. A parting tug line, or one loaded at the wrong angle, causes serious injuries. Work with the tug is coordinated within the bridge–pilot–tug master triangle.

Sentetik halat esnerken enerji depolar;.en: A synthetic line stores energy as it stretches; when it parts, this energy is released as snap-back. The modern view is that "the whole deck is a potential snap-back zone", because the danger zone changes as the direction of the line changes. The Bosun teaches the crew to stand out of the line's path and, wherever possible, behind the winch/bitt.

Yeni MEG4 yaklaşımı, sabit \"snap-back z.en: The new MEG4 approach stresses that fixed "snap-back zone" markings can be misleading, because the line changes direction around the fairlead. Instead of relying blindly on static markings, the Bosun develops the crew's awareness of the hazard as a dynamic one.

Bir halat koparsa Reis derhal \"line par.en: If a line parts, the Bosun immediately warns "line parted", informs the bridge and checks that the crew are safe. If anyone is injured, first aid and the MOB/medevac procedure are started. Since the load on the remaining lines increases, the operation is reassessed; if necessary, additional lines are put out.

Dar sularda veya akıntılı yanaşmada pilo.en: In confined waters or when berthing in a current, the pilot may use an anchor to hold the ship's head ("dredging anchor"). The Bosun keeps the windlass ready on the fo'c'sle, handles the chain stopper and brake, and pays out the cable under control on the bridge's order (e.g. "walk back two shackles"). Details of the anchoring equipment are covered in a separate section (task 8).

Baş istasyonu demir/halat ile, kıç istas.en: The forward station works with the anchor/lines and the aft station with lines, at the same time. The Bosun reports clearly to the bridge what is happening at the Bosun's own station, so that the bridge can manage both ends in step. A breakdown in communication creates dangerous situations, such as one end of the ship coming free while the other end is still made fast.

\"Single up\" komutuyla fazla halatlar t.en: On the "single up" order, surplus lines are taken in and the ship is held by single lines; on "let go", the last lines are released. The Bosun confirms that the released line has been recovered cleanly from the quay and has not fallen into the water and fouled the propeller ("all gone and clear"). The engine is not used until this confirmation has been given to the bridge.

Halatlar toplandıktan sonra düzgün ranza.en: After the lines have been taken in, they are stowed neatly on the racks, the fairleads are cleared and the winch is disengaged. The Bosun brings the station to the "secured for sea" condition and reports to the bridge.

Kış ve kutup operasyonlarında halatlar/g.en: In winter and polar operations, lines and decks ice up, synthetic lines stiffen and decks become more slippery. The Bosun manages the risk by removing ice, providing extra grip (anti-slip) and operating more slowly. A frozen line makes both hand grip and winch control more difficult.

Dünya genelinde mooring snap-back kaynak.en: Worldwide, deaths caused by mooring snap-back are regularly reported by the MAIB and other authorities. The common factors are: crew standing in the path of a taut line, fatigue, poor lighting and rushed operations. Lesson: no port schedule is more important than the safe positioning of a single crew member.

Bağlama ve manevra, denizciliğin en eski.en: Mooring and maneuvering is one of the oldest, yet still one of the deadliest, operations at sea. The Bosun's disciplined leadership at the station — clear orders, correct technique, snap-back awareness and an unshakeable "safety first" attitude — keeps the crew alive and the ship safe. At this station, the smallest slackness is paid for at the highest price.

Gemide meydana gelen yaralanmaların önem.en: A large share of injuries on board is caused by "slip, trip and fall" accidents. Lines left lying about, hand tools left out, spilled oil and paint, loose deck plates and blocked passageways are all low-severity but high-frequency causes of accidents. The Bosun's housekeeping discipline stops these accidents at the source.

Düzen aynı zamanda acil durum hazırlığın.en: Order is also a precondition for emergency preparedness. Being unable to reach the foam monitor when a fire breaks out, a blocked route to the muster station at the moment of abandon ship, or stowed material blocking access to a liferaft all turn into disaster at moments when seconds save lives.

Endüstriyel 5S yöntemi (Seiri-ayıkla, Se.en: The industrial 5S method (Seiri – sort, Seiton – set in order, Seiso – clean, Seiketsu – standardize, Shitsuke – sustain) can be applied directly on deck. The Bosun fixes "what belongs where" for each storage area; the places of hand tools are marked with shadow boards, so a missing tool is noticed at once.

Standartlaştırma; bir kişinin değil, eki.en: Standardization must become a shared habit of the whole team, not of one person. The Bosun ensures that everyone knows "where things go", so that order is kept even when a deckhand is on leave or being relieved.

Açık güvertede yağ, gres, boya, su ve öz.en: On open deck, oil, grease, paint, water and especially ice are the main causes of slipping. The Bosun gives priority to keeping walkways clean; in cold climates, the Bosun plans anti-slip application, salt spreading and ice breaking. Non-slip paint and anti-slip strips on deck are checked periodically.

Açıkta bırakılmış lashing malzemesi, hor.en: Lashing material, hoses, cables and line ends left lying about are the most frequent causes of tripping. Hoses and cables laid out temporarily are hung up where possible, or gathered to the side so that they do not obstruct passage; if necessary, they are marked with warning tape/cones.

Açık manhole, ullage port, sounding pipe.en: Open manholes, ullage ports, sounding pipe caps, hold accesses and missing guard rails are fatal fall hazards. The Bosun ensures that every opening is kept under supervision while open and is closed securely as soon as the work is finished. A manhole left open and unattended can cost a crew member's life in the dark at night.

Guard rail, stanchion, bulwark ve safety.en: The integrity of guard rails, stanchions, bulwarks and safety chains is checked periodically; missing or loose railings are reported immediately and temporary safety measures (warning, barrier) are taken.

SOLAS Chapter II-2, kaçış yollarının her.en: SOLAS Chapter II-2 requires escape routes to be kept open and unobstructed at all times. The Bosun checks that no material is stowed in front of corridors, stairways, doors and emergency exits. In a fire, one extra meter along a smoke-filled corridor is the difference between life and death.

Watertight ve fire door'ların serbest ka.en: Wedges, lashings and stowed items that prevent watertight and fire doors from closing freely are removed. A fire door wedged open "to let the air through" is one of the most common inspection findings and directly endangers the safety of the ship.

Can salları, can filikası, MOB botu, yan.en: Access to liferafts, the lifeboat, the MOB boat, fire hose boxes, foam monitors, portable fire extinguishers and EEBDs must always be kept clear. The Bosun ensures that nothing is ever stowed around this equipment and that the signage remains visible.

Acil ekipman erişim yolları boyaması (ge.en: The painted access routes to emergency equipment (usually marked in yellow) and the equipment location signs are checked periodically; faded or covered markings are renewed. The muster station area is always kept clear and accessible.

Bakım sırasında boya kutuları, tiner, ha.en: During maintenance, materials such as paint tins, thinner, rope reels and lashing material are temporarily kept on deck. The Bosun ensures that they are stowed lashed (so that they cannot shift at sea), without obstructing passage, and, if they are dangerous substances, properly segregated.

Denizde hiçbir gevşek malzeme güvertede.en: At sea, no loose material is left on deck; even a single drum of paint can be thrown about by rolling and cause injury or be lost overboard. "Sea-fastening" is an integral part of finishing any job.

Boya, tiner, gres, oksijen-asetilen tüpl.en: Flammable/dangerous materials such as paint, thinner, grease, oxygen-acetylene cylinders and solvents are kept in suitable, ventilated stores away from sparks. On open deck, gas cylinders are secured upright and firmly (with chains/clamps); oxygen and fuel gas cylinders are kept apart.

Paçavra ve solvent emmiş bezler; self-ig.en: Rags and cloths soaked with solvent are collected in metal bins with lids because of the risk of self-ignition (spontaneous combustion) and are disposed of regularly. This is a simple but vital housekeeping rule.

Güverte üzeri su drenajı (scupper) tıkal.en: When the deck drains (scuppers) are blocked, water collects on deck; this is both a slip hazard and a cause of damage to cargo/stores. The Bosun checks that the scuppers are kept clean and clear. However, during tanker/cargo operations, scupper plugs are fitted because of the risk of pollution; the balance between these two requirements is managed case by case.

Boya, yağ veya kimyasal döküntüsünün den.en: Paint, oil or chemical spills getting into the sea is a serious MARPOL violation. During maintenance, the scuppers are plugged (plug + putty), and when the work is finished the deck is cleaned and drained in a controlled way. Save-all trays are kept ready during oil/paint transfers.

MARPOL Annex V kapsamında güverte atıkla.en: Under MARPOL Annex V, deck waste (plastics, metal, food, operational waste) is collected separately; the Bosun checks that the garbage stations on deck are kept in order and that waste is segregated correctly. Working records are kept on deck for the Garbage Record Book entries.

Liman, denetimlerin (PSC, vetting, klas,.en: Port is where inspections (PSC, vetting, class, terminal) are most frequent. Before arrival, the Bosun makes the deck ready for inspection: order on the mooring deck, cleanliness of open areas, visibility of markings and access to equipment. After dusty/noisy work in port (chipping, grinding), the area is tidied up immediately.

Seyirde öncelik, denizde gevşek malzeme.en: At sea, the priority is to leave no loose material on deck and to sea-fasten everything. When bad weather is expected, the Bosun carries out a "secure for sea" check over the whole open deck: lashings, store doors, hose reels, gas cylinders and deck equipment. An object thrown about by rolling causes injury, loss overboard and damage.

Hava uygun olduğunda seyir, rutin temizl.en: When the weather is suitable, the passage is an opportunity for routine cleaning and tidying; however, the safety constraints (harness, weather window, supervision) are tighter than in port.

Yetersiz aydınlatma, gece operasyonların.en: Inadequate lighting increases the risk of accidents during night operations and in passageways. The Bosun routinely checks that deck lights, passageway lighting and emergency lighting are working, and reports defective lights. Lighting of the mooring deck, access ways and store entrances has priority.

Tehlike işaretleri, ekipman lokasyon lev.en: Hazard signs, equipment location signs, mandatory PPE signs and walkway markings are kept legible and visible. Faded, rusted or covered signs are renewed as part of housekeeping. Visible marking is for the safety of both the crew and visitors (pilot, surveyor, stevedores).

Denetçiler güvertede; temizlik, korkuluk.en: On deck, inspectors look at cleanliness, the integrity of railings, clear escape routes, access to equipment, markings, drainage and the general state of maintenance. The Bosun follows a regular self-inspection routine "through the inspector's eyes"; deficiencies found are reported to the Chief Officer and rectified.

Housekeeping; tek başına bir tutuklama (.en: Although housekeeping alone is not a reason for detention, a poor general impression puts the inspector into "look deeper" mode and opens the way to other findings. Good housekeeping, on the other hand, sets a positive tone for the inspection.

Reis, haftalık güverte tur kayıtlarını (.en: The Bosun keeps records of the weekly deck rounds; housekeeping deficiencies found are documented together with the measures taken and photographs showing completion. Under ISM, these records are evidence of "continuous improvement" and show the discipline of the ship's management during inspections.

Reis, güverteyi sorumluluk bölgelerine a.en: The Bosun divides the deck into areas of responsibility and makes each deckhand responsible for keeping a particular area in order ("zone ownership"). This solves the problem of untidiness being "everybody's job, so nobody's job". A sense of ownership is the foundation of lasting order.

Housekeeping; toolbox meeting'lerin sabi.en: Housekeeping is a standing agenda item at toolbox meetings. The Bosun praises good examples and treats deficiencies as system issues, not personal ones. When a deckhand reports a hazard (e.g. a loose railing), the report must be welcomed; a reporting culture is the guarantee of order and safety.

Güverte housekeeping; gösteriş için deği.en: Deck housekeeping is done for life, not for show. A tidy deck means fewer accidents, faster emergency response, cleaner inspections and a more motivated team. The Bosun is both the architect and the guardian of this order; a good Bosun's ship is ready at any moment to receive even an inspector who arrives without notice.

Reis, yük operasyonu öncesi Birinci Zabi.en: Before a cargo operation, the Bosun receives instructions from the Chief Officer: the loading/discharging sequence, which hold/hatch is to be opened and when, the lashing plan, the required level of hold preparation and the safety restrictions. The Bosun passes these instructions to the team at a toolbox meeting and keeps radio contact with the duty officer throughout the operation.

Sahada bir sapma görülürse (ekipman arız.en: If a deviation is seen on deck (equipment failure, inadequate lashing, unexpected water ingress, stevedore error), the Bosun informs the Chief Officer immediately. The Bosun is the eyes and ears on deck; if the reporting chain breaks, the safety of the operation is weakened.

Operasyon başlamadan Reis; PPE kontrolü.en: Before the operation starts, the Bosun reviews PPE (hard hat, safety shoes, gloves, high-visibility vest), lighting, escape routes, the working order of equipment and the points where the crew and stevedores interact. In cargo operations, coordination between the crew and shore workers (stevedores) is a significant factor in accidents.

Folding (katlanır), side-rolling (yana k.en: Folding, side-rolling, piggy-back and pontoon type hatch covers each require a different operating discipline. Before opening/closing, the Bosun confirms that the cleats have been released, the drainage channels are clean, there are no obstructions on the rails and the hydraulic system is ready.

Hatch cover operasyonu sırasında ezilme.en: The risk of crushing and falling during hatch cover operations is high. No crew member may be between a moving cover and the fixed structure; a "no-go zone" must be clearly defined and supervised. Nobody stays under or in the path of a cover while it is moving.

Hatch cover'ın weathertight (su geçirmez.en: A weathertight hatch cover protects the cargo in the hold from seawater. The Bosun checks the condition of the rubber gaskets, compression bars, drainage channels and non-return valves. Water entering a loaded hold is critical, as it damages the cargo and causes stability/strength problems for the ship.

Kapama sonrası compression mark (rubber'.en: After closing, the compression mark (the even impression of the rubber) is checked; uneven compression indicates a gasket or bar adjustment problem. Cleating is done correctly and tightly; a loose cleat at sea means cover damage and water ingress in bad weather.

Her gemi, klas onaylı Cargo Securing Man.en: Every ship carries a class-approved Cargo Securing Manual (CSM). This manual contains the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) values of the lashing equipment and the approved lashing patterns and methods. The Bosun ensures that the lashing applied on deck complies with this manual; "improvised" lashing causes accidents and cargo loss.

Twist lock, lashing rod, turnbuckle, web.en: Twist locks, lashing rods, turnbuckles, web/chain lashings, dunnage and shoring are selected according to the type of cargo and applied with the correct torque/tension. The Bosun checks lashing tightness and corrects slack lashings immediately.

Lashing işi, sırt-bel yaralanmaları, par.en: Lashing work carries a risk of back injuries, crushed fingers and falls from height. The Bosun supervises correct lifting technique, the use of harnesses on lashing bridges, teamwork when carrying heavy lashing rods and the use of the right hand tools. Fall protection is mandatory when working on a lashing cage/platform.

Sefer boyunca lashing rutin olarak kontr.en: Lashings are checked routinely throughout the voyage; a "lashing inspection" is carried out especially before and after bad weather. Slack lashings are retightened. The Bosun keeps records of these checks and reports to the Chief Officer.

Dökme yük gemilerinde hold hazırlığı; bi.en: On bulk carriers, hold preparation is graded according to the next cargo and the charter terms: load-ready (swept), shovel-clean, grain-clean, hospital-clean. The Bosun obtains the required level from the Chief Officer and directs the team accordingly.

Hold temizliği; süpürme, deniz suyu yıka.en: Hold cleaning includes sweeping, seawater washing, freshwater rinsing, drying, deodorizing, paint touch-up and cleaning of the bilge wells. Residues of the previous cargo (taint) can contaminate the next cargo; therefore, the cleaning standard is strict.

Cargo hold, bir enclosed space'tir. Reis.en: A cargo hold is an enclosed space. Before anyone enters a hold, the Bosun ensures that the requirements for an enclosed space entry permit, atmosphere testing (O2, LEL, H2S, CO), ventilation and a standby person are met. The hold ladder, lighting and escape route are checked.

Yıkama suyu ve kimyasal kullanımı, kayma.en: The use of washing water and chemicals creates slipping and breathing hazards; suitable PPE and ventilation are essential. After washing, the used water is discharged in compliance with MARPOL rules (especially if it contains cargo residues), in coordination with the Chief Officer.

Reis ve güverte ekibi, ballast/freshwate.en: The Bosun and the deck team assist with ballast/fresh water/void space soundings and hold bilge measurements. It is important that the sounding pipe heads are clean and open, that the correct sounding tape is used and that the readings are recorded correctly. A wrong sounding corrupts the stability and strength calculations.

Hold bilge sounding'i, hold içine su gir.en: Hold bilge soundings give early warning of water entering the hold. If regular bilge soundings during operations and on passage show an increase, the Chief Officer and the bridge are warned immediately; this is the early alarm for a hatch seal problem or a hull leak.

Bilge well'ler temiz tutulur; tıkalı str.en: Bilge wells are kept clean; a blocked strum box or bilge suction prevents water from being pumped out of the hold. The Bosun checks the condition of the bilge well rose boxes and non-return valves. On bulk carriers, a bilge well blocked with cargo residue makes sounding and drainage impossible; this is critical for hold safety.

Güverte üzeri yük (container, boru, proj.en: Cargo on deck (containers, pipes, project cargo, timber) is directly exposed to sea conditions. On deck, the Bosun checks that the lashing pattern is correct, the dunnage is sufficient and the cargo distribution is in line with the plan. For special cargoes such as timber deck cargo, the requirements of the TDC Code are applied.

On-deck reefer container'ların plug bağl.en: The plug connections, air circulation and access routes of on-deck reefer containers are checked. Deck cargo must not obstruct escape routes or access to equipment; this is both a safety issue and an inspection issue.

Reis, hava elverdiğinde ve güvenliyse gü.en: When the weather permits and it is safe to do so, the Bosun periodically checks the lashings of the deck cargo. Going out on deck in bad weather is dangerous; therefore, the checks are made within a weather window, under supervision and with harnesses. Slackened lashings or shifted cargo are reported immediately.

Yük operasyonunda sahil işçileri (steved.en: During cargo operations, shore workers (stevedores) work on deck. The Bosun watches stevedore movements, manages overlaps between crew and stevedore working areas and monitors compliance with safety rules. Differences in language and practice can create a risk of accidents; clear marking and supervision are important.

Stevedore kaynaklı hasar (hatch cover, k.en: Damage caused by stevedores (hatch covers, railings, paint, equipment) is common. The Bosun identifies the damage at once, photographs it and reports it to the Chief Officer; if necessary, a stevedore damage report and a Letter of Protest are issued. Damage not documented in time later becomes the responsibility of the ship/company.

Yük operasyonunda bazı işler permit gere.en: In cargo operations, some jobs require a permit: enclosed space entry (hold), working aloft (upper tier of the lashing bridge), working overside and hot work. Through supervision on deck, the Bosun ensures that the team does not go beyond the scope of the permit, and monitors that the job-specific risk assessment is applied.

Yorgunluk yönetimi de operasyon güvenliğ.en: Fatigue management is also part of operational safety. During long port operations, MLC rest hours are observed; a tired crew increases the risk of accidents in lashing and hatch operations.

Her vardiya/operasyon öncesi Reis, ekibe.en: Before each watch/operation, the Bosun holds a toolbox meeting explaining the steps of the job, the risks, the equipment and the emergency procedure. Junior ratings are taught lashing technique, hatch operations and hold safety in practice; this training is recorded in the deck training book.

Yükleme sonrası Reis, ekiple birlikte tü.en: After loading, the Bosun and the team check the lashing pattern in all bays: are the twist locks locked, are the lashing rods tight, are the turnbuckles tightened? Before a voyage on which bad weather is expected, all lashings are checked twice and records are kept. In mid-voyage, the inspection is repeated during a weather window.

Coal boşaltması sonrası grain yükleme iç.en: After discharging coal, the hold is prepared for grain loading by sweeping, seawater washing, freshwater rinsing, drying and checking for odor/stains. The Bosun ensures that each hold is entered in line with enclosed space discipline and is ready for the NCB or surveyor inspection.

Yük operasyonunda Reis'in başarısı; plan.en: In cargo operations, the Bosun's success comes from carrying out the plan on deck completely, safely and on time. The weathertightness of the hatches, the soundness of the lashings and the correct preparation of the holds determine the safety of the cargo, the crew and the ship. A good Bosun never misses even a single slack lashing, because what is left loose at sea is what is lost in bad weather.

Bosun's store, geminin baş tarafında (ge.en: The Bosun's store is a closed compartment in the forward part of the ship (usually under the forecastle) where rope, wire, paint, chemicals, hand tools, securing gear and small spare parts are stored. For the Bosun, this store is the logistical heart that sets the pace of daily work: if the right material is not at hand at the right time, planned maintenance stops and work orders fall behind.

Store'un bir diğer kritik boyutu emniyet.en: Another critical aspect of the store is safety. Paints and solvents are flammable, some chemicals give off harmful vapors, and heavy gear (metal shackles, steel wire reels) can shift with the ship's motion and cause injury. The store is therefore not just a "storeroom" but also a controlled hazardous area.

Endüstriyel 5S yaklaşımı (Seiri-ayıkla,.en: The industrial 5S approach (Seiri – sort, Seiton – set in order, Seiso – clean, Seiketsu – standardize, Shitsuke – sustain) applies directly to the ship's store. The Bosun sorts out unused/expired material, places the rest on labeled shelves, keeps the floor and ventilation clean, sets a labeling standard and keeps it going through watch changes.

Deniz hareketine karşı her ağır kalem la.en: Every heavy item is secured against the ship's motion with lashings or shelf barriers. Wire reels that could roll are chocked, and paint tins are boxed to stop them toppling over. No heavy object is left loose in the store; it is a risk of both injury and damage.

Modern gemilerde mooring rope olarak HMP.en: On modern ships, HMPE (Dyneema), polyester, polyamide (nylon) and mixed ropes are used as mooring rope. Each rope has a Line Design Break Force (LDBF) and a certificate; under OCIMF MEG4, ropes are entered in the inventory with their type, diameter, length, date of manufacture and MBL. The Bosun tracks the ropes in use and the spare ropes in the store separately.

Yeni halat tesliminde sertifika (test ce.en: When a new rope is delivered, its test certificate is checked and filed. Rope reels are kept in the store in a dry area, out of sunlight, away from heat sources and out of contact with chemicals; UV and contact with solvents quickly reduce the strength of synthetic rope.

Reis, store'daki yedek halatları \"first.en: The Bosun rotates the spare ropes in the store on a "first in, first out" (FIFO) basis; synthetic rope that sits on a shelf for years ages even without use. The date of manufacture of the spares is kept visible on the label. When a mooring line reaches its retirement criteria (outer fiber damage exceeds the company threshold, or core damage is seen), a new one is taken from the store, and the old line is tagged and either downgraded for use as a utility rope or put on the disposal list.

Halat kesip iş halatı (heaving line, gan.en: Cutting rope to make utility lines (heaving lines, gantlines, lashings) is also part of store management. The Bosun does not waste leftover pieces; by heat-sealing or whipping the ends, the Bosun turns them into useful short lengths of rope.

Cargo wire, mooring wire ve crane wire i.en: For cargo wires, mooring wires and crane wires, the store holds spare wire reels, OEM wire lubricant, wire clips, thimbles and sockets. The Bosun protects the wire reels from moisture; rusted wire loses its strength and flexibility. Spare wire certificates are kept in the same file as the rope certificates.

Tel greasing için kullanılan yağ ve tine.en: Consumables such as the lubricant and thinner used for wire greasing are classed as hazardous substances; they are kept in the paint/solvent section, in a ventilated and labeled area.

Shackle (kilit), turnbuckle (liftin), pa.en: Cargo securing gear such as shackles, turnbuckles, pad eyes, chains, lashing bars, twist locks, bottle screws and hooks is stamped with its SWL (Safe Working Load). The Bosun keeps these items in separate boxes according to SWL and size; a mixed box of shackles leads to a part with the wrong SWL being selected during maneuvering, and to accidents.

Her bağlama teçhizatı periyodik görsel k.en: All securing gear undergoes periodic visual inspection: deformation, cracks, excessive corrosion, damaged threads. A damaged item is removed from the inventory immediately and placed in the "out of service" box, so that it cannot come back into circulation.

Chipping hammer, needle scaler, angle gr.en: Chipping hammers, needle scalers, angle grinders, disc sanders, hand scrapers, wire brushes, paint brushes, rollers and airless spray guns are part of the store inventory. The Bosun tracks the number and condition of these tools and their spare consumables (grinding discs, scaler needles, brushes). Electric tools undergo periodic electrical safety checks (megger/insulation test); the hoses and connections of pneumatic tools are checked.

Boya, tiner, solvent ve epoxy sertleştir.en: Paints, thinners, solvents and epoxy hardeners are flammable and are usually kept in a separate paint locker with ventilation and a fire-extinguishing system. The Bosun enforces the ban on smoking/naked flames in this space and checks that the ventilation works and that spillage precautions are in place. Opened paint tins are closed tightly; a mix whose pot life has expired is disposed of, treated not as waste but as a safety risk.

Boya stoğu batch number, üretim/son kull.en: Paint stock is recorded by batch number, production/expiry date and system (primer/intermediate/topcoat). When a painting program is being planned, the Bosun calculates from the store stock how many liters are needed to reach the target DFT; if there is a shortfall, the Bosun raises a requisition in time.

Her kimyasalın Güvenlik Bilgi Formu (MSD.en: The Safety Data Sheet (MSDS/SDS) for every chemical must be accessible on board. The Bosun ensures that the labels of the chemicals in the store are legible and undamaged; unlabeled containers are not accepted. Incompatible substances, such as acids and alkalis, or oxidizers and flammables, are kept apart.

Paket halinde tehlikeli madde (IMDG kaps.en: The difference between dangerous goods in packaged form (within the scope of IMDG) and deck consumable chemicals is important; however, the storage logic is the same: segregation, labeling, ventilation and spill control. Waste chemicals and empty paint tins are collected separately in accordance with MARPOL Annex V.

Reis her ana kalem için bir asgari stok.en: For each main item, the Bosun sets a minimum stock (min) and maximum stock (max) threshold. When stock approaches the min threshold, a requisition is triggered; the max prevents unnecessary overstocking and clogging of the store. A stock-take is usually done at the end of each month and at the start/end of the voyage; the results are reported to the Chief Officer.

Pek çok gemide envanter, gemi yönetim ya.en: On many ships, the inventory is kept in the ship management software (PMS/inventory module). The Bosun keeps the physical count reconciled with the digital record; a difference between the record and the shelf points to "unrecorded consumption", theft or a recording error, and is investigated.

Malzeme israfı, hem maliyet hem de denet.en: Waste of materials is a problem in terms of both cost and inspections. The most common sources of waste are: paint mixed incorrectly and thrown away, epoxy left to dry in the open, cutting unnecessarily long lengths of rope, lost hand tools and undisciplined drawing of consumables. The Bosun records the issue of materials, so that "who took how much" is known.

İsrafın önlenmesi cimrilik değil, doğru.en: Preventing waste is not stinginess but the discipline of correct use.
