All have an expiry date printed on them (usually manufacture + 3-4 years); expired pyrotechnics cannot be used and produce a PSC finding directly.

Safety Officer, tüm pyrotechnics'in expi.en: The Safety Officer keeps an expiry list of all pyrotechnics and obtains new stock before they expire. Expired pyrotechnics are not thrown away carelessly; they are disposed of properly (port facility or authorized disposal). These items are stored in easily accessible watertight boxes, protected from moisture.

LSA ekipmanının \"yerinde olması\" yetme.en: It is not enough for LSA equipment to be "in place"; in a real emergency it must be freely accessible and ready for use. The embarkation deck is kept clean, the area in front of the lifeboat is kept clear and no material is stowed in the davit area. The Safety Officer checks this access during routine safety rounds.

Tüm LSA istasyonları IMO Res. A.760(18).en: All LSA stations are marked with IMO Res. A.760(18) symbols; the muster station, lifejacket lockers, embarkation points and liferaft positions are shown by illuminated signs. Emergency lighting and photoluminescent escape markings must be in working order.

Operasyonel hazırlık; ekipmanın hem çalı.en: Operational readiness means that the equipment both works and can be used by the personnel. The Safety Officer periodically tests the integrated operation of the davit motor, winch brake, limit switches, embarkation ladder, emergency lighting and general alarm. Whether a lifeboat can be launched depends not only on its engine running but on the whole davit-brake-falls chain.

PSC ve flag/class survey'de LSA denetimi.en: In PSC and flag/class surveys, LSA inspection stands on three legs: the physical condition of the equipment, the consistency of the records and the crew's competence in using it. The inspector often picks out an item (e.g. an immersion suit), asks for its expiry/test date and then compares it with the record in the logbook.

En sık deficiency'ler: expired pyrotechn.en: The most frequent deficiencies are: expired pyrotechnics, overdue liferaft service, expired/missing HRUs, painted lashings, lifeboat engines that do not work, incomplete lifeboat inventory and inconsistencies between "records and physical condition". By tracking these items proactively, the Safety Officer comes through inspections without findings.

Safety Officer'ın LSA yönetimindeki başa.en: The Safety Officer's success in LSA management remains invisible as long as no abandon ship situation occurs; but in a real abandonment, the lives of the crew depend on exactly this disciplined, recorded and date-tracked routine. Saying "the equipment is in place" is only the beginning; being able to say "it works, it is accessible, it is valid and it is documented" means the task is complete.

Safety Officer, geminin fire control pla.en: The Safety Officer must know the ship's fire control plan by heart (under SOLAS II-2/15.2.4, it is kept on the bridge, at the entrances to the engine room and the bottle room + in an enclosure outside) and must know the location of every fire station, fixed system, detection zone, fire damper and ventilation stop. The FFE inventory is verified by comparing it with the Record of Equipment (Form E).

Sistem dört katmandan oluşur: passive pr.en: The system consists of four layers: passive protection (A/B class divisions, fire doors), detection (smoke/heat/flame detectors), containment (fire dampers, watertight/fire doors, ventilation shutdown) and extinction (portable + fixed systems). The Safety Officer monitors the readiness of each layer.

Her FFE kalemi PMS'te bir job ile izleni.en: Each FFE item is tracked in the PMS with a job: monthly extinguisher checks, quarterly hose/nozzle checks, annual SCBA service, five-yearly extinguisher hydro-test and so on. All checks, maintenance and refills are recorded with the date + the person responsible + the findings. Maintenance without a record is considered "not done" in an inspection.

Safety Officer, her tüpün dolu (tartı/ma.en: The Safety Officer checks that each extinguisher is full (weighing/pressure gauge), sealed (safety pin + tamper seal), accessible and of the correct class, and that its expiry/service date is valid. The extinguisher bracket must be sound, and the content pressure must be in the green band.

Boşalan veya kullanılan her tüp derhal r.en: Every extinguisher that has been discharged or used is refilled immediately, and a spare extinguisher is hung at the station in the meantime. CO2 and dry powder extinguishers are weighed annually; a weight loss of more than 10% requires refilling. The shell is subject to a hydrostatic test every 5–10 years according to the manufacturer's/flag requirements. All work is documented with date-stamped labels and records.

Emergency fire pump, ana pompadan bağıms.en: The emergency fire pump is located in a space separate from the main pump and runs on a separate power source; a weekly/monthly running test is carried out and the pressure is verified. The international shore connection (water connection from ship to ship/shore) is kept accessible near the bridge.

Safety Officer, periyodik olarak en uzak.en: The Safety Officer periodically verifies that the fire main pressure is sufficient by taking jets simultaneously from the two most remote hydrants. The emergency fire pump is isolated and tested separately. These tests are recorded in the logbook with the pressure value and date.

SCBA, fireman's outfit'in parçasıdır; ya.en: SCBA is part of the fireman's outfit; it allows the fire team to work in smoky/toxic atmospheres. The Safety Officer checks the cylinder pressure (usually ~300 bar when full), the low-pressure whistle (~50-55 bar), mask tightness, demand valve function and the condition of the harness. The cylinder is refilled after every use.

SCBA tüpleri belirli aralıklarla hydrost.en: SCBA cylinders are subject to hydrostatic testing at set intervals (composite ~5 years, steel ~10 years — determined by the manufacturer/flag). There must be at least two spare charged cylinders or a compressor on board. The mask and regulator are sent to an authorized service provider annually.

EEBD, yangın/duman durumunda kaçış için.en: An EEBD is a single-use escape device that provides ~10-15 minutes of air for escape in a fire/smoke situation; unlike an SCBA, it is not used for fire-fighting. EEBDs are located on the accommodation and engine room escape routes, in the numbers marked on the fire control plan. SOLAS II-2/13 sets the minimum numbers.

Safety Officer; her EEBD'nin mühürünün (.en: The Safety Officer checks that the seal of each EEBD is intact, the pressure gauge is in the green band, the expiry date is valid and the device is visible/accessible on the escape route. An EEBD with a broken seal is regarded as tested and is sent for servicing.

Fireman's outfit; alev geçirmez koruyucu.en: The fireman's outfit consists of flame-resistant protective clothing, boots/gloves, a helmet, a safety lamp (at least 3 hours), a fire axe and an SCBA. Depending on the type of ship, at least two sets are carried. The Safety Officer checks each set for completeness, the condition of the lamp battery and the soundness of the clothing.

Yangına müdahale eden ekibin lifeline ve.en: The team responding to a fire must be equipped with a lifeline and fireproof lifeline, and supported by low-location lighting and communications (intrinsically safe portable VHF). A missing or damaged component makes the whole outfit unusable.

Ekipmanın çalışması yeterli değildir; ek.en: It is not enough for the equipment to work; the team must be able to use it quickly and correctly. The Safety Officer shows newly joined personnel SCBA donning, EEBD activation, laying out hoses and the fire alarm points, observes these skills during fire drills and turns any gaps into training.

Makine dairesi ve kargo mahalleri için f.en: Fixed CO2 (or foam/water-mist/aerosol) systems are provided for the engine room and cargo spaces. The Safety Officer checks the cylinder pressures, release manifold seals, the alarm-before-release system, the ventilation/fuel shut-off interlocks and the warnings at the bottle room entrance. Before CO2 is released, the sequence of clearing all personnel from the space + alarm + ventilation stop must always be followed.

Fixed CO2 sistemi MSC.1/Circ.1318'e göre.en: Under MSC.1/Circ.1318, the fixed CO2 system is subject to annual, two-yearly and ten-yearly maintenance: annual visual and alarm test, two-yearly hose/manifold check, ten-yearly cylinder hydro-test. These services are carried out and certified by an authorized company.

Smoke, heat ve flame dedektörleri zone b.en: Smoke, heat and flame detectors are monitored by zone; alarms and faults are shown on the bridge panel. The Safety Officer periodically tests selected detectors with test smoke/heat, and operates the manual call points (MCP) and the general alarm. Zones that are disabled (isolated) are entered in the logbook and followed up.

FFE, PSC'de en sık deficiency çıkan alan.en: FFE is one of the areas with the most frequent PSC deficiencies: expired/discharged extinguishers, an emergency fire pump that does not work, missing SCBA cylinders, broken EEBD seals, blocked fire stations and inconsistencies between "records and physical condition" are typical findings. By tracking these items proactively and keeping the records without gaps, the Safety Officer goes into inspections prepared.

Denetçi sıklıkla bir crew üyesine \"Show.en: The inspector often says to a crew member, "Show me how you start the emergency fire pump" or "Don this SCBA". FFE competence is therefore measured not only by the equipment but also by training; familiarization records must be ready.

Yangın ekipmanı, kullanılmadığı sürece g.en: Fire-fighting equipment is an insurance that remains invisible as long as it is not used; but in a real fire, the survival of the ship and the crew depends directly on this equipment working and on the team being able to use it. The Safety Officer's task is to keep this chain, from "being there" to "working and usable", intact every day.

Bir yangın söndürücüye veya can salına s.en: When a fire extinguisher or a liferaft has to be reached within seconds, an obstruction in front of it causes a fatal delay. A blocked escape route means being trapped. That is why safety equipment and routes must always be accessible, working and clear.

Üçüncü Zabit, rondlarında şunları arar:.en: On rounds, the Third Officer looks for: obstructed fire-hose cabinets/extinguishers, material on escape routes, a deteriorated lifebuoy light, liferaft lashings stuck with paint (release not free), a hydrant box seized with rust and a fire door wedged open.

Yangın kapıları, yangın ve dumanın yayıl.en: Fire doors must be closed (or self-closing) to prevent fire and smoke from spreading. Holding them open with a wedge completely defeats this protection. The Third Officer corrects this common violation firmly.

Üçüncü Zabit düzenli emniyet rondları ya.en: The Third Officer carries out regular safety rounds to catch housekeeping defects and corrects them, or has them corrected, immediately. For recurring problems, the Third Officer briefs the team; housekeeping is the continuous responsibility of the whole crew, not of one person.

Safety housekeeping, sadece denetim önce.en: Safety housekeeping is not a clean-up done before an inspection but a daily habit. The Third Officer spreads awareness of "putting things back in their place" and "not blocking the way" throughout the team. Lasting safety is the sum of these small, correct daily actions.

Housekeeping kusurları PSC'de sık çıkan.en: Housekeeping defects are frequent PSC findings and create an impression of the ship's general safety culture. A ship that is consistently in good order also inspires confidence during inspections. The Third Officer maintains this order every day.

Safety housekeeping, emniyetin en somut.en: Safety housekeeping is safety in its most concrete, everyday form: keeping the front of the equipment clear, the routes free and the doors in the right position. The Third Officer's constant rounds and "fix it immediately" discipline ensure that, in a real emergency, every second and every item of equipment can save lives.

Emniyet Komitesi, mürettebatın emniyet k.en: The Safety Committee is a platform where the crew talk openly about safety matters and share problems and suggestions. The aim is to turn safety into a culture that "everyone owns" rather than one "imposed by management". The Third Officer makes this meeting participatory and productive.

Üçüncü Zabit; gündem hazırlar (önceki ak.en: The Third Officer prepares the agenda (previous actions, new near-misses, drill evaluations, inspection findings, suggestions), determines the participants and runs the meeting. The meeting is conducted so that everyone can speak, with the focus on solutions rather than blame.

Toplantı tutanağı; kararlar, atanan aksi.en: The minutes of the meeting are recorded together with the decisions, the assigned actions and the persons responsible, and are forwarded to the DPA (Designated Person Ashore). This allows shore management to keep a finger on the pulse of safety on board and to give the necessary support.

Near-miss (ramak kala), zarara yol açmam.en: A near-miss is an event that did not cause harm but could have. Every near-miss is a forerunner of an accident that can be prevented in the future. According to the accident pyramid principle, behind a large number of reported near-misses lies a smaller number of serious accidents; by managing near-misses, serious accidents are prevented.

Near-miss kültürünün en büyük düşmanı ko.en: The greatest enemy of a near-miss culture is fear: the perception that "reporting is punished" kills reporting. The Third Officer stresses that reporting is a tool for learning, not for blame, and builds an environment focused on solutions, not punishment. Open reporting is the sign of a living safety culture.

Her near-miss veya bulgu için kök neden.en: For each near-miss or finding, the root cause is investigated and corrective and preventive actions are defined. Each action is assigned a responsible person and a deadline and is followed up until it is completed. The Third Officer prevents open actions from being forgotten and left unclosed.

Safety Committee ve near-miss yönetimi,.en: The Safety Committee and near-miss management only work when they are kept up continuously. By making sure that meetings are regular, minutes are true and actions get closed, the Third Officer keeps the safety culture alive; a committee that becomes a "formality" loses its value.

The Safety Committee and near-miss management are the pulse of the ship's safety culture. The open reporting, serious root-cause analysis and closed actions that the Third Officer keeps alive turn today's small warnings into tomorrow's prevented accidents.

Uyuşturucu veya alkol etkisindeki bir ki.en: A person under the influence of drugs or alcohol loses attention, judgment and reflexes and becomes a time bomb in terms of safety. This is why ships generally apply a zero-tolerance D&A policy. As the person who applies this policy in practice, the Third Officer protects safety.

Rastgele test programı, testlerin öncede.en: A random testing program requires tests to be carried out at unpredictable intervals and with impartial selection. Targeting particular people or a predictable schedule undermines the deterrent effect and the fairness of the program. The Third Officer handles these logistics impartially and keeps records.

Alkol genellikle breathalyzer ile, uyuşt.en: Alcohol is usually measured with a breathalyzer, and drugs with urine/saliva test kits. The Third Officer ensures that the test procedure is applied correctly and that the results are recorded.

Test kitleri ve breathalyzer'ın çalışır,.en: Test kits and the breathalyzer must be in working order, calibrated and within their expiry dates. An expired kit may give a false result. The Third Officer monitors the kit stock and expiry dates and replenishes any shortages.

Pozitif bir sonuç, gizlilikle ve doğruda.en: A positive result is reported confidentially and directly to the Master, and then to the company. The process is carried out in a way that protects the person's dignity and does not give rise to gossip. Under company policy, a positive result usually leads to removal from duty and further action.

Numune alımından sonuca kadar gözetim zi.en: The chain of custody is maintained from sample collection to result: who took the sample, how it was stored and who tested it are recorded. This ensures that the result remains valid against challenges, especially when it is positive. Disposal records are also kept.

Bazı liman devletleri (örn. USCG) veya t.en: Some port States (e.g. USCG) or terminals may request a D&A inspection. The Third Officer coordinates the process during these inspections and presents the records of the ship's program. A ready and well-organized program gets through these inspections without problems.

D&A test yönetimi, emniyetin en hassas a.en: D&A test management is one of the most sensitive but most necessary areas of safety; it requires impartial application, confidentiality and a sound chain of custody. The Third Officer's regular and fair program is a deterrent shield that prevents one person under the influence from endangering the whole ship.

Safety Officer, geminin SMS'i ve SOLAS g.en: Based on the ship's SMS and SOLAS requirements, the Safety Officer sets up a test matrix: which equipment, at what interval, by whom and in which record. Weekly tests are usually done together on a set day (e.g. every Monday); monthly tests are completed before the end of the month. The matrix is approved by the Master and followed up on the bridge.

Her test bir PMS job'ına bağlanır; yapıl.en: Each test is linked to a PMS job; when it is done, the job is closed by entering the date, the result and the person responsible. A skipped or delayed test appears as "overdue" in the system and goes onto the Safety Officer's follow-up list.

Test sonuçları logbook ve PMS'e işlenir;.en: Test results are entered in the logbook and the PMS; abnormal findings are also raised separately as defect reports. At the end of the month, the Safety Officer prepares a summary report (tests carried out, defects found, open actions) and submits it to the Master. This report serves as evidence for SMS internal audits and PSC.

Haftalık lifeboat ve launching appliance.en: In the weekly visual inspection of the lifeboat and launching appliance, the lifeboat and davit are inspected visually, and the condition of the falls, the presence of the release gear and hook connection, and the visual condition of the embarkation ladder and brake are checked. If a deficiency is noticed, it is recorded at once and, if necessary, a defect is raised.

Free-fall filikalarda haftalık kontrol,.en: For free-fall lifeboats, the weekly inspection includes the visual condition of the simulated launching equipment and of the free-fall system; the interval for an actual free-fall test is different. For a davit-launched liferaft, the davit and release system are also checked.

Motorun ileri/geri kavramaları (eğer güv.en: The ahead/astern engagement of the engine is tested separately (if it is safe, when the boat has been lowered into the water, not in the davit). The running time, observations and battery condition are entered in the logbook.

Haftalık general alarm testi, tüm gemide.en: The weekly general alarm test verifies that the alarm can be heard throughout the ship and that it works from the standby power source (battery). The crew are informed in advance, so that it is not mistaken for a real emergency. The PA (public address) system must work intelligibly on every deck and in every space; if dead spots are found, a defect is raised.

Safety Officer, alarm testini emergency.en: The Safety Officer also verifies the alarm test via the emergency switchboard; it is checked that the alarm is fed from the battery when the main power is cut. The test is recorded with the date and result.

Acil aydınlatma, ana güç kaybında belirl.en: Emergency lighting must work for a set period after loss of main power (usually 3-36 hours, depending on the space). In the weekly check, the emergency lighting is switched on to verify that the escape routes, muster stations, embarkation deck and engine room escape routes are adequately lit. The charge and visibility of the photoluminescent (low-location lighting) strips are checked.

Tüm yangın istasyonlarını her hafta test.en: It is not practical to test all fire stations every week; the Safety Officer sets up a rotation and tests a different group of hydrants/hoses/nozzles each week, so that all stations are covered within the month. The hose at the station being tested is pressurized and the jet/spray function of the nozzle is tried.

Emergency fire pump da haftalık/aylık ça.en: The emergency fire pump is also run weekly/monthly to verify that it can work independently of the main pump. The test pressure, flow observation and station numbers are recorded.

Test sırasında çıkan her kusur (sızdıran.en: Every defect found during the test (leaking gland, cracked coupling, blocked nozzle) is immediately turned into a defect report; if necessary, the station is marked "out of service" and a compensating measure is decided. After repair, it is retested and the record is updated.

Aylık olarak tüm portatif tüpler görsel.en: Every month, all portable extinguishers are inspected visually: is the pressure gauge in the green band, are the safety pin and tamper seal in place, is the shell free of corrosion, is the bracket sound, is it at the correct station? The annual weighing dates of CO2 and dry powder extinguishers are tracked separately.

Eksik veya geçersiz tüp anında yedekle d.en: A missing or invalid extinguisher is replaced with a spare at once; a discharged extinguisher is sent for refilling. All checks are recorded via the checklist and the PMS.

Aylık olarak SCBA tüp basıncı, low-press.en: Every month, the SCBA cylinder pressure, low-pressure whistle and mask tightness; the EEBD seal, pressure gauge and expiry; and the completeness of the fireman's outfit and the safety lamp battery are checked. Deficiencies found are raised as defects.

Safety Officer, aylık olarak tüm tarihli.en: Every month, the Safety Officer updates all dated items (pyrotechnics, EPIRB/SART batteries, HRUs, liferaft service, immersion suit seam test, SCBA hydro-test, lifejacket lights) in a single expiry table. For upcoming dates (e.g. 3 months in advance), a resupply/service request is raised, so that no item suddenly becomes invalid.

Inventory güncellemesi; kullanılan, boşa.en: The inventory update brings the count of used, emptied or replaced items up to date and adds missing items to the replenishment list. This list forms the basis for port call and service planning.

Haftalık ve aylık testler, emniyet siste.en: Weekly and monthly tests are the "pulse" of the safety system: when they are carried out regularly, the equipment is always ready, the records are continuous and inspections pass without problems. The Safety Officer's disciplined test schedule is the strongest guarantee against the surprise of "it didn't work" in a real emergency.

SOLAS III/8 ve III/37, muster list'in yo.en: SOLAS III/8 and III/37 require the muster list to be prepared before the voyage and posted in conspicuous places on board (bridge, engine control room, crew accommodation). The list clearly shows the details of the general alarm and abandon ship signals, the action each person is to take when the alarm sounds, the muster stations, the persons assigned to close watertight doors, fire doors and valves, and the persons responsible for preparing the survival craft and fire-fighting equipment.

Muster list, kaptanın yokluğunda kimin y.en: The muster list also defines who takes charge in the Master's absence and the persons responsible for using the LSA and radio equipment. The Safety Officer continuously checks that the list matches the persons actually on board, one for one; at a crew change the list must be updated immediately, otherwise in an emergency some people end up with "no duty" and others with "two duties".

Muster list (genel) ile bireysel station.en: The muster list (general) and the individual station card (a personal card posted on the cabin door) complement each other. The station card reminds each crew member of their muster station, their abandon ship duty, the equipment they are to carry and which survival craft they are to board. The Safety Officer checks that every cabin has an up-to-date station card.

Görev kartları kişiye özel ve dilden bağ.en: Duty cards are prepared for each individual and independent of language (supported by symbols); with a multinational crew, the IMO standard symbols (Res. A.760(18)) and the ship's working language are used. When a new crew member joins the ship, the station card is prepared at once and handed over during safety familiarization.

Abandon ship (gemiyi terk) senaryosunda.en: In an abandon ship scenario, the muster list assigns every duty individually: lifeboat commander (usually an officer), engine operator, painter/line handler, embarkation ladder and davit operator, the person bringing the portable VHF, the person collecting the EPIRB and SART, the person carrying extra blankets, water and rations, the stretcher party, and the person taking the head count. The Safety Officer makes sure that no link in this chain is left empty.

Kritik ekipmanın taşınması isim isim ata.en: Carrying critical equipment is assigned by name: the person who will take the EPIRB and SART from their brackets, the person who will bring the portable GMDSS VHFs, and the person who will bring extra pyrotechnics, water and rations are known in advance. In a real abandonment, the answer to "Who took the EPIRB?" must already have been given.

Fire senaryosunda muster list; fire part.en: In a fire scenario, the muster list defines the fire party leader (usually the Chief Officer or the Safety Officer), the nozzle man, the hose handler, the boundary cooling team, the BA (breathing apparatus) team and the engine room boundary cooling coordinator. The bridge control team manages the ventilation, the fuel valves (quick-closing) and the emergency shut-offs.

Flooding/collision senaryosunda watertig.en: In a flooding/collision scenario, duties are assigned for closing watertight doors, monitoring draft and list, ballast/bilge pumping and preparing damage control materials (cement box, wooden plugs, shoring). The Safety Officer verifies that these duties are rehearsed in drills and that the related equipment is accessible.

MOB senaryosunda muster list; gözcü (kaz.en: In a MOB scenario, the muster list assigns the lookout (the person who keeps pointing at the person in the water), the person who releases the MOB marker/lifebuoy, the rescue boat crew (boat commander, engine operator, helmsman), the bridge maneuvering team and the person in charge of communications. Having the rescue boat crew designated and trained in advance is decisive in the golden minutes of the rescue.

General emergency alarm, en az yedi kısa.en: The general emergency alarm is a signal of seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle/bell; it must be audible throughout all accommodation and working spaces of the ship. This signal means "go to your muster station"; the order to abandon ship is given by the Master verbally (PA/radio) and has no separate automatic signal.

Safety Officer, general alarm sisteminin.en: The Safety Officer periodically tests that the general alarm system can be heard at a sufficient decibel level at all points (cabins, corridors, engine room, open deck). In high-noise areas such as the engine room, a visual (flashing) alarm must be provided in addition to the audible alarm.

Acil durumda emir zinciri ve haberleşme.en: In an emergency, the chain of command and the communication route are defined in advance: the bridge (Master/OOW) is the command center; communication with the muster stations and the fire party is by portable VHF or talkback. The Safety Officer checks that the portable VHFs are charged, set to the correct channels and sufficient in number (at least one per party).

Her muster station; aydınlatmalı, IMO se.en: Each muster station must be lit, marked with IMO symbols, freely accessible and large enough. On routine safety rounds, the Safety Officer checks that the escape routes to the muster station are not blocked or obstructed, that the emergency lighting and photoluminescent signs work, and that spare lifejackets are kept at the station.

Embarkation deck (binme güvertesi) özel.en: The embarkation deck is particularly important: the area in front of the lifeboats and liferafts must be clear, the davit area free of stores, the embarkation ladder ready and the deck safe against slipping. Using these areas as storage leads to fatal delays in a real emergency.

Readiness'ın insan ayağı, her mürettebat.en: The human side of readiness is that every crew member knows their own station and duty. The Safety Officer keeps this knowledge fresh by asking random people during drills and in daily contact: "Where is your muster station, what is your duty, which lifeboat do you board?" For the head count, an up-to-date crew list and passenger list (if any) are kept at each muster station.

Baş sayımı, terk kararında kimsenin geri.en: The head count is the critical step that ensures nobody is left behind when the decision to abandon is made. The responsible person ticks off everyone at their station on the list and reports anyone missing to the bridge immediately; search and rescue is directed on the basis of this information.

SOLAS, geminin bir çalışma dili (working.en: SOLAS requires the ship to establish a working language and the muster list and emergency instructions to be written in that language (and in additional languages where necessary). With a multinational crew, the Safety Officer confirms that the instructions are understood by everyone; where necessary, the language barrier is overcome with IMO standard symbols and illustrated instructions.

Familiarization sırasında dilden kaynakl.en: Misunderstandings caused by language are identified early during familiarization. It is not enough for a crew member to "appear to read" the instructions; real understanding is verified by the crew member physically showing their station.

Yolcu gemilerinde muster organizasyonu,.en: On passenger ships, the muster organization also covers directing the passengers: a muster drill is held at the start of the voyage, the passenger lifejacket donning points are marked and marshalling personnel are assigned. The Safety Officer checks that the passenger counting system and the plan for passengers with special needs are ready.

SOLAS III/19 gereği abandon ship ve fire.en: Under SOLAS III/19, abandon ship and fire drills are held at least once a month; each drill tests the muster list under real conditions. During the drill the Safety Officer times the muster, notes people who are left without a duty or are confused, identifies conflicting duties and revises the muster list based on these findings.

Drill, sadece \"yapıldı\" damgası için d.en: A drill is held not just to get a "done" stamp but to find the weak link in the organization. A department that musters late, equipment that cannot be found or a duty that nobody knows must be caught in a drill and corrected before a real emergency.

Her drill sonrası debrief'te ortaya çıka.en: Organizational errors revealed in the debrief after each drill are reflected in a revision of the muster list and station cards. The Safety Officer updates all copies at the same time (the list on the notice board, the cabin cards, the bridge and MCR copies); an old version left on display causes confusion.

PSC ve flag/class survey'de denetçi, mus.en: In PSC inspections and flag/class surveys, the inspector checks that the muster list is up to date, correctly posted and consistent with the crew on board, then goes out on deck and asks a random crew member: "Where is your muster station, what is your duty, how is the rescue boat engine operated?" If the paperwork is perfect but the people do not know, there will be a finding.

En sık deficiency'ler: güncel olmayan mu.en: The most common deficiencies: an out-of-date muster list (crew who have left the ship still on the list), conflicting or missing duty assignments, instructions not in the working language, crew without a station card, and inconsistencies between the drill records and the muster list. The Safety Officer checks these points proactively.

Muster list'in başarısı, hiçbir acil dur.en: The success of the muster list stays invisible as long as no emergency occurs. In a real abandonment, fire or MOB, however, the lives of the crew depend on exactly how this list works on deck: on everyone knowing their station and duty by reflex. The paper on the notice board is only the start; being able to say "everyone knows their station, the equipment is being carried, the head count is complete" means the job is done.

STCW Code A-VI/1, gemiye atanan herkesin.en: STCW Code A-VI/1 requires everyone assigned to a ship to complete basic safety familiarization before taking up duties: mustering in an emergency, recognizing the alarm signals, the location and donning of lifejackets, how to raise the alarm, and knowing the escape routes. This is the maritime world's "life-saving on day one" training.

ISM Code, şirketin personelin görevlerin.en: The ISM Code requires the Company to ensure that personnel are familiarized so that they can perform their duties safely. The Safety Officer carries out this responsibility on board: meets the new joiner, shows the critical information, confirms that it has been understood and keeps a signed record. The principle is not "I told them" but "I showed them and confirmed it".

Familiarization katmanlıdır: (1) safety/.en: Familiarization is layered: (1) safety/emergency familiarization (emergencies, LSA, escape), (2) company/SMS familiarization (procedures, reporting), (3) job/role familiarization (the person's own duties). The Safety Officer is primarily responsible for the safety part; the other parts are carried out by the Chief Officer, the Chief Engineer or the relevant supervisor.

Bridge ve engine room watchkeeper'lar iç.en: For bridge and engine room watchkeepers, duty-specific familiarization (equipment, alarms, procedures) is also carried out as required by STCW. The Safety Officer ensures that the safety part has been completed and recorded; without this record, a new crew member should not be put on watch.

Yeni mürettebata önce hayat kurtaran tem.en: A new crew member is first shown the life-saving basics: where their own lifejacket is (cabin + spare at the muster station), how to don it (practical demonstration), where the immersion suit is and how to don it, their muster station, their abandon ship duty and which survival craft they will board. This information is reinforced by the station card.

Alarm sinyalleri tanıtılır: general emer.en: The alarm signals are explained: the general emergency alarm (≥7 short + 1 long), the fire alarm and other signals, and the fact that abandon ship is ordered verbally by the Master. A new crew member must know by reflex where to go and what to do for each signal.

Yeni personele en yakın fire alarm call.en: New crew members are shown the nearest fire alarm call points (manual push buttons), the locations and types of portable extinguishers, and the locations of the fire hydrants and hoses. It must be clear how they raise the alarm on discovering a fire (call point, telephone, radio) and to whom they report.

Fire door ve watertight door kullanımı g.en: The use of fire doors and watertight doors is demonstrated: why they are kept closed, how they are opened and closed, and how the automatic closing system works in an emergency. It is stressed that holding a fire door open with a chock/wedge is prohibited and dangerous.

Yeni mürettebata kendi kamarasından ve ç.en: New crew members are shown the primary and alternative escape routes from their cabin and work area to the muster station by actually walking them. The photoluminescent escape signs, the emergency lighting, the EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) locations and the engine room escape trunk are pointed out.

EEBD'nin yangın/duman içinde sadece kaçı.en: It is explained that the EEBD is used in fire/smoke only for escape (not for firefighting), that its typical duration is 10-15 minutes, and how to don it. The Safety Officer repeats the demonstration until sure that the new crew member can find the escape route in darkness or smoke.

Yeni personele fire door (yangın bölmesi.en: New crew members are taught the difference between a fire door (fire division) and a watertight door (watertight subdivision), the conditions in which they are kept closed and the emergency closing mechanism. They are shown that power-operated watertight doors can be closed remotely from the bridge and that local controls are also provided.

Door'ların yanındaki uyarı levhaları, ka.en: The warning signs next to the doors, the risk of trapping fingers or limbs while a door is closing, and the correct way to pass through are taught. It is stressed that these doors are critical barriers protecting the integrity of the ship (fire/flooding containment).

Familiarization, kapıların neden önemli.en: Familiarization makes clear why the doors matter: a closed fire door delays the spread of a fire for minutes, and a closed watertight door can limit flooding to one compartment. When new crew members understand that these barriers protect the ship and themselves, they internalize compliance with the rules.

Yeni personele kim kime rapor verir, aci.en: New crew members are told clearly who reports to whom, whom to notify in an emergency and what to do when they see a hazardous situation. Typical chain: seaman → bosun/officer → relevant supervisor → Master. The right to report directly to the bridge (OOW) in an emergency is always stressed.

Near-miss ve unsafe condition raporlaman.en: The "just culture" approach, in which reporting near misses and unsafe conditions is not punished but encouraged, is passed on from the very beginning. New crew members knowing that they can report without fear is the foundation for keeping the safety culture on board alive.

Familiarization, geminin temel emniyet k.en: Familiarization also covers the ship's basic safety rules: enclosed space entry permit, hot work permit, working aloft/overside, lockout-tagout (LOTO) and PPE requirements. New crew members learn that starting such work without these permits is prohibited.

Her familiarization, şirket SMS'inde tan.en: Each familiarization is conducted using a checklist defined in the company SMS; each item is ticked off when it has been shown, and at the end both the new crew member and the person giving the familiarization (Safety Officer) sign. The signature is a statement that "it was shown and I understood"; in an ISM audit, this document is evidence of safe operation.

Checklist, gemiye katılım tarihiyle birl.en: The checklist is kept, together with the date of joining, in the personnel file and the SMS records. The date must show that the person received familiarization before taking up duties or within 24 hours; late or incomplete records generate a PSC/ISM finding.

SOLAS III/19.3.2 gereği, mürettebatın %2.en: Under SOLAS III/19.3.2, if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, a drill is held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. The Safety Officer makes sure that new crew members take an active role in their first drill; the knowledge taught in familiarization is reinforced by rehearsing a real scenario.

PSC ve ISM denetiminde denetçi, familiar.en: In PSC and ISM inspections, the inspector asks for the familiarization records and then goes out on deck, asking a new crew member: "Where is your muster station, where is your lifejacket, where is the fire alarm button?" If the records are complete but the person does not know, it is clear that familiarization was done "on paper" and a finding is raised.

En sık deficiency'ler: imzasız/eksik fam.en: The most common deficiencies: unsigned or incomplete familiarization checklists, late familiarization, inconsistency with the drill records, and new crew members without basic safety knowledge. While making the record, the Safety Officer also ensures that real learning takes place on board.

Safety familiarization, gemiye yeni katı.en: Safety familiarization is an investment made in the first few hours after a person joins the ship, but its effect lasts throughout the voyage. A well-conducted familiarization turns a person who "does not know the ship" into someone who "knows what to do" in a real emergency. Signing the record is the start; the job is done when the new crew member can don their lifejacket, walk to their station and recognize the alarm.

SOLAS III/19, her mürettebat üyesinin ay.en: SOLAS III/19 requires every crew member to take part in at least one abandon ship drill and one fire drill every month. If more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, an abandon ship drill and a fire drill must be held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. On ships with a high crew turnover, this rule requires the Safety Officer to build the drill plan around the voyage schedule.

Aylık zorunlu abandon ship ve fire drill.en: In addition to the mandatory monthly abandon ship and fire drills, enclosed space entry & rescue drills (at least once every 2 months, SOLAS III/19.3.3), man overboard (MOB), collision/grounding, oil spill (SOPEP), steering gear failure, blackout, security (ISPS) and medical emergency drills are also held periodically as required by the SMS. The Safety Officer tracks the schedule of all these drills in a single matrix.

Tanker, gas carrier ve yolcu gemilerinde.en: On tankers, gas carriers and passenger ships, additional drills apply (cargo emergency, enclosed space, mass rescue). The Safety Officer takes the mandatory drills specific to the ship type from the SMS and the additional flag requirements and enters them in the annual plan; a "due date" table is kept so that no interval is missed.

Muster list (toplanma cetveli), her müre.en: The muster list shows where each crew member is to go and which duty they will take on in an emergency. Under SOLAS III/8 it must be posted in conspicuous places on the bridge, in the engine control room and in the crew accommodation. The general alarm signal, the abandon ship signal, each person's duty and their substitute are shown on the muster list.

Muster list ve emergency instruction'lar.en: The muster list and emergency instructions must be in a working language understood by the crew; with multinational crews they are supported by IMO standard symbols (Res. A.760(18) / A.1116(30)). Every cabin must have lifejacket donning instructions and directions to the muster station.

İyi bir drill gerçekçi bir senaryoyla ba.en: A good drill starts with a realistic scenario: "fire in the engine room purifier room", "unconscious person in an enclosed space in No. 2 cargo hold", "MOB from the bridge wing". General, vague "there is a fire" scenarios teach nothing. The Safety Officer shares the scenario in advance with the Master and the Chief Officer and sets the intended learning outcome.

Senaryo, her ay farklı olmalıdır; aynı \.en: The scenario should be different every month; if the same "lower the lifeboat" routine is repeated, the team memorizes it but does not think. Targeting different skills in turn, such as boundary cooling, re-flash watch, enclosed space rescue and casualty handling, makes the team competent across the whole range of emergencies.

Drill öncesi kullanılacak ekipman çalışı.en: Before the drill, the equipment to be used must be in working order: full SCBA cylinders, fire pump pressure, fire hoses and nozzles, the rescue boat engine, the davit and the release gear. The Safety Officer plans which equipment will actually be operated during the drill; it is made clear whether the drill will be dry (tabletop) or physical.

Drill'in kendisi en büyük kaza riskidir..en: The drill itself is the biggest accident risk. In accordance with MSC.1/Circ.1206/Rev.1, in lifeboat launching drills the release gear is tested while no personnel are on the hook, and maintenance pins are managed strictly. Weather and sea state, crew fatigue and the maneuvering area are assessed before the drill; if the risk is high, the drill is postponed.

Drill genel alarm (yedi kısa + bir uzun).en: The drill starts with the general alarm (seven short + one long) or a signal suited to the scenario. The crew come to the muster station with lifejackets/immersion suits; each station leader takes a head count and reports to the bridge. Anyone missing must be identified at once; in a real emergency, the answer to "who is missing?" must be clear within minutes.

Safety Officer veya atanan gözlemci, mus.en: The Safety Officer or an appointed observer measures the muster time, how well equipment is donned and how the reporting chain works. Typical target: the whole crew mustered and the head count completed within the set time (usually a few minutes, depending on the ship).

Fire drill'de fire party SCBA donar, hos.en: In a fire drill, the fire party dons SCBA and runs out hoses, boundary cooling is set up, and the machinery stop/ventilation shut-down procedure is applied. In an abandon ship drill, the lifeboat/liferaft station is prepared, embarkation is explained and the engine is started. In an enclosed space drill, the permit to work, atmosphere testing, rescue and casualty handling are demonstrated.

Gözlemci, her adımda \"doğru prosedür iz.en: At every step, the observer notes whether the correct procedure was followed: was the SCBA pre-use check done, was the buddy system applied, was communication clear, was the equipment used correctly? These notes form the basis of the debrief and the record; simply saying "drill held" is not enough.

Drill bittiğinde mutlaka debrief yapılır.en: When the drill is over, a debrief is always held: what went well, what went badly, which equipment was missing or defective, which procedure was slow. A debrief is a learning session, not a blame session; the question is not "who made the mistake?" but "where is the system weak?". Every finding is tied to a concrete action.

Safety Officer, debrief'te ortaya çıkan.en: The Safety Officer turns equipment defects found in the debrief into work orders, procedural gaps into training/familiarization, and individual skill gaps into targeted coaching. The scenario of the next drill can target the weakest point of this drill.

Debrief'te belirlenen aksiyonlar bir tak.en: Actions identified in the debrief are entered in a follow-up list and tracked until they are closed. Clear assignments are made, such as "Rescue boat battery to be replaced — responsible: 2/E — date X". An action that has not been closed is carried over to the agenda of the next Safety Committee meeting.

Her drill official log book'a ve ayrıca.en: Every drill is entered in the official log book and also in a detailed drill record. The record includes the date, drill type, scenario, participants, equipment used, observations, deficiencies and corrective actions. Under SOLAS III/19.5, the dates and details of drills are recorded; if a drill is incomplete or shortened, the reason is also recorded.

Safety Officer'ın altın kuralı LSA bölüm.en: The Safety Officer's golden rule is the same as for LSA: what is not done is not recorded, and what is not recorded is considered not done. However, "filling in" records without holding a real drill (paper drill) is both an ISM violation and a deception that can be fatal in a real emergency. The record must reflect reality.

Drill kaydı ile mürettebatın gerçek bilg.en: The drill record and the crew's actual knowledge must be consistent. If the record shows a monthly enclosed space drill, a random crew member must be able to explain the permit to work and atmosphere testing. The Safety Officer maintains this consistency by actually holding the drills and ensuring participation by rotation.

Kayıtlar survey ve PSC için kritik delil.en: Records are critical evidence for surveys and PSC; however, the real aim is not to pass the inspection but to build a team that is ready for a real emergency. A well-kept drill record based on reality gets the ship through both the inspection and a real crisis.

PSC, drill kaydını okumaktan çok crew'ı.en: PSC tests the crew rather than just reading the drill record: "Where is your muster station? What is your duty in this fire? How do you start the rescue boat engine? How do you use the EEBD?" If the answers are fluent and correct, the drill regime is real; if they are hesitant or wrong, training is inadequate whatever the record says, and a deficiency is raised.

Safety Officer, denetim öncesi müretteba.en: Before an inspection, the Safety Officer holds short rehearsals with the crew; new joiners in particular are reminded of their muster station, lifejacket donning and their own emergency duties. This prevents the picture of "good records but unprepared people".

Drill'in başarısı, hiçbir gerçek acil ya.en: The success of drills stays invisible as long as no real emergency occurs. In a real fire or abandonment, however, the crew's reflexes depend on exactly this disciplined, realistic and recorded drill routine. Saying "the drill was held" is the start; being able to say "the team knows, the equipment works, the gaps are closed and the record reflects reality" means the job is done.

Emniyet ekipmanındaki bir kusur gizlendi.en: When a defect in safety equipment is concealed, the equipment will not work in a real emergency and the result can be fatal. The Third Officer knows that reporting a defect honestly is both a legal and an ethical obligation; hiding a fault "so that it is not seen in the inspection" is the most dangerous decision.

Üçüncü Zabit, rutin rondlarda emniyet ek.en: On routine rounds, the Third Officer picks up defects in safety equipment: an SCBA low-pressure whistle that does not work, a weak lifeboat battery, a cracked fire hose coupling, a broken EEBD seal, a leaking hydrant valve gland. Each one is opened as a defect.

Kusur, PMS/defect sisteminde açılır: eki.en: The defect is opened in the PMS/defect system: the equipment, a description of the defect, the date it was found and a risk assessment are recorded. If the equipment cannot be used safely, it is marked "out of service" and physically tagged so that nobody relies on it by mistake.

Bir emniyet ekipmanı devre dışıyken risk.en: While a piece of safety equipment is out of service, the risk is compensated for: standby equipment is brought into use, an additional watch or precaution is put in place, or operations are restricted. The Third Officer determines this compensating measure and informs the Master; a gap is unacceptable, especially in fire-fighting and life-saving equipment.

Açılan defect, bir iş emrine (work order.en: The defect that has been opened is linked to a work order and tracked until the repair is complete. When the work is finished, the work order is closed by recording the work done, the parts used and the test result. The Third Officer prevents open safety defects from piling up on the "overdue" list.

PSC/klas denetiminde, açık ve telafi ted.en: In a PSC/class inspection, an open defect with a compensating measure is received much better than a concealed fault. Transparent defect management shows that the ship's safety culture is healthy. The Third Officer keeps the defect and work order records ready for inspection.

Defect raporlama ve work order takibi, Ü.en: Defect reporting and work order tracking are how the Third Officer keeps safety equipment actually working, not just working "on paper". Honest reporting, compensating measures and disciplined follow-up ensure that the equipment works the first time in an emergency.

Gemi; klas sörveyleri, bayrak devleti de.en: The ship is subject to various inspections, such as class surveys, flag State inspections, PSC and vetting. Each examines LSA/FFE compliance to a different depth. The Third Officer ensures that, as far as safety equipment is concerned, the ship is always ready for inspection.

Denetçi tipik olarak: ekipmanın yerini b.en: The inspector typically expects you to know where the equipment is, to be able to operate it, to show the logbook/records and to know the expiry and service dates, and expects the crew to be trained. The Third Officer keeps these competences ready, both for themselves and for the team.

Bir kusur varsa, açık defect ve telafi t.en: If there is a defect, showing it as an open defect with a compensating measure is always better than hiding it. When an inspector finds a concealed fault, trust is completely shaken and the ship is examined more closely.

LSA/FFE sertifikaları, liferaft/lifeboat.en: LSA/FFE certificates, liferaft/lifeboat/fire extinguisher service reports, drill records and the maintenance log are kept ready for inspection. The Third Officer monitors validity periods and plans renewals; an expired service directly produces a finding.

Denetçi, rastgele bir mürettebata \"must.en: The inspector may ask a random crew member: "Where is your muster station, how do you use this equipment?" Through regular drills and familiarization, the Third Officer ensures that the team can answer these questions with confidence. Safety is the sum of individual competences.

Denetimde bulgu çıkarsa, düzeltici aksiy.en: If a finding is raised during the inspection, a corrective action plan is prepared and the finding is closed within the deadline. The Third Officer contributes to the follow-up of safety-related findings and supports a permanent solution that prevents the same finding from recurring.

Survey ve PSC hazırlığı, Üçüncü Zabit iç.en: For the Third Officer, survey and PSC preparation is not an "exam day" but the natural result of everyday safety discipline. Equipment that is always ready, up-to-date records and a trained crew turn the inspection from a threat into a confirmation of the ship's safety.

Süresi dolan bir işaret fişeği tutuşmaya.en: An expired distress flare may not ignite, a liferaft whose service is overdue may not inflate correctly, and a flat battery may give no signal. This is why tracking dates is about the equipment "being in working order" as much as "being there". The Third Officer treats this tracking as a priority.

Üçüncü Zabit; roket paraşüt fişeği, el m.en: The Third Officer tracks rocket parachute flares, hand flares, buoyant smoke signals (pyrotechnics), the HRU (Hydrostatic Release Unit), liferaft service dates, EPIRB/SART/portable radio batteries and immersion suit check/seam test dates. Each has a different validity period and service interval.

Yangın söndürücü servis/yeniden dolum, S.en: Fire extinguisher service/recharging, SCBA cylinder hydrostatic testing, fire hose/nozzle checks and fixed system (CO2/foam) service dates are also tracked. Pressure vessels such as SCBA cylinders are subject to a statutory test interval.

Tüm tarihler bir takvim/PMS sisteminde t.en: All dates are kept in a calendar/PMS system, and items coming due give an advance warning. The Third Officer identifies renewal/service needs before the port supply window; if a liferaft service or a flare replenishment is not planned at a suitable port, the date may expire at sea.

Süresi yaklaşan ekipman, uygun limanda y.en: Equipment approaching its expiry date is renewed at a suitable port or sent for service. The Third Officer reports missing or soon-to-expire items to the Chief Officer and the Master and prepares the requisition. Old pyrotechnics are also disposed of in accordance with the rules (usually ashore).

Tüm servis/yenileme işlemleri kayıt altı.en: All service and renewal work is recorded and the certificates are kept. These records are presented during inspections and prove that the equipment is kept up to date. The Third Officer ensures that the records are orderly and accessible.

Emniyet stok ve tarih takibi, \"küçük am.en: Tracking safety stock and dates is a typical example of "small but vital" work. The Third Officer's disciplined schedule and timely replenishment ensure that every liferaft, every flare and every battery works the first time in a real emergency.

Safety Officer, emniyet ekipmanını yönet.en: Because the Safety Officer is the person who manages the safety equipment, they are a natural on-scene leader in an emergency. According to the station bill, they take on roles such as leading the fire team and coordinating life-saving. This is a role that "directs the response", not one that "keeps records".

Yangında Safety Officer; ileri yangın ek.en: In a fire, the Safety Officer may lead the attack fire team (fire party), directs the team wearing SCBA and coordinates boundary cooling, that is, cooling the adjacent surfaces to prevent the fire from spreading to neighboring compartments. Team safety (air time, withdrawal signal) is the priority.

MOB durumunda Safety Officer, rescue boa.en: In a MOB situation, the Safety Officer may coordinate the preparation and launching of the rescue boat and directs the rescue team. A fast and organized response is critical because survival time in cold water is limited. MOB equipment (lifebuoy, light, smoke signal) is thrown overboard quickly.

Abandon ship'te Safety Officer; can fili.en: In abandon ship, the Safety Officer may coordinate boarding of the lifeboats/liferafts (embarkation), the crew head count and the transfer of distress equipment. Making sure that everyone has been counted, so that nobody is left behind, is the most critical part of this role.

Eksik bir sayım, geride kalmış bir müret.en: An incomplete head count means a crew member left behind. The Safety Officer verifies against the muster list that everyone is present; if anyone is missing, a search is organized. This verification is the most critical step of abandon ship.

Bu rollerin gerçek bir acilde işe yarama.en: These roles can only work in a real emergency through realistic and regular drills. The Safety Officer plans drills with a wide variety of scenarios and also rehearses their own role; drills held only on paper turn into panic when it really matters.

Safety Officer'ın acil durum rolü, emniy.en: The Safety Officer's emergency role is a natural extension of managing the safety equipment: being the person who uses that equipment and leads the team in a crisis. Clear awareness of roles, priority on team safety and realistic drills ensure that this critical duty saves lives in a real emergency.

Lookout görevi; çevredeki tüm gemilerin,.en: The lookout's duty is to watch for all ships, small craft, buoys, coastlines, ice/debris/floating objects, navigation lights and sound signals in the vicinity and to report them to the OOW at once. The AB does not make decisions; they report what they see, and the decision to maneuver belongs to the OOW. This separation is the basic discipline of the watch: the lookout "reports", the officer "interprets and maneuvers".

Helmsman (dümenci) görevinde AB, OOW vey.en: As helmsman, the AB keeps the ship on the required course by repeating back the course/helm orders given by the OOW or the pilot and carrying them out correctly. Even when the autopilot is engaged, the helmsman stands by so that a change-over to hand steering can be made immediately in narrow waters, traffic separation schemes and maneuvering situations.

Tek kişi aynı anda hem lookout hem helms.en: One person cannot be lookout and helmsman at the same time; when steering by hand, the person is focused on the helm and the compass, so a "proper look-out" cannot be kept. For this reason, a separate lookout is posted when hand steering is in use. STCW A-VIII/2 and many accident reports stress that the "sole lookout" arrangement is acceptable only in daylight, in good visibility and low traffic, and after the OOW has assessed all factors.

OOW; kısıtlı görüş (sis, yağmur, kar), g.en: The OOW calls for additional lookouts when factors such as restricted visibility (fog, rain, snow), darkness, heavy traffic, narrow channels/canals, navigation close to the coast, concentrations of fishing boats or fatigue arise. The AB is called to duty with orders such as "stand by the wheel" or "extra lookout on bridge wing".

STCW dinlenme saatleri (her 24 saatte mi.en: STCW rest hours (min. 10 hours in any 24-hour period, min. 77 hours in any 7-day period) directly affect lookout effectiveness; a tired lookout is a hazard. If the AB feels too tired to perform their duty, they are obliged to inform the OOW.

Etkili lookout, ufku sistematik tarar: b.en: An effective lookout scans the horizon systematically: starting from the bow, they check both sides and the stern at regular intervals. 360° awareness, not just looking ahead, is essential; overtaking ships in particular approach from astern. Scanning is done both with the naked eye and with binoculars.

Rapor formatı kerteriz (bearing) + cisim.en: The report format is bearing + object + range/status. The bearing is given as a "clock" bearing (one o'clock, dead ahead) or as "port/starboard ... degrees". Example reports: "Light dead ahead!", "Vessel two points on the starboard bow!", "Object red one-zero!" (port 10°). If a danger is detected, it is reported immediately, loudly and clearly.

Sabit kerteriz / azalan mesafe (constant.en: A constant bearing with decreasing range (CBDR) is the classic indicator of risk of collision. If, while watching a ship, the AB notices that the bearing is not changing, they must report it; the OOW confirms this information with a radar plot and decides on the maneuver.

Gece lookout'ta karanlığa adaptasyon (da.en: On a night lookout, dark adaptation takes 20-30 minutes; this is why bridge lighting is dimmed, white light is not used and red lighting is preferred. Even a phone/tablet screen or the glow of a cigarette spoils night vision. The AB picks out faint lights better by looking slightly to one side (off-center vision) rather than directly at the horizon, because the peripheral part of the eye is more sensitive in low light.

Fener tanıma lookout'un en kritik beceri.en: Recognizing lights is the lookout's most critical skill: green (starboard) and red (port) sidelights, white masthead/stern lights, the all-round white light of a ship at anchor, and the special light combinations for fishing, towing and restricted in ability to maneuver are defined in COLREG Part C. Although the AB does not have to know the meaning of every light by heart, they must describe what they see correctly and clearly (color, number, arrangement) and pass it on to the OOW.

Sis, yoğun yağmur veya kar gibi kısıtlı.en: In restricted visibility, such as fog, heavy rain or snow, a visual lookout is not enough and the aural lookout comes to the fore. Under COLREG Rule 35, the fog signals of other ships (prolonged blasts, short-short blasts, the bell/gong of a ship at anchor) are listened for. Listening in the open air on the bridge wing, away from engine/generator noise, is more effective.

Kısıtlı görüşte AB, radar/AIS değerlendi.en: In restricted visibility, the AB knows that radar/AIS assessment is the OOW's job, but keeps up their own aural and limited visual lookout. Every fog signal heard is reported with an estimated bearing ("fog signal, fine on the port bow").

Komut verildiğinde dümenci komutu birebi.en: When an order is given, the helmsman repeats it exactly (e.g., OOW: "Starboard ten" — Helmsman: "Starboard ten"), applies the helm and reports when the rudder reaches the ordered angle ("Ten of starboard wheel on"). When the ship is to be steadied on a course, the OOW gives the new course ("Steady on one-two-zero"); once the helmsman has the ship steady on that course by the compass, they confirm "Steady on one-two-zero". This discipline prevents misunderstandings caused by noise, accents or fatigue.

Açık denizde otomatik pilot rotayı tutar.en: On the open sea, the autopilot keeps the course; however, hand steering is engaged for traffic, maneuvering, narrow waters and system failures. The change-over is a procedure: the OOW says "hand steering", the helmsman switches the mode to manual, checks the compass and confirms "hand steering, on course one-two-zero". SOLAS V/24 requires a helmsman to be ready so that hand steering can be engaged immediately in areas where maneuvering is required.

Otomatik pilot devredeyken dümenci dümen.en: While the autopilot is engaged, the helmsman may leave the helm, but stays in the "stand by the wheel" position if the OOW so orders. In the event of a steering gear failure, an alarm sounds; the helmsman is immediately ready to change over to an alternative steering mode/emergency steering and alerts the OOW.

Dümenci hem gyro repeater hem manyetik p.en: The helmsman uses both the gyro repeater and the magnetic compass. The gyrocompass gives the true heading; the magnetic compass is critical as a backup (in case of gyro failure). The difference between the gyro and the magnetic compass is checked periodically; if the error increases, the OOW is informed. At the change of watch, the course and the status of the compasses are handed over.

Steering konsolundaki rate-of-turn göste.en: The rate-of-turn indicator on the steering console shows the ship's rate of turn (°/min); especially on large ships, the helmsman also monitors the turn with this instrument to prevent over-swinging. The rudder angle indicator confirms the rudder angle; agreement between the ordered angle and the angle on the indicator is monitored continuously.

AB, \"ben gördüm ama önemli değildir\" d.en: The AB does not filter reports by thinking "I've seen it but it's not important"; every object is reported, including small craft, sailing boats, unlit fishing boats and buoys. In many collisions, the lookout had seen a target but did not report it, assuming that "the officer must have seen it already".

Trafik Ayrım Düzenlerinde (TSS), kanalla.en: In Traffic Separation Schemes (TSS), canals and straits, the lookout workload increases: there are many targets, fast-developing situations and frequent helm orders. In these conditions, the OOW usually calls for hand steering; the helmsman concentrates on the orders while a separate lookout scans the surroundings. In this high-tempo environment, the AB must repeat back orders even more clearly and must not let their attention wander.

Vardiya değişiminde, görevi devralan AB.en: At the change of watch, the AB taking over comes to the bridge fit for duty (awake, with night vision adapted). The relieving helmsman takes over and confirms the present course, the steering mode (auto/hand), the compass status and the OOW's special instructions. The handover is not carried out while the ship is maneuvering or during a critical passage; it is postponed to a suitable moment.

Devralan lookout; mevcut trafik durumunu.en: The relieving lookout takes over the current traffic situation, the targets being watched, the weather/visibility conditions and points requiring special attention (e.g., "group of fishing boats on the starboard bow"). STCW A-VIII/2 provides that relieving personnel are not considered fully on duty until their eyes have fully adjusted to the light conditions.

Çok sayıda çarpışma ve karaya oturma rap.en: A common factor in many collision and grounding reports is "inadequate look-out": the OOW on a one-man watch being busy with radar/ECDIS/paperwork and not looking outside, night vision discipline breaking down, or the lookout not being called to duty. The AB's presence and effective reporting break this chain.

Yorgunluk (fatigue) lookout etkinliğini.en: Fatigue is the number one factor that reduces lookout effectiveness. Late at night and on long watches, the risk of micro-sleep increases. The AB must report fatigue or the risk of dozing off to the OOW and use strategies to stay alert, such as standing, moving around or stepping out into the fresh air.

Repeat-back yapılmaması, komut yönünün k.en: Not repeating back, confusing the direction of the order (port/starboard) and believing that the autopilot has been switched to manual (when it is in fact still in automatic mode) are classic helmsman errors. At every change-over, confirming by the rudder angle indicator and the ship's response that the mode really is correct saves lives.

Usta Gemici'nin köprüüstü vardiyasındaki.en: The AB's value on the bridge watch comes from disciplined lookout and error-free helmsmanship, which stay invisible "when nothing happens" but are the ship's first line of defense "when a target becomes a danger". A correctly reported bearing, a small helm action taken in time, dark adaptation preserved at night: each of these can prevent a collision. Lookout and helmsman duty may look routine, but it is the most basic safety-of-life duty in seafaring.

Standart mooring düzeninde her halatın g.en: In a standard mooring arrangement, each line has a different function. The head line and stern line bring the ship in to the berth and limit movement fore and aft; breast lines lead at right angles to the berth and stop the ship's side from moving off; spring lines hold the ship against longitudinal (fore-and-aft) movement. A typical ship sends out lines distributed forward and aft in a 3+2+1 or similar combination.

AB, manevra planında kendi istasyonunun.en: From the Bosun and the station officer, the AB learns which lines their own station (forward/aft) will send out, and in which order, according to the maneuvering plan. Sending a line in the wrong order (e.g., sending the spring late) can make the ship move out of position; this is why the AB waits for the order and never sends lines on their own initiative.

Halatlar bollard'a (rıhtım babası) \"eye.en: Lines are put over the shore bollard by the eye; if there are lines from more than one ship on the same bollard, the "dip the eye" technique is used: the eye of the ship arriving later is passed up through the eye of the earlier ship's line from below, so that each ship can let go its own line independently.

Mesafe ve durum köprüüstüne sürekli rapo.en: Distance and status are reported to the bridge continuously: "Two shackles to go", "All gone forward" (all lines forward have been let go), "Made fast forward" (the forward station is made fast). Without this feedback the bridge carries out the maneuver blind; clear and timely reporting by the AB is the eyes of the maneuver.

Gerilim altındaki bir halat veya tel kop.en: When a line or wire under tension parts, it releases its stored elastic energy by recoiling like a whip; the area swept by this recoil is called the snap-back zone. Synthetic lines (especially nylon) recoil far more dangerously because of their high elasticity; in less than a second, the parted end moves fast enough to tear a human body apart. This is why most mooring injuries are fatal or involve the loss of limbs.

Snap-back bölgesi sadece halatın doğrult.en: The snap-back zone is not only along the lead of the line: at every point where the line is bent around a bollard, fairlead or pedestal roller, the direction of recoil can change. MEG4 takes the approach that "the whole deck is a potential snap-back zone when lines are under tension"; the old "painted snap-back zone line" alone is not considered safe.

AB, halat alırken/verirken ayağını asla.en: When taking in or paying out a line, the AB never puts a foot inside a coil of line or on top of a line running underneath; if the line suddenly comes under tension, the foot is caught and the person is dragged. Hands are kept away from the turns on the bollard, the mouth of the fairlead and the winch drum; "nip points" are the main cause of lost fingers and hands.

Çalışma alanında daima açık bir kaçış yo.en: An open escape route is always planned in the work area; where to jump clear when the line comes under tension is known in advance. A crowded, slippery or obstructed deck makes escaping snap-back impossible; this is why the deck preparation described in 3.1 is critical.

İşe başlamadan toolbox talk / risk asses.en: Before starting work, a toolbox talk / risk assessment is held: which lines will go out in which order, the snap-back zones, wind/current conditions and the allocation of duties are discussed. The AB knows their own role and the "stop" signal clearly; if anything is unclear, they ask.

Mooring istasyonunda zorunlu PPE: baret,.en: Mandatory PPE at the mooring station: safety helmet, steel-toe safety shoes, mooring gloves (a type that gives grip but will not get caught in a roller), coveralls and, for night operations, a reflective vest. The choice of gloves is important; loose or torn gloves increase the risk of being caught by the drum.

Gece veya kötü görüş koşulunda istasyon.en: At night or in poor visibility, station lighting must be adequate but directed so that it does not spoil the view from the bridge. The AB keeps their radio and whistle at hand; hand signals can also be used in a noisy environment.

Brake (fren) ayarı kritiktir: MEG4'e gör.en: The brake setting is critical: according to MEG4, the winch brake is set to "render" (slip, relieving the tension) at a specified percentage of the line's MBL (Minimum Breaking Load), so that under excessive tension the brake slips before the line parts. The AB carries out the brake holding (rendering) test and applies the correct brake pressure on the Bosun's instructions.

AB, winch panelindeki mod (manuel/auto),.en: The AB knows the mode (manual/auto) on the winch panel, the selection between drum and warp end (warping head), and the emergency stop button. Work is not done on the warp end at the same time as a line is on the drum; mechanical confusion is dangerous.

Mooring halatı doğrudan rıhtıma uzanamay.en: Because the mooring line is too heavy to reach the berth directly, a light heaving line is thrown first; the weight at its end (monkey's fist) carries it ashore, and the mooring gang ashore hauls in this line to bring the eye of the main line onto the berth. The AB coils the heaving line neatly, takes half of it in the throwing hand, aims according to the target and the wind, and throws.

Monkey's fist içine asla metal/ağır cisi.en: Metal or heavy objects are never put inside the monkey's fist; this can seriously injure the person ashore. MEG4 and COSWP require the weight of a heaving line to be soft and of limited mass. Warning the people on the quay when throwing ("heads up — line coming over") is good practice.

AB, \"make fast\" komutunda halatı doğru.en: On the order "make fast", the AB makes the line fast at the correct tension; on the order "single up", before departure, the surplus lines are let go one by one to reduce them to the minimum. While letting go, the AB keeps checking which line is under tension; a line under tension is never cast off by hand: the tension is first taken off with the winch.

Yanaşma/kalkmada römorkörler gemiye iter.en: When berthing and unberthing, tugs push or pull the ship. When making fast a tug, the tug line sent by the tug with a messenger (light line) is usually taken on board and made fast on a suitable bollard or tug bitt, through a Panama lead. When taking the tug line, the AB learns from the Bosun which fairlead the line will pass through and which bollard it will be made fast on; a wrong lead chafes the line against the ship's structure and cuts it.

Tug operasyonu sırasında gemi ile römork.en: During tug operations, the line between the ship and the tug can come under sudden tension; this is also a source of snap-back. The AB keeps clear of the lead of the tug line and allows for the tug's pulling direction ("ahead/astern"). Coordination between the bridge and the tug is carried out by the pilot/Master; on deck, the AB is responsible for making fast and letting go safely.

Manevra bitince tug çözülür. Gergin tug.en: When the maneuver is completed, the tug is let go. A tug line under tension is never cast off by hand; the bridge passes "ease the line" to the tug, and once the tension is off, the AB lets go the line under control and returns it to the tug. If a quick-release arrangement is fitted, the AB knows how to use it and in which situations it is to be used.

Windlass çalışırken AB, zincir hareketin.en: While the windlass is running, the AB stands clear of the moving cable and the gypsy (cable lifter) area; a parting cable, or being caught by the cable, is fatal. Goggles and ear protection are recommended against the dust, sparks and noise generated when the anchor is let go. The ship should not lie at anchor for long without the bow stopper; the whole load must not be left on the windlass brake alone.

Mooring güvenliği büyük ölçüde ekipman d.en: Mooring safety depends to a large extent on the condition of the equipment. The AB regularly checks lines for wear, cuts, glazing (shine caused by heat) and internal fiber damage, and wires for broken wires, birdcaging, rust and loosening. Damaged lines/wires are reported and taken out of service; the "it will hold a bit longer" mindset produces snap-back accidents.

MEG4, halatların bir Line Management Pla.en: MEG4 recommends that lines be tracked with a Line Management Plan (retirement criteria, usage records). The AB helps to record at which station and for how long each line has been used; periodically turning the lines end-for-end evens out the wear.

Fairlead ve roller'lar serbest dönmeli;.en: Fairleads and rollers must turn freely; a seized roller chafes and cuts the line. Stoppers (chain/rope stoppers), bollard welds and Panama leads are checked for cracks and wear. The winch brake is tested periodically, and greasing is carried out according to the greasing schedule. This maintenance is closely linked with the deck maintenance covered under duty no. 3.

Mooring ölümlerinin büyük kısmı, AB'nin.en: Most mooring deaths result from an AB standing in the recoil zone of a line under tension. In some cases, the person started in the right area, but the direction of recoil changed because the line was bent around a fairlead. Lesson: do not rely on a single "safe line"; treat the whole deck as dangerous while lines are under tension and keep the escape route clear.

Diğer sık hata, çalışma alanının dağınık.en: Another common error is an untidy or slippery work area that makes escape impossible. Coils of line laid out underfoot, pools of oil or water and an overcrowded station make an accident worse.

Bağlama ve manevra, Usta Gemici'nin en g.en: Mooring and maneuvering is the AB's most visible but most dangerous duty. A line sent out in the right order, a correctly set winch brake and a disciplined seaman standing outside the recoil zone: each of these saves a limb, a life. Mooring is routine, but carelessness within the routine is fatal; the AB must take every maneuver as seriously as on the first day.

Demirde veya rıhtımda gemi \"park edilmi.en: At anchor or alongside, the ship may look "parked", but the anchor may drag, a line may part or the surrounding conditions may change suddenly. An anchor/mooring watch is an active watch kept to catch these silent dangers early. The AB knows how serious this watch is.
