Usta gemici belirli aralıklarla pozisyon.en: At set intervals, the AB checks the position (bridge display/transits/landmarks), the weather and sea state, the surrounding traffic and the tension/lead of the anchor cable, and reports to the bridge. Any abnormality (position shifting, sudden jerking of the cable, an approaching ship) is reported immediately.

Demir tarama belirtileri; pozisyonun rüz.en: Signs of a dragging anchor are the position starting to shift in the direction of the wind/current, the cable alternately coming taut for long periods and then slackening (jerking), and the ship swinging differently from what is expected. The AB recognizes these signs and informs the bridge immediately; delay has irreversible consequences.

Limanda bağlı iken usta gemici halatları.en: When moored in port, the AB monitors the tension of the lines; the tide and swell can over-tension the lines or let them go slack. Over-tensioned lines are eased/adjusted safely, staying clear of the snap-back zone. Slack lines can allow the ship to move off the berth.

Mooring watch sırasında gangway güvenliğ.en: During the mooring watch, gangway safety, unauthorized access and the condition of the quay and surroundings are also watched. The AB reports any abnormal situation (chafed line, fire, leak, unauthorized person) to the bridge.

Halat ayarlarken usta gemici gergin hat.en: When adjusting lines, the AB does not stand on or in front of a taut line; they position themselves clear of the snap-back zone, at a point with an escape route. PPE is worn and care is taken against sudden changes in tension. Rushing with a line under tension can lead to a fatal accident.

Usta gemici, düzenli kontrollerini ve he.en: The AB reports their regular checks and every abnormality clearly to the bridge. In an emergency (dragging, a parted line, fire, an approaching danger), they raise the alarm. Accurate and timely reporting determines the whole value of the watch.

Anchor ve mooring watch, geminin hareket.en: Anchor and mooring watches are the guardians of safety during the hours when the ship appears motionless but the danger persists. The AB's regular checks, early detection of signs of dragging and snap-back awareness keep the ship safe at anchor and alongside.

Çelik gemi, tuzlu su, nem, güneş ve meka.en: A steel ship is under constant attack from salt water, humidity, sun and mechanical wear. Corrosion is not just a cosmetic problem but a safety issue that threatens structural integrity; thinning plates, cracked welds and corroded deck equipment put cargo safety and the safety of life at risk. This is why surface protection (the paint system) and regular maintenance directly affect the ship's class certificate and PSC (port State control) compliance.

Boya sistemi bir kalkandır: önce yüzey h.en: The paint system is a shield: first the surface is prepared, then the primer, intermediate coat and top coat are applied. When one of these layers breaks down, corrosion advances silently underneath. The AB's job is to keep this shield intact: removing rust early and restoring protection with the right paint.

Reis, hava durumu, liman programı ve mev.en: The Bosun allocates the daily jobs according to the weather, the port schedule and the current state of corrosion: one group chips on the forecastle while another washes the deck and another greases wire ropes. The AB knows their own job but must also understand the maintenance logic of the whole deck; for example, no painting is done when rain is expected, and nobody walks on fresh paint.

AB, çalışırken fark ettiği kusurları (ça.en: The AB reports defects noticed while working (cracks, heavy corrosion, loose connections, damaged equipment) to the Bosun. This feedback feeds the PMS; catching a small rust spot before it turns into major plate thinning depends on this reporting.

İyi boyanın sırrı yüzeyde gizlidir: pas,.en: The secret of a good paint job lies in the surface: paint applied before rust, old loose paint, oil and salt have been removed completely will soon flake off. Chipping is done with a hand hammer/scraper or a pneumatic needle gun; loose rust and blistered paint are removed from the surface. The surface is then roughened and cleaned with a wire brush or a disc grinder (grinding).

Pnömatik ve elektrikli aletler (needle g.en: Pneumatic and electric tools (needle gun, disc grinder, sandblasting) produce high noise, vibration and flying particles. The AB carries out the pre-use check of the tool (air hose, disc condition, guard), wears the correct PPE and isolates the work area from its surroundings. Disc grinding produces sparks; keep away from flammable materials and paint thinner.

Mekanik temizlik tek başına yetmez; tuz.en: Mechanical cleaning alone is not enough; salt deposits draw moisture under the paint and cause early breakdown. This is why the prepared surface is washed with fresh water to remove the salt and then left until completely dry. Oil/grease stains are removed with a suitable solvent or detergent; otherwise the paint will not adhere.

Nem ve sıcaklık boyanın yapışmasını doğr.en: Humidity and temperature directly affect paint adhesion. Painting just above or below the dew point traps moisture on the surface; this is why the Bosun usually does not paint in the morning before the dew has lifted or in the evening once the moisture settles. The AB does not start painting without asking: "Is the surface really dry and clean?"

Boya sistemi katmanlıdır: astar (primer).en: The paint system is layered: the primer adheres to the steel and forms the first barrier against corrosion; the intermediate coat provides thickness and barrier; the top coat gives UV, abrasion and cosmetic protection. For each coat, the thickness, drying time and overcoating interval given in the manufacturer's technical data sheet (TDS) are followed. Applying the next coat too early spoils the coat underneath.

Uygulama yöntemi fırça, rulo veya airles.en: The application method may be brush, roller or airless spray. Brushes are used for corners, welds and tight areas, rollers for wide flat surfaces, and spray for large areas and fast application. Spraying carries the risk of overspray and solvent vapor; the wind direction is taken into account and surrounding equipment is protected.

Boya, üreticinin belirttiği sıcaklık ve.en: Paint is applied within the temperature and humidity range specified by the manufacturer. In very cold weather, drying takes longer and adhesion is poor; in very hot weather, the solvent evaporates too early and the film does not form properly. No painting is done in rain, sea spray or high humidity. During application, the AB keeps the film thickness even by eye, taking care not to leave sags, pinholes or missed spots.

Taze boyalı alan \"WET PAINT\" işareti v.en: A freshly painted area is protected with a "WET PAINT" sign and a barrier; nobody steps on it and no equipment is placed on it until it is dry. If the overcoating interval is not observed, solvent entrapment and film breakdown occur. Quality work means correct thickness + clean surface + suitable weather + correct waiting time.

Halatın doğru sarılması ve istifi de bak.en: Correct coiling and stowage of ropes are also part of maintenance; a kinked rope wears quickly and creates a hazard during operations. The AB coils ropes neatly in a figure-of-eight or another suitable coil and stores them where air can circulate.

Çelik tel halatlar (kreyn, vinç, mooring.en: Steel wire ropes (crane, winch and mooring wires) are greased against corrosion and internal friction; the grease both prevents external corrosion and reduces friction between the wires. Before greasing, the wire is cleaned and inspected for damage (broken wires/birdcaging/crushing). If the limit for the number of broken wires is exceeded, the wire rope is replaced.

Greasing kirli ve kaygan bir iştir; AB e.en: Greasing is dirty and slippery work; the AB wears gloves, takes care not to slip and does not let grease residue get onto the deck or into the sea. Waste grease and dirty rags are collected as appropriate waste under MARPOL Annex V and are not thrown overboard.

Deniz suyu serpintisi güvertede ve ekipm.en: Sea spray deposits salt on the deck and equipment; this salt accelerates corrosion and damages paint. Regular fresh water washing removes these deposits. Because washing makes surfaces more slippery, it requires careful walking and suitable footwear; hose pressure and slippery surfaces carry a risk of injury.

Yıkama suyunun ve temizlik kimyasalının.en: Discharge of wash water and cleaning chemicals into the sea is subject to MARPOL rules; deck water containing oil is not discharged directly overboard, the scuppers (deck drains) are plugged when necessary and the waste is collected appropriately.

Yağ çözücü, pas sökücü, deterjan gibi ki.en: Chemicals such as degreasers, rust removers and detergents are used in accordance with the Safety Data Sheet (SDS): the rules on correct PPE, ventilation, preventing skin/eye contact and not mixing incompatible chemicals apply. The AB must know the SDS of every chemical they use and must not put chemicals in unlabeled containers.

Her bakım işi öncesi, ekip kısa bir tool.en: Before each maintenance job, the team holds a short toolbox talk: the steps of the job, the hazards (falls from height, sparks, chemicals, enclosed spaces, slippery surfaces), the control measures and what to do in an emergency are discussed. If the risk is high (work at height, overside work, enclosed space, hot work), a Permit to Work is also issued.

AB, kendi işinin risk değerlendirmesini.en: The AB does not start a job without understanding its risk assessment and applying the control measures. When a step changes (the weather deteriorates, equipment fails), the job is stopped and the situation is reassessed. "Stop work authority", the authority to stop any job they consider unsafe, is every seafarer's right.

PPE işe göre seçilir: chipping/grinding'.en: PPE is selected according to the job: eye/face protection and a dust mask for chipping/grinding; ear protection for noisy pneumatic tools; suitable gloves and goggles for chemical work; a solvent mask for painting; a safety harness for work at height. A safety helmet, steel-toe shoes and coveralls are the basic outfit on deck.

PPE, doğru takıldığında ve sağlam olduğu.en: PPE protects only when it is worn correctly and is in good condition. The AB checks their PPE before use (cracked goggles, a worn harness or a clogged filter are not used) and replaces anything damaged. PPE is not an excuse but the last line of defense; the job is first planned to be safe, and PPE is the final layer.

Sık görülen kalite hataları: paslı/ıslak.en: Common quality errors: painting over rusty, wet or salty surfaces, not observing the overcoating interval, painting in the wrong weather conditions and insufficient film thickness. These cause the paint to flake off within months and corrosion to advance unseen; the job has to be redone from the start, wasting both time and material.

Emniyet hataları daha ağır sonuç doğurur.en: Safety errors have more serious consequences: skipping PPE (eye, hand and respiratory injuries), doing spark-producing work near flammables, using paint or solvent in an enclosed space without ventilation, and moving carelessly on a slippery wet deck. Each of these is the first link in a serious accident chain.

Disiplinli bir AB; yüzeyi hak ettiği gib.en: A disciplined AB prepares the surface properly, paints in the right weather with the right coats, wears full PPE, uses chemicals according to the SDS and collects waste in accordance with MARPOL. This way of working keeps the ship's defense against corrosion strong and protects the safety of the AB and the team. Maintenance is valuable not because it is "visible" but because it "extends the ship's life and ensures safety".

Güverte bakımı, denizciliğin \"görünmeye.en: Deck maintenance is the "unseen heroism" of seafaring: when it is done well, nobody notices, because the ship stays sound, clean and safe; when it is neglected, it comes back as corrosion, accidents and PSC detentions. The hammer, brush and grease gun in the AB's hands are really tools that extend the ship's life and protect the crew. Quality, safe maintenance is possible with patience, the right sequence and disciplined PPE and risk management.

Her yük operasyonu öncesi tool-box talk.en: Before every cargo operation, a toolbox talk (on-site briefing) is held; the deck officer explains the cargo plan, the sequence, the holds to be opened, the lashing requirements and the hazards. In this briefing, the AB learns clearly their own duty, the equipment to be used and what to do in an emergency. Operations do not start without a briefing.

Görev dağılımında winch/vinç operatörü,.en: In the allocation of duties, the persons who will operate the winch/crane, operate the hatch cover controls, carry out lashing and handle communications are designated. The AB usually takes on more than one role; however, conflicting duties, such as operating machinery controls and working under a load at the same time, are not given. Communication is maintained by hand-held radio or hand signals.

AB; baret, çelik burunlu bot, eldiven, k.en: The AB uses a safety helmet, steel-toe boots, gloves, safety goggles and, depending on the task, a high-visibility vest. A dust mask is added for dusty cargoes such as grain or ore, and ear protection in noisy environments. For dangerous cargoes (IMDG/IMSBC classified), additional precautions and special PPE apply; the AB learns these from the Bosun.

İşe başlamadan önce risk değerlendirmesi.en: Before starting work, the risk assessment is reviewed: falls, crushing, trapping, slipping, parting of equipment under tension and atmosphere risks are assessed. If anyone is to go down into a hold, atmosphere testing and the enclosed space procedure also apply; the AB does not enter a hold or tank without permission.

Modern kuru yük gemilerinde folding (kat.en: Folding, side-rolling and pontoon (lift-off) type hatch covers are common on modern dry cargo ships. Each type has its own hydraulic/mechanical controls and safety pin system. Before a cover is opened, the AB confirms that the cleats, wedges and safety locks have all been removed; otherwise the hydraulics are overstressed and damage or collision results.

Açma/kapama sırasında kapağın hareket yo.en: During opening and closing, the path of travel of the cover is cleared; nobody stands under the cover or in its path. On side-rolling covers there must be no chocks or obstructions on the rails, and on pontoon covers the crane/forklift operation must be coordinated. While the cover is moving, the AB acts as lookout, watching for hazards, and if necessary stops the operator with "stop".

Hatch cover'ın su geçirmezliği, geminin.en: The weathertightness of the hatch covers is a basic element of the ship's seaworthiness; water entering the hold damages the cargo and endangers stability. After closing, the AB checks that the rubber packing, drain channels, compression bars and cleats are correctly seated. Old or crushed rubber, rusty compression bars and clogged drains cause leaks.

Su geçirmezlik kontrolünde tebeşir testi.en: For the weathertightness check, a chalk test, hose test or ultrasonic test is used; the AB assists with these tests and keeps the rubber and bar surfaces clean. Any defects found are reported to the Bosun/officer and recorded.

Lashing'te lashing rod, turnbuckle (germ.en: Lashing uses lashing rods, turnbuckles, chains, lashing belts/webbing, shackles, twistlocks and cones (on containers). The AB secures the cargo without exceeding the MSL (Maximum Securing Load) and SWL (Safe Working Load) of the equipment, at the correct angle and symmetrically. Worn, cracked or deformed equipment is not used; it is removed.

Doğru lashing açısı kritiktir: çok dik v.en: The correct lashing angle is critical: lashings that are too steep or too flat reduce the effectiveness of the equipment. Because turnbuckles can slacken as the cargo settles, they are re-tightened at the start of the voyage and as necessary (re-lashing). During the voyage, the AB checks the lashings according to the Bosun's schedule and tightens any that have slackened.

Her gemi, bayrak devleti/klas onaylı bir.en: Every ship carries a Cargo Securing Manual approved by the flag State/class; this manual specifies how each cargo is to be secured and with how many lashings. The AB works to this approved plan, not to personal habit. For non-standard or heavy/high cargoes, the officer issues a special lashing plan.

Açık güvertede taşınan yükler (konteyner.en: Cargo carried on the open deck (containers, timber, pipes, project cargo) is exposed to the high accelerations of the ship's motions at sea (rolling/pitching); it therefore requires extra lashing and regular checks. When bad weather is expected, the Bosun plans an additional lashing round; the AB carries out this round under safe conditions (if going out on deck is risky, only on the officer's decision).

Yeni yük öncesi ambar; önceki yük artıkl.en: Before a new cargo, the hold is cleaned of residues of the previous cargo, rust, water, oil and bad odors. The cleaning standard depends on the cargo: grain/food cargoes require "grain clean" or "hospital clean", whereas scrap metal can be loaded to a lower standard. The AB learns the required cleanliness level from the Bosun and sweeps, washes and dries accordingly.

Temizlik sonrası ambar kuru ve kokusuz o.en: After cleaning, the hold must be dry and odor-free; the bilge wells are cleaned, the strum boxes are checked and the bilge pumping is verified to work. Protrusions, sharp surfaces and remains of earlier lashings that could damage the cargo are removed. Any structural damage found (holes, dents, corroded areas) is reported to the officer.

Bazı yüklerde \"kargo terlemesi\" (cargo.en: With some cargoes, "cargo sweat" and "ship sweat" cause moisture damage; hold ventilation is opened or closed according to the dew point difference. This decision is the officer's; the AB carries out the physical work, such as opening/closing ventilator flaps and running the ventilation fans, and helps with the records.

Draft survey ve yükleme/boşaltma kontrol.en: For draft surveys and loading/discharging checks, the forward, aft and midship draft marks are read. The AB reads the draft marks at the mean water level between waves and surges, from a boat or the pilot ladder if possible, in a safe position. Readings are taken in meters (m) or feet, according to the arrangement of the marks.

Trim (baş-kıç farkı) ve list (yatıklık).en: Trim (the difference between the forward and aft drafts) and list are determined from the draft differences; during loading, the drafts are monitored until the required trim is achieved. The AB reports readings clearly and accurately, giving the actual reading and not an estimate, because a poor reading leads to a wrong cargo quantity calculation and stability errors.

Sounding, tank içindeki sıvı yüksekliğin.en: Sounding measures the height of liquid in a tank (ballast, fuel, fresh water); ullage measures the empty space from the tank top to the liquid surface (common on tankers). The AB takes measurements with a sounding tape (measuring tape + weight) or an electronic gauge, checks the water/fuel interface with "water finding paste" and records the value.

Sounding sırasında tank kapağı/ölçüm boş.en: When a tank cover or sounding pipe is opened for sounding, there is a risk of flash/gas (especially with fuel and on tankers) and of falling; the AB follows the rules on earthing, anti-static measures and PPE. The measured values are passed to the officer and confirm the accuracy of bilge/ballast operations. A wrong sounding can lead to an overflow or pollution.

Güverte üstünde taşınan konteyner, keres.en: Containers, timber, pipes, machinery or project cargo carried on deck are tested by the ship's motions, green water and wind loads. At intervals set by the Bosun, the AB makes a lashing round, tightens slack turnbuckles and reports any signs of damage or shifting. In bad weather, if going out on deck is risky, the check is made on the officer's decision, with safety of life as the priority.

Yükün gemi yapısına (deck fitting, lashi.en: The loads that the cargo imposes on the ship's structure (deck fittings, lashing points) are monitored; points of excessive stress, cracked welds or deformed fittings are reported. Deck cargo must also not block escape routes, bilge channels or access to safety equipment.

Sık görülen hatalar: cleat/wedge sökülme.en: Common errors: forcing a cover open without removing the cleats/wedges (hydraulic damage), insufficient or asymmetric lashing, not re-lashing during the voyage, and slack turnbuckles. These errors result in loss of cargo, damage to the ship and detention by port State control (PSC).

Konteyner gemilerinde twist-lock'un tam.en: On container ships, failing to notice that a twistlock was not fully locked has led to container stacks collapsing in bad weather. The AB must physically confirm that every twistlock has engaged and avoid the assumption that "it is probably locked".

Yanlış draft okuması yük miktarı uyuşmaz.en: A wrong draft reading leads to cargo quantity discrepancies (cargo claims) and stability errors; inadequate hold cleaning leads to cargo contamination and rejection. The AB must report readings honestly and accurately and fully meet the cleaning standard required for the cargo. "Approximate" readings and the assumption that a hold is "clean enough" have expensive consequences.

Yük operasyonlarına destek, AB'nin deniz.en: Supporting cargo operations is where the AB's seamanship is seen most concretely: a lashing applied at the correct angle, a properly sealed hatch cover, an honestly read draft and a hold cleaned to the required standard ensure that the cargo arrives in port in good condition, the ship remains stable and the crew stay safe. In this work, haste and assumptions are expensive; discipline, checks and honest reporting protect both the cargo and the ship.

Muster List, SOLAS III/8 gereği gemide g.en: Under SOLAS III/8, the muster list is posted in conspicuous places on board (bridge, engine room, corridors, cabins) and shows who does what for each type of emergency (general emergency, fire, abandon ship, man overboard, pollution). From the card on their cabin door and at the muster station, the AB learns their duty, team and muster station.

Genel acil durum sinyali yedi veya daha.en: The general emergency signal is given by seven or more short blasts followed by one long blast on the whistle (and the same pattern on the electric bell); the order to abandon ship is given by the Master verbally/over the PA, and the signal itself is not an order to abandon ship. The AB must be able to tell these signals apart by heart and, on hearing the signal, immediately take their lifejacket and go quickly to the muster station.

Sinyali duyan AB önce kendi can güvenliğ.en: An AB who hears the signal first ensures their own safety (lifejacket, suitable clothing, head covering), then goes to the assigned muster station. Any fire or injured person seen on the way is reported at the muster. The principle is quick, orderly movement in accordance with the procedure, not panic.

SOLAS III/19.3.2, gemiyi terk (abandon s.en: SOLAS III/19.3.2 requires every crew member to take part in abandon ship and fire drills at least once a month; if more than 25% of the crew have not taken part in drills on board in the previous month, a drill is held within 24 hours of the ship leaving port. Enclosed space entry and rescue drills are held at least once every two months (III/19.3.3) and security (ISPS) drills at least once every three months; man overboard and pollution scenarios are planned according to the company SMS.

Tatbikat gerçek gibi yürütülür: alarm ve.en: The drill is conducted as if it were real: the alarm is raised, the crew muster, a head count by name is taken and the teams actually carry out their duties (preparing to lower the lifeboat, running out fire hoses, boundary cooling). The AB does not see the drill as "a waste of time"; this is where they acquire the reflexes that will save lives in a real emergency.

Her tatbikat sonrası debrief (değerlendi.en: After each drill, a debrief is held; points that fell short, late mustering, equipment failures and proposals for improvement are discussed and recorded. The AB reports any problem noticed during the drill (e.g., a blocked escape route, a light that does not work). These records are audited under the ISM Code.

Can yeleği (lifejacket) doğru giyilmeli,.en: The lifejacket must be donned correctly, with the straps tightened, and its light and whistle must work. The AB must know the lifejacket well enough to don it correctly even with eyes closed; a lifejacket worn incorrectly can turn the wearer face down in the water. On inflatable lifejackets, the automatic/manual inflation mechanism and the CO₂ cartridge are checked.

Soğuk sularda dalış elbisesi (immersion.en: In cold water, the immersion suit extends survival time by delaying hypothermia; SOLAS requires an immersion suit for every crew member under certain conditions. The AB must be able to don the suit quickly (usually with a target of 1-2 minutes) and check that the zipper and face seal are watertight. Donning time is measured during drills.

Can salı (liferaft) genelde hidrostatik.en: The liferaft is normally released automatically by the hydrostatic release unit (HRU) and inflates as the ship sinks; the AB must know manual launching (throwing overboard and pulling the painter) and how the HRU works. The lifeboat is lowered by davits; during drills the AB learns about the davit brake, the falls, the embarkation ladder and starting the engine.

Davit-launched ve free-fall filikalarda.en: On davit-launched and free-fall lifeboats, releasing the safety pins, gripes and brakes in the correct order is critical; the wrong order causes premature release accidents. If the AB is in the lifeboat crew, they must clearly know their own duty (painter, brake, helm, engine) and follow the chain of command.

Yangın drill'inde AB genelde yangın part.en: In a fire drill, the AB usually serves in the fire party or the support team: duties such as running out the fire hose, holding the nozzle, handling the branch pipe or boundary cooling (cooling the surfaces adjacent to the compartment on fire) are assigned. Boundary cooling prevents the fire from spreading to adjacent spaces and lowers the temperature.

AB, yangın ekipmanının (hortum, nozzle,.en: The AB must know the location and use of the fire equipment (hoses, nozzles, foam, portable extinguishers) and must select the extinguisher suited to the type of fire (spraying water on an oil or electrical fire is dangerous). The AB follows the chain of command (the fire team leader) and does not attempt heroics alone; a coordinated response as a team is essential.

Yangın/duman ortamına giriş yapacak ekip.en: The team that will enter a fire or smoke-filled area wears SCBA (Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus, supplied by compressed-air cylinders); if trained, the AB knows how to don the SCBA, check the cylinder pressure and manage the working time. SCBA allows the fire party to make a protected entry; when the low-pressure alarm sounds, the wearer withdraws immediately.

EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device).en: The EEBD (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) is intended for escape, not for fighting fire or smoke; it is single-use, supplies air for a short time (usually ~10-15 min) and is used to escape from a smoke-filled area. The AB knows where the EEBD is, how to put it on quickly (hood type) and that it is for escape only (NOT for firefighting).

AB, çalıştığı ve yaşadığı tüm bölgelerde.en: The AB must know at least two escape routes from every area where they work and live, the emergency exit doors, the escape lighting (low-location lighting) and the locations of EEBDs and fire equipment. Escape routes are always kept open, unobstructed and marked; blocking an escape route with stores or cargo is prohibited, and an AB who sees this clears it and reports it.

Duman içinde görüş sıfıra iner; AB karan.en: In smoke, visibility drops to zero; the AB must know how to get through a dark, smoke-filled corridor by following the wall by hand, keeping low and following the escape lighting. In drills, the escape routes are learned by physically walking them; in a real emergency, memory and reflexes show the way.

Muster station'da isim sayımı (head coun.en: The head count (roll call) at the muster station is a critical stage; if anyone is missing, a search team is sent. The AB reports their own presence and, if assigned to communications, maintains the flow of information between the bridge and the muster station by radio/PA. A wrong count leads to someone left inside being overlooked.

LSA ve yangın ekipmanı haftalık/aylık/yı.en: LSA and fire-fighting equipment are checked at weekly, monthly and annual intervals; the AB assists with these checks. Weekly, the lifeboat engine is run and the alarms are tested; monthly, a visual check of the LSA and fire extinguishers is made. Annual and five-yearly services are carried out by an authorized company (renewal of lifeboat falls, liferaft service, SCBA hydrostatic test).

AB; can simidi, can yeleği ışıkları, pyr.en: The AB checks lifebuoys, lifejacket lights, pyrotechnic (distress flare) expiry dates, the condition of hoses and nozzles, and the emergency lighting, and reports anything missing. Expired pyrotechnics and lights with flat batteries are useless when it really matters; maintenance saves lives.

AB, kontrol sırasında bulduğu her eksik/.en: The AB immediately reports every deficiency or fault found during checks (an empty extinguisher, a light that does not work, a leaking SCBA, a missing lifejacket) to the Bosun/Safety Officer. A "we'll deal with it later" attitude means equipment that does not work in a real emergency. Records and follow-up are also looked for in ISM audits and PSC inspections.

En tehlikeli hata, tatbikatı \"göstermel.en: The most dangerous mistake is to hold drills "for show": writing "done" on paper without raising the alarm, and not actually using the equipment. Crew who meet the equipment for the first time in a real emergency panic and are late. The AB must take drills seriously and actually carry out every duty.

Filika indirme kazaları (free-fall erken.en: Lifeboat launching accidents (premature free-fall release, davit brake failure, parting of falls) account for a significant share of fatal accidents at sea; most are caused by the wrong sequence or poorly maintained equipment. The AB must follow the lifeboat procedure step by step, paying attention to the safety pins and brakes.

Kaçış yolunun malzeme ile kapatılması, k.en: Blocking escape routes with stores, leaving escape lighting defective and incorrect head counts at muster lead to people left inside being overlooked. The AB must keep escape routes clear, be honest in the head count and report every deficiency they see.

Emniyet ekipmanları ve tatbikatlar, \"hi.en: Safety equipment and drills are duties that "we hope will never be needed, but which save lives when they are". The AB's value lies in knowing the equipment and internalizing the procedures well enough to respond correctly without thinking in a crisis. Sweat shed in drills means lives saved in a real emergency; this is why no drill is rushed through, no check is skipped and no defect is hidden.

Gemiye erişim; rıhtım yüksekliği, freebo.en: Access to the ship is provided by a gangway, an accommodation ladder or a combination of the two, depending on the height of the quay, the freeboard and the operation. For pilot transfer, a pilot ladder and, where necessary, a combination arrangement (accommodation ladder + pilot ladder) are used. The AB learns from the Bosun/officer which equipment is to be used in which conditions.

Erişim ekipmanı, güvenli açıyla, sağlam.en: Access equipment must be rigged at a safe angle, securely fastened, with non-slip steps and adequate lighting. After rigging and before use, the AB and the officer check the equipment; if there are loose fastenings, cracked steps, missing guardrails or insufficient light, it is not used. Access safety is not something to "fix later".

Kurulum öncesi AB; düşme, ezilme, sıkışm.en: Before rigging, the AB assesses the risks of falling, crushing, trapping, a tensioned line parting and falling overboard. If the job involves work at height or overside, a safety harness, a lifebuoy with lifeline on standby and suitable weather and sea conditions are required. PPE (safety helmet, gloves, non-slip boots and, where required, a lifejacket) is used in full.

Gangway, vinç/davit ile kaldırılıp rıhtı.en: The gangway is lifted with a crane/davit and landed on the quay/pier at a suitable angle. The AB checks that the lower end of the gangway sits firmly on the quay and will not slip, that the wheels/support leg work properly and that the gangway can move freely (without jamming) as the tide and draft change. The guardrail ropes/chains on both sides must be taut.

Gangway altına ve yanına düşmeyi önleyen.en: A safety net is rigged under and beside the gangway to prevent falls; the net must be wide enough to cover the gap between the quay and the ship and must be securely fastened. It must not be forgotten that the angle will change with the tide; the gangway is checked and adjusted periodically. An excessively steep or flat angle increases the risk of falling.

Accommodation ladder, geminin bordasına.en: The accommodation ladder is a ladder mounted on the ship's side, designed so that its steps always remain horizontal. The AB checks that the lower platform of the ladder is at a safe angle, that the steps are non-slip and sound, and that the guardrails are rigged. The SWL (safe working load) is not exceeded; the number of persons allowed on it at one time is observed.

Vinçle indirme/kaldırmada halat, troley.en: When lowering or hoisting with the winch, it is verified that the hoisting rope, trolley and brakes are working properly; the ladder must never be moved while anyone is on it. When the accommodation ladder and the pilot ladder are used together in a combination arrangement, the safety of the transfer point is particularly important.

Pilot ladder; sağlam yan halatlar (side.en: The pilot ladder consists of strong side ropes, non-slip steps that remain horizontal and, at set intervals, longer steps that prevent the ladder from twisting (spreader steps). The steps must be equally spaced, free of cracks and unpainted (paint hides cracks). The ladder is rigged securely on the ship's side; man-ropes are rigged when requested.

Pilot ladder'ın su seviyesinden istenen.en: The pilot ladder must be adjusted to the required height above the water (usually level with the pilot boat's deck); a ladder that is too long or too short is dangerous. If a climb of more than 9 meters is required, a combination arrangement (accommodation ladder + pilot ladder) is mandatory. After rigging, the AB checks the ladder visually; if a step is missing, a rope is broken or a fastening is loose, it is not used.

Combination arrangement'ta pilot ladder,.en: In a combination arrangement, the pilot ladder is combined with the lower platform of the accommodation ladder; the pilot first climbs the pilot ladder and then steps onto the platform. The transfer point is the most critical area: the platform must be horizontal, fitted with guardrails and level with the pilot ladder, with no gap or difference in height at the transfer. The AB rigs this combination in accordance with the rules.

Bütün düzenek, IMPA/SOLAS posterindeki ş.en: The whole arrangement must be rigged according to the diagram on the IMPA/SOLAS poster; if the pilot sees an unsafe arrangement, they may refuse the transfer, which delays the ship and/or leads to a report. The AB aims for rigging that matches the diagram exactly, not one that is "roughly right".

Erişim noktasında, ışıklı/dumanlı işaret.en: At the access point, a lifebuoy with a self-igniting light/smoke signal and a heaving line attached to it are kept ready. If the pilot or anyone else falls into the sea, the AB immediately throws the lifebuoy, keeps the person in sight and raises the alarm. The rescue boat/MOB boat must be ready; for night transfers, a searchlight is ready to illuminate the water.

AB, denize düşme anında ne yapacağını ez.en: The AB must know by heart what to do if someone falls into the sea: throw the lifebuoy, shout "man overboard", do not lose sight of the person, inform the bridge. Seconds save lives; hesitation and searching ("where is the lifebuoy?") cause delay, which is why the equipment is always kept ready in the same, accessible place.

Gangway, ladder ve pilot transfer noktas.en: The gangway, ladder and pilot transfer point must be adequately lit at night; however, the lights are positioned so that they do not dazzle the pilot or other persons. When the pilot ladder area is illuminated, the ladder and the water surface must be visible, with no shadows. Backup lighting (portable lamp) is kept ready.

Pilot biniş/inişinde AB; ladder bölgesin.en: During pilot embarkation/disembarkation, the AB stands at the ladder area, watches the pilot's climb, helps if necessary with the man-ropes and the line for the pilot's bag, and keeps an eye on the safety equipment (lifebuoy, light). Full attention is maintained until the pilot is fully on deck or has climbed down into the pilot boat. The person meeting the pilot escorts them to the bridge by a safe route.

Transfer sırasında gemi hızı, rüzgâr ve.en: During the transfer, the ship's speed, the wind and the sea state are important; the bridge maneuvers to make a lee for the pilot boat. The AB watches to ensure that the ladder does not slam against the ship's side or get caught, and that nobody gets trapped between the boat and the ship, and warns the bridge/officer of any danger.

Operasyon bitince pilot ladder dikkatlic.en: When the operation is over, the pilot ladder is recovered carefully and stored in a dry, ventilated place, without tension or crushing; storing it wet or twisted rots the ropes. While recovering the ladder, the AB checks it for damage (broken fibers, cracked steps) and reports any defect found. The gangway/accommodation ladder is brought to its stowed position and secured.

Pilot ladder düzenli görsel ve periyodik.en: The pilot ladder undergoes regular visual checks and periodic inspections; a worn ladder is taken out of service. The AB helps to keep the ladder clean, unpainted and labeled (manufacture/service information). A poorly maintained pilot ladder is a leading cause of fatal accidents.

Pilot her yıl ladder kaynaklı kazalarda.en: Every year pilots are injured or killed in ladder-related accidents; the main causes are incorrect securing, missing or broken steps, wrong height, missing combination arrangements and defective or worn ladders. Most of these accidents could have been prevented if the rigging rules had been followed exactly.

IMPA/IMO posterindeki uyarılara rağmen \.en: Despite the warnings on the IMPA/IMO poster, non-compliant practices such as "securing the steps with shackles", "unsuitable combination arrangements" and "securing with magnetic chocks" have led to accidents. The AB must correct any non-compliance they see or report it to the officer; the pilot has the right to refuse.

Güvenlik ağının eksik gerilmesi, can sim.en: A safety net that is not properly rigged, no lifebuoy at the access point, failure to monitor tide and draft changes, and inadequate lighting are the main causes of gangway-related falls and drownings. The AB must treat the access point as a fully equipped area that is checked continuously.

Borda iskelesi ve erişim ekipmanlarının.en: Rigging the accommodation ladder and other access equipment is a task that looks ordinary, but neglecting it can lead directly to death. The AB's discipline is shown in rigging every step of the pilot ladder, every guardrail of the gangway and every lashing of the safety net according to the rules. Whether a pilot, a crew member or a visitor gets on and off the ship safely depends on the AB's approach of rigging "exactly right, not roughly right".

Güvertedeki dağınık halat, takım, hortum.en: Loose ropes, tools, hoses, spills and unnecessary materials on deck are the main causes of slip, trip and fall accidents. These accidents account for a significant share of lost workdays and injuries at sea. By tidying the area after every job, putting materials back in place and cleaning up spills, the AB eliminates this risk at its source.

Düzen aynı zamanda acil duruma hazırlık.en: Order also means emergency preparedness: in a fire, flooding or when evacuating, an unobstructed deck allows fast and safe movement. An untidy deck both causes accidents in routine work and hinders escape and response in a crisis. This is why housekeeping is not a "cleaning job" but a continuous safety discipline.

Güvertede bırakılan boya kutusu, takım,.en: Paint tins, tools, rope reels and equipment left on deck are secured (lashing/securing) so that they do not slide and become dangerous with the ship's motions at sea. Unsecured heavy items cause crushing or impact accidents, or slide overboard, when the ship rolls. The AB puts away or secures every piece of equipment not in use.

İstifleme yaparken kaçış yolları, kapıla.en: When stowing materials, escape routes, doors, safety equipment and maneuvering stations (mooring stations, fire stations) are kept clear. No material is ever placed in front of a lifebuoy, fire extinguisher, hose box or emergency exit. The AB knows that even material left "temporarily" can turn into a risk.

Kaçış yolları (escape routes), koridorla.en: Escape routes, corridors, emergency exit doors and stairways are always kept open, unobstructed and marked. The AB immediately removes any material left in an escape route, because in a corridor filled with smoke during a fire, even the smallest obstacle causes a fatal delay. Emergency exit doors are not locked and are never blocked.

Kaçış aydınlatması (escape lighting, low.en: Escape lighting (low-location lighting) and direction signs must be visible and working; they are not covered with paint or materials. The AB reports defective escape lighting or worn-off signs. During drills, the escape routes are physically checked, and any obstruction found is removed.

Yangın söndürücü, hortum kutusu (fire st.en: The fronts of fire extinguishers, hose boxes (fire stations), lifebuoys, EEBDs, the first aid cabinet and emergency stop buttons are always kept clear. The AB prevents materials from being stowed in front of these points and removes them if they have been. A piece of safety equipment that cannot be reached is as good as non-existent when it really matters.

Emniyet ekipmanı işaretleri (levha, fosf.en: Safety equipment signs (plates, photoluminescent direction arrows) are kept visible and clean; they are not covered with paint or dirt. During deck painting and cleaning jobs, the AB takes care not to damage these signs and the equipment, protecting them by masking if necessary.

Scupper'lar (güverte tahliye delikleri).en: Scuppers (deck drain holes) and drain channels (waterways/gutterways) allow rain, seawater and wash water on deck to drain quickly overboard or to the bilge. The AB clears these channels of leaves, rust, paint residue, ropes and debris. A blocked scupper leads to water collecting on deck and a risk of freezing and slipping.

Yağlı operasyonlarda (yakıt ikmali, maki.en: During operations involving oil (bunkering, engine work), scupper plugs are fitted so that any spill does not go overboard (MARPOL). When the operation is over and any spill has been cleaned up, the plugs are removed; a plug forgotten in place causes the next rain or sea water to accumulate. The AB manages this cycle carefully.

Freeing port'lar, gemi bordasındaki ment.en: Freeing ports are hinged flaps at the ship's side; they allow sea water shipped on deck (green water) to be cleared quickly. Water collecting on the well deck adds weight to the ship and endangers stability through free surface effect; freeing ports prevent this. The AB checks that the freeing port flaps move freely, are not rusted or jammed, and have not been lashed or closed.

Freeing port'lar kesinlikle bağlanmaz, t.en: Freeing ports must never be lashed, blocked or permanently closed; otherwise water shipped on deck cannot drain away and the ship is endangered. The AB greases jammed hinges, reports rusted ones and does not block them with materials. These small flaps are the ship's stability safeguard in bad weather.

Yağ, gres, su, buz, gevşek halat ve dökü.en: Oil, grease, water, ice, loose ropes and spilled materials make the deck slippery and dangerous. The AB cleans up spills immediately, marks wet or oily surfaces and reports worn anti-slip coating where it is needed. An icy deck creates a fatal risk of slipping in winter; salt or sand is spread and the ice is broken up.

Yürüme yolları, geçiş güvertesi (fore-af.en: Walkways, the fore-and-aft passage, railings and lifelines are kept sound and continuous. The AB immediately marks and reports loose or broken railings, missing lifelines and deck openings left open (manholes, deck openings). An open deck opening is a risk of falling and even of an enclosed space accident.

Yetersiz aydınlatma, gece güverte çalışm.en: Inadequate lighting increases the risk of accidents during night work and when moving about the deck. The AB reports defective deck lighting, uses a portable lamp for night work and takes visual obstructions (steam, smoke) into account. High-visibility PPE helps the wearer to be noticed by others and increases safety in maneuvering areas.

Güverte temizliği reisin yönettiği günlü.en: Deck cleaning is carried out according to the daily/weekly program run by the Bosun: washing off salt deposits (especially after a voyage and before painting), cleaning up spills, checking drains and general tidiness. Because sea salt accelerates corrosion, equipment on the open deck is washed with fresh water. The AB follows the program and reports when it is completed.

Temizlik kimyasalları (deterjan, yağ çöz.en: When cleaning chemicals (detergents, degreasers) are used, the manufacturer's instructions and the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) are followed; suitable gloves and goggles are worn and chemicals are not discharged into the sea. If wash water contains oil or chemicals, it is collected in accordance with MARPOL. The AB considers environmental rules part of the cleaning routine.

Güverte düzeni, geminin Planned Maintena.en: Deck housekeeping is closely linked with the ship's Planned Maintenance System (PMS) and maintenance program; rust, cracks, broken railings and defective equipment noticed during cleaning are reported into the maintenance system. The AB is not "just a cleaner" but also an observer who detects defects; a small defect reported early prevents large maintenance costs.

En sık hatalar: scupper plug'ın takılı u.en: The most common errors: forgetting a scupper plug in place (water accumulation), lashing or blocking a freeing port, blocking an escape route with temporary materials, and leaving spills to be "cleaned later". This neglect leads both to routine accidents and to a serious stability/flooding risk in bad weather.

Slip/trip/fall kazalarının çoğu önlenebi.en: Most slip, trip and fall accidents could have been prevented: cleaning up spilled oil immediately, coiling up a loose rope and marking a wet floor would have been enough. The AB acts in the knowledge that disorder that looks "small" can turn into a real injury.

Emniyet ekipmanı önünün malzeme ile kapa.en: Blocking access to safety equipment with materials, covering signs with paint or dirt and leaving escape lighting defective cause vital delays in a real emergency. During cleaning and painting work, the AB must protect safety equipment and signs and always keep access clear.

Güverte düzeni ve temizlik, denizciliğin.en: Deck housekeeping and cleanliness are among the least noticed but most life-saving duties in seafaring. An open escape route, a working scupper, a freely moving freeing port and a clean deck prevent accidents in routine work and make survival possible in a crisis. The AB's value lies in this continuous, quiet discipline, which stays invisible "when all is well" but safeguards the ship and crew in a fire, in a storm or at the moment someone slips.

Kapalı mekan (enclosed space); sınırlı g.en: An enclosed space is a space with limited means of entry and exit, without continuous ventilation and not designed for continuous occupancy: ballast/fuel/cargo tanks, cofferdams, double bottoms, the chain locker, the pump room, empty holds, waste water tanks, and some cofferdams and void spaces. These spaces may have an oxygen-deficient, toxic or flammable atmosphere.

En tehlikeli yanı, tehlikenin görünmez v.en: The most dangerous aspect is that the hazard can be invisible and odorless: in a tank where the oxygen level has dropped, a person loses consciousness and collapses within a few breaths and cannot even give a warning. Rust (oxidation), decaying organic cargo, inert gas, welding gases and bilge gases consume oxygen or create a toxic atmosphere. This is why even a space where the air "looks clean" can be fatal.

Standby (attendant / gözcü), girişin dış.en: The standby (attendant) is the person who stays outside the entrance, maintains continuous communication with the person inside, monitors the atmosphere and the time, and raises the alarm in an emergency. It is a big mistake to think of this duty as "passive waiting"; the standby has the most active safety role in the operation. The AB must not leave the standby post, go off to another job or let their attention wander.

AB standby olarak; giriş izninin (permit.en: As standby, the AB continuously confirms that the entry permit is valid, that the atmosphere has been tested, that the ventilation is running, and the condition of the person inside. In any uncertainty (loss of communication, the person inside not responding), the AB first raises the alarm and then acts according to the protocol WITHOUT going in.

Kapalı mekana giriş, sorumlu zabit (gene.en: Entry into an enclosed space is made with an enclosed space entry permit approved by the responsible officer (usually the Chief Officer). The permit states the atmosphere test results, the ventilation status, the entry duration, the job description, the standby and rescue arrangements and the communication method. The permit is time-limited and conditional; it is canceled if conditions change.

AB, izinde kendi rolünü (standby/giren).en: The AB clearly knows their own role in the permit (standby/entrant) and its conditions; no entry is made without a permit or with an expired permit. The permit is not a "paper formality" but confirmation that all precautions have been taken. A briefing (toolbox talk) is held, and everyone learns by heart what to do in an emergency.

AB, atmosfer ölçüm cihazını (multi-gas d.en: The AB must know how to use the atmosphere measuring instrument (multi-gas detector / personal monitor), the principles of calibration and bump testing, and the meaning of the alarms. The entrant carries a personal monitor and leaves immediately if the alarm sounds. The standby AB monitors the atmosphere readings and stops the entry at any sign of deterioration. The atmosphere is not something "measured once and forgotten" but a parameter that is monitored continuously.

Standby AB ile giren kişi arasında sürek.en: Continuous, pre-agreed communication is established between the standby AB and the entrant: radio (intrinsically safe/non-sparking type), lifeline signals or voice confirmation. Communication is confirmed at set intervals (e.g., every 1-2 minutes); no response from the person inside is a sign of an emergency. In an explosive atmosphere, the radio must be suitably (Ex) certified.

AB, iletişimi bir an bile bırakmaz; içer.en: The AB never lets communication lapse, even for a moment: they do not lose contact with the person inside, do not get involved in other work and do not leave the entrance. If communication is lost, the alarm is raised immediately and the protocol is started. Silence does not mean "all is well"; it means "must be checked".

Giren kişi, mümkünse harness ile bağlı b.en: Where possible, the entrant wears a harness attached to a lifeline (rescue line); the standby AB holds the line and watches its slack and condition. Rescue equipment stands ready outside the entrance: spare SCBA, a rescue harness, a tripod/winch recovery arrangement (if required), resuscitation equipment and first aid. The AB knows where this equipment is and how to use it.

Standby AB, içeri girmeye uygun ek perso.en: The standby AB does not attempt a rescue alone without additional personnel fit to enter and without SCBA; their duty is to raise the alarm and direct the rescue team. If the rescue equipment is missing or not ready, the entry is not started; this is part of the permit conditions.

İçerideki kişi yanıt vermez, düşer veya.en: If the person inside does not respond, collapses or is taken ill, the standby AB's first action is NOT to jump in but to raise the alarm: call the rescue team by general alarm/PA and inform the bridge/officer. Seconds matter, but entering alone and unprepared loses two people instead of saving one. The alarm sets the rescue chain in motion.

Alarm sonrası AB; havalandırmayı artırma.en: After the alarm, the AB increases ventilation, prepares the rescue equipment and directs the team. Only a trained rescuer wearing SCBA, attached to a lifeline and with their own standby outside goes in. This rule of sequence is one of the strictest safety rules on board.

Kurtarma ekibi geldiğinde: havalandırma.en: When the rescue team arrives: ventilation is increased to the maximum, the rescuer dons SCBA, has their own standby outside, is attached by lifeline/harness and reaches the casualty. The casualty is lifted out through the vertical/narrow opening using a rescue harness or a tripod/winch arrangement. The recovery plan must have been thought out before entry; getting an unconscious person out through a narrow manhole is very difficult.

Kurban temiz havaya alındığında derhal i.en: Once the casualty is in fresh air, first aid/CPR is given immediately, oxygen is administered and medical assistance (radio medical advice/MEDEVAC) is requested. The AB must know basic first aid and CPR. In H₂S/CO poisoning, the casualty is kept under observation even if they appear "recovered"; there may be delayed effects.

SOLAS III/19.3.3, kapalı mekan giriş ve.en: SOLAS III/19.3.3 requires enclosed space entry and rescue drills to be held at least once every two months. In these drills, atmosphere testing, use of the permit, donning SCBA, recovering a casualty with a lifeline and resuscitation are simulated. In these drills, the AB acquires the reflexes to act without thinking in a real emergency.

Tatbikatta kurtarma ekipmanının çalıştığ.en: During the drill, it is confirmed that the rescue equipment works, the SCBA cylinders are full and the recovery arrangement (tripod/winch) functions. After the drill, deficiencies are reported and rectified. A "drill on paper" is useless in a real emergency; the AB takes every drill seriously.

Gaz dedektörleri düzenli kalibrasyon ve.en: Gas detectors require regular calibration and a daily bump test (a quick response check with a known gas); otherwise a false "safe" reading can be fatal. Before use, the AB checks the instrument's charge, calibration date and function. SOLAS XI-1/7 requires ships to carry an appropriate atmosphere testing instrument.

Kapalı mekan ölümlerinin ortak nedenleri.en: The common causes of enclosed space deaths are: atmosphere testing skipped or inadequate, "quick" entry without a permit, inadequate ventilation, neglect of the standby duty and loss of communication. Most cases began with the thought "I was only going in and out for a second" and ended in death.

AB, hiçbir gerekçenin (acele, kısa süre,.en: The AB must know that no reason (haste, a short duration, 'the air looks clean') justifies skipping precautions. Enclosed space rules are written in blood; every skipped step is a potential death.

Kapalı mekan kazalarının en trajik örünt.en: The most tragic pattern in enclosed space accidents is that people who jump in unprepared to rescue the first casualty also die; in one case, several people died one after another in a tank, each trying to rescue the one before. The standby AB's discipline of "alarm first, never enter without SCBA" breaks this chain.

Kapalı mekan standby ve kurtarma desteği.en: Enclosed space standby and rescue support is the most vital duty an AB can take on. A standby who waits attentively outside, never loses communication and, in an emergency, applies the protocol instead of instinctively diving in saves the life of the shipmate inside as well as their own. One lesson sums up everything in this duty: an enclosed space is unforgiving, and heroic rescues kill; alarm first, then entry with preparation. Here, discipline directly means life.

Yüksekte çalışmada (working aloft) temel.en: In work aloft, the basic hazard is falling: slipping, loss of balance, equipment failure or the roll of the ship can make a person fall. Overside work adds the risk of falling overboard (man overboard); a person who falls into cold water faces hypothermia and drowning, and when the ship is under way there is also the propeller hazard. When these two risks combine, overside work becomes one of the most dangerous operations on board.

Ek tehlikeler: çalışılan ekipmanın enerj.en: Additional hazards: energy from the equipment being worked on (rotating radar antenna, hot funnel gases, electricity), dropped tools or materials striking people below, fatigue, and weather and sea conditions. The AB assesses all these risks before starting work and never goes aloft or overside until suitable precautions have been taken.

Yüksekte/overside çalışma yalnızca yetki.en: Work aloft/overside is carried out only by authorized personnel who are physically and psychologically fit; a person who suffers from dizziness or fear of heights, or who is tired, is not given this work. The work is not started without the required permit and suitable weather and sea conditions. If the AB does not feel fit, they are obliged to tell the Bosun/officer.

Permit to Work, yüksek riskli işin tüm ö.en: The Permit to Work is a written control system that ensures high-risk work does not start until all precautions have been taken. The permit for work aloft/overside contains the job description, location, risks, precautions taken (harness, fall arrest, MOB preparation), energy isolation (switching off radar/antennas, isolating the electrical supply), the appointment of a lookout, the duration and the approving officer.

Permit süreli ve şart bağlıdır; iş bitin.en: The permit is time-limited and conditional; it is canceled when the job is finished or when conditions change (weather deteriorating, sea getting up). The AB does not start work without a permit or without its conditions being met; the permit is not "paperwork" but confirmation of everyone's safety. In the toolbox talk before the job, everyone learns their role and the emergency arrangements.

Direk veya baca yakınında çalışırken rad.en: When working near the mast or the funnel, the energy to the radar antenna, radio transmitters, whistle and electrical equipment is switched off, locked out and tagged (lock-out/tag-out). A rotating radar antenna can strike a person, a transmitter emits radiation and a whistle sounding suddenly can cause shock. The AB does not start work until the isolation has been confirmed by the bridge.

Yüksekte/overside çalışmada full body ha.en: For work aloft/overside, a full body harness is used; a waist belt alone is not sufficient for fall arrest, because in a fall it causes internal organ and spinal injuries. The AB dons the harness correctly: leg and chest straps tight, buckles fastened, the dorsal D-ring centered between the shoulder blades. A loose harness can let the person slip out in a fall.

Harness ve lanyard kullanım öncesi kontr.en: The harness and lanyard are checked before use: if there is cut or worn webbing, cracked or deformed buckles or karabiners, or rusty snap hooks that do not lock, they are not used. A harness that has been shock-loaded (has arrested a fall) is taken out of service. The equipment must be certified and periodically inspected.

Çift karabinalı (twin/double lanyard) si.en: The purpose of the twin (double) lanyard system is for the person to stay attached to a secure point by at least one karabiner at all times ("100% tie-off"). When changing position, one karabiner is clipped to the new point, and only then is the other unclipped; in this way the connection is never broken. Climbing with a single karabiner and unclipping from time to time creates a fatal fall window.

Lanyard mümkün olduğunca bel hizası veya.en: The lanyard is attached, as far as possible, to a fixed point (anchor point) at or above waist level; if the attachment is low, the fall distance increases and a higher impact results. A shock-absorbing lanyard reduces the fall impact to a level that is safe for the body. The AB confirms that the anchor point can really take the load; railings and weak pipes cannot be relied on as anchor points.

Yüksekte/overside erişimde bosun's chair.en: For access aloft/overside, a bosun's chair, a stage (hanging staging platform) or scaffolding is used. The hoisting line (gantline) and the safety line must be SEPARATE, so that if one parts, the other holds. The AB checks the soundness of the ropes, the connecting knots and shackles, and the blocks and sheaves. If a rope passes over a sharp edge, a chafe guard is fitted.

Bosun's chair'da çalışan kişi ayrıca har.en: A person working in a bosun's chair also uses a harness + independent fall arrest (attached to a separate safety line); relying on the chair's rope alone is a single-point-of-failure risk. When rigging a stage or scaffolding, an independent lifeline and a harness are also required. The AB always applies the "two independent systems" principle.

Yüksekte kullanılan takım (anahtar, fırç.en: Tools used aloft (spanners, brushes, paint, removed parts) are tied on (tool lanyard) or carried in a closed bag; a falling object can kill a person below. The work area below is cleared, and a "falling objects" warning and, if necessary, a barrier are put in place. When working above, the AB thinks of the team below; those below wear safety helmets and keep out of the drop zone.

Overside çalışmada, ışıklı can simidi +.en: During overside work, a lifebuoy with light and line is kept ready right next to the work position; the rescue boat/MOB boat crew is also kept ready. If a person falls into the sea, the lookout immediately throws the lifebuoy, shouts "man overboard", keeps the person in sight and informs the bridge. Overside work is generally not done while the ship is under way; at anchor, in port or other stationary conditions are preferred.

Soğuk sularda düşen kişide hipotermi dak.en: In cold water, hypothermia sets in within minutes for a person who has fallen in; fast rescue is vital. The AB knows by heart what to do if someone falls overboard and confirms the location of the MOB equipment before starting work. Overside work at night requires additional lighting and stricter precautions.

Yüksekte/overside çalışma yalnızca uygun.en: Work aloft/overside is done only in suitable weather and sea conditions; increasing wind, precipitation, icing, rolling of the ship or reduced visibility require the work to be stopped immediately. If the AB or the lookout sees that conditions are deteriorating, they stop the job; the "almost done, let's finish" mindset is an invitation to an accident.

Düşme kazalarının ana nedenleri: harness.en: The main causes of fall accidents: not wearing a harness at all or wearing it loosely, using a single lanyard and unclipping from time to time instead of using a twin lanyard, choosing a weak or unsuitable anchor point, and working with a waist belt instead of a full body harness. Each of these errors means death or serious injury in the event of a fall.

\"Sadece kısa bir iş\" veya \"deneyimliy.en: Skipping the harness or permit with the thought "it's only a short job" or "I'm experienced, there's no need" has led to accidents in which even experienced seafarers have died. The AB knows that experience is no substitute for precautions; every job aloft or overside is done with full equipment.

Radar/anten enerjisinin kilitlenmemesi,.en: Failure to lock out the radar/antenna energy, dropped tools injuring people below and MOB equipment not being ready during overside work are among the causes of reported serious accidents. The AB must confirm energy isolation, tie on tools and check MOB preparations before starting work.

Yüksekte ve overside çalışma, AB'nin en.en: Work aloft and overside is among the AB's highest-risk duties, and no shortcut is forgiven here. A correctly worn harness, a connection that is never broken, a locked-out radar, a tied-on tool and a lifebuoy standing ready make the difference between a seafarer coming home safely from the mast or the ship's side and not coming home at all. The AB's skill is shown in the discipline of "always full equipment, never rush, stop when conditions deteriorate", because falls from height and falls overboard are accidents that give no second chance.

Yük tanklarında hidrokarbon buharı (HC).en: In cargo tanks, hydrocarbon (HC) vapor forms a flammable/explosive atmosphere; crude oil may also contain substances such as toxic hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) and benzene. Tank cleaning releases this vapor and generates static electricity. If mismanaged, the combination of an ignition source (static spark) + flammable atmosphere + oxygen leads to an explosion.

Bu nedenle tankerlerde temel strateji, y.en: For this reason, the basic strategy on tankers is to control the "oxygen" side of the fire triangle: inert gas is used to reduce the oxygen content of the tank atmosphere to a level that cannot support combustion (typically below 8% by volume). The AB must understand why work is carried out in an inert atmosphere and that any error that upsets this balance (air ingress, a static spark) can be fatal.

AB; güverte üstü işlemleri (butterworth.en: The AB carries out deck operations (opening/closing Butterworth machines, connecting hoses, handling tank lids/manholes, earthing, supporting atmosphere measurements) under the instructions and supervision of the responsible officer (Chief Officer). The operation plan, the sequence and approval rest with the officer; the AB carries out the plan and reports any deviation or abnormality immediately.

AB, atmosfer testleri tamamlanıp giriş i.en: The AB never enters a tank before the atmosphere tests have been completed and an entry permit has been issued; an inerted tank is oxygen-deficient and may contain toxic or flammable gas. Tank cleaning is a job that "cannot be rushed and accepts no shortcuts"; every step is carried out in accordance with ISGOTT and the ship's procedures.

AB, tankın \"inert\", \"gas-free\" veya.en: The AB must not confuse the "inert", "gas-free" and "non-inert" states of a tank; these states require different precautions. An inerted tank is not entered because it is oxygen-deficient; a gas-free (ventilated and tested) tank may become suitable for entry. The atmosphere status is monitored and recorded continuously.

IGS; oksijen analizörü, basınç göstergel.en: The IGS is fitted with an oxygen analyzer, pressure gauges, a deck water seal (to prevent backflow) and alarms. The AB helps to monitor the IGS indicators on deck; if the oxygen rises, the pressure drops or an alarm sounds, the operation is stopped and the officer is informed. An IGS failure means a risk of a flammable atmosphere forming; COW/washing is stopped immediately.

COW'da sabit veya taşınabilir yıkama mak.en: In COW, fixed or portable washing machines spray pressurized crude oil onto the tank surfaces to dissolve the sediment (clingage) and make it pumpable; this both improves discharge efficiency and reduces the quantity of slops (waste) (as required by MARPOL Annex I). COW is carried out only when the tank is inert (low oxygen) and the IGS is working properly.

COW boyunca oksijen seviyesi, IGS basınc.en: Throughout COW, the oxygen level, IGS pressure, line pressure and leaks are monitored continuously. If the oxygen rises, the IGS fails, there are signs of a leak or fire, or air ingress is suspected, the operation is stopped IMMEDIATELY. When the AB notices an abnormality (pressure drop, smell, noise), they report it without waiting; seconds matter.

COW sonrası tank tortusu azalmış olur; a.en: After COW, the sediment in the tank is reduced; however, the tank is still inert and contains hydrocarbons, and it cannot be entered. A separate gas-freeing and testing process is required before tank entry. The AB does not consider a tank "clean/safe" just because COW has finished.

AB, statik riskini azaltmak için: tüm il.en: To reduce the static risk, the AB bonds all conductive equipment (washing machines, hose nozzles, measuring instruments) to the ship's structure, observes the waiting period (relaxation/settling time) for sounding and measurement, and prevents free-falling jets and splashing. Anti-static (conductive) PPE and equipment are used; synthetic clothing or tools that hold a charge are not used.

Tanka indirilen her metal cisim (soundin.en: Every metal object lowered into a tank (sounding weight, measuring instrument, lamp) is earthed or is of an approved anti-static type; an unearthed conductive object remains "isolated" and becomes a source of static sparks. Mobile phones, cameras, uncertified flashlights and spark-producing tools are prohibited in the hazardous area; only Ex (explosion-proof) certified equipment is used.

Tanka giriş gerekiyorsa (inspeksiyon, on.en: If tank entry is required (inspection, repair), the tank is first made gas-free: the hydrocarbon vapor is reduced to a safe level by ventilation, the oxygen is brought back to normal (20.9%) and toxic gases (H₂S/benzene) are reduced to safe limits. This transition "from inert to air" is controlled; care is taken that during the intermediate stage (purging), the atmosphere does not pass through the dangerous flammable range. The process is carried out under the officer's control, using fans/eductors.

AB, gas freeing'in fiziksel işlerini (ve.en: The AB carries out the physical work of gas freeing (opening vents, running fans, handling tank lids), but the authority to declare a tank "gas-free" rests with the responsible officer and is given only on the basis of verified atmosphere tests. Tests are made at different levels, not at a single point; some gases collect at the bottom.

Tank gas-free ve test edilmiş olsa bile,.en: Even if the tank is gas-free and tested, entry is an enclosed space entry: an entry permit, atmosphere testing (O₂/LEL/toxic), continuous ventilation, a standby outside (lifeline + communication) and rescue arrangements are mandatory. If the AB is to enter, they carry a personal gas monitor; the standby watches from outside and, in an emergency, applies the 'alarm first, then SCBA + team' protocol.

Tank dibinde kalan tortu/slop oksijen tü.en: Sediment or slops remaining on the tank bottom may continue to consume oxygen or release gas; this is why the atmosphere is monitored throughout the entry. If the readings deteriorate during work, the tank is left immediately. The AB does not fall into the trap of thinking "tested once, so it's safe".

Güvertede scupper tıpaları (scupper plug.en: Scupper plugs are kept fitted on deck so that any spill does not go overboard; spills are collected with absorbent. Sea and air pollution (including VOC emissions) is prevented, and port/terminal rules are followed. Environmental violations lead to heavy fines and detention of the ship.

Tank temizliği, COW ve giriş işlemleri i.en: Tank cleaning, COW and entry operations are carried out with the relevant permits (an entry/COW permit even when there is no hot work) and records; the ship-shore safety checklist (at the terminal) and the IG/COW records are kept. The AB knows their own duty within the scope of the permit, keeps in contact with the officer/pump control by radio (Ex-certified) and reports every abnormality.

En ölümcül hatalar: oksijen sınırı doğru.en: The most fatal errors: starting washing without verifying the oxygen limit, continuing operations after an IGS failure, using equipment without earthing it, and water washing in a tank that is not inert. The major tanker explosions in history (including several VLCCs) resulted from a combination of these errors and led to the introduction of the IG/COW rules.

AB, \"muhtemelen güvenlidir\" varsayımın.en: The AB knows that the assumption "it's probably safe" is fatal on tankers; every value is measured, every connection is earthed and every doubt stops the operation. In this work, patience and discipline are worth more than speed.

İnert tanka izinsiz baş uzatma, gas-free.en: Putting one's head into an inerted tank without permission, not monitoring the atmosphere continuously in a tank considered gas-free, and entering without a standby are causes of enclosed space deaths on tankers. Even at the end of tank cleaning, the AB must treat the tank as an enclosed space and apply the entry rules in full.

Tankerde tank temizliği ve butterworth o.en: Tank cleaning and Butterworth operations on tankers are the least error-tolerant work in seafaring, because here one wrong step can destroy not just one person but the whole ship. The AB's value lies in applying the rules on inert atmosphere, earthing, atmosphere monitoring and entry without exception, and in having the discipline to stop the operation at the slightest abnormality. Skill in this work lies not in speed but in unwavering attention that takes every measurement, every earthing connection and every permit condition seriously.

Her vardiya, bir önceki vardiyadan resmi.en: Every watch begins with a formal handover from the previous watch. When taking over, the oiler receives verbally and in writing the condition of the machinery, work in progress, the alarm history, expected maneuvers/operations and especially the "points requiring attention". Under STCW A-VIII/2 the handover must be complete; in a doubtful situation, the relieving person does not accept the watch without personally checking the machinery.

Devir-teslimde standby jeneratör durumu,.en: At the handover, the status of the standby generator, the separators in operation, boiler pressure, bilge and sludge tank levels, ongoing bunkering/transfer operations and the jobs to be done during that watch under the PMS (Planned Maintenance System) are made clear. The oiler includes this information in their own rounds plan.

Modern gemilerin çoğu UMS (Unmanned Mach.en: Most modern ships are UMS (Unmanned Machinery Space) certified; at night the engine room is left unmanned and the alarms are routed to the bridge and to the cabin of the duty engineer. However, during maneuvering, port operations, passages through narrow waterways and critical maintenance, the engine room is "manned" and the oiler is present on site at all times.

Yağcı, turunu rastgele değil sabit bir g.en: The oiler makes rounds along a fixed route, not at random, so that no equipment is missed. The general approach is systematic, from top to bottom and from forward to aft: first the upper platforms (purifier room, air compressors, boiler), then the middle platform (generators, upper part of the main engine), and finally the tank top level (lower part of the main engine, bilges, pumps, shaft bearings).

Her durakta beş duyu kullanılır: göz (sı.en: At every stop, all five senses are used: sight (leaks, levels, color), hearing (abnormal noise, knocking), touch (bearing/casing temperature — the limit that can be felt with the back of the hand is ~60°C), smell (burnt oil, electrical burning, exhaust) and the feel of vibration. This sensory check picks up early signs that no sensor can detect.

Yağcı tur sırasında portatif sıcaklık öl.en: During rounds, the oiler carries a portable temperature gauge (infrared thermometer), a flashlight and a logbook/tablet. Readings at critical points (exhaust temperatures, bearing temperatures, cooling water outlet temperature) are noted and compared with the previous round. The trend is more important than the instantaneous value; a temperature that rises slowly is a warning of a fault before it reaches the alarm threshold.

Herhangi bir anormallik (yeni sızıntı, s.en: Any abnormality (a new leak, a change in sound, vibration, a loose connection, spilled oil) is reported immediately to the engineer on watch. The Oiler does not intervene on their own and knows the limits of their authority. However, if the Oiler sees an immediate danger (a fire starting, a high-pressure steam/oil spray), they first ensure safety and raise the alarm.

Ana makinede her silindir için egzoz gaz.en: On the main engine, the exhaust gas temperature of each cylinder is a critical indicator. A temperature imbalance between cylinders (deviation) indicates a fuel injector fault, a combustion problem or a leaking exhaust valve. Bearing temperatures (main bearing, crankpin, crosshead), cooling water inlet/outlet temperatures and lubricating oil temperature are monitored on every round.

Yardımcı dizel jeneratörlerde yük dağılı.en: On auxiliary diesel generators, exhaust temperatures, jacket water temperature and oil temperature are monitored in relation to load sharing. A generator that is overloaded or insufficiently cooled may drop off line during harbor/sea changeovers; this is a blackout risk.

Tropik sularda deniz suyu sıcaklığı 32°C.en: In tropical waters, when the sea water temperature exceeds 32°C the cooling margin narrows; under these conditions the Oiler checks the cooling outlet temperatures more frequently. Clogging of the sea chest strainer (especially in areas with heavy marine growth/weed) causes a sudden temperature rise and requires a changeover between the high and low sea chests.

Yağlama yağı basıncı (LO pressure), maki.en: Lubricating oil pressure (LO pressure) is the lifeblood of the engine; low oil pressure causes bearing damage within seconds. The inlet oil pressures of the main engine and the generators are verified on every round. Fuel supply pressure (FO supply/booster pressure) affects injection quality and is monitored together with the viscosity control unit (viscotherm).

Çalışma havası (control air, ~7 bar) ve.en: Control air (~7 bar) and starting air (~25-30 bar) pressures are critical. If the starting air pressure is low, the engine cannot start; for this reason the air compressors and the pressure of the air bottles are monitored continuously. The air bottles are drained daily to remove condensate.

Yağ, yakıt ve hava filtrelerinde diferan.en: On oil, fuel and air filters, the differential pressure gauge (DP gauge) shows how far the filter is clogged. When the DP rises, the filter is cleaned or replaced; on automatic backwash (auto-backwash) filters, the backflush frequency is monitored.
