Ignoring a high DP leads to the filter bypass opening and dirty fuel/oil reaching the engine.

Yağcı, filtre değişim sırasında ana hatt.en: During a filter change, the Oiler turns the duplex filter lever (changeover) without interrupting the main line, so the engine keeps running without interruption. The contents of the removed filter (metal particles, coal-like residue) are examined and any abnormality is reported to the engineer — metal swarf coming from a bearing is an early sign of failure.

Yağcı her turda günlük servis tanklarını.en: On every round, the Oiler checks the levels of the daily service tanks (FO/DO settling and service tanks), the lubricating oil sump/storage tanks, and the bilge and sludge tanks. A sudden drop in the crankcase (sump) oil level indicates an oil leak, while a sudden rise indicates fuel or water contamination (sump dilution) — the latter is a warning sign of a crankcase explosion risk.

Sludge ve atık yağ tankı seviyeleri MARP.en: Sludge and waste oil tank levels are critical under MARPOL Annex I; when a tank becomes full, the Oiler informs the engineer, and discharge ashore (shore disposal) or incineration is planned. Tank levels must never be falsified; PSC inspections and ORB (Oil Record Book) checks examine whether the levels are consistent.

Soğutma sistemi genleşme tankı (expansio.en: The level of the cooling system expansion tank is monitored; a continuous drop means a leak in the cooling circuit. Sight glasses — particularly those on the oil return lines — are used to check the oil flow and its color; foamy or cloudy oil indicates water contamination.

Pompalar, fanlar, kompresörler ve separa.en: Pumps, fans, compressors and separators have a steady sound and vibration signature. A change in this signature (a new hum, knocking, a screeching sound) is a sign of bearing wear, imbalance, cavitation or a loose connection. Through experience, the Oiler knows "what normal sounds like" and catches deviations early.

Kavitasyon (pompa emişinde basınç düşmes.en: Cavitation (vapor bubbles forming because of a pressure drop at the pump suction) produces a typical gravel-like rattling sound and wears the pump impeller rapidly. A clogged suction filter or a low tank level is a common cause; the Oiler recognizes the sound and reports it to the engineer.

Ana makinede yeni bir vuruntu (knocking).en: A new knocking sound in the main engine may indicate a problem with injection timing, a combustion anomaly or a bearing clearance problem; it is reported to the engineer immediately. The color of the smoke from the exhaust funnel also gives information: black smoke (incomplete combustion/overload), blue smoke (burning oil), white smoke (water/fuel problem or cold combustion).

Scavenge space (süpürme havası bölgesi).en: A fire in the scavenge space (scavenge air space) is a hidden but dangerous event in large two-stroke engines; it shows itself through a local temperature rise and smoke. By monitoring the deposits and the temperature at the scavenge drains, the Oiler can catch the early signs.

Büyük iki zamanlı makinelerde silindir y.en: On large two-stroke engines, cylinder lubrication is carried out in proportion to load by electronically controlled lubricators (alpha lubricator); the feed rate (g/kWh) is monitored. The Oiler verifies that the lubricator pumps are running, that the oil tank is full and that there is no no-flow alarm.

Manuel yağlama noktaları (greasing point.en: Manual lubrication points (greasing points) — fan bearings, valve spindles, door hinges, crane/winch bearings — are greased with a grease gun according to the PMS schedule. Over-lubrication is at least as harmful as under-lubrication (strain on seals, dirt sticking). The Oiler uses the correct type of grease (according to temperature/application).

Yağcı, sirkülasyon yağının renk, koku ve.en: The Oiler observes the color, smell and appearance of the circulating oil. Darkening or thickening, a burnt smell or foam are signs of water/contamination. Periodic oil samples (LO sampling) are taken and sent for laboratory analysis; viscosity, water content, TBN (Total Base Number) and metal content are evaluated.

Sızıntı tespiti, Yağcı'nın en kritik gör.en: Leak detection is one of the Oiler's most critical duties. Flange weeping, pump gland leaks, valve bonnet leaks, pipe cracks and casing cracks are looked for during the round. When a new leak is found, its source, quantity and risk (proximity to hot surfaces) are reported to the engineer.

Yüksek basınçlı yakıt borularında (HP fu.en: A leak in high-pressure fuel pipes (HP fuel pipe) is contained by the double-walled pipe (double-walled / sheathed pipe) system; the leak alarm of this system is never disabled. Under SOLAS II-2, shielding of fuel/oil lines near hot surfaces is mandatory.

Sızıntıların toplandığı drip tray ve sav.en: The drip trays and save-all trays in which leaks collect are emptied regularly and kept clean; accumulated oil creates a slipping hazard and a fire load. By tracing where these accumulations come from, the Oiler identifies hidden/slow leaks. The trays are always emptied into the sludge/waste oil tank and are never mixed into the bilge.

Vardiya verileri makine logbook'una (eng.en: Watch data are recorded in the engine room logbook (engine room log) at regular intervals: main engine rpm/load, generator loads, temperature and pressure readings, fuel/oil consumption, tank levels and notable events. These records are official evidence both for operational monitoring and for PSC/class/insurance inspections.

Kayıtlar dürüst ve zamanında tutulur; so.en: Records are kept honestly and on time; filling them in afterwards in bulk (pencil whipping) is prohibited and, if found during an inspection, leads to serious sanctions. Although alarm and data logging on modern ships is done by automation (AMS), the responsibility for manual verification and signature remains.

Bir alarm çaldığında Yağcı önce alarmın.en: When an alarm sounds, the Oiler first identifies the type of alarm (sensor fault or real fault) and then immediately informs the engineer on watch. Within the limits of their authority, the Oiler may take simple actions (filter changeover, draining, starting the standby pump — if trained and authorized); however, critical interventions are carried out on the engineer's instructions.

Slowdown veya shutdown gibi otomatik kor.en: If an automatic protection (safety trip) such as slowdown or shutdown is activated, the Oiler observes on site and passes real-time information to the engineer. The locations of the emergency shutdown buttons and the quick-closing valves are known by heart.

Yağcı'nın değeri, otomasyonun göremediği.en: The Oiler's value lies in seeing what automation cannot see. Disciplined rounds, conscious use of all five senses, trend monitoring and timely reporting are the first line of defense that prevents a small fault in the engine room from turning into a major accident. A good Oiler is the person who notices a problem before the alarm sounds.

Mekanik bakımların büyük çoğunluğu PMS (.en: Most mechanical maintenance is triggered through the PMS (Planned Maintenance System); jobs such as valve overhauls, opening up pumps and cleaning coolers are planned by running hours or by calendar. The Fitter reads the work order and verifies that the necessary spare parts, gaskets, O-rings, packing and consumables are in stock; if anything is missing, the Fitter informs the engineer.

Plansız (arıza kaynaklı) işlerde de aynı.en: The same discipline applies to unplanned (breakdown) jobs: first, an effort is made to understand the root cause of the failure, and unnecessary replacement of parts is avoided. Before the job, the manual of the machine/system (the manufacturer's technical manual) is studied; in particular, torque values, tolerance ranges and the assembly sequence are taken from it.

Hiçbir mekanik iş, ekipman emniyetli hal.en: No mechanical job starts until the equipment has been made safe. With LOTO (Lock-Out / Tag-Out), the electrical supply is isolated, locked and tagged; pressurized systems are isolated and depressurized (de-pressurize); hot systems are allowed to cool down; rotating equipment is verified to be stopped. If these steps are skipped, an unexpected release of energy can be fatal.

Risk değerlendirmesinde sıcak yüzey, bas.en: The risk assessment identifies hot surfaces, pressurized fluids, heavy parts falling (trapping/crushing), sparks, chemicals and enclosed space risks, and sets out mitigation measures (PPE, crane/slings, ventilation).

Gemide globe, gate, butterfly, check (no.en: On board there are various types of valve, such as globe, gate, butterfly, check (non-return), safety/relief and quick-closing valves. Before an overhaul, the valve is isolated and the system depressurized. The Fitter removes the bonnet by loosening its bolts gradually (crosswise), takes out the internal parts (disc, seat, spindle, gland packing) and inspects them for wear, gouging and erosion.

Globe ve gate valflerde sızdırmazlık sea.en: In globe and gate valves, tightness is achieved by the contact surface between the seat and the disc. If there is erosion/pitting, lapping (grinding with lapping compound) is carried out; heavy damage requires replacement of the seat or a new valve. Quick-closing valves (fuel tank quick-closing) are tested as required by SOLAS; a malfunctioning one is a gap in fire safety.

Lapping işleminde uygun grit (kaba→ince).en: Lapping is done with lapping compound of suitable grit (coarse→fine) using circular/figure-of-eight movements, and continues until the surface is even with a uniform matte-bright finish. Afterwards, all compound is carefully cleaned off — abrasive left in the system will damage the valve again. New gland packing is cut to the correct size and inserted ring by ring, with the joints staggered.

Montaj sonrası valf, hidrostatik veya pn.en: After assembly, the valve is tested for tightness by a hydrostatic or pneumatic test. Safety/relief valves are adjusted to the set pressure and sealed. All bolts are tightened to the manufacturer's torque values in a crosswise sequence.

Santrifüj pompalarda (deniz suyu, balast.en: Maintenance of centrifugal pumps (sea water, ballast, fire, general service) covers checking impeller wear, wear ring clearance, shaft condition, bearings and the gland packing/mechanical seal. When the wear ring clearance increases, pump efficiency falls and recirculation increases; the clearance is compared with the manufacturer's limit.

Mekanik salmastra hassas bir parçadır; m.en: A mechanical seal is a precision part; when it is fitted, the faces must be perfectly clean and free of scratches, and the correct compression must be applied. On pumps with gland packing, a slight drip is normal and provides cooling; tightening the packing until it is completely leak-free burns it.

Vidalı (screw), dişli (gear) ve pistonlu.en: For screw, gear and piston pumps (fuel, lubrication, hydraulic), clearance and wear checks follow different criteria. In fuel transfer and booster pumps, pressure drops as internal clearances increase; the suction/discharge valves and the safety valve are checked. For bilge pumps, priming capability (removing air from the suction) and check valve tightness are important.

Doğru conta seçimi, sızdırmazlığın temel.en: Choosing the correct gasket is the basis of tightness. The type of fluid (oil, fuel, water, steam, exhaust), its temperature and its pressure determine the material and thickness. A wrong gasket — for example, a low-temperature gasket on a steam line — soon deforms and leaks. Non-asbestos materials are standard; asbestos is prohibited.

Conta, flanş yüzeyine birebir uyacak şek.en: The gasket is cut to match the flange face exactly; the bolt holes, inside diameter and outside diameter are marked accurately. Gasket cutting tools (gasket cutter, punch set) and templates are used. The inside diameter of the gasket must not be smaller than the inside diameter of the pipe and must not restrict the flow.

Flanş yüzeyleri eski conta kalıntısından.en: Flange faces are cleaned completely of old gasket residue, burrs and dirt. The new gasket is fitted dry or with the lubrication recommended by the manufacturer. Bolts are always tightened in a crosswise (star) sequence with the torque applied in stages; applying full torque in one go crushes the gasket and causes leakage. A torque wrench is mandatory on high-pressure/high-temperature joints.

Boru onarımında doğru ölçü almak işin ya.en: In pipe repairs, taking correct measurements is half the job. The Fitter determines the routing, diameter, wall thickness and material (steel, galvanized, copper-nickel, stainless) of the existing line. The pipe is cut with a pipe cutting machine or a grinder; after cutting, the end is reamed (deburring) to remove burrs and any internal obstruction to flow.

Kaynaklı bağlantı yapılacaksa kaynak ağz.en: If a welded joint is to be made, a weld bevel is prepared; for a flanged joint, the flange type (slip-on, weld-neck) and the pressure class are selected to match. On threaded joints, threads are cut (threading) and tightness is achieved with suitable flax/Teflon tape plus sealing compound.

Flanş yüzeyleri paralel ve hizalı olmalı.en: Flange faces must be parallel and aligned; a flange joined out of alignment strains the bolts and leaks. After the gasket has been fitted, the bolts are torqued in a crosswise sequence. Before being put back into service, a repaired pressure line is hydrostatically tested above its working pressure and its tightness is verified.

Geçici onarımlarda (acil sızıntı) boru k.en: For temporary repairs (an emergency leak), a pipe clamp or a cold repair kit may be used; however, these solutions are temporary and are replaced by a permanent welded/flanged repair at the first opportunity. The class society approves permanent repairs.

Fitter, atölye düzeyinde elektrik ark ka.en: At workshop level, the Fitter uses electric arc welding (MMA/stick) for tack welding, joining parts and simple repairs. The right electrode (according to material and position), the right current setting (according to electrode diameter) and a clean surface (free of rust/oil/paint) are the conditions for a good-quality weld. A damp electrode causes porosity; electrodes are kept dry.

Basınçlı sistem ve yapısal (structural).en: Welding on pressure systems and structural welding require an authorized/certified welder and generally class approval; the Fitter knows this limit and does not go beyond their authority. In critical repairs, weld quality may be verified by NDT (non-destructive testing).

Kalın metal kesimi için oksi-asetilen (g.en: Oxy-acetylene (gas cutting) or plasma cutting is used to cut thick metal. Cylinder pressures (oxygen/acetylene) and the flashback arrestors are checked; the acetylene cylinder is always kept upright. Before cutting, the surrounding area is made safe against fire.

Taşlama (grinding) işlemlerinde doğru di.en: For grinding work, the correct disc is used (a cutting disc for cutting, a grinding disc for grinding); a disc is never used for the wrong purpose (side grinding with a cutting disc causes the disc to burst). The expiry date of the disc and any cracks are checked, and the guard is never removed.

Torna, gemi atölyesinin en kullanışlı ma.en: The lathe is the most useful machine in the ship's workshop; it is used for machining shaft bearings, making bolts/studs, refacing gasket surfaces and repairing worn parts. The workpiece is centered correctly in the chuck; the chuck key is always removed after use (a key left in the chuck can be thrown out and kill). Cutting speed and feed are selected according to the material and the cutting tool.

Dönen tezgahta bol giysi, eldiven, krava.en: Loose clothing, gloves, ties, necklaces and loose sleeves are prohibited at a rotating machine; if they are caught by the workpiece, they can lead to the loss of an arm or fingers. Swarf is cleared with a brush/hook, never by hand; coolant (cutting fluid) is applied.

Matkap tezgahında (drill press) iş parça.en: On the drill press, the workpiece must always be secured with a vise/clamp; a part held by hand spins when the drill bit grabs it and is flung around like a whip, causing injury. The correct drill bit (HSS, suitable for the material), the correct speed and cooling are used. The machine is stopped to remove the bit.

Sabit taşlama tezgahında (bench grinder).en: On a bench grinder, the gap between the tool rest and the wheel is kept at ≤3 mm; otherwise the workpiece can jam in the gap. Work is done on the front face of the wheel, not on its side; a workpiece that overheats is cooled. A face shield and goggles are mandatory.

Mekanik bakımın kalitesi doğru ölçümle b.en: The quality of mechanical maintenance begins with correct measurement. The Fitter uses instruments such as calipers, micrometers, feeler gauges, dial gauges and bore gauges skillfully. Bearing clearances, shaft diameter, ovality (oval wear) and flatness are compared with the manufacturer's tolerances; a part outside the limits is replaced.

Ölçü aletleri hassas ekipmandır; düşürme.en: Measuring instruments are precision equipment; dropping them, letting them rust or storing them incorrectly spoils their calibration. A micrometer is zeroed before use and stored clean and oiled after use.

Onarılan ekipman devreye alınmadan önce.en: Repaired equipment is tested before it is put back into service: pumps undergo tightness and pressure tests, valves a tightness test, and welded/flanged lines a hydrostatic test. On first start-up (commissioning), vibration, noise, temperature and leaks are watched; the equipment is stopped immediately if there is any abnormality. Commissioning is carried out under the supervision of an engineer.

İş tamamlandığında kullanılan tüm alet,.en: When the job is finished, all tools, parts and consumables used are checked; a tool left behind in the work area (foreign object) can be caught by rotating equipment and cause damage or an accident. Cleaning and tidying up are an integral part of the job.

Fitter, kullandığı yedek parça ve sarf m.en: The Fitter updates the stock records of the spare parts and consumables used; the engineer is informed when items such as gasket sheet, O-ring sets, packing, bolts/studs, electrodes and grinding discs are running low. It is important that critical spares (the minimum spare parts required by class) never run out.

Atölye aletleri temiz, tam ve yerli yeri.en: Workshop tools are kept clean, complete and in their proper places. Damaged hand tools (a cracked hammer handle, a deformed wrench, a power tool with damaged insulation) are taken out of use; a bad tool is a source of both accidents and poor work.

Düzenli atölye güvenli atölyedir. Yağ/ta.en: A tidy workshop is a safe workshop. Oil/swarf is not allowed to build up on the floor (slip/fire risk), gas cylinders are secured with chains, electrical cables do not create trip hazards and heavy parts are stowed securely. Lighting must be adequate and ventilation (for welding fumes) must be in working order.

Fitter'ın ustalığı; ölçü disiplini, doğr.en: The Fitter's craftsmanship comes down to measurement discipline, choosing the right materials, uncompromising compliance with safety rules and clean workmanship. A well-made gasket change or valve overhaul goes unnoticed; a badly made one shows itself through leaks, breakdowns and even fire. That is why, for the Fitter, "correct and safe" always comes before "fast".

Makine dairesi yangınlarının büyük çoğun.en: Most engine room fires start when a pressurized oil/fuel leak sprays onto a hot surface (>220°C) such as an exhaust manifold, a turbine casing or a steam line. Oil accumulated on the floor and on equipment becomes the fuel for this fire, which then spreads rapidly. A clean engine room removes this fire load.

Aynı şekilde yağlı zemin, kayma-düşme ka.en: Likewise, an oily floor is the main cause of slip-and-fall accidents; slipping on ladders and platforms leads to serious injuries. By cleaning up oil deposits immediately, the Wiper reduces both the fire risk and the accident risk. For this reason, the Wiper's job is low in rank but of high importance for safety.

Silici; zeminler (floor plates), ekipman.en: The Wiper is responsible for a wide area covering floors (floor plates), equipment surfaces, handrails, ladders, platforms, drip trays, save-all trays and bilge wells. The Wiper also keeps track of the stock of cleaning materials and helps with waste oil/sludge management.

Bu görevler, vardiya turlarıyla iç içe y.en: These tasks are carried out together with the watch rounds; while cleaning, the Wiper also looks out for leaks, loose connections and abnormalities, and reports anything noticed to the engineer or the Oiler. In this way, cleaning is also an early-warning activity.

Çelik ızgara zeminler (floor plates) ve.en: Steel grating floors (floor plates) and platforms are degreased regularly. The oil is dissolved using hot water, detergent/degreaser and a brush, and the surface is rinsed so that it does not become slippery. Deposits that fall between the gratings are also cleaned out; otherwise oil is carried down into the bilge below.

Kullanılan temizlik malzemesi (degreaser.en: The cleaning agent (degreaser) is chosen correctly; some aggressive chemicals damage paint/seals/metal surfaces and pose a respiratory hazard. When chemicals are used, the MSDS is read, gloves and eye protection are worn and ventilation is provided.

Makine, pompa ve boru yüzeyleri temiz tu.en: When machinery, pump and pipe surfaces are kept clean, a new leak (weeping) is noticed immediately; clean equipment is therefore also a diagnostic tool. During cleaning, electrical panels, cable connections and hot surfaces are not exposed to water/chemicals.

Boru hatları renk koduyla işaretlidir (y.en: Pipelines are marked with a color code (fire line red, sea water green, etc.); cleaning helps keep these markings readable. If a loose bolt, cracked insulation or corrosion is noticed on a surface being wiped, it is reported to the engineer.

Sintine kuyuları (bilge wells), makine d.en: Bilge wells are the places at the lowest point of the engine room where leaking water, oil and dirt collect. If they are not cleaned regularly, an oil-water mixture builds up, causes odors and makes the bilge alarms/sensors malfunction. The Wiper cleans the well strainers and collects the deposits properly.

Sintinedeki yüzen yağ, sintine pompası ç.en: Oil floating in the bilge risks getting into the sea when the bilge pump runs; oily bilge contents must therefore first be passed through the oil separator (OWS — Oily Water Separator) or transferred to the sludge tank. The Wiper collects leaks at their source so that excess oil is not carried into the bilge.

Makine, pompa ve filtre altlarındaki dri.en: The drip trays and save-all trays under machinery, pumps and filters are designed to collect leaking oil; however, when they become full, they overflow and stop doing their job. The Wiper empties these trays regularly and keeps them clean. The oil removed is always transferred to the sludge/waste oil tank and is never mixed into the bilge or the sea.

Tepsideki birikinti, gizli bir sızıntını.en: Deposits in a tray are a clue to a hidden leak; their origin is traced and the source is reported to the engineer. A tray that keeps filling up points to a leak that needs to be fixed.

Makine dairesi merdivenleri dik ve metal.en: Engine room ladders are steep and made of metal; a film of oil on them leads to serious falls. The Wiper gives priority to keeping ladder steps, handrails and walkways clean and dry, and checks that anti-slip surfaces remain effective.

Geçiş yollarında engel (hortum, kablo, a.en: No obstacles (hoses, cables, tools, parts) are left on walkways; tripping accidents are at least as common as slipping. Good housekeeping means both cleanliness and order.

Gemi yalpa/baş-kıç vururken kayma riski.en: When the ship is rolling/pitching, the risk of slipping multiplies; in bad weather the Wiper gives cleaning priority to the walkways and works on the principle of "one hand always on a handhold". A wet/oily floor may be marked with a warning sign, but the real solution is to dry the floor quickly.

Separatör (purifier) sludge'ı, drip tray.en: Separator (purifier) sludge, drip tray deposits, filter oil and oil from the oily bilge are collected in the sludge/waste oil tank. The Wiper directs these flows to the correct tank and helps monitor the tank levels. When the tank is full, the engineer is informed; delivery ashore or burning in the ship's incinerator is planned.

MARPOL Annex I, tüm bu işlemlerin Oil Re.en: MARPOL Annex I requires all these operations to be recorded in the Oil Record Book (ORB Part I); the quantities delivered/incinerated, the tank levels and the dates must be consistent. The Wiper provides observation and on-site support for these operations; the accuracy of the records is the engineer's responsibility.

İnsineratör (incinerator) ile atık yağ/s.en: When waste oil/sludge is burned in the incinerator, the Wiper provides feeding and cleaning support under the engineer's supervision. During delivery ashore (shore disposal), the Wiper helps with anti-pollution measures such as hose connections, drip trays and plugging the scuppers. The receipt (waste receipt) issued for each delivery is kept.

Silici, temizlik malzemelerinin (degreas.en: The Wiper keeps track of the stock of cleaning materials (degreaser, detergent, rags, absorbent pads, brushes, gloves, garbage bags) and informs the engineer when stocks run low, so that nothing is missing from the port supply order (requisition). Chemicals are stored in their original/labeled containers, with their MSDSs kept accessible.

Kimyasalların depolanması güvenlik kural.en: The storage of chemicals is subject to safety rules; flammable solvents are kept in a ventilated place away from heat/sparks. Incompatible chemicals are stored separately. Empty containers are disposed of properly.

Temizlikte kullanılan PPE (kimyasal eldi.en: The stock of PPE used for cleaning (chemical gloves, goggles, a mask where necessary) is also monitored; worn/damaged PPE is replaced. The right job is done with the right materials — for example, near an electrical panel a dry method is preferred instead of wet cleaning.

Silici, temizlik yaparken güvenlik ayakk.en: When cleaning, the Wiper wears safety shoes, gloves, goggles and, where necessary, ear protection (engine room noise). The Wiper keeps clear of hot surfaces, moving/rotating equipment and electrical systems; cleaning these points may require the equipment to be stopped or isolated.

Dar/kapalı alanda (bilge, tank top altı).en: If cleaning is to be done in a confined/enclosed space (bilge, below the tank top), the enclosed space procedure is applied — no entry without gas measurement, a permit and standby personnel. The Wiper knows the limits of their authority and consults the engineer when in doubt.

Temizlikten doğan atık (yağlı su, kimyas.en: Waste from cleaning (oily water, chemical residue, oily rags) is never thrown into the sea or onto the open deck; it is segregated in accordance with the ship's waste management plan (Garbage Management Plan, MARPOL Annex V) and the oily waste procedure. Even with a small act, the Wiper can protect or damage the ship's pollution record.

Silici'nin işi rütbece mütevazı olsa da.en: Although the Wiper's job is modest in rank, it is critical for safety; a clean and tidy engine room directly reduces the risk of fire and accidents, allows faults to be noticed early and is the first indicator of the ship's professionalism during inspections. A good Wiper is someone who sees cleaning as a safety duty.

Yakıt ve yağ sistemlerine kontaminasyon.en: Contamination enters fuel and oil systems in three ways: from outside (solids/water received during bunkering, air intake), from inside (wear metal, gasket remnants, rust) and from chemical breakdown (oxidation, thermal degradation). If these particles are not caught by filters, they lead to costly failures such as injector nozzle wear, bearing scoring, pump impeller erosion and sticking valves.

Gemi makine dairesinde duplex (çift koll.en: The engine room has duplex (twin, allowing uninterrupted changeover), simplex (single), automatic backwash (auto-backwash), self-cleaning and magnetic filters. Duplex filters are standard on the main fuel/oil lines; while one side is being cleaned, the other remains in service and the engine does not stop.

Filtreler genelde pompa basma tarafında.en: Filters are generally installed in two stages: on the pump discharge side (fine filter) and on the suction side (suction strainer / coarse filter). The Oiler must know by heart the location of each filter, its mesh size, the direction of the changeover lever and the drain/vent valves.

Her ana filtrede bir diferansiyel basınç.en: Every main filter has a differential pressure (DP) gauge, which shows the difference between the filter inlet and outlet pressures. On a clean filter the DP is low; as particles accumulate, the DP rises. When the threshold set by the manufacturer (e.g. 0.8-1.5 bar) is exceeded, the filter is cleaned or replaced.

Yağcı, DP değerini her turda not eder ve.en: The Oiler notes the DP value on every round and monitors its trend. A sudden jump in DP (within hours) is usually a sign of dirty fuel after bunkering or of an in-line fault; a slow rise is normal build-up. When the bypass valve opens, the filter is taken out of action and dirty fluid goes to the engine — this is never regarded as normal.

Changeover, makineyi durdurmadan yapılan.en: Changeover is a critical operation carried out without stopping the engine. First, the side that is not to be cleaned (the new side) is vented to remove air and slowly equalized with the line; then the changeover lever is turned to direct the flow to the new side. The dirty side is isolated, its pressure is drained and the cover is opened.

Kapak açılırken sıcak yakıt/yağ fışkırma.en: There is a risk of hot fuel/oil spraying out when the cover is opened; it is therefore verified that the pressure has been fully released, a drip tray is placed and suitable PPE (gloves, goggles) is worn. The cartridge is removed and its contents are examined (metal swarf, water or unusual residue is reported to the engineer), a new/clean cartridge is fitted, the O-ring is checked and the lever is left in the "standby" position.

Ağır yakıt (HFO/RMG) yüksek viskoziteli.en: Heavy fuel oil (HFO/RMG) has a high viscosity and carries a heavy load of contaminants; it contains cat fines (aluminum-silicon particles), water, sludge and asphaltenes. For this reason, HFO systems are protected by a combination of purifier + booster + fine filter. When dismantling an HFO filter, the Oiler knows that the fuel is heated (60-90°C) and viscous, and that it will solidify as it cools.

Cat fines özellikle tehlikelidir; enjeks.en: Cat fines are particularly dangerous; they wear the surfaces of the injection pump and nozzle like sandpaper. If the Al+Si value in the bunker specification is close to the ISO 8217 limit (60 mg/kg), purifier and filter maintenance is carried out more frequently. If shiny, sand-like particles are seen in the filter contents, the engineer must always be informed.

Yağlama sisteminde full-flow filtre tüm.en: In the lubricating oil system, the full-flow filter filters the entire oil flow, while the bypass (partial-flow) filter keeps the oil clean by continuously passing a small portion of it through a fine filter. Auto-backwash filters discharge the dirt they have caught to the sludge side during backflushing; if the backflush frequency is increasing, oil contamination has increased.

LO kartuş değişiminde changeover yapılır.en: When an LO cartridge is changed, a changeover is made and the old cartridge is examined. Particles of bearing metal (white metal/babbitt, bronze, steel) are a sign of early bearing wear and are cross-checked against the OMD/oil analysis. The Oiler photographs the finding and passes it on to the engineer.

Büyük iki zamanlı makinelerde sistem yağ.en: In large two-stroke engines, the system oil is generally not changed completely; it is cleaned continuously by the purifier and refreshed by topping up. The oil properties (TBN, viscosity, water) are monitored by analysis; if they go outside the limits, a partial or complete change is planned. In four-stroke auxiliary engines, however, the oil is changed completely more often (according to PMS running hours).

Yağ değişimi planlanırken eski yağın boş.en: When an oil change is planned, the old oil is drained, the system is flushed, new oil of the correct grade and quantity is filled and the level is verified. The drained oil never goes to the bilge; it is transferred to the waste oil/sludge tank and entered in the ORB.

Yağ analizi ancak doğru alınmış numune k.en: Oil analysis is only as reliable as the sample taken. The sample is taken while the engine is running and the oil is hot, from a representative point of the system (usually a dedicated sampling cock on the circulation line). First, the line is flushed for a few seconds (stagnant oil is discarded), then the clean sample bottle is filled.

Numune şişesi temiz, kuru ve doğru etike.en: The sample bottle must be clean, dry and correctly labeled: ship's name, engine, date, running hours, oil grade, last top-up information. A sample exposed to contamination (dirty funnel, wet bottle) gives a wrong result and causes unnecessary alarm/cost.

Onboard hızlı test kitleri (su tespiti i.en: Onboard quick test kits (crackle test/hot plate for detecting water, a titration kit for TBN, a Karl Fischer-type kit for water) allow an immediate assessment, while laboratory analysis gives the definitive result. The two are used together.

Türboşarjer (T/C) emiş tarafındaki hava.en: The air filter/silencer (air filter silencer) on the intake side of the turbocharger (T/C) protects the compressor blades from dust and engine room contamination. A dirty filter reduces the air flow; this lowers the scavenge pressure, raises exhaust temperatures and impairs fuel efficiency. The filter panel is washed or replaced periodically.

Yağcı, T/C filtresinin yağ banyolu (oil-.en: The Oiler knows whether the T/C filter is of the oil-bath or dry type; on the oil-bath type, the oil level and cleanliness are checked. When the filter is cleaned, the greatest care is taken that no foreign object falls into the compressor inlet.

Kontrol havası (control air) ve start ha.en: The control air and starting air systems have air dryers and filters, which remove moisture and oil vapor. Damp control air leads to valve and actuator failures, and to corrosion in the starting air bottles. The air bottles are drained daily to remove condensate.

Purifier (santrifüj separatör), filtrede.en: The purifier (centrifugal separator) is the main cleaning stage that comes before the filter; it separates water and solid particles from the fuel/oil by centrifugal force. Filters catch the remaining dirt that the purifier misses. If purifier efficiency falls, the load on the filter increases and the DP rises quickly; the two are therefore assessed together.

Yağcı, purifier'ın desludging (çamur atm.en: The Oiler monitors the purifier's desludging (sludge discharge) timing, the feed temperature (~98°C for HFO), the gravity disc (dam ring) selection and the operating water system. Detailed separator maintenance is a separate task; here the Oiler provides operational support and daily monitoring.

Filtre temizliği, purifier desludging, d.en: Waste from filter cleaning, purifier desludging, emptying of drip trays and oil changes is collected in the sludge/waste oil tank. Under MARPOL Annex I, these fluids are classified as "oily residue (sludge)" and must not be discharged into the sea; they are disposed of by delivery to a shore facility (shore disposal) or by burning in the ship's incinerator (incineration).

Yağcı, her transfer ve bertaraf işlemini.en: The Oiler reports every transfer and disposal operation to the engineer so that it is entered in Oil Record Book Part I with the correct codes; tank levels, transferred quantities and operation times are recorded. ORB inconsistencies are among the most frequent PSC findings and lead to detention of the ship.

Kullanılmış yağ/yakıt filtre kartuşları.en: Used oil/fuel filter cartridges are oil-soaked waste and must not be thrown into the garbage at random. The oil is drained off (into the sludge tank), and the cartridge is suitably packaged and landed ashore under garbage/oily rag management. Oily rags and gloves are also kept in a closed metal container — there is a risk of spontaneous combustion.

En yaygın hata, changeover sırasında yen.en: The most common mistake is putting the new side into service during a changeover without venting it; an air pocket lowers the oil/fuel pressure and puts the engine at risk. The second common mistake is closing the cover without renewing the O-ring/gasket; this creates a risk of hot oil leakage and fire. The third is using oil of the wrong grade or a filter with the wrong mesh.

Numune alırken hattı flush etmemek, kirl.en: Not flushing the line when taking a sample, using a dirty bottle or filling in the label wrongly spoils the analysis result and leads to wrong decisions. Accidentally mixing drained oil into the bilge is a direct violation of MARPOL.

Bir gemide bunker sonrası purifier verim.en: On one ship, purifier efficiency dropped after bunkering; the Oiler noticed shiny, sand-like particles in the LO/FO filter contents and informed the engineer. A fuel analysis showed a high Al+Si value (cat fines); purifier maintenance was made more frequent, the filter changeover interval was shortened and the injection equipment was protected from premature wear. Had this not been detected, nozzle and pump erosion would have been unavoidable.

Filtre ve yağ işleri tekrarlayan ama asl.en: Filter and oil jobs are repetitive, but they must never be treated as mere routine. Disciplined changeovers, correct sampling, careful examination of filter contents and meticulous waste management protect both the engine and the environment. A good Oiler is not someone who simply changes a filter, but someone who reads what comes out of it and diagnoses the health of the engine.

Makine dairesinde tehlikeler katmanlıdır.en: Hazards in the engine room come in layers: physical (noise, vibration, temperature, pressure), mechanical (rotating shafts, belts, couplings, rotating machine tools), chemical (fuel vapor, oil, coolant, cleaning chemicals, battery acid), electrical (high-voltage panels) and atmospheric (O₂ deficiency in enclosed spaces, toxic/flammable gas). Each type requires its own control method.

Sıcak yüzeyler (egzoz manifoldu, türbin.en: Hot surfaces (exhaust manifold, turbine casing, steam line) exceed 200°C; in contact with a flammable liquid, they become the source of engine room fires (the most frequent type of fire). Noise in most engine rooms is in the range of 85-110 dB(A) and carries a risk of permanent hearing loss. The Oiler keeps this layout in mind and assesses the relevant hazards before starting any job.

Riskler bir öncelik sırasıyla kontrol ed.en: Risks are controlled in order of priority: first removing the hazard (elimination), then substitution, engineering controls (guarding, ventilation, isolation), administrative controls (procedures, training, permits) and finally PPE. PPE is the weakest defense because it depends on the individual and can fail; it is therefore regarded as the "last line of defense".

Pratikte Yağcı, bir işe başlamadan \"bu.en: In practice, before starting a job the Oiler asks: "how can I control this hazard at the highest level?" For example, isolating and cooling down a hot line (engineering) is always better than relying on PPE. PPE covers the risk that remains after the higher controls have been applied.

Permit to Work (PTW), yüksek riskli işle.en: Permit to Work (PTW) is a formal system that ensures high-risk work is carried out in a controlled and authorized manner. Separate permits are issued for hot work, enclosed space entry, electrical isolation, working at height and overside work. The permit documents the hazards, the precautions taken, the persons responsible and the period of validity.

Yağcı/Fitter, PTW kapsamındaki bir işe i.en: The Oiler/Fitter does not start a job covered by the PTW before the permit has been signed. The permit is usually issued by the responsible engineer; the person doing the work reads, understands and applies the precautions in the permit. When the job is finished, the permit is closed (sign-off); a permit is not left open without the area having been made safe.

Her yüksek riskli iş öncesi toolbox meet.en: A toolbox meeting (on-site briefing) is held before every high-risk job; the steps of the job, the hazards, the precautions, the allocation of tasks and the emergency plan are discussed with the participants. The risk assessment form documents the hazards and controls in writing; the question "what can go wrong, and how do I prevent it?" is answered systematically.

Yağcı, toolbox meeting'te aktif rol alır.en: The Oiler takes an active part in the toolbox meeting and, drawing on experience, raises hazards that may have been overlooked (e.g. a hot surface on an adjacent line, difficulty of escape from a confined space). A good briefing turns the risk assessment on paper into real safety.

Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO), bir ekipman üze.en: Lock-Out/Tag-Out (LOTO) is the procedure that prevents equipment from starting or becoming energized unexpectedly while work is being done on it. The electrical supply is isolated, valves are closed and pressure is released; these isolation points are then secured with a lock, and a tag with the warning "work in progress, do not operate!" is attached. The key of the lock stays with the person doing the work.

Enerji sadece elektrik değildir: hidroli.en: Energy is not only electrical: hydraulic/pneumatic pressure, steam, spring tension, heat and gravity (a suspended load) are also "stored energy". Before dismantling a pump, the Oiler both isolates/locks out its electrical supply and closes the suction/discharge valves and drains the line; otherwise back pressure or an inadvertent start can cause serious injury.

İzolasyon yapıldıktan sonra \"sıfır ener.en: After isolation, "zero energy" is verified: the start button is pressed to test that the equipment really does not start (try-out), the pressure gauge reads zero and rotating parts have stopped. If this step is skipped, someone may put their hands on equipment that appears to be isolated but is in fact energized.

Makine dairesinde temel PPE her zaman gi.en: Basic PPE is always worn in the engine room: steel-toe safety shoes (non-slip soles), coveralls (non-flammable/cotton, not loose-fitting), a safety helmet (falling objects/impact) and, in the engine room, hearing protection. Job-specific PPE is added on top: a face shield and leather apron for welding/grinding, chemical gloves for chemicals, heat-resistant gloves for hot work.

PPE doğru seçilmeli, doğru takılmalı ve.en: PPE must be correctly selected, correctly worn and in good condition. Worn-out PPE, or PPE of the wrong size or class, gives no protection. The Oiler checks PPE before use (cracked goggles, torn gloves or a defective mask are not used) and selects the correct type.

İşitme koruması (kulak tıkacı veya manşo.en: Hearing protection (earplugs or earmuffs) is mandatory in the engine room when noise is above 85 dB(A), and it is worn continuously in the main engine area. As the exposure time increases or the level rises, a higher attenuation rating (SNR) is required. Hearing loss is insidious; by the time it is noticed, it is permanent.

Göz koruması kıvılcım, sıçrayan sıvı ve.en: Eye protection is used against sparks, splashing liquids and dust, and respiratory protection against dust, fumes and chemical vapors. Respiratory protection is selected according to the MSDS/risk assessment; a dust mask does not stop gas — for gas, a mask with a suitable filter or an air-supplied system is needed. In an enclosed space, only SCBA/SAA is safe.

Kaynak, kesme (oksi-asetilen, plazma), t.en: Hot work such as welding, cutting (oxy-acetylene, plasma), grinding and open flames is the work with the highest risk of fire and explosion. The hot work permit documents that the area has been cleared of combustible materials, that a gas test has been carried out (especially around tanks/fuel), that firefighting equipment is ready and that a fire watch has been assigned.

Yağcı/Fitter, sıcak çalışma yapacağı ala.en: The Oiler/Fitter prepares the area where the hot work is to be done: removes combustible materials, cleans up oil/fuel leaks, checks adjacent compartments (sparks can pass through openings), sets up a fire blanket/curtain and keeps an extinguisher and a hose at hand. In a confined/enclosed space, ventilation is essential, as welding gases can accumulate.

Yangın gözcüsü (fire watch), sıcak çalış.en: The fire watch is the person who watches the area during and after the hot work. The fire watch's duty is to detect at an early stage any hidden fire caused by sparks/heat, to be ready to use the extinguisher and to raise the alarm if necessary. The fire watch is not occupied with any other work; their only task is to keep watch.

Sıcak çalışma bittikten sonra gözetim he.en: Monitoring does not stop as soon as the hot work is finished; the area continues to be watched for half an hour to several hours (depending on the risk), because heat can remain hidden and cause delayed ignition. The back face of the welded metal, adjacent compartments and the area under insulation are checked in particular.

Yağcı, \"sadece bir bakayım\" diyerek iz.en: The Oiler never enters an enclosed space without a permit just to "take a quick look". Many deaths in the past have occurred when a second or third person rushing to rescue someone who had entered without a permit suffocated in the same atmosphere. Ventilation is kept running continuously and measurements are repeated throughout the entry.

Her kapalı alan girişinde dışarıda bir s.en: For every enclosed space entry, there is a standby person outside who keeps in continuous communication with the person inside, tends the lifeline and, in an emergency, raises the alarm and starts the rescue. The rescue plan is prepared in advance: rescue equipment (tripod, winch, harness, SCBA) is ready and the rescue route is kept clear.

Torna, matkap, taşlama tezgahı ve dönen.en: Loose clothing, gloves (gloves can be caught on a rotating tool), jewelry and long hair are dangerous near lathes, drills, grinders and rotating shafts/couplings; they can get caught and tear off a limb. Guards are never removed; the workpiece is clamped securely.

Yağcı, döner tezgahta çalışırken talaş i.en: When working at a rotating machine, the Oiler uses a face shield/goggles against swarf, never takes measurements or cleans without stopping the machine, and knows where the emergency stop button is. Checking the grinding wheel for cracks/wear and using it at the correct speed prevents the risk of it bursting.

Makine dairesinde yüksek gerilim panolar.en: There are high-voltage panels and circuits in the engine room. The Oiler/Fitter does not undertake electrical work for which they are not authorized; electrical work is done by an authorized person after isolation, locking and testing (LOTO + voltage test). Using power tools on a wet floor, damaged cables and unearthed equipment carry a risk of electric shock.

Yorgunluk, dikkat ve refleksi düşürerek.en: Fatigue increases the risk of accidents by reducing attention and reflexes. STCW A-VIII/1 and MLC 2006 make minimum hours of rest mandatory (at least 10 hours in any 24 hours, at least 77 hours in any 7 days). When fatigued, the Oiler does not start critical/high-risk work and reports the situation to the engineer.

Her gemiadamının, güvensiz bir durum gör.en: Every seafarer has the right (and the duty) to stop work when they see an unsafe situation. When a job becomes unsafe (missing permit, defective PPE, an unexpected hazard), the Oiler stops the job and informs the engineer; this is not "cowardice" but professionalism. No commercial/time pressure overrides this right.

Makine dairesinde tipik yaralanmalar: ya.en: Typical injuries in the engine room are burns (hot surfaces/steam/fluids), cuts/crushing (tools, rotating equipment), eye injuries (swarf/chemical splashes), chemical contact and electric shock. The Oiler knows where the nearest first-aid cabinet, eye wash and emergency shower are.

Kimyasal göz/cilt temasında derhal bol s.en: In case of chemical contact with the eyes/skin, the area is washed immediately with plenty of water (eye wash/shower), the first-aid instructions in the MSDS are followed and the person in charge of medical care is informed. In a serious injury, the scene is first made safe (energy isolation) and only then is the casualty attended to; a second victim must not be created.

Her kaza, yaralanma ve ramak kala (near-.en: Every accident, injury and near-miss is reported. A near-miss is an "it almost happened" situation and a free warning of a future accident. The Oiler reports without fear any dangerous situation seen or near-miss experienced; the aim is a learning culture, not a blame culture.

İş güvenliği, bir prosedür dosyası değil.en: Occupational safety is not a file of procedures but a working culture. The safety of the Oiler/Fitter depends on recognizing hazards, complying with the permit system, isolating energy, using the correct PPE and the "stop and ask" discipline. The safest job in the engine room is one that is never rushed, is covered by a permit, is isolated and has someone keeping watch. Getting home safe and sound is the one priority ahead of every task.

Muster list (station bill), her acil dur.en: The muster list (station bill) sets out where each person goes and what they do in each type of emergency (fire, flooding, abandon ship, man overboard). The duties of the Oiler/Fitter are generally engine-room-focused, such as fire party membership, boundary cooling, operating the emergency generator/pump or closing shut-off valves.

Yağcı, kendi muster station'ını, görev r.en: The Oiler knows by heart their own muster station, their role, the equipment they are to carry (e.g. nozzle, hose, SCBA) and their alternative duty (if the person originally assigned is absent). The muster list is posted on the board, but real readiness means being able to carry out one's duty without looking at the paper.

Genel acil durum alarmı (general emergen.en: The general emergency alarm is a signal of seven short blasts plus one long blast on the whistle/bells; it calls everyone to the muster station. The fire alarm, the abandon ship signal and other signals are defined in the SMS. To be sure of noticing an alarm in the high noise of the engine room, the Oiler also watches the visual alarm beacons and follows telephone/UHF communication.

Acil durumda iletişim disiplinlidir: köp.en: Communication in an emergency is disciplined: the bridge (command), the engine control room and the teams on scene coordinate by UHF/internal telephone. The Oiler reports observations (location of the fire, spread, smoke) clearly and briefly and does not give vague messages that could cause panic.

Makine dairesi yangınlarının çoğunluğu,.en: Most engine room fires start when a pressurized fuel/oil leak sprays onto a hot surface (exhaust manifold, turbine casing >220°C). Fuel sprayed as a fine mist ignites instantly. By catching leaks early (routine rounds), the Oiler prevents a fire before it starts; this is the first defense.

Yangın çıktığında ilk adımlar: alarmı ve.en: When a fire breaks out, the first steps are: raise the alarm, report the location of the fire, cut off the fuel source if possible (quick-closing valve, stop the pump) and make a first attack with a portable extinguisher (if trained and if it is safe). If the fire grows, the engine room is evacuated so that the fixed system can be used.

İlk müdahalede doğru söndürücü seçilir:.en: For the first response, the correct extinguisher is selected: for oil/fuel fires (class B), foam or dry chemical powder; for electrical fires (C/E), CO₂ or dry powder; water is not sprayed directly onto a liquid fuel fire (it spreads the flames). The Oiler knows the types of extinguisher, their range and how to use them (PASS: pull-aim-squeeze-sweep).

Yangın büyükse yangın hortumuyla müdahal.en: If the fire is large, it is attacked with a fire hose; the fog setting gives both protection and extinguishing. The fire party advances in pairs, the retreat route is kept open and the team withdraws when heat/smoke increases. No one enters a smoke-filled space without SCBA.

Makine dairesi yangını kontrol edilemezs.en: If an engine room fire cannot be controlled, the fixed CO₂ total flooding system is activated. This system extinguishes the fire by smothering it of oxygen; however, CO₂ is lethal to people. For this reason, before release, the engine room is completely evacuated, a head count is made and all openings (ventilation flaps, doors) are closed.

CO₂ salımı iki kademeli güvenlik kontrol.en: CO₂ release requires a two-stage safety control (first alarm/time delay, then release); the authorized person (usually with the approval of the Chief Engineer/Master) gives the order. After release, the engine room is kept closed for a certain time (to prevent re-ignition) and is entered only with SCBA and after a gas test.

Modern gemilerde su sisi (water mist) ve.en: On modern ships, water mist and local application foam systems tackle a fire around the ME/AE/incinerator without the engine room having to be evacuated. Water mist works through both cooling and oxygen dilution and is less hazardous than CO₂. The Oiler knows the manual release points of these systems and the areas they cover.

Yangın bir bölmede kontrol altına alınma.en: While a fire in one compartment is being brought under control, the boundary bulkheads and decks of the adjacent compartments heat up; this heat can cause the fire to spread and combustible materials in the adjacent space to ignite. Boundary cooling is the task of cooling the surfaces surrounding the compartment on fire by spraying them with water.

Yangının kontrol edildiği veya yayıldığı.en: Whether the fire is being controlled or is spreading is assessed continuously. If a boundary bulkhead is too hot to touch by hand, the fire is at risk of spreading to the adjacent space; cooling is intensified or the area is evacuated. The boundary cooling team works in coordination with the main fire team and reports the situation to the command center.

Makine dairesi tahliye/CO₂ salımı öncesi.en: Before the engine room is evacuated and CO₂ released, the remotely operated emergency shutdowns are activated: the quick-closing valves of the fuel service/settling tanks are closed (cutting off the fuel supply), the fuel transfer/booster pumps, ventilation fans and purifiers are stopped remotely, and the ventilation flaps/dampers are closed. These are generally operated from a panel/box outside the engine room.

Yağcı, bu acil kapatma noktalarının (eme.en: The Oiler knows by heart where these emergency shutdown points (emergency stop and QCV control boxes) are and can find them in the dark/in smoke. These shutdowns cut the fire off from fuel and air, so that the fixed system can be effective.

Makine dairesinin en az iki ayrı kaçış y.en: The engine room has at least two separate means of escape, at least one of which is protected (escape trunk). The Oiler knows by heart the normal and alternative escape routes, the locations of the EEBDs (Emergency Escape Breathing Device) and the emergency lighting. An EEBD provides ~10-15 minutes of breathing for escape from a smoke-filled space; it is used for escape, not for firefighting.

Tahliye sırasında panik değil disiplin e.en: When evacuating, discipline, not panic, is essential: the space is left by the shortest safe route, it is verified that no one has been left behind (head count) and doors are closed behind. By keeping the escape route free of obstacles (housekeeping) in normal times, the Oiler makes this moment easier in advance.

Blackout, tüm jeneratörlerin devre dışı.en: A blackout is the loss of the ship's electrical power when all generators drop off line; the main engine stops, the steering gear and pumps do not work, and the ship loses navigational control. This is a very dangerous situation, especially in confined waters/during maneuvering. The emergency generator starts automatically and supplies the critical consumers (steering gear, emergency lighting, communications).

Yağcı, blackout anında sahada gözlem yap.en: At the moment of a blackout, the Oiler observes on site and gives the engineer real-time information: which generator tripped, what the alarm is, the state of fuel/oil pressure. The Oiler verifies that the emergency generator has started and that the emergency switchboard is energized.

Blackout recovery, jeneratörleri ve ana.en: Blackout recovery is the process of bringing the generators and the main engine back into service step by step. The engineer starts the standby generator, energizes the busbar and loads the consumers in sequence; the main engine is restarted. The Oiler provides on-site support in re-establishing pumps, lubrication and cooling, monitors fuel/starting air pressure and carries out the engineer's instructions.

Recovery sırasında start havası tüplerin.en: During recovery, the adequacy of the starting air bottles is critical; repeated start attempts use up starting air. The Oiler monitors the air compressors and the air pressure. During recovery, each action is taken in sequence and on the engineer's order.

Makine dairesine su girişi; deniz suyu h.en: Water may enter the engine room as a result of a burst sea water line, a sea chest/valve failure, hull damage, a crack in a cooling line or back-flooding. The bilge high-level alarm gives early warning. When the Oiler notices water ingress, they immediately raise the alarm, try to identify the source (which valve/line) and isolate it if possible.

İlk müdahale: kaynağı kes/izole et (valf.en: First response: cut off/isolate the source (close the valve), start the bilge/ballast pumps and, if necessary, use the emergency bilge suction (the main sea water pump drawing directly from the bilge). The aim is to bring the water level under control before it reaches electrical panels/machinery.

Su basması hem makine kaybı hem stabilit.en: Flooding is a risk of both loss of machinery and loss of stability; the free surface reduces GM and can capsize the ship. Flooding is therefore managed at the same time as a technical matter (pumping out water) and as a stability matter (coordination with the bridge). The Oiler continuously reports the water level and the pumping rate to the engineer.

Makine dairesi yangınında ana yangın pom.en: In an engine room fire, the main fire pump may be unusable; in that case the emergency fire pump, located outside the engine room and with its own power source, is started and pressurizes the fire main. The Oiler knows the location of the emergency fire pump, its starting procedure and its suction line.

Dümen sistemi arızasında emergency steer.en: In the event of a steering system failure, the emergency steering procedure is applied; steering is controlled from the steering gear room by manual/local control, in coordination with the bridge by telephone/signals. The Oiler knows their duty at this position and the emergency steering drills.

Terk gemi (abandon ship) durumunda Yağcı.en: In an abandon ship situation, the Oiler, according to their role in the muster list, helps with preparing the lifeboats/liferafts, carrying portable equipment or the head count. In a man overboard situation, the engine is kept ready for maneuvering; the Oiler carries out their maneuvering support duty in the engine room.

Yağcı, her drill'i kendi görevini gerçek.en: The Oiler sees every drill as an opportunity to rehearse their own duty as if it were a real emergency: time taken to find the equipment, donning SCBA, closing valves, the escape route. Deficiencies identified in the debrief after the drill (equipment failure, unclear duties) are reported and corrected.

Acil durumda kullanılacak ekipmanın yeri.en: The location and use of the equipment needed in an emergency are learned in normal times: SCBA, EEBD, portable extinguishers, fire stations, emergency stop and QCV boxes, escape routes, emergency generator/pump. A newly joined Oiler learns these points by walking round them at the first opportunity after joining the ship (familiarization), and this is recorded.

Acil durumda Yağcı/Fitter'ın değeri, pan.en: In an emergency, the value of the Oiler/Fitter lies in relying on procedure, not on panic. Cutting off the fuel source, choosing the right extinguisher, evacuating with discipline and giving the engineer a clear report stop a small incident before it turns into a disaster. The best emergency response is the routine round that prevents a fire before it starts; the best way out is an escape route kept clear in normal times. Preparedness is gained long before the moment of crisis, not during it.

Makine dairesinde kullanılan başlıca kal.en: The main lifting equipment used in the engine room comprises chain blocks / lever hoists, overhead travelling cranes and monorails (overhead crane above the ME), wire rope slings, chain slings, textile/web slings (polyester webbing slings), shackles, eye bolts and trolleys. Each has its own SWL, limits of use and inspection criteria.

Bu ekipmanlar bir \"kaldırma planı\" çer.en: This equipment is used together within a "lifting plan": the load is attached with the correct sling and shackle, lifted with a chain block or crane, and moved with a trolley. The weakest link in the chain determines the strength of the whole system; each component must therefore be sound in its own right.

SWL (Safe Working Load) veya WLL (Workin.en: SWL (Safe Working Load) or WLL (Working Load Limit) is the maximum load that a piece of equipment can lift safely, and it is marked/labeled on the equipment. This value is obtained by dividing the breaking load of the equipment by a safety factor (usually 4:1, 5:1, or 7:1 for textile slings). The SWL is never exceeded.

Sling'lerde efektif SWL, kullanım açısın.en: For slings, the effective SWL decreases with the sling angle; as the slings move away from the vertical (as the angle increases), the load in each leg increases. In multi-leg slinging, the Oiler allows for the angle factor; a wide angle (>120°) is very dangerous. If the SWL label cannot be read, the equipment is not used.

Çelik tel sapanlar zamanla yorulur ve ha.en: Wire rope slings fatigue and become damaged over time. Defects looked for during inspection: broken wires, kinks (permanent bends/loops), bird-caging (wires opening out like a cage), excessive wear, corrosion (rust), heat damage (discoloration) and damage at the eye/termination area (ferrule/splice). A specified number of broken wires (ISO 4309 criteria) takes the equipment out of service.

Yağcı, sapanı boylu boyunca elle (eldive.en: The Oiler checks the sling along its full length by hand (wearing gloves) and by eye; broken wires prick, and kinks can be felt by hand. If an oily rag is run along the full length of the sling, broken wires snag on the rag — a practical way of checking. The eye and the pressed ferrule area are the most critical inspection points.

Çelik sapan keskin köşelerden geçerken y.en: If no softeners (softener/packing) are used where a wire sling passes over sharp edges, the wire is crushed and breaks. A sling is not knotted or kinked and is not bent under load. When not in use, it is stored dry, hung up and protected from corrosion; it is not dragged along the floor.

Tekstil/web sling'ler hafif ve yüzeyi ko.en: Textile/web slings are light and protect the surface of the load, but they are sensitive to cuts, abrasion, chemical damage and UV degradation. Inspection looks for: tears/cuts, worn webbing, chemical burns (oil/acid stains and stiffening), heat damage (melting/glazing), broken stitching and fading. The label (SWL, material, date of manufacture/test) must be legible; a sling without a label is not used.

Tekstil sling'lerde renk kodu kapasiteyi.en: On textile slings, the color code indicates capacity (e.g. violet = 1 t, green = 2 t, yellow = 3 t — a standard convention); however, the SWL is always confirmed from the label. If no protection is used at a sharp edge, the sling is cut instantly. A damaged sling is not repaired; it is discarded.

Zincir sapanlar yüksek sıcaklık ve aşınm.en: Chain slings are resistant to high temperature and wear and are often used in the engine room. Inspection looks for: link wear (reduced diameter), stretching/elongation (stretch — the links look elongated), cracks, nicks, deformation, damage to welds/joints and the condition of the master link/hook. The safety latch on the hook must work.

Zincir halkalarındaki uzama, aşırı yükün.en: Elongation of chain links is a sign of overloading; it is detected by measurement (with a gauge). When wear exceeds a specified percentage, the chain is scrapped. The Oiler checks the chain link by link along its full length; a single damaged link takes the whole chain out of service.

Shackle (D veya bow tipi), sapan ile yük.en: A shackle (D or bow type) connects the sling to the load/lifting point. Inspection looks for: SWL marking on the shackle and its pin, deformation (opening/bending), wear, cracks and the condition of the pin thread. The pin must be fully seated, and the correct shackle pin must be used (a wrong/improvised pin is lethal). The pin is not rigged in a position where it can turn/work loose under load.

Shackle'ın gövdesine yan (transverse) yü.en: No side (transverse) load is applied to a shackle; it is loaded only along the axis for which it was designed. A shackle with an unsuitable item such as a screw/nail fitted in place of its pin must never be used. A shackle without an SWL marking, or one that is deformed, is out of service.

Eye bolt (mapa), ekipmana vidalanan kald.en: An eye bolt is a lifting point screwed into a piece of equipment (e.g. a pump casing, a motor). A plain eye bolt is suitable only for axial (vertical) loads; if it is loaded at an angle, it breaks — collar/swivel eye bolts are used for angled loads. The eye bolt must be screwed fully home (shoulder in contact) and its threads must be in good condition.

Ekipman üreticisinin belirlediği kaldırm.en: The lifting points specified by the equipment manufacturer (lifting points / pad-eyes) are used; lifting is never done from a random pipe or a weak flange. The Oiler checks the lifting diagram in the equipment manual.

Chain block (zincir palanga), makine dai.en: The chain block is the most widely used lifting device in the engine room. Inspection looks for: wear/elongation/cracks in the load chain, smooth operation of the hand chain, the brake mechanism (load holding — the block must not slip when it takes the load), the hook and safety latch, and deformation of the housing. The SWL plate must be legible.

Fren testi kritiktir: yük kaldırıldığınd.en: The brake test is critical: when the load has been lifted and the hand chain is released, the load must stay where it is and must not slip. A slipping brake is lethal. A chain block is pulled straight; pulling it at a side angle jams the chain and damages the device.

ME üstündeki tavan vinci (overhead trave.en: The overhead travelling crane above the ME and the monorail are fixed equipment designed for lifting heavy engine parts; their SWL is marked on their rails/girders. Inspection looks for: rail condition, trolley movement, limit switches, brake, hook and hoist wire/chain, and operation of the control pendant. Periodic load testing and certification are required.

Yağcı, crane'i kullanmadan önce hareket.en: Before using the crane, the Oiler checks the path of travel (that no one is under the load), the limit switches and the brakes. A load above the SWL of the crane is never lifted; a lifting plan and a risk assessment are made before a heavy lift.

Tüm kaldırma ekipmanları bir \"register.en: All lifting equipment is recorded in a "register of lifting appliances and cargo gear"; the SWL, last test date, certificate and inspection history of each item are kept in this register. Periodic (usually annual) inspection and inspection with load testing by an authorized person/company are mandatory; the validity of certificates is tracked.

Yağcı, kullandığı ekipmanın sertifikasın.en: The Oiler verifies that the certificate of the equipment being used is current (date on the tag/in the register). Equipment that is out of date is not used, even if it looks sound; this is a finding both for safety and in class/PSC inspections.

Birçok gemi, muayene durumunu görsel tak.en: Many ships use a color coding system to track inspection status visually; equipment fitted with the colored tag/tape for the current inspection period is fit for use. If the color is out of date or there is no tag, the equipment is set aside. Damaged equipment is clearly marked with an "out of service" tag and physically removed from use (collected/locked away) so that it is not used by mistake.

Yağcı, kullandığı ve kontrol ettiği ekip.en: The Oiler records the condition of the equipment used and checked and the lifting operations carried out; the maintenance records must be available for the PMS and for class inspections. The decision to take equipment out of service is made without hesitation.

Her ağır kaldırma öncesi plan yapılır: y.en: A plan is made before every heavy lift: the weight and center of gravity of the load, the equipment to be used and its SWL, the lifting points, the sling angle, the route of travel and the allocation of tasks are determined. The load is slung so that it is balanced; if the center of gravity is misjudged, the load rotates or slips. Soft edge protectors (softeners) are used.

Sapanlamada açı kontrol edilir, bacak yü.en: When slinging, the angle is checked, the leg loads are balanced and correct seating on the hook is ensured. The lift starts slowly and under control; as soon as the load leaves the ground (a few cm), the lift is stopped to check the balance and the seating of the slings, and only then continued.

Kaldırma sırasında tek bir yönlendirici.en: During the lift, a single signaller (banksman/signaller) directs the operation with clear hand/verbal signals; mixed orders are dangerous. Absolute rule: no one stands under a suspended load or in its path. If a taut rope/chain parts, the snap-back is lethal.

Yağcı, kaldırma sırasında geri çekilme a.en: During the lift, the Oiler keeps a clear area to withdraw to, wears gloves and keeps their hands away from pinch points. If the ship is rolling, the load can swing freely; in bad weather/when rolling, heavy lifts are postponed or carried out with extra safety measures.

En yaygın hatalar: SWL aşımı (yükü hafif.en: The most common mistakes are: exceeding the SWL (underestimating the load), a wrong sling angle (excessive leg loads at a wide angle), using unlabeled/uncertified equipment, slings without protection at sharp edges, side-loaded shackles/eye bolts and using a chain block without testing its brake. Another is using damaged equipment with an "it's a short job, it'll do" mentality.

Gemi hareketinin (roll/pitch) yükü dinam.en: It is often forgotten that the ship's motion (roll/pitch) increases the load dynamically; a static SWL calculation may be inadequate when the ship is rolling. The Oiler leaves a safety margin, allowing for the sea state.

Bir gemide silindir kapağı kaldırılırken.en: On one ship, while a cylinder cover was being lifted, the load started to slip slowly because the brake of the chain block in use was worn; the Oiler noticed this early, immediately lowered the load onto a secure support and moved personnel out of the line of the load. The investigation revealed that the periodic inspection date of the block had passed; the equipment was taken out of service. A few seconds of attention prevented a serious crushing accident.

Kaldırma ekipmanı kuru, temiz ve korozyo.en: Lifting equipment is stored dry, clean and protected from corrosion; slings are kept hanging (not dragged along the floor), and chain blocks are lubricated and stored covered. Equipment left carelessly in a damp/oily environment deteriorates and is unsafe at its next use. Maintenance is included in the PMS program.

Hasarlı ekipman onarılmaya çalışılmaz (ö.en: No attempt is made to repair damaged equipment (especially slings and shackles); the standard is to discard the damaged item and replace it with a new certified one. An attempt to "repair it and use it" leaves an invisible weakness.

Güvenli kaldırma, eğitim gerektiren bir.en: Safe lifting is a skill that requires training: sling angles, center of gravity, equipment selection and signaling have to be learned. Inexperienced personnel work under the supervision of a competent person. Over time, the Oiler/Fitter masters this skill and passes correct practice on to newcomers.

Kaldırma ve taşıma ekipmanı güvenliği, m.en: Lifting and handling equipment safety prevents the most fatal accidents in the engine room. Meticulous checking of every sling, every shackle and every brake, correct slinging and the discipline of "never go under a suspended load" make working with heavy parts safe. A good Fitter is someone who lifts even the heaviest part in the safest way, does not use any equipment they have doubts about and keeps complete records. There is no shortcut here; there is only the right way.

Bunker, transfer ve bilge operasyonları.en: Bunkering, transfer and bilge operations involve oily liquids and are therefore the jobs with the highest risk of marine pollution. MARPOL Annex I prohibits oil pollution from the engine room under strict rules; the oil content of bilge water that may be discharged into the sea must not exceed 15 ppm (parts per million), and such discharge is only possible through an approved separator + 15 ppm alarm.

Yağcı, bu operasyonlarda \"sıfır kirlili.en: In these operations, the Oiler works to a "zero pollution" target: every flange, every hose and every valve is a potential leak point. Drip trays, scupper plugs and SOPEP material are prepared in advance. Even a small overflow or leak is reported immediately and cleaned up; it is never concealed.

Tüm yağ ile ilgili işlemler (bunker alım.en: All oil-related operations (bunkering, internal transfer, bilge discharge, sludge disposal, incineration) are recorded in the Oil Record Book (ORB) Part I with the standard codes, promptly and correctly. The ORB is the document most frequently examined in PSC and flag State inspections; tank levels, quantities and times must be consistent.

Yağcı, kayıtları bizzat tutmasa da opera.en: Although the Oiler does not keep the records personally, they observe the operational data (start/finish times, quantity received, tank levels, alarm events) accurately and pass them to the engineer; these data are entered in the ORB. An ORB that is incorrect or filled in afterwards in bulk is regarded as falsification.

Bunker öncesi kapsamlı hazırlık yapılır:.en: Thorough preparation is made before bunkering: the bunker plan (how much into which tank, sequence), verification of tank levels and available capacity (ullage), checking that the air vent pipes are clear, checking the manifold connections, plugging the scuppers, placing drip trays and having the SOPEP material ready. The Ship-Shore (or ship-barge) Safety Checklist is completed and the communication/emergency stop signal is agreed.

Yağcı, scupper tıkaçlarının (deck scuppe.en: The Oiler verifies that the scupper plugs (deck scupper plugs) are fitted; these plugs prevent a possible deck spill from going into the sea. Drip trays are placed around the manifold, and absorbent material and shovels/rags are made ready. The no-smoking/no-naked-flame rule for bunkering is applied and the "B flag" (Bravo) is hoisted.

SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency.en: The SOPEP (Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan) locker contains absorbent pads/pillows, shovels, rags, plastic bags, dispersant (if appropriate) and warning material. Before bunkering, this material is moved close to the manifold. If a spill occurs, the plan is activated immediately: stop the source, limit the spread, collect and report (Master, terminal, port authority).

Bunker başlarken düşük debiyle (slow rat.en: Bunkering starts at a slow rate; the rate is increased after the tightness of the connections and flow to the correct tank have been verified. The Oiler stands at the manifold and continuously watches the flange, hose and valve connections, reporting even the slightest weeping/leak. A separate person monitors the tank levels (sounding/ullage or level gauge).

Tank dolmaya yaklaştığında \"topping off.en: As a tank approaches full, the rate is reduced in the "topping off" stage; the risk of overflow is highest at this moment. Fuel spraying from the air vent pipes is a sign of overflow and requires an immediate stop. Filling stops when the tank is 90-95% full (manufacturer/company limit), and the next tank is started.

Bunker sırasında, MARPOL Annex VI ve şir.en: During bunkering, a representative fuel sample is taken (usually with a continuous drip sampler at the manifold) as required by MARPOL Annex VI and company procedure. This sealed sample (MARPOL sample) is kept and, if necessary, sent for laboratory analysis in the event of a dispute. It is recorded together with the Bunker Delivery Note (BDN).

İç transfer; storage tanktan settling ta.en: Internal transfer is the transfer of fuel from a storage tank to a settling tank, from a settling tank to a service tank, or between tanks. On the engineer's instructions, the Oiler opens/closes the correct valves (line-up), starts the transfer pump and watches the levels of both the tank being emptied and the tank being filled. A wrong valve line-up can cause a transfer to the wrong tank or an overflow.

Transfer boyunca tank seviyeleri sürekli.en: Tank levels are monitored continuously throughout the transfer; the transfer is stopped as the target level is approached. Settling and service tanks generally have high/low-level alarms; action is taken when an alarm sounds. The tank being emptied is not allowed to run completely dry, which would make the pump run dry (draw air).

Farklı bunker partileri (özellikle farkl.en: When different bunker batches (especially from different suppliers/of different types) are mixed, incompatibility can cause sludge precipitation and clogging of purifiers/filters. Where possible, batches are kept in separate tanks; if mixing is unavoidable, a compatibility test is carried out. Low-sulfur fuel for ECA areas is kept ready in a separate service tank.

Makine dairesinde biriken yağlı sintine.en: Oily bilge water accumulated in the engine room must not be discharged directly into the sea; it is first processed by the Oily Water Separator (OWS / 15 ppm bilge separator). The OWS separates the water from the oil, and the Oil Content Monitor (OCM / 15 ppm alarm) continuously measures the oil content of the water leaving it. If 15 ppm is exceeded, the three-way valve automatically redirects the discharge back to the bilge tank (not to the sea).
